text:
Commanding Heights is either a fragmented thoughtful analysis or a hit piece on certain kinds of technological progress, or both.

Commanding Heights views the current evolving societal paradigm shift through an outdated vertical lens. Decentralized protocols add horizontal organizing principles to top-down command and control creating a sturdier, smarter, wealthier and more real-time connected social fabric. The result isn't a few owned heights but omnidirectional, fractal expansion, with firms shrinking on average and every person a prime mover in their own contexts.

"Own the rails or pay those who do" assumes the rails must be owned. We're adding horizontal organizing principles, via rigorously decentralized protocols, to the age-old top-down command and control architecture of the global economy and society. This Commanding Heights framing ends up serving the incumbent concentrations of wealth and power that have reasserted control with every past upgrade to the system of the world.

It also assumes a bipolar US–China world and misses the internet nation, the network state and a possibly massively multipolar (read: more decentralized) future. Nation-states will use decentralized protocols and crypto, and some will craft their own permissioned DeFi. But global DeFi will move faster, with deeper liquidity and more powerful innovation.

They cite Coase, and in this context Coase points the other way: the firm gets more granular. Large firms will fragment into spin-outs that serve their old parents or fill new niches. Firms will get smaller on average and far more plentiful. Many more people will become sense-making, prime-mover nodes, conducting their own team of agents, larger machine intelligences and other humans, on a credibly neutral trust layer like Ethereum that fosters real-time discovery, composability and frictionless coordinated collective actions. That's omnidirectional agile fractal expansion, not perpetual command and control with its inherent rigidities.

We're becoming a hybrid human-machine cognitive apparatus for the planet, molting from poking at machine intelligence with our fingers into the hybrid organisms' next quasi-stable form. For a while, human needs/constraints, motivations and judgment will be a key rate limiter so while it will move fast it will remain manageable.

Every human will be empowered to do what they want and build what they want. Every person will have access to world-class expertise in nearly every domain and to a credibly neutral, protocol-based decentralized trust machine: the modular Ethereum ecosystem. No one gets deplatformed or censored, everyone shares one source of economic truth about what happened and in what order, and everyone has unprecedented control over their financial life.

And Web3 is under construction. It is the user-centric web, where properly privileged, often bespoke compute, crafted by machine intelligence, comes to our secure and private data, not the other way around.

今天起正式加入 @MojoAI_HQ 了，和 @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee 等很多小伙伴一起build AI 个人财富助手事业 🫡 . 

半年以前和一个资深做量化的朋友探讨，AI之于交易到底能有什么意义。他的看法是团队至少探索了7～8年了，目前得出的结论是没什么意义。

但在我的视角里，如果一场全面改写交互方式的革命已经席卷一切软件，而唯独金融/交易领域还没开始 / 还没有人做的足够好，那么这就是值得投入的红利期，虽然这种红利可能在大多数whales眼里看不上，也不会太久，且以后窗口期也只会越来越短。

更朴实的，这个世界属于绝大多数人。尽管 AI 在“赚钱”“暴富”上可能还无法成为无所不能的印钞机，但用过 mojo 以后，我发现至少我们“抓机会”的能力已经可以全面平权了。

“AI 交易” 实际上是一种对 AI 金融领域能力的狭隘想象。这个行业真的靠交易暴富的人，我相信也孑孑寥寥。我相信绝大多数能够翻身的人，本质还是靠的毒辣的机会嗅觉、敢于重仓的赌性和超绝执行力。而最后一步，往往是很多人止步于机会大门前的最后一道门槛。链上信号、狙击、快进快出、多号快速分发与收集…… 很多人不是不知道什么机会好，但是工具和执行细节的缺失让他们无法抓住机会。

用过 Mojo 以后，我发现这是我想做的事情。一句话跨链，一句话创建原本大科学家才能创建的监控和脚本，一句话学习&模仿其他作者的agent模板（是的，就像grok bot那样）…… 我不指望 AI 能让我赚多少钱，但我相信钱包 / 交易所 / 跨链 / DEX ……这些2018/2019 以来就没怎么变过的行业基础设施，应该变一变，变得更顺手，好用，理解我，能够救急，能够真的抓住机会。 

综上，很荣幸能和 Mojo 团队一起探索这种未来。🫡 

Glad to announce that I've officially joined @MojoAI_HQ to build an AI personal wealth agent with @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee and a lot of other great people 🫡

About six months ago, I was talking with a friend who's a veteran quant about what AI actually means for trading. His take: his team had been exploring it for at least 7-8 years, and their conclusion so far was that it doesn't mean much.

But the way I see it, if a revolution in how we interact with software is sweeping through everything, and finance/trading is the one place where it hasn't started, or where no one has done it well enough yet, then this is a window worth betting on. Most whales probably won't care about it, it won't last long, and these windows will only keep getting shorter.

Put more simply, this world belongs to the vast majority of people. AI may not be an all-powerful money printer that makes you rich overnight, but after using Mojo, I've realized that at the very least, the ability to catch opportunities can now be truly democratized.

"AI trading" is actually a pretty narrow way to imagine what AI can do in finance. I believe the people who've truly gotten rich from trading alone are few and far between. Most people who turn their lives around do it with a razor-sharp nose for opportunity, the guts to go big, and insane execution. And that last step is often the final barrier that stops people right at the door. On-chain signals, sniping, fast in and out, dealing assets on multiple chains... Plenty of people know a good opportunity when they see one, but they miss it because they don't have the tools or can't handle the execution details.

After using Mojo, I knew this was what I wanted to work on. Bridge across chains in one sentence. In one sentence, create the kind of monitors and scripts that only elite degen could build before. In one sentence, learn from and copy other creators' agent templates (yes, just like grok bot)... I don't expect AI to make me a ton of money, but I do believe that wallets, exchanges, bridges, DEXs ... all this infra that has barely changed since 2018/2019, should change. It should be smoother and easier to use, it should understand me, it should be able to bail me out in a pinch, and it should actually help me catch real alphas.

All of which is to say: I'm honored to explore this future with the Mojo team. 🫡

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

quoted_text:
Just read Commanding Heights.

It sketches a fairly depressing future: AI displaces white-collar workers, while wealth concentrates among those who own scarce physical assets and infrastructure.

There is a more optimistic possibility: AI changes where human ambition goes.

Many talented 20-year-olds chose banking, law, consulting or software engineering partly because those careers offered the highest rewards. They weren’t all passionate about financial models or corporate contracts. They followed the incentives.

If AI makes that work abundant and cheap, while building things in the physical world remains difficult and valuable, those incentives would shift.

More of our brightest people would be incentivised to build careers and companies in areas like medicine, energy, architecture, physical engineering and space exploration - with cheap intelligence helping them tackle problems that were previously too expensive or complex.

The same scarcity that pushes up prices and rewards physical asset owners could also attract the talent and investment needed to expand supply and overcome those bottlenecks.

Losing white-collar jobs would still be painful. But over time, we could see an enormous redirection of human ambition towards improving the physical world.

text:
💰 Anthropic 的 IPO，我最在意的是那 940 人。這是 2024 年底的員工總數。如果 Anthropic 最後以 2 兆美元上市，光是 2024 年加入的那一批，手上股權平均可能值 2 億到 3 億美元。

做出 Claude 的 Anthropic，2021 年 1 月才成立，今年 10 月就公開遞交招股書。SpaceX 花了 24 年，以 1.77 兆美元估值上市。Anthropic 如果能以 2 兆美元掛牌，成立不到六年就會打破這個 IPO 估值紀錄。

🧮 同一家公司，差一年報到，股權差多少？Andrew Benson 用招股書的資料試算，假設上市估值是 2 兆美元，各梯次平均每人的帳面股權大約是：

・截至 2023 年底已加入｜約 300～500 人｜1.1 億～4 億美元
・2024 年加入｜約 440～640 人｜2 億～3 億美元
・2025 年加入｜約 1,360 人｜7,000 萬～9,500 萬美元
・2026 年前三季加入｜約 3,000 人｜1,000 萬～2,000 萬美元

這是把公司每年發的股權和員工人數放在一起估。個人最後能拿到多少，還得看當初拿了多少股、多少已經歸屬，以及解禁後能賣什麼價。

🇹🇼 那台灣有多少人？台灣籍、在台任職，以及整個亞洲的員工總數，目前都查不到官方統計。日本團隊倒是有數字，一年從 3 人增加到超過 50 人。Anthropic 也在招負責台灣半導體和製造業客戶的業務，工作地點在新加坡。

亞洲薪資也有個參考：新加坡一個研究經濟學家職缺，刊登的年薪約 31 萬到 33 萬新幣。至於亞洲員工究竟拿了多少股，公司沒有公開，不能直接套用上面那張表。

👀 所以，如果你有朋友在 Anthropic 工作，下次吃飯可以先問一句：「你是哪一年進去的？」如果他說 2024，坐你對面的搞不好就是一位準億萬富翁，而且是美元計價。這頓先各付各的，等他股票解禁再約。

text:
Legal is a hard place to write a verifier. Two good lawyers can disagree and both be right, so a verifier that accepts only one answer will mark good lawyering as incorrect.

We built the legal tasks for @SemiAnalysis_'s GDPx with practicing lawyers - for questions where they could reasonably disagree, we accept either conclusion as long as it’s properly reasoned. We check the grader against their own grading, and grade every output repeatedly to catch criteria the judge decides inconsistently.

The best models still miss what a good lawyer catches! On our public task, we ask an agent to mark up a Series B charter for the lead investor. In 13 of 20 runs across four models, the agent missed that the cap table gives the other shareholders enough votes to strip away the investor’s protections. In all 20, it missed that the company could route around those protections through a subsidiary.

If you’re building verifiers for work where experts disagree, I'd love to hear your thoughts.

https://t.co/q8Xs4hcGNr

text:
I don't think people realize how bad the situation at Binance is getting

Less than 24 hours ago Binance began enabling withdrawals for 21 coins

But there are still 531 coins that you can't withdraw

And of the 21 that you can withdraw they have a "Partial Withdrawal Suspended" status which means that you have a limit on how much you can withdraw

But even with all of these precautions and limitations Binance still experienced an all time record net outflow of $6.1 billion today

That is more than the total net outflows during the 72 hours before FTX collapsed

$6.1 billion is the largest daily net outflow ever recorded for a crypto exchange

So over the coming days as Binance continues to enable withdrawals for more coins and then eventually removes the partial withdrawal limitations the weekly and monthly net outflows will balloon

What makes this even more concerning is that this is in addition to the $6.3 billion hack that occurred several days ago

Remember that Binance is an unregulated black box that keeps their balance sheet and liabilities top secret

We have no way of knowing if they used customer deposits as collateral in an off-chain deal to replenish their reserves

It has been long suspected that Binance operates on fractional reserves and given they don't publish their financials publicly nobody can prove to you that they don't

By every metric Binance is experiencing the start of a bank run

When the cracks will begin to appear is unknown

But it is very clear that trust in CZ and Binance is deteriorating rapidly

All it would take is a single FUD post from Elon to trigger a death spiral that could end in Binance's collapse the same way that CZ's post triggered a bank run on FTX  four years ago

Right now the only responsible thing to do is to withdraw all of your funds from Binance immediately

There is zero upside to waiting around to find out what happens next

Remember that in bankruptcy the secured creditors will get priority over normal customers

If your funds are on Binance they are not safe and anybody telling you differently is lying

text:
Thanks to @koolkrypto223 for his comments, I do not see his post as FUD at all but rather constructive discourse. 

On single dealer
I think we've been quite transparent about being a broker-like model rather than an exchange. This actually necessitates the use of a single dealer: unlike spot assets, derivatives in crypto cannot be transferred between different exchanges. If we were to route your order split across 5 exchanges, you would not want to see 5 different positions displayed in your account. You want a sophisticated counterparty to do the liquidity aggregation. We've achieved the benefits you describe: 

✅ more listings than any other DEX
✅ best in class liquidity on any asset class even as a new entrant
✅ liquidity aggregation of the best primary venues; no need to open 20 different exchange accounts and keep switching between them

On the moat
Bringing all of TradFi onchain will take years, if not decades. Swaps, for example, are a fundamentally bilateral contract that cannot be replicated by DEXes, and I don't even think any are trying. This is the first time we've seen direct TradFi liquidity ported onchain with stable funding rates (the routing actually doesn't touch a single crypto venue). Getting the partnerships in place for this was not easy; I think we'll see the same type of consolidation into a few winners as we see with CEXes, DEXes, and TradFi brokerages. 

On price discovery
Our opinionated take: 
a) You do not give a flying fuck as a user where price discovery is happening 
b) In fact most users should not touch exchanges directly at all 

Currently, no price discovery happens on any DEX, except in very niche scenarios. To say otherwise is massive cope. To build a venue for price discovery means catering to the very fastest HFTs: wake me up when DEXes have matching engine latency on the order of nanoseconds. Do a lead-lag analysis on prices between DEXes and CEXes, or DEXes vs CME, and it's obvious where price discovery originates. The only question is do you want a shallow clone of TradFi liquidity or direct access?

As a user, you primarily care about best execution, and that's what we optimize for. Additionally, the reason why brokerages exist in TradFi is to add another layer of protection between the user and the exchange. 

▶️ When 10/10 occurred and billions of dollars of ADL were forced upon users at other venues, Variational came out squeaky clean. 
▶️ When Binance was hacked for billions, we immediately put out a statement that said that user funds are safe in self-custodied smart contracts and not moved to offchain hedging venues. OLP puts up its own capital for that. 

Variational Pro 
Variational Pro will be multi-dealer: you will be able to request a quote and dealers will bid for your flow. This increases the complexity of the product but will have massive unlocks for institutions, including allowing for subnetworks of markets where OLP is not involved. 

If two parties want to trade swaps or other derivatives peer-to-peer at infinite size we will facilitate the infrastructure for order matching, clearing, and margining for that.

Reminder that the tech for this has already been built; it's the same underlying protocol that clears billions every day for Omni! I hope you will see our vision to bring TradFi onchain is a multi-year one and cannot be cleanly segmented into "oh it's just a DEX" or "oh it's just a CFD broker".  It's so much more than that and we encourage everyone to follow our roadmap which we publicize on our docs page.
author: yh_0x
quoted_text:
The discourse over @variational_io is...bizzare.

Everyone knows it's a single dealer RFQ platform (or at least I'd hope by now). 

This is neither inherently good nor bad, but it should shape your expectations.

Similar to a CFD broker, I'd expect Variational to trade at lower multiples than actual exchanges. IG Group trades at ~half the multiple of CME for example.

There's nothing terribly new or interesting about "RFQ", I'm not sure why people think it's a big value proposition or moat.

The real value prop of Variational is that in crypto, UI for DEXs is largely solved, and UX all comes down to liquidity. Variational can potentially list assets faster, get better liquidity on long tails, and generally abstract away a lot of the awkwardness of bootstrapping a brand new marker that a CLOB has. This has been and will likely continue to be enormously successful with their RWA swaps.

That's a very real value prop, for now. The problem is that they have much less moat than actual exchanges; they are not the venue where actual price discovery is happening. It's significantly harder for TradFi entrants to replicate what @HyperliquidX has built than it'll be for them to do what Variational does, but better. B-booking retail crypto traders and points farmers in OLP is enormously lucrative now, but how durable will those margins be over time?

Depending on the exact flavour of regulatory clarity we get, the value prop they offer for TradFi liquidity can pretty easily shrink as more TradFi market makers are willing/able to quote directly on permissionless CLOBs. I don't know where regulators will land here though; there's worlds that it's very good for Variational and very bad.

I see Variational as more of a bandaid fix/reg arb, but a lot of crypto falls into that category. It's attempting to solve a very real issue, but will that issue be as prevalent in 6 months? 1 year? 2 years? Hard to say.

Personally, I see $LIT and hyperliquid:native as more pure expressions of longing the proliferation of perps as an instrument and DeFi as a sector, where as I see $VAR as more of a business with more operator risk, but it could easily print money for months-years. $GMX might be a good example in that it printed fees for a long time and then eventually became more obsolete.

I actually don't think any of this impacts point price much at TGE, and that's what everyone seems to care about. Market conditions at the time of TGE probably dictate $VAR performance way more than any of this.

3. 拓扑协同（Graphs）：抛弃单线流水线，把多 Agent 连成拓扑图，并行执行、交叉审查、对抗验证。

4. 自进化系统：系统开始自己调用自己。人类退回指挥席，只负责设定验收目标和看最终结果。

以前是你一句一句求着模型给答案；

Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

现在的 AI 产品太擅长让人惊艳十分钟了，难的是让人放心用上十个月。

尤其是交易类 Agent。让 AI 分析一次行情没什么门槛，但一旦涉及个人资产数据、研究文件，以及需要连续执行的监控任务，用户对产品的要求就完全不一样了。

刚发现 Minara 最近发布了 Web V2，开放了 Early Access，他们给每个用户都配置了独立隔离的云端沙箱，让数据和任务运行在各自的环境里。

我一直觉得金融可能是最需要这种架构的 Agent 场景之一。

毕竟交易涉及的是真金白银，用户需要知道自己的数据放在哪里、任务在哪里运行，以及自己究竟能控制多少东西。模型的分析能力决定了你会不会尝试，安全和信任才决定了你敢不敢长期使用。

另外，这次 Minara 还把桌面端同一套 UI 和代码搬到了 Web，原来的 Chat 升级成 Agent，文件预览、功能推荐等体验也补齐了。Workflow 也在向 Automation 升级，希望让 Agent 能在后台持续执行任务，目前部分监控功能仍以桌面端为主。

我觉得这里有个挺值得关注的产品趋势。

过去大家做 AI 交易工具，都喜欢比谁能分析更多资产、生成更复杂的策略。但这些能力随着模型进步，差距可能会越来越小。

接下来的竞争，很可能会转向谁能让 Agent 真正进入用户的日常工作流，既能保护数据，又能持续做事，还能在不同设备上无缝接续。

text:
I just sat down with @Tiny_Fish's founder to talk about the future of web agents. 

5 things from that conversation that stuck with me:

1. Agents are becoming the primary users of the web. Sites that block them today will be making themselves agent-friendly, even agent-certified, to get that traffic.

2. Human-in-the-loop is a transition phase. Next come headless agents that handle login, pricing, and multi-step execution across services on their own, with a person stepping in only for something new or risky.

3. Subscriptions don't fit agents. Tinyfish replaced them with a prepaid wallet so each agent task can be a micro-transaction.

4. Trust is the biggest competition in this space. Tinyfish keeps credentials in a vault the model never sees, and a separate safeguard model checks every action for risk before it executes.

5. Shuhao runs 12 parallel Claude Code sessions as a founder and Chief Product Officer to quickly build and iterate on new features.

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

EveryFrame (#SN117) is quietly assembling the full AI film stack and $TAO is the engine underneath it. 

AI filmmaking today is fragmented: video here, images there, voice somewhere else, editing in another tab. EveryFrame is collapsing that mess into one script to screen studio: generation, direction, editing, sound and export under a single workspace and credit balance.

One studio, every format

@xeveryframe brings leading models:  MiniMax, Seedance, Google Veo, Kling, image tools and ElevenLabs audio into one place, with visible generation costs and no need for separate provider accounts.

It goes beyond clips: Director tools handle background swaps, people replacement, lighting, lip sync, sound, and upscaling, while Cinema Studio supports screenplays, consistent characters and locations, storyboards, shot planning, timelines and final export.

That is the difference between an AI toy and an AI production suite.

SN117: the competitive serving layer

The real asymmetric bet is Subnet 117. Independent miners compete to serve eligible AI generation jobs, using existing provider accounts and lightweight TEE secured workers with no GPU fleets required.

Every job produces a signed receipt linking the request, model, and output, giving EveryFrame verifiable execution and validators a basis for rewarding reliable miners.

If more Studio workloads route through SN117, miner competition could compress serving costs and eventually make frontier AI creation cheaper for creators and developers.

Why the bull case works

Real product, real demand: EveryFrame is not a mining only subnet; it has a creator facing studio, subscriptions, credits and a developer API.

Capital light network: Miners contribute access and reliability, not expensive hardware, broadening participation.

Verifiable by design: Signed receipts and trusted execution make the marketplace accountable rather than opaque.

Multiple revenue paths: Creator plans, credit top ups, $TAO/crypto payments and pay per render API usage create several ways to monetize demand.

Early but live: #SN117 began serving verified mainnet jobs on September 28, 2026, with public miner onboarding already open.

The thesis

EveryFrame’s opportunity is to own the creative front end while #SN117 becomes the open, competitive infrastructure layer beneath it. If miner discounts increasingly reach Studio credits, EveryFrame could offer a rare combination: premium AI models, complete production tooling, transparent pricing and verifiable execution.

The execution risks are real: model coverage, reliability and passing savings to customers still need to be proven.

But the setup is clean: one studio for creators, one market for miners, one receipt for proof. EveryFrame is not just another AI video platform; it is building the OS for AI native filmmaking on Bittensor.

text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

我觉得很多人还没有意识到，币安现在的情况有多严重。

不到24小时前，币安才开始恢复21种币的提币功能。

但目前仍有531种币无法提币。

而且就连已经开放提币的这21种币，状态也仍然显示为“部分提币暂停”，也就是说，用户能提取的金额依然受到限制。

可即便采取了这么多限制措施，币安今天的资金净流出仍然创下了67亿美元的历史纪录。

这个数字甚至超过了FTX崩盘前72小时的资金净流出总额。

67亿美元，也是加密货币交易所历史上最高的单日资金净流出纪录。

这意味着，接下来几天，随着币安逐步恢复更多币种的提币功能，并最终取消现有的提币额度限制，其单周和单月的资金净流出规模很可能会进一步暴涨。

更令人担忧的是，几天前币安才刚刚发生了一起涉及63亿美元的黑客攻击事件。

别忘了，币安本质上就是一个不受监管的黑箱。它的资产负债表和实际负债情况从来不对外公开。

我们根本无从得知，币安是否曾经在链下交易中拿客户存款作为抵押，来补充自己的储备金。

外界长期以来一直怀疑币安采用的是部分准备金模式。由于币安从不公开财务报表，也没有人能够向你证明它没有这么做。

从各项指标来看，币安正在经历一场挤兑的初期阶段。

至于问题什么时候会真正爆发，目前还没人知道。

但有一点已经非常明显，市场对赵长鹏和币安的信任正在迅速瓦解。

现在可能只需要马斯克发一条制造恐慌的推文，就足以引发一场死亡螺旋，最终导致币安像FTX一样倒闭。

就像四年前，赵长鹏的一条推文引发了FTX的挤兑潮一样。

在目前这种情况下，唯一负责任的做法，就是立刻把你在币安的所有资金全部提出来。

继续观望，等着看接下来会发生什么，对你没有任何好处。

别忘了，一旦进入破产程序，有担保债权人的受偿顺序会排在普通客户前面。

如果你的资金还放在币安，那就谈不上安全。任何告诉你资金绝对安全的人，都是在撒谎。

Anh Lợi Lưu chia sẻ một góc nhìn khá đáng chú ý sau vụ hack Binance: Có lẽ bài học lớn nhất không nằm ở Binance hay cách họ quản lý private key, mà nằm ở tốc độ chuyển tiền quá nhanh của blockchain.

Một giao dịch 6 tỷ USD có thể rời khỏi ví nóng chỉ trong khoảng 20 phút. Blockchain xử lý giao dịch 100 triệu USD gần như nhanh ngang 10 USD, và đó cũng chính là một lỗ hổng về mặt thời gian phản ứng.

Anh Lợi đề xuất một cơ chế mới: Amount-Weighted Delayed Settlement – giao dịch càng lớn, thời gian chờ xác nhận càng dài. Trong thời gian chờ, người gửi vẫn có quyền hủy giao dịch và lấy lại tiền.

Một số nguyên tắc được đề xuất:

Giao dịch nhỏ vẫn được xử lý tức thì.
Giao dịch lớn phải chờ lâu hơn trước khi hoàn tất.
Muốn tắt cơ chế bảo vệ phải chờ 24 giờ.
Tính tổng lượng tiền rút trong 24 giờ để tránh hacker chia nhỏ giao dịch né giới hạn.

Cơ chế này có thể giúp ví cá nhân có thêm thời gian phản ứng khi seed phrase bị lộ hoặc người dùng vô tình ký giao dịch độc hại.

Tất nhiên, giải pháp cũng có những đánh đổi về tính tương thích, quyền riêng tư và tốc độ thanh toán.

Một góc nhìn đáng suy ngẫm: Blockchain không nhất thiết phải hy sinh tốc độ, nhưng có lẽ cần thêm một lớp bảo vệ để tốc độ không trở thành lợi thế của hacker.

text:
🚨 Security advisory for all IoTeX delegates and node operators.

CVE-2026-98432 is a critical Linux kernel bug (CVSS 9.8) that can let an attacker get remote root over TCP. If you are running an IoTeX delegate on an affected Linux kernel, please patch today. 🧵

Why nodes are affected: 
Go 1.24+ turns on Multipath TCP (MPTCP) for listeners by default, so iotex-core's P2P port 4689 listens over MPTCP. That is exactly the path the demonstrated remote-root exploit uses. You don't need to have enabled anything yourself.

Fix: upgrade the kernel, then reboot
• Debian 12/13: apt update && apt install linux-image-amd64 → 6.1.190+ / 6.12.113+
• Ubuntu (all releases): no fixed kernel yet. Apply the mitigation below 👇

Mitigation (no reboot):
Drop IPv4 packets that carry IP options, which the exploit needs:
     nft add table ip ipopt_guard
     nft add chain ip ipopt_guard pre '{ type filter hook prerouting priority -300; }'
     nft add rule ip ipopt_guard pre ip hdrlength gt 5 drop

We've been working with delegates directly and many have already patched. If you run a node, please don't wait. 👀
author: iotex_io
quoted_text:
🚨 Critical Linux kernel TCP flaw enables remote root code execution; CVE-2026-98432

A race condition in the Linux kernel’s IPv4 TCP implementation can trigger a use-after-free before application authentication, potentially allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to leak kernel memory, corrupt memory or crash the system.

Anthropic says Claude developed a working exploit that executed attacker-chosen commands as root against Linux servers with a Multipath TCP listener. The exploit took approximately 53 minutes to complete during testing and has not been publicly released.
⠀
• CVSS: 9.8 Critical, according to the Linux kernel CVE team
• Affected: Linux kernels beginning with version 4.4
• Fixed: 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and 7.3
• Attack requirements: Network access, no credentials and no user interaction
• Exploitation status: No known attacks in the wild
⠀
Ubuntu and Red Hat Enterprise Linux had not released corrected kernel packages as of October 29. Debian, Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux and SUSE have released fixes for at least some affected branches.

Distribution severity ratings differ substantially. Red Hat rates the flaw 5.9 because it considers the race difficult to win and describes denial of service as the most likely practical impact.

text:
Variational won't delay its TGE

If they do, I'd see it as a bearish signal rather than a bullish one

Lucas and the team were consistently saying on podcasts and in Discord throughout the year up until September that they had no plans to extend the points program. So when they announced on September 24 that they were extending it due to upcoming major partnership announcements, the trading API launch, and other developments, CT took it pretty well

Any further extension would only fuel more FUD around Variational and invite comparisons with other perp DEXs like GRVT, Paradex, and others that kept extending their points programs multiple times to squeeze more money out of users while they still had people trading on their platforms

The broader crypto market doesn't have that much of an impact on Variational. Back in September, when BTC was at $87k, the odds of a $1B FDV were around 70%. Now, after the Binance hack and BTC dropping from $87k to $77k, those odds are still at around 56%. That's because Variational is expanding beyond crypto and moving into RWAs. So I don't think there's much point in looking at current market conditions or where BTC is trading. Lighter launched its TGE with BTC at $87k, while Backpack did it with BTC at $69k. If a project starts using market conditions as an excuse to push back its TGE, then it's just OpenSea all over again, repackaged. Another project hiding its greed behind the excuse of "market conditions."

However, now that we're already in November, if we still don't see any major partnership announcements or the trading API launch this month, and their X account continues to be filled with nothing but podcast snippets and posts about how cheap their spreads are on RWA assets, then it would genuinely be a reason for concern

But I don't see any reason to spread FUD prematurely. Let's just wait for Variational to deliver something big in November. I'm confident the team is preparing something interesting for us
author: muarmemuar
quoted_text:
VARIATIONAL MIGHT DELAY TGE. AND THAT COULD BE BULLISH

Polymarket gives Variational a 77% chance to launch a token by December 31.

By November 30? Only 18%, and dropping.

I think the market is too confident.

Launching a token into current sentiment is a risk. Weak demand, thin liquidity, farmers ready to dump on day one. Nobody wants their TGE to become a chart that only goes down.

There's a real chance Variational pushes TGE back another 1-2 quarters. And that might be the best outcome for farmers:

> more time to farm = more points
> room to give a bigger % of supply to the airdrop
> time to raise more capital at a better valuation
> more bullish catalysts before launch: new markets, partnerships, product updates
> launching into a strong market, not a weak one

A rushed TGE in a bad market helps nobody. A delayed TGE with a bigger drop, more funding and better timing helps everyone holding points.

Pure speculation, nothing confirmed. If it happens, don't panic. Keep farming.

Karpathy just fixed YouTube in 2 hours. On a weekend.

> He got tired of YouTube's recommendations
> So he had Claude go through 43 million Hacker News comments from the last 20 years
> It found the YouTube videos smart people kept recommending again and again
> That boiled down to 6,454 videos actually worth watching
> He turned them into a site called HackerTube
> Total build time was about 2 hours with Claude Opus 5.5
> No algorithm chasing your clicks, just 20 years of real recommendations

Cool stuff I would say 🫡
author: enisco
quoted_text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

Say what you will about Tucker, but he is well sourced, Netanyahu is backed into a corner and President Trump is impulsive and does what he wants. 

If this 90% exaggerated we should be concerned. 

Stopping unnecessary wars in the Middle East is the one thing DJT was elected to do.
author: Palgrani2
quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

Withdrawals pass through a 24-hour holding period, while an external watcher monitors transactions and sends email alerts. Users can trigger an emergency transfer of funds to a backup wallet if unauthorized activity is detected.

The system is designed to operate without custodians, with an open-source implementation available for independent use.

text:
阶段性复盘 polymarket ！

原 @Polymarket  的CMO @MatthewModabber 的官方徽章已经被摘了。

似乎 PM 内部的发币派已经被清理。

这或许也解释了为什么 PM 不能执行自己的线路图的原因，老的直接管理层已经被整体清算，自下而上，CEO或许是下一个目标。

没有人会说具体的原因。当然，也对于我们也不重要。我们不考虑空投，不考虑团队的个人行为和决策，我们把PM当成一个整体，现在站在事后来复盘这个项目。

我看到的是，一个站在web2和web3十字路口被反复拉扯的项目。

诚然，PM在 web3 获得了成功，他有更大的野心，把版图拓展到 web2，似乎是想做一个横跨web3-web2之间的杀手级应用。

在 web3 并没有 HL 那样的深厚根基的情况下，贸然把web3当成垫脚石，全面投诚web2。

这笔帐算的太精明了，可以说是既要又要。既要给web3灌输梦想以收获利益，又要全面拥抱美国合规的web2市场以继续扩大收益。说白点，就是既不想承担web3的义务，又要享受合规化的权利。

选择最大化收获利益，付出的代价是失去了项目原本的根基。

多年的web3基石被项目方不断透支，直到信用的完全崩塌。

在这些年出现过很多独角兽项目（web3），而我第一次看到这么多社区的核心用户在不断公开质疑或谩骂项目方，而项目方大部分时候选择无视。

如果连早期的核心用户圈都是一直FUD，这样的加密项目怎么可能越做越好呢？

这些种种现象在说明，项目方已经放弃了这些早期的加密用户，他们的贡献价值周期已经结束。包括清算团队内部的发币派，或许都是投诚美国市场的必然。

还是站在利益最大化上来考量，现在没有加密方向的回头路了，拥抱美国市场拉高估值是利益最大化的选择。

TGE? 空投？

醒一醒，一方面，发币派已经基本肃清。另一方面，加密用户已经“贡献”完了，为什么要回过头来给他们钱呢？

回过来头，我们反思这个事情。也许，之前 PM 想要发行代币，打入美国市场，股币双发，但是事实是不会发币了。

问题在哪里？

在web3作为独角兽他做到了，布局美国增量市场也没有错，甚至在美国市场业务还在稳定增长。

按照成绩上来说，不算失败。问题出在作为一个加密项目的信用已经破产。 为了达到目的，可以不择手段。

这对于以共识作为基础的加密行业来说，是礼崩乐坏。大项目可以死，但是不能欺骗社区。

今天 PM 可以这样，明天大项目 B 也可以如法炮制。在web3不折手段吃干抹净后，转身拥抱合规。站在行业上来看，PM的做法无异于杀鸡取卵，产生的影响其实更加恶劣。

区块链保证代码不会骗人，却无法保证项目方不会骗人。

PM 是站在web3-web2 十字路口的项目，他的选择也更多折射的是当下时代的选择。

也就是，PM 不会是最后一个。

另外，那也给我们一个重要的启示：项目方无法实现web3-web2的统一。一旦选择二者兼得，就是选择了后者，等于抛弃了前者。

或许可以像 @HyperliquidX 一样，只做基层设施，应用让社区去做。

如果 PM 真的想走 HL 的路线，我认为应该很早就搬出纽约，专注于全球站，从polygon迁移出来，主要做预测市场的基础设施。不要直接拿纽交所的投资，让社区去做美国站。有高度自由的权限，可以掌握自己的节奏。

如今，我们看到的是可能身不由己的PM 。

选择了保险箱，就是选择了死胡同。

预测市场还会继续向前，直到真的集大成者开发出更酷的场景！

text:
Ice accumulates preferentially on the horizontal stabilizer's thin leading edge, disrupting its downward force. Nose drops, plane enters steep dive and overspeeds beyond structural limits. Loads can detach the stabilizer, removing all pitch control. Unrecoverable.

Avoid by turning on anti-ice systems at first sign of icing, immediately climbing or descending out of the layer, and steering clear of thunderstorms or convective cells that produce severe or SLD icing.

text:
Increasingly this will be the new job description for a lot of roles, not just coding. We’re clearly moving from a world where agents help us do our work incrementally better or faster, to us helping agents do their work.

This turns everyone in one of these positions to that of a manager of a team of agents, instead of an individual contributor with just some added leverage from AI. The biggest areas of impact will be information-heavy jobs, like coding, cybersecurity, legal work, biotech, engineering, and many other fields. 

And as a result, in these jobs your leverage will begin to be decoupled from the normal ratio of hours spent working to output generated. For essentially the history of knowledge work the main variable you had to play with was hours of work done (assuming fixed level talent/coordination/strategy). 

Now we’ve separated these variables because agents can parallelize work for us, to in theory execute as much as we need to pull off whatever goal we’re trying to accomplish. The people and organizations that discover this sooner, and orient their operations around it, will see compounding gains in their workflows.

BREAKING: Inside Starcloud, the $2.3B Startup Putting Data Centers in Space

FACTORY TOUR - Redmond, WA

Primes quoted them $75M-$100M to build their first data center in space. They did it for $2.5M.

In just 21 months, Starcloud is one of the fastest companies to go from founding to orbit.

With $450M in total funding from Manhattan West, Nvidia, Cisco, Benchmark & EQT, the team walks me through their mission for AI in space.

I toured the new HQ w/ CEO @PhilipJohnston + co-founders @EzraFeilden & @AdiOltean

AI compute on Earth is limited by power & permitting. @Starcloud_ is moving it to orbit, where solar power is nearly constant. Philip says the dawn-dusk orbit alone could fit about 10 TW of compute, roughly 20x the entire US power grid. Once launch costs fall below $500/kg, he says compute in space will be cheaper than on the ground.

From Starcloud 1, Starcloud 2, to Starcloud 3, we saw: 

Tracking Starcloud 1 live in orbit, circling Earth every 90 minutes at 17,000 mph with the first Nvidia H100 in space.

Co-Founder & Chief Engineer Adi Oltean walks through Starcloud 2 as the team fires the latches that deploy its 120 ft solar wingspan. It launches in January with 100x the power of Starcloud 1. 

Co-Founder & CTO Ezra Feilden shows the 16-ton secondhand vibe table. The team bought it for $200K, instead of paying $1.5M & waiting 2 years for a new one, they rebuilt it over a weekend.

Engineering Manager Bailey Montaño leak checks the ion thruster after vibe. Bailey designed the radiators, which have 10x less mass & cost 500x less per watt than the ISS’s. 

In the fab shop, Ezra shows the Starcloud 3 demonstrator, a 2-ton, 235 kW vehicle that fits 50 to a Starship. 

Camilo Lopez cuts stainless on the laser cutter. 

Engineering Operations Lead Miguel Rivera, formerly of Helion Energy, teaches me to MIG weld.

The tour ends in the new campus, about 100,000 sqft built to produce 100 satellites a week toward an 88,000-satellite constellation.

15. @temple_ny settled $764.5 million in spot trades on Canton in October, up 91% from about $400.7 million in September.

16. On @Visa’s October 27 earnings call, CEO Ryan McInerney highlighted the company’s existing role as a Canton Super Validator. He put that work in the context of Visa’s plan to connect traditional payments, stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

quoted_text:
There is an absolute barrage of inference providers popping up that get to $1M/mo extremely quickly.

This is the rough economics of inference providers:

Even if you rent on-demand B300s at $8/GPU-hr, many open source models (GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, DeepSeek 4.1 Flash / Pro) can get you >$10-20/GPU-hr at reasonable throughputs (100tok/s). DeepInfer from DeepSeek directly shows they can get $38/GPU-hr on off-peak hours. Every chip / model has a different throughput / interactivity curve, but there is a lot of arbitrage between even high rental spot prices and token prices. New chips (Vera Rubins) also change this meaningfully. Your ability to be making gross margin relies on your utilization and how good your stack is.

Gateways like OpenRouter, Vercel and more help solve that problem by aggregating demand to you. May inference providers discount their tokens to get longer term commits too. I've even heard stories of selling back Chinese model tokens to Chinese labs!

One thorn in the economics of these players is that many Chinese open source model labs are now asking for rev share if you're at a certain scale, espp for pre-release access to their models for day 1 support. That further pushes the threshold to be in the money.

The barrier to entry seems low and falling. There are even stories of smaller ones who can "vibe code" a way to stand up OSS models on a cluster they rent. And as a result, we're seeing 10s of such companies pop up almost every week and immediately skyrocketing revenue at low-ish gross margin and raising rounds on the back of that.

Unsurprisingly, because the actual service provided seems commodity, this eventually drives up compute prices and drives down token prices. In theory, it would seem like neoclouds who have the lowest cost of compute and themselves have started inference businesses would win the race to the bottom (Crusoe Coreweave Nebius and GMI all have inference businesses), with larger players (Modal Fireworks Baseten) being second because they are well capitalized to make bigger compute commits cheaply and have demand (high utilization), but the reality is the pie is growing so quickly that even upstarts are absolutely crushing it and growing aggressively (inference dot net, DeepInfra, Wafer, Relace, Morph).

Strategies vary across the board: neoclouds want to serve inference, inference players want to be neoclouds and do higher margin reserved instances / post training, and some want to go heterogeneous hardware or creatively flexible compute constructs.

The risks are: do open source models continue to be competitive? Will their creators rent seek more? Will their shape change compute needs? How do different chips change economics? Who gets compute in a supply crunch?

Below is a aggressive sketch of how gross margin scales with utilization for various models / chip sets.

For now, there are many inference providers and they’re all ripping!

text:
I respected the thesis in the long run but pretty skeptical in the short run. 
Cybersecurity market is a slow market growing at roughly 5% CAGR, and it takes roughly 5-8% of enterprise's IT spend. 
Yes, with the rise of the AI threat, cybersecurity is getting more and more critical. It's a big threat to open source repos and any public APIs.  If you work in tech, you know what I'm saying. The efforts spent in this area is increasing enormously recently. 
So in a few years, would CTO double the budget? Very likely. But probably they would need to taste the consequences of being hacked with big loss first to walk out of the complacency. 
However, in the short term, my argument is currently the market overly priced the bright future and probably will be disappointed at the next few ERs.
Another potential threat in the long run is the AI labs can easily cut through this domain by selling add-on security features on top of the AI coding business. Seems like no-brainer to me.

text:
Pivot to Elysium

@Enter_Elysium is the L2 @Kinetiq_xyz is shipping for Hyperliquid. Mainnet is set for Nov 9.

The design intent is more blockspace for quoting, prop AMMs, launchpads, and active spot markets without touching HL core execution. Looks like everyone is ready:

- Distribution includes @fomo, @Pumpfun, and @HyperFlow_fun

- Liquidity routing covers @Uniswap, @KyberNetwork, @matchaxyz, and @NestExchange

- Launch and discovery tools include @AscendLaunch, @MontraXYZ , @oxleydotfun auctions, and @kalosfun

- Derivatives and tokenized assets are represented by @DeriveXYZ V3 options and @xStocksFi (non-US).

- Sequencing is handled by @conduitxyz and indexing by @goldskyio .

The path they want is Elysium AMMs → prop AMMs → HyperCore spot → HIP-3 perps. Native HyperCore reads and trading come about 4 weeks after launch.

Fees: 50% to $KNTQ buybacks (aimed at the Assistance Fund), 25% builders, 25% ops. That ties it to $HYPE more than a normal L2, but only if people pay fees.

Versus Robinhood/Base/Solana:

- Those have distribution: over a billion in DeFi TVL and multi-billion weekly DEX volume.

- Elysium doesn't start with that. Its edge is sitting next to HL trading flow, HYPE gas, and a clear graduation path into HyperCore.

- Kinetiq $kHYPE business helps with relationships, but deposits don't automatically become volume.

The test is whether fee-paying flow sticks after the launch noise, whether projects graduate to HyperCore markets, and whether the buybacks are real money.

A useful chain that makes Hyperliquid spot and launches better is realistic. Matching Robinhood or Base scale is possible but not the base case.

text:
🚨 本週資安重點一次看（2026/11/02）

🏦【幣安 63 億美元被駭：怎麼被打進去的？】

這次被稱為史上最大的加密貨幣竊案。根據幣安的初步調查，起點是一名 DevOps 工程師的筆電被入侵，攻擊者藉此進入內部的服務容器，送出未經授權的提幣交易。

後來執行長 Richard Teng 補充，被入侵的不只那台筆電，還有其他入侵點。攻擊者利用以太坊 EIP-7702 的帳戶委託功能，繞過審批流程，直接控制熱錢包，還用自毀機制清掉痕跡。官方說目前沒有私鑰外洩的證據。

🔍 鏈上偵探 ZachXBT 發現，贓款和 Bitget 被駭的資金匯進同一個地址。TRM Labs、Chainalysis 也高度懷疑是北韓的 TraderTraitor（Lazarus 相關組織）。

💸 駭客把 UNI、ENA、PEPE、LINK、AAVE、ONDO、WLD，還有約 810 萬顆 CRV 等山寨幣，在 Uniswap 一池一池地砸，換成 ETH。這也是當天 CRV 重挫的原因之一。

🧊 Tether、Circle、Ripple、Arbitrum 合計凍結了約 30 億美元。

✅ 11/1 起分批恢復提幣，首批 15 條鏈已經恢復，官方說已經補足約 95% 的損失。

💥【DeFi 接連出事】
⚡ Premia（Arbitrum）：駭客用閃電貸搭配空的流動池，把金庫裡的抵押品抽走，損失約 43.7 萬美元。

🔑 Troves（Starknet）：一份已經淘汰的舊合約還留著權限，被拿來盜走約 8.6 顆 BTC。舊合約的權限沒撤乾淨，就是一顆定時炸彈。

🌐 約 12 個 DeFi 網站（Pickle、Origami、FluxBeam、Echelon 等）的網域被劫持，網頁被植入盜錢腳本。合約本身沒問題，是你打開的網站被換掉了。

👉 簽名前看清楚授權內容，大額操作用硬體錢包。

🛠️【必修漏洞】
🐧 Linux 核心 CVE-2026-98432（嚴重度 9.8）：TCP 建立連線時的記憶體漏洞，4.4 版以後的核心都受影響。開著 MPTCP 的伺服器，攻擊者不用帳密就能遠端拿到 root。Ubuntu 的修補還沒全部出來。

👉 用不到 MPTCP 就先關掉，修補一出就更新核心並重開機。

🧩 Cursor 擴充市集出現假的「Claude Code」擴充（2.1.312 / 2.1.313），會在你的電腦植入 SSH 後門。有裝過的趕快檢查。

🐛 npm 套件 tensorlake@0.5.144 是一種會自我擴散的蠕蟲，會偷 GitHub、npm、雲端的憑證和加密錢包。還藏了一個陷阱：你一撤銷 token，它就刪掉你的家目錄。

👉 中招的話，要先移除它裝的服務，再去換憑證。

💸【底層開源，誰來養？】
很多人以為 PHP 這類底層語言沒人維護，其實不是。PHP Foundation 有 11 位領薪水的開發者，PHP 大約四成的程式碼是他們寫的。

但問題是錢越來越少：2025 年收入 73 萬美元、支出 78.4 萬美元，虧了約 13.9 萬，贊助者也在減少。有些關鍵工作甚至只靠一個人撐。

🇩🇪 德國政府的 Sovereign Tech Agency 已經出錢資助 PHP 和其他關鍵開源專案。

🇪🇺 歐盟提案設立「開源維護基金」，7 年投入 20 億歐元，還會列一份關鍵開源清單來決定錢給誰，不過還沒通過。

⚠️ 真正危險的其實是成千上萬個只有一兩個人在維護的小套件。2024 年的 xz 後門、這次的 npm 蠕蟲，都是從這裡被打進來的。

text:
The reason most fail in crypto

I warned that this would happen, but most didn't listen

Back then, everyone on CT was calling for $90K $BTC and another 2x–5x on alts

Leverage and hype were everywhere, but people kept chasing the next pump

Now look how quickly things flipped

- A few weeks ago → scared of missing the pump
- Now → scared of losing everything

Then came the Binance hack, with around $6.3B stolen and billions more withdrawn as panic spread

First @binance → people worry about CEX solvency

Then @Trezor warns about suspected hardware tampering involving a specific reseller

Imagine pulling your funds off CEXs, only to start worrying about your cold wallet too lol

I wasn't predicting a Binance hack

But from my POV, I think the market was already due for a correction. The Binance hack just gave people a reason to dump

I've seen this play out across enough cycles

Price dumps hard → leveraged traders get liquidated, others panic sell whatever they have left

The same people begging for lower entries suddenly don't want to buy anymore

Some have already lost most of their capital. Others are too scared to put their money back in

And when the market eventually recovers?

CT turns bullish again → FOMO kicks in → they come back buying at higher prices

Next correction comes and they're holding another bag

Cycle repeats

That's why I think so many people spend years in crypto and still make the same mistakes

They watch CT more than they "feel" the market, chase 5x–10x without an exit plan, then let fear decide when to sell

The worst part?

Markets often find bottoms after brutal selloffs, when panic reaches its peak

But how are you supposed to take advantage of those opportunities if you've already been liquidated or panic sold everything?

With the US midterms tomorrow, I still wouldn't rule out another ugly selloff

For me, capital preservation comes first

Learning to feel when the market is getting overheated, taking profits and knowing when to step aside are just as important as finding a good entry

The mindset should be simple:

Invest for low risk, not high returns

Especially when you're sitting on a big bag, hoping for another 2x while the risk keeps rising

For now, I'd rather reduce leverage, protect my capital and watch from the sidelines

Missing a bounce? Fine

There will always be another opportunity

But what good is catching the next bottom if you've already lost the money to buy it?

Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

第一时间没买进去，昨天睡醒看到市值已经不低，0.24一直没入，后来去研究了下玩法，又和 @xing8047  聊了后，是我眼光短浅了，@tapeuptony 他们的这个机制确实牛逼！布局不论早晚，只看时机。

Tapeout @tapeupio是 TapeOut 生态中基于 DeWEB 构建的全链账本协议， 是BunnyPark 创始团队重返 BNB Chain 打造的。

协议原生资产是 $UP,上线才1天在内盘市值直接突破 1000 万美金，已经发射，可以在BNB链上双向跨链了，而且跨链不增加总量，原来的 PoB 流动性保留锁定。

PoB Trading Engine核心机制：
PoB 解决“发行快、建设慢”的错位→把一次买入预算拆成即时成交 + 蓄水池分期释放，延长买盘窗口，给产品交付和社区协作留时间。卖出无任何分期限制。

UP机制 ：
-开盘首 24 小时：10% 即时买入，90% 进入 25 天线性释放蓄水池。
-满 24 小时后：30% 即时买入，70% 进入 25 天线性释放。
-蓄水池中的资金只能继续买 UP，不能提取为自由 BEM。后续成交量按执行时的实时价格计算。
-支持 BEM 直接买，或者 BNB/USDT 路由先换 BEM 再买。

Builder Code绑定能加速释放，这个是重点！！！
每位用户有唯一 Builder Code。填写有效 Code 能触发双方等额加速，点击Early release ，绑定，具体看👇图片

费用与分配：
两本账独立，不能简单相加：
1.1% BEM 交易手续费（核心协议收入，以 BEM 收取）：
-50% → 地铁站网络：40% 电路质押验证节点（按验证工作量）、10% BEM 质押。
-40% → UP 回购预算（购回的 UP 计划 20% 销毁、80% 用于生态发展）。
-10% → 团队（其中 20%，即总手续费的 2%，计划回购销毁 BEM；其余 8% 团队留存）。

1.5% UP 建设税（以 UP 收取）：
-进入独立奖励池。
-按前一日 Builder Code 产生的主动+被动加速权重分配（首次发放覆盖前两天池子给第一天权重）。
-公式：奖励 = 池子 × 用户有效权重占比。

100% 公平发行 + 时间分布式买盘 + 可核验的协作激励 + 手续费回流网络与回购，把交易参与延续到建设过程，代币UP不是短期fomo，整个机制太有可玩性了，感兴趣的可以去研究看看。

在Tapeout 生态上有很多好玩且造富能力很强的东西，已经有很多人拿到不错的结果，一定不要忽略！

⚠️ 严重漏洞警告

Linux 内核 IPv4 TCP 握手存在远程 UAF，无需认证即可触发，可能导致内核内存泄露、崩溃甚至远程 root。

也就是说，黑客不需要密码就能攻击你的服务器，甚至完全控制。

Go 1.24+ 程序（包括 geth 等节点）默认启用 MPTCP 监听，正好匹配已知利用条件。

请尽快升级并重启到已修复内核！

author: Goupenguin
quoted_text:
Grok Bot 额度机制天机泄露😱

1. Grok Bot 的额度不按消息条数扣，按 Bot 实际干的活扣：模型调用、上下文体积、工具调用全都算。每走一步都要把整段历史重读一遍，最忙的 Bot 每步要重读 8-9 万 token。

2. 搜 X 走 Bot 自带的免费额度（每分钟 30 次、每天 1000 次），不扣周额度。但搜回来的大批推文要存文件，别贴进聊天。

3. 最大的坑是看图看视频。截图、视频帧、扫描件直接丢进对话，上下文会迅速膨胀；有人一天发 4 张图、搜一次、处理两份扫描件，就吃掉顶档周额度的 11%。我自己用它剪视频，也是掉得最快的。先让命令行工具出文字摘要，Bot 只读摘要。

4. 读网页别让它截图点点点。同一个网站，Computer use 约 21.3 万 token，浏览器里跑脚本约 5.1 万，纯脚本执行期间模型 0 token。能走 API 连接器就别开浏览器。

5. Bot 当包工头，别当搬砖工。在它的云电脑上装 Grok Build、Codex、Claude Code、Pi + DeepSeek 这些 CLI，重活让 CLI 跑，Bot 只调度。有人把写代码交给 Grok Build，两天半 Bot 池用了 70%，开发池才用 6%。

6. 但这里有个坑我天天踩：CLI 跑完没有明确提醒，Bot 派完活就睡了，经常忘了回来查，你就干等半天没结果；让它一直盯着，又费 token 效果还一般。目前看到的解法是 Webhook 叫醒：CLI 一跑完就把 Bot 叫起来验收，范凯和一泽都开源了现成的。

7. 定时任务是隐形吸血鬼。每 15 分钟跑一次 = 一周 672 次唤醒，改成每小时 = 168 次，一天 3 次 = 21 次。没变化也照样扣。

8. 盯数据的活改成"有变化才叫醒"：在云电脑里跑个脚本盯着，不过模型、不扣额度，有变动再用 Webhook 叫醒 Bot。注意 Webhook 实测约 1 小时 200 次上限，打满会中断。

9. 同一个 Bot 别聊太久。聊长了它会自动压缩上下文，你根本不知道它压掉了什么，效果越来越差，每一步还要重读一大坨。一个任务开一个新对话，长资料存成文件，聊天里只回结论和路径。放着不聊的旧对话不扣额度，不用清。

10. 别开 Bot 群聊。群里每条消息每个 Bot 都要读一遍，纯重复浪费；有个团队账号约三分之一的轮次是 Bot 在互相叫醒。让 Bot 之间单独对话，消耗反而可控。

11. 同理，别让主 Bot 一次给所有 Bot 派活。我之前有个定期更新记忆、推送文件的任务，主 Bot 每次给所有 Bot 发一遍，它们就各自把文档重新总结一遍。可我平时就让它们日常总结了，这一轮纯属重复烧额度。

12. 先小样本，再放量。复杂任务先跑 1-2 个样本，停下确认再继续；同一步失败 2 次就让它停下来问你。有人 2 小时试错就烧掉过半周额度。

13. 两个无效技巧：想切轻量模型省额度——没有模型选择器，系统自动分配；多订几份想叠加——不叠加，只用额度高的那份。

14. 现在是大一统订阅：Grok、Grok Bot、Cursor 共用一个每周池。Grok Bot 从 $30 的 Premium 起才有，Super $100 是它的近 4 倍，Ultra $200 是 12 倍多。第三方模型不在池子里，按 API 原价另算。

15. 官方没公布每档多少 token。有人从 Cursor 后台反推：$30 周限额约 2.76 亿 token，$100 约 13.27 亿，$200 约 44 亿（个人实测反推，非官方）。

----
数字大多来自 个人实践 + 中推几位 Grok 大使和高玩的实测，官方至今没公布每档具体多少 token。 
特别感谢 @cgnot996 铁柱的 12 招长文，一半以上的数字出自那篇🙏 
也谢谢 @KinGao476942 @fankaishuoai @eze_is_1 @Michael_Fenech_ 的实测分享。

我觉得很多人还没有意识到，币安现在的情况有多严重。

不到24小时前，币安才开始恢复21种币的提币功能。

但目前仍有531种币无法提币。

而且就连已经开放提币的这21种币，状态也仍然显示为“部分提币暂停”，也就是说，用户能提取的金额依然受到限制。

可即便采取了这么多限制措施，币安今天的资金净流出仍然创下了67亿美元的历史纪录。

这个数字甚至超过了FTX崩盘前72小时的资金净流出总额。

67亿美元，也是加密货币交易所历史上最高的单日资金净流出纪录。

这意味着，接下来几天，随着币安逐步恢复更多币种的提币功能，并最终取消现有的提币额度限制，其单周和单月的资金净流出规模很可能会进一步暴涨。

更令人担忧的是，几天前币安才刚刚发生了一起涉及63亿美元的黑客攻击事件。

别忘了，币安本质上就是一个不受监管的黑箱。它的资产负债表和实际负债情况从来不对外公开。

我们根本无从得知，币安是否曾经在链下交易中拿客户存款作为抵押，来补充自己的储备金。

外界长期以来一直怀疑币安采用的是部分准备金模式。由于币安从不公开财务报表，也没有人能够向你证明它没有这么做。

从各项指标来看，币安正在经历一场挤兑的初期阶段。

至于问题什么时候会真正爆发，目前还没人知道。

但有一点已经非常明显，市场对赵长鹏和币安的信任正在迅速瓦解。

现在可能只需要马斯克发一条制造恐慌的推文，就足以引发一场死亡螺旋，最终导致币安像FTX一样倒闭。

就像四年前，赵长鹏的一条推文引发了FTX的挤兑潮一样。

在目前这种情况下，唯一负责任的做法，就是立刻把你在币安的所有资金全部提出来。

继续观望，等着看接下来会发生什么，对你没有任何好处。

别忘了，一旦进入破产程序，有担保债权人的受偿顺序会排在普通客户前面。

如果你的资金还放在币安，那就谈不上安全。任何告诉你资金绝对安全的人，都是在撒谎。

text:
关于 @SolRocketPad  的打新项目 @bb84sh，我们来研究一下具体是干嘛的

bb84是一个为 Solana 构建的后量子（Post-Quantum）安全基础设施项目，口号是 “Quantum-born. Quantum-proof.”（量子原生，量子安全）。

### 核心问题

当前区块链钱包使用的签名算法（如 Solana 的 Ed25519、以太坊的 ECDSA）在未来大型量子计算机面前会被 Shor 算法破解。区块链上的公钥是公开的，存在“现在收集、未来破解”（Harvest Now, Decrypt Later）的风险。而协议级升级又很慢、需要共识，bb84 选择在应用层先把后量子能力做出来。

### 基本原理

它把两件事结合在一起：

1. 真实量子硬件（QPU）

通过 IBM Quantum、Amazon Braket 等调用真实量子计算机（Rigetti、IBM、IQM、IonQ 等），用来生成密钥种子和量子随机数。每个量子作业都会在 Solana 上留下收据，并用链上的电路模拟器做校验，确保结果真实可信。

2. 后量子密码学（主要是 Falcon-512）

用户的钱包/金库使用 Falcon-512 这种抗量子签名算法。
- 公钥在链上只注册一次（约 897 字节）。
- 之后每笔交易只需要带上较短的签名。
- 提供一个不可逆的 Q-Day 开关：开启后，即使经典的 Ed25519 私钥被盗，资金也只能通过 Falcon 签名才能移动。

### 一句话总结

真实量子计算机负责“生”出密钥和随机性，Solana 负责链上验证和托管，用户通过 Falcon-512 钱包/金库提前获得后量子级别的资金保护，且不需要修改 Solana 协议本身。目前核心功能已在 devnet 运行。

项目同时规划了 Quantum ID（.quantum / .pqc 域名）、量子随机数服务、后量子消息等，构成一套完整的量子安全栈。

### 写在最后

SolRocket 上线多年但是发射的项目很少，总共就3个，其中 $Solchat 1500x，ath 180m， $OCTO 高点33m，整体质量还是可以，而且上面的项目都得到 @toly  的支持

量子区块链是个很好的方向，所以可以留意看看

当然上面说这些这不意味着新项目肯定能赚钱，但也需要是个机会，总之DYOR
