SpaceX Bare Metal Competition for Neoclouds?

So yes, SpaceX will put up alot of bare metal. All of the customers buying bare metal capacity will use it to produce tokens, so competition is coming across the entire Neocloud stack. 

Is this new supply or replacing supply that will fail to come up?

SPCX Replacing Nscale
I have heard that SPCX is in talks to sell bare metal capacity to MSFT and Anthropic for their 2027 buildout. We can look at one Neocloud's capacity that was suppose to go to these two but will not materialize.

Nscale needs to provide 200k GB300s for MSFT by end of 2027 (1). 104k GB300s for ~240MW so 200k GB300s is 500MW (1). MSFT has options for additional 700MW from Nscale. Nscale also is responsible for compute for Anthropic. 

Nscale from their IPO prospectus file on Sept 18, 2026 has a grand total of 55MW up (2). Nscale, FirmusAI, SharonAI and alot of the 200 Neoclouds will not deliver. Sign with bad Neoclouds that don't deliver? Solution is to pay premium for SpaceX to bail you out.

Google
Now Google for the first time has stated in their earnings call they will buy 3P capacity aka bare metal. Previously there were very adamant of only buying colocation. 

Who has the scale to build for Google? $SPCX? Is this bad for Neoclouds? No, Google was suppose to bring that capacity online anyways. But now with colocation market getting tighter with TikTok in the market for 5GW, Google is has to buy bare metal capacity.

Meta
People are scared Meta will sell bare metal capacity on their old H100s/H200s/B200s as they upgrade to VR200s. 

Either they are selling the old GPUs outright to make space to retrofit for VR200s, or they are signing contracts on them to get backed financing for their VR200s GPUs and DCs. 

Those H100s/H200s/B200s were going to be used either way. CRWV just signed A100s to extend their lifetime to 9yrs a few months ago.

Meta is also going to spin up their own AI cloud, they just hired MongoDB CEO as their Enterprises sales guy. All this will eventually be competition for inference too at the end of the day whether Meta sells inference themselves or bare metal to Baseten/Modal/etc who will see it as inference, don't let some bias expert convince you competition is coming for bare metal only.

Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
关于 Personal Agent 的两个根本性问题：

1、用户可能不需要一个 AI 健康管家，但是他希望少生病、睡得好；用户可能不需要一个 AI 助理，但希望自己的事情能自动处理好。AI 产品如果要求用户主动提出任务、持续管理 Agent，本身就创造了新的使用成本。一个每月只能帮我节省半小时，却需要我花一小时配置和检查的 AI 助理，缺少足够的经济价值。

2、早期的电力革命催生了冰箱、洗衣机和空调，解决的是高频、刚需的物理世界问题。AI 当前的价值更多集中在认知和决策领域，比如让孩子拥有私人教师、让家庭拥有健康管家、让每个人拥有私人事务助理。但普通人真的需要这么多专业服务吗？供给能力的爆炸，并不一定带来需求的爆炸。我们可能严重高估了人类对 AI 服务的需求。

Personal Agent 的最大竞争对手，可能是用户什么都不做😂。宁愿忍受一些低效率，也不愿意为解决这些问题额外投入精力。

text:
Just read Commanding Heights.

It sketches a fairly depressing future: AI displaces white-collar workers, while wealth concentrates among those who own scarce physical assets and infrastructure.

There is a more optimistic possibility: AI changes where human ambition goes.

Many talented 20-year-olds chose banking, law, consulting or software engineering partly because those careers offered the highest rewards. They weren’t all passionate about financial models or corporate contracts. They followed the incentives.

If AI makes that work abundant and cheap, while building things in the physical world remains difficult and valuable, those incentives would shift.

More of our brightest people would be incentivised to build careers and companies in areas like medicine, energy, architecture, physical engineering and space exploration - with cheap intelligence helping them tackle problems that were previously too expensive or complex.

The same scarcity that pushes up prices and rewards physical asset owners could also attract the talent and investment needed to expand supply and overcome those bottlenecks.

Losing white-collar jobs would still be painful. But over time, we could see an enormous redirection of human ambition towards improving the physical world.

其实这个和 @StantyAi 在几年前吃饭的时候就深入聊过，并且取得共识，今天靠argon更加准确的描述出来。

底层的中心化物理瓶颈就会向上“泄漏”，直接消解上层的去中心化假设。

这句话，其实更加通用一些，可以讲 “现实世界的中心化物理瓶颈就会“泄漏传导”，从而消解L4的去中心化假设。” 

如果对安全感兴趣，其实不妨认真的思考一下这里面宏观的关系。
author: drjingle
quoted_text:
区块链、密码学与底层基础设施（TCP/IP、硅基硬件、物理通信网络）的关系，被定义为覆盖网络（Overlay Network）与底层承载网络（Underlay Infrastructure）的耦合系统，其安全性遵循跨层安全（Cross-Layer Security）与最弱环节原则（Weakest-Link Principle）。

无论上层的椭圆曲线密码学（ECC）、零知识证明（ZKP）或拜占庭容错（BFT）共识在数学上多么无懈可击，只要它们运行在真实的物理世界中，就必须向下委托信任。

软件工程学者 Joel Spolsky 提出的抽象泄漏法则（Law of Leaky Abstractions）指出：所有非平凡的抽象在某种程度上都是有漏洞的。区块链试图在 L4 构建一个“去中心化、抗审查”的理想逻辑世界，但当 L2 的 BGP 路由被少数电信运营商（ISP）控制，或 L0 的晶圆代工与手机安全芯片集中在极少数巨头手中时，底层的中心化物理瓶颈就会向上“泄漏”，直接消解上层的去中心化假设。

当密码学家把 L4 层的哈希函数和零知识证明加固到需要耗费全宇宙能量才能破解的程度时，理性的攻击者（遵循成本收益最大化）绝不会去硬撞数学难题，而是会将攻击向量转移到成本极低的 L5（发送钓鱼链接欺骗用户授权、入侵交易所热钱包服务器）、L2（DNS 投毒与 BGP 劫持）或 L0（供应链投毒）。

这就是为什么近年来密码学理论突飞猛进，但加密货币领域的资产被盗规模依然居高不下——数学层的绝对安全，反而将全部风险挤压到了工程实现层、硬件终端层与人类交互层。

量子计算与人工智能（AI）对密码学和加密货币的冲击，恰好构成了对这一技术栈的“上下夹击”：

量子计算是针对 L4（密码学与数学层）的“降维打击”：它直接动摇了现代密码学的计算复杂性理论根基（单向陷门函数假设），属于远期但具有毁灭性的底层范式颠覆。

AI 是针对 L0（物理侧信道）与 L5（应用代码与人类交互层）的“非对称加速打击”：它无法直接违背数学定律去暴力猜出私钥，但它将寻找系统工程漏洞、侧信道提取以及社会工程学欺诈的成本降到了趋近于零，属于当下正在发生的系统性工程危机。

A few things I've been hearing from some Hong Kong-based funds:

They believe 2027 will mark the peak in AI capex growth. Spending may continue to rise in 2028–2029, but a slowdown in the growth rate is inevitable. Interestingly, I've been hearing this same argument from them for the past 2–3 years.

Their valuation argument follows from this: once capex growth starts slowing, these stocks can no longer justify 20–30x earnings.

One of them put it this way: "Even if a stock looks cheap at 10–15x today, that valuation doesn't mean much if capex growth starts decelerating next year."

They also believe the market needs a much stronger "new narrative" to trigger a meaningful reversal in sentiment.

Personally, I find this reasoning a little amusing. It's almost the complete opposite of what I've been hearing from funds in Taiwan and the US.

Same industry, same data, yet such different conclusions.

text:
Grok Bot - what it is and how I use it day to day

I'm non-technical and not from a CS background but with @bot and its army of specialised bots I've been able to build things and run automations to make work more streamlined 

What it is
• @grok is the chatbot you ask a question. OTOH Grok Bot is a team of agents that stay on since each agent has its own computer, memory, scheduled routines and connectors (X, Notion, GitHub)
• They browse the web, message each other and keep working EVEN while I'm asleep 
• You can even use it together with @claudeai Code (Grok Bot handles all ongoing work, and hands the job to a cloud coding agent on my GitHub using Claude code

How I use it
• All you need to run a company in this time and age is 1-2 devs and the rest can be automated with AI with a swarm of agents doing different tasks 
• Agents can do the following: QA and security (subagents run stress tests and vulnerability scans in parallel with development), some element of design, and project management (tracking, notes, daily team updates)
• For research: we mainly use it for tracking governance forums and @github repos, and a content room (Scout, a writer, an Editor) 
• (Still backtesting and iterating daily): set up a group with different agent functions - Trader,  Analyst and a Risk Manager 
• A Chief of Staff sits on top to coordinates everyone through a Notion "second brain" (basically to store memory)
• Make use of Group chats in Grokbot: let your agents argue it out 
• Telegram bots on a small VPS: to provide real time news monitoring, exploits or hacks 

Misc
• dr eggbot made by @poteto. It's a bot that designs other bots: it asks you a few questions about what you need, then creates them for you
• Make use of Skills: saved playbooks like your writing style, trade rules 
• Find other bots: https://t.co/VpF2nzaWZ4 -> Plugins -> Bots
• Use the connector: connect to Notion, Slack, Figma
• Prefer using grokbot as it can read @X directly and access who I am already following here 
• Downside is that usage runs out pretty fast @elonmusk pls sir 

If you're not technical, start with one bot plus dr eggbot and add more when there's a real job for them

Built at a cost of 72.7 billion yuan (about $10.75 billion), the 134.2-km canal runs from Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to the Beibu Gulf, the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China.

author: AvailProject
quoted_text:
There are a few benefits to this actually:

1. it makes it harder for copy bots to follow your next trade because each position uses a fresh wallet.

2. that also makes it harder for competitors to piece together your strategy or see your full book.

3. with fewer people copying your moves, you could get less price pressure while you're still building a position.

Your positions are still public, but they're harder to link back to you, so you get some privacy without leaving Hyperliquid.

I can see more platforms adding this because being able to trade onchain shouldn't mean sharing your whole strategy with everyone.

But what do you guys think?

Russia's 48-hour-long massive Geran drone attack on Ukraine has finally concluded. 

Over 1,400 Geran-4/5 jet-drones and Geran-2 drones were used in total, attacking dozens of different towns and cities across 22 out of 23 regions (excluding Kherson Oblast due to the ceasefire). Of these 1,400 drones, around 1,000 Geran-2/Gerberas and 400 Geran-4/5s were used.

The main targets were electrical substations and railway infrastructure, as well as some airbases used by the Ukrainian Air Force. Widespread power outages occurred across large parts of Ukraine, including the cities of Dnipro and Kyiv, and the implementation of rolling blackouts has been intensified. 

In the second half of the attack (the last 24 hours), explosions were heard in/near the following locations: 

- Lviv City

- Multiple different districts of Kyiv City
- Vylkove, Odesa Oblast

- Dolyns'ka, Kirovohrad Oblast
- Baburka, Zaporizhzhia Oblast

- Okhtyrka, Sumy Oblast
- Nosivka, Chernihiv Oblast

The first half (24 hours) of the attack involved a little over 600 Geran-2/4/5 drones, and focused primarily on targeting energy infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, as well as railway and energy infrastructure across Vinnytsia, Khmelnytskyi, Zhytomyr, and Ternopil Oblast. There were also a large number of strikes on Kyiv and its surroundings, and heavy attacks on Sumy City and its surroundings. Southern Ukraine (Odesa, Mykolaiv, Kherson, Kirovohrad, and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts) were largely spared from attacks.

The second half (24 hours) of the attack involved around 700 Geran-2/4/5 drones, and continued to focus on energy and railway infrastructure in the western regions of Ukraine, although strikes on Ternopil Oblast were swapped for heavier attacks on the neighbouring Rivne Oblast. Kyiv and its surroundings continued to see a lot of activity, although this decreased compared to the first half. Odesa Oblast was struck this time, and there was also more activity seen in Zaporizhzhia Oblast too. Strikes on energy infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava Oblasts decreased compared to the first half. 

In my opinion, this is a prelude to the upcoming combined missile and drone attack involving strategic aviation, which will likely occur sometime this week. It has helped exhaust Ukrainian air defence and aviation capabilities, and put further strain on the power grid, which will be hit even harder once the missiles start flying. I will make a separate post about the preparations for this upcoming missile attack in the near future. 

I do find it funny, though, that this massive attack involving over 1,400 long-range drones, hundreds of successful strikes, and almost every region of Ukraine hit was almost entirely ignored in the information space in favour for two Russian refineries being hit by a few Ukrainian drones each. 

(Note: The attached map shows only the strikes from the second half of the attack. You can find the map of the first half in the quoted post)

他倒不是在黑 Hyperliquid。Don Wilson 是传统期货圈的大佬，本身就是芝加哥老牌自营交易公司 DRW 和加密做市商 Cumberland 的创始人兼 CEO。

他是站在大做市商和机构的角度提了六个质疑，最核心的一条是 Hyperliquid 的 ADL (自动减仓) 机制。

他判断 CFTC 大概率不会放行 ADL。原因是清算出事时，ADL 是把损失往上推给盈利方，跟传统清算所的逻辑正好反过来。传统的顺序是先扣保证金，再动用保险基金和违约基金，最后由清算所自己兜底。

他预计 2027 年会见分晓，答案交给市场。

依我看——Hyperliquid 合规进入美国之路，从来都不会是坦途。路是一个个问题解掉才铺出来的。

CFTC 既然嘴上已经承诺，且行动上也已经在推进，那就交给时间吧... 正好让我们能多囤点便宜的 HYPE。

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

今天起正式加入 @MojoAI_HQ 了，和 @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee 等很多小伙伴一起build AI 个人财富助手事业 🫡 . 

半年以前和一个资深做量化的朋友探讨，AI之于交易到底能有什么意义。他的看法是团队至少探索了7～8年了，目前得出的结论是没什么意义。

但在我的视角里，如果一场全面改写交互方式的革命已经席卷一切软件，而唯独金融/交易领域还没开始 / 还没有人做的足够好，那么这就是值得投入的红利期，虽然这种红利可能在大多数whales眼里看不上，也不会太久，且以后窗口期也只会越来越短。

更朴实的，这个世界属于绝大多数人。尽管 AI 在“赚钱”“暴富”上可能还无法成为无所不能的印钞机，但用过 mojo 以后，我发现至少我们“抓机会”的能力已经可以全面平权了。

“AI 交易” 实际上是一种对 AI 金融领域能力的狭隘想象。这个行业真的靠交易暴富的人，我相信也孑孑寥寥。我相信绝大多数能够翻身的人，本质还是靠的毒辣的机会嗅觉、敢于重仓的赌性和超绝执行力。而最后一步，往往是很多人止步于机会大门前的最后一道门槛。链上信号、狙击、快进快出、多号快速分发与收集…… 很多人不是不知道什么机会好，但是工具和执行细节的缺失让他们无法抓住机会。

用过 Mojo 以后，我发现这是我想做的事情。一句话跨链，一句话创建原本大科学家才能创建的监控和脚本，一句话学习&模仿其他作者的agent模板（是的，就像grok bot那样）…… 我不指望 AI 能让我赚多少钱，但我相信钱包 / 交易所 / 跨链 / DEX ……这些2018/2019 以来就没怎么变过的行业基础设施，应该变一变，变得更顺手，好用，理解我，能够救急，能够真的抓住机会。 

综上，很荣幸能和 Mojo 团队一起探索这种未来。🫡 

Glad to announce that I've officially joined @MojoAI_HQ to build an AI personal wealth agent with @ForestBai1 @msfew_eth @jenniekusu @0xBenniee and a lot of other great people 🫡

About six months ago, I was talking with a friend who's a veteran quant about what AI actually means for trading. His take: his team had been exploring it for at least 7-8 years, and their conclusion so far was that it doesn't mean much.

But the way I see it, if a revolution in how we interact with software is sweeping through everything, and finance/trading is the one place where it hasn't started, or where no one has done it well enough yet, then this is a window worth betting on. Most whales probably won't care about it, it won't last long, and these windows will only keep getting shorter.

Put more simply, this world belongs to the vast majority of people. AI may not be an all-powerful money printer that makes you rich overnight, but after using Mojo, I've realized that at the very least, the ability to catch opportunities can now be truly democratized.

"AI trading" is actually a pretty narrow way to imagine what AI can do in finance. I believe the people who've truly gotten rich from trading alone are few and far between. Most people who turn their lives around do it with a razor-sharp nose for opportunity, the guts to go big, and insane execution. And that last step is often the final barrier that stops people right at the door. On-chain signals, sniping, fast in and out, dealing assets on multiple chains... Plenty of people know a good opportunity when they see one, but they miss it because they don't have the tools or can't handle the execution details.

After using Mojo, I knew this was what I wanted to work on. Bridge across chains in one sentence. In one sentence, create the kind of monitors and scripts that only elite degen could build before. In one sentence, learn from and copy other creators' agent templates (yes, just like grok bot)... I don't expect AI to make me a ton of money, but I do believe that wallets, exchanges, bridges, DEXs ... all this infra that has barely changed since 2018/2019, should change. It should be smoother and easier to use, it should understand me, it should be able to bail me out in a pinch, and it should actually help me catch real alphas.

All of which is to say: I'm honored to explore this future with the Mojo team. 🫡

text:
AI中场的冰与火，市场的担忧和期望都在三大云厂商财报里，详细聊聊我对三大云厂商财报的理解：
1、先说“冰”的部分
1）毫无疑问市场最担忧就是资本开支狂飙（见下图一），过去六个季度资本开支在肉眼可见的提速，然后谷歌和亚马逊自由现金已经为负，微软还可以本季甚至27年都为正。三家巨头现金流的梯度已经拉开。当然谷歌财报如果加回TPU库存和欧盟罚款、自由现金流其实持平的，上周这里https://t.co/wOyDCpGqtX有聊过。

但需要明确，三家公司并非已经陷入流动性危机——缺口可以靠发债或股从资本市场筹资，甚至谷歌自由现金筹备还能支持当下的现金流缺口三到四年当然不能完全这么做、得给公司留下安全垫。

2）“冰”的第二点，主业没预期的强
（1）谷歌的AI mode搜索量激增但是转化率还没起来、商业化没跟上。AI Mode的低变现，才是本次最值得跟踪的结构性因素。处于范式转移阶段、商业化有一段时间低于预期其实正常，需要时间跟上来。AI mode下答案的准确性提高、其实单个点击成本可以更高，来对冲点击次数的减少；

当然在AI mode商业化没有明显跟上来，那么市场还是会担心、这种担忧可以理解

（2）亚马逊营收略低于预期，很大程度是今年会员日Prime Day在公司的多数重要市场地区均提前至二季度去年则是在三季度。而广告业务三季度表现低于预期，公司表示广告收入受到Prime Day时点等因素影响，并预计四季度广告收入同比增速将回升至高十位数区间。

而对于亚马逊个人理解市场更担心的是：如果外部AI Agent成为用户商品搜索与比价的主要界面 ，亚马逊或许仍能保住交易量、佣金和物流收入，却可能失去最有价值的那一层：站内广告的定价权。

但整体来说、在资本开支大幅提升，自由现金流为负的状态下、主营业务不及预期自然会加重市场的担忧。

2、再说说“火”的部分
1）云业务的增速确实令人振奋。
AWS本季度同比增长39.3%，Azure为48%，Google Cloud同比增长103%。这个数字说明，AI浪潮带来了真实的算力需求，企业客户正在用实际采购行为为这一判断背书。

而且细看三家巨头云业务过去六个季度的增速（下图2），你会发现最近三个开始加速了。最近三个季度，云业务同比增速，之前这里https://t.co/O4acqETi9q也聊到，按照数据中心建设节奏，25年三季度开始资本开支提速；那么今年三季度到明年数据中心算力陆续上线，那意味着云厂商的云业绩还会处于加速趋势。

虽然资本开支和自由现金流很差、但不能忽略云业务业绩在快速增长，甚至亚马逊ceo贾西在电话会上明确说27、28年AWS增速最低都是40%以上、按照最低40%测算、到28年AWS年营收能超过3600亿美金。其实保守测算微软和谷歌云业务28年至少也是3000亿美金的营收体量。

2）更重要的是AI采用在深化和扩散
三家云厂商本季财报披露的企业AI采用情况中，最值得重视的并非单纯的新客户或席位数量增长，而是已有客户支出的大幅扩容，以及付费模式从席位许可向使用量/按量计费的明确延伸。

（1）微软Foundry客户超12万、收入同比超3倍，Copilot主动消耗按量credits的客户环比增长超75%，GitHub Agent功能credits消耗自引入按量计费后超翻倍；
（2）谷歌去年已使用Gemini Enterprise的客户今年对谷歌支出超去年4倍，且过去12个月已形成超2600家百亿token级、约75家十万亿token级的高强度用户；
（3）AWS Fortune 500企业在Bedrock上的支出同比近7倍、token使用量近17倍，AgentCore本季部署Agent数量也达到此前三个季度合计的2倍。

这些数据共同指向同一趋势：企业AI正从“购买席位”进入“持续消耗算力与Agent”的阶段，存量客户的消费深度和付费意愿，已成为当前最核心的增长引擎。然后增量客户还在提升。

那么这次三大云厂商的财报给我的启示是：
1）7月份这里https://t.co/vxahSNjCBJ就聊到的AI基建时间差问题，其实我们现在已经看到新容量上线转化到订单和营收、但是还没有到经营现金流完全覆盖资本价值的时候、市场的担忧自然会暴增、在加上中期选举的不确定性、油价还在高位，自然引发市场的激烈调整；

2）还是之前一直聊到的AI主线其实迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

大家不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

当然市场真正要看的是资本开支扩张后，经营现金流能否以更快速度增长，以及客户付费能否覆盖推理、折旧、能源和网络成本。核心是“投入何时开始产生足够多的回报”，个人认为可能再过一两个季度我们就能看到

quoted_text:
昨晚跟168X的交流要点，上一次8月底https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC参与168X聊到：美股临近中期选举市场动荡加大，然后大饼和加密到10月因为流动性收紧会回踩。梳理下这次聊的要点：
1、美国经济正在进入由AI基建驱动的新基建周期，这种大基建趋势下名义GDP的增速会很好；

2、中东局势中期选举后可能会是一个时间窗口，如果能解决油价回落宏观环境压力会减少很多；
但如果一直不能解决油价持续在高位，通胀持续强势那么联储不仅12月会加息，明年也可能会加，如果原来预期 2 次，最后变成 3 次、4 次甚至更久，则整个估值体系都会重新定价、市场会扛不住。

3、ARR这个指标需要抛后，Anthropic上市后就要看真实的季度营收、年度营收了。大云平台已经是AI Operating System：企业会从结果和成本考虑，切换不同的模型。

4、大型科技公司真正大规模提高 CapEx，是从 2025 年三季度左右开始的，所以今天 Microsoft、Google Cloud 增长出来的 Revenue，很多对应的其实是一年前甚至更早花出去的钱。去年下半年开始加速建设的 Capacity，现在才进入投产期，而过去几个季度所有云厂商一直在讲同一句话：Demand > Supply，算力不够。如果需求还在增长，而且你新上线多少 Capacity 都能马上被吃掉，那未来几个季度 Revenue 自然会继续加速。所以我觉得AI商业化现在不是见顶，而是才刚开始加速。

5、要看Cloud Revenue Growth 何时开始超过 CapEx Growth
不能永远只看 Revenue，第二阶段要看 ROIC。2026 年是 CapEx 爆发的一年。去年几千亿美元，今年接近翻倍，这种 CapEx Growth 不可能每年都 100%。
真正漂亮的拐点是什么？就是未来 CapEx Growth 开始自然下降，但 AI Revenue Growth 还继续加速、意味着开始算的过账来。

所以接下来几个季度，最想看的就是：Revenue Growth、CapEx Growth、Depreciation Life、FCF，这几个东西开始怎么收敛。

6、AI主线已经迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

7、真正需要让 AI Thesis 转空的信号，不是 Semi 再跌 20%，而是 AI商业化（云厂商业绩增速）开始降速、当下是出于加速的阶段。这才是未来的市场的真正的大风险，

而另一个问题则是伊朗问题迟迟得不到解决，油价高位、通胀向上趋势被强化、联储不得不多次加息而非两次。

8、高收益率时代不再普涨：以后市场只奖励真实 Cash Flow。
当 Bond Yield 高以后，股票自然也要给更高的 Risk Premium，这就是为什么现在市场越来越挑剔。Google Cloud很好，Search、FCF 出现问题，市场照样先卖。所以之后选股票一定要分清楚：哪些公司只是 Narrative，哪些公司的业务已经真正兑现，Revenue 是真的、Cash Flow 是真的，而且未来 2、3 年增长空间还能算出来。

大公司如果因为短期逆风被杀估值，我反而觉得是好事，因为它给你重新上车的价格。高利率不是所有股票不能涨，而是市场会越来越“优中选优”。

9、中期选举后很多不确定性会减弱如国会的归属，再看伊朗问题是不是能解决，谨防Anthropic上市路演开始后的吸血。

昨天有一点现在看是不对的“昨天聊到如果亚马逊的财报还不错、市场有一波能到anthropic路演前、今年亚马逊财报云业务很好但是广告放缓、资本开支远超预期、也是加重了市场担忧”可能这种担忧要到中期选举之后再看了。

多谢@168MrZ

Collecting earned protocol fees could make the next Microchain user cover the withdrawal.

In a co-audit of its Mira AMM, Zealynx and the audit team found that `collect_protocol_fees` transferred tokens out but left `contract_reserves` unchanged.

The next LP deposit or swap was measured against that stale reserve figure. Part of the user's input could silently absorb the gap, or a smaller input could underflow and revert.

Microchain fixed the High finding by deducting collected fees from `contract_reserves`.

text:
The most interesting part of $ORE's design isn't live yet.

TLDR: Today, revenue generated by the ORE Reserve auto-compounds in isolation. Eventually, that revenue could be streamed to uORE holders (miners holding unclaimed rewards) as SOL mining credits, allowing the protocol to increasingly fund its own mining activity. The result is a flywheel that could strengthen mining incentives, lift staking yield, and put ORE on a path to net deflation.

First, it's worth understanding why ORE is different.

Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, and Solana all use their native assets to incentivize network security. ORE doesn't have that requirement. It inherits Solana’s security, so it can direct its incentives toward a different objective: rewarding those who accumulate and hold the asset.

ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.

Consider how value flows through ORE today:

- Miners deploy SOL to earn ORE, aiming to acquire it below market price.
- A 10% refining fee on claimed rewards is redistributed to holders of unclaimed rewards (uORE).
- Mining revenue funds ORE buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and the Reserve.
- The Reserve provides liquidity while generating its own revenue through LP fees and yield-bearing assets like JitoSOL and USDv.

The result is a system where mining activity supports holders through multiple mechanisms, while the Reserve continues to grow and generate additional liquidity and revenue.

But there's one more piece to the design. Arguably the most interesting.

In AI, recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system capable of improving its own capabilities, with each improvement enabling further improvements.

ORE has a potential economic equivalent.

Today, the simplified flow looks like this:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → Reserve.

The Reserve grows, generates revenue through LP fees and yield, and reinvests that revenue into itself. A straightforward compounding mechanism.

But the loop back to mining remains open.

Now consider what happens when Reserve revenue is redirected to uORE holders as SOL credits, usable exclusively for mining ORE.

The flow becomes:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → SOL mining credits → Mining → Reserve.

The loop closes.

This is the recursive moment.

Consider the significance of this change.

Today, mining depends on SOL supplied by users. With mining credits, the Reserve’s own revenue becomes a new source of capital to fund that same activity.

Originally powered by user capital, ORE could become increasingly self-powered.

A protocol generating its own fuel.

There are two particularly interesting second-order effects here.

First, Reserve-funded mining credits could increase competition for ORE rewards, driving up production costs. To the extent this stimulates incremental mining activity, it generates additional protocol revenue, supporting buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and Reserve growth.

Second, and perhaps most importantly, this creates a potential path toward sustained net deflation.

At sufficient scale, additional protocol revenue could fund enough buybacks and burial to consistently exceed new ORE issuance.

To be clear, mining credits aren't live today, and it may be years before the economics justify turning them on.

The Reserve first needs sufficient scale and sustainable revenue to fund meaningful mining incentives without compromising its liquidity or long-term growth.

More importantly, the incremental mining activity needs to generate enough additional value to justify redirecting revenue away from direct compounding.

But the potential end state is worth considering: an economic system that compounds recursively, under its own power.

text:
Gavin's right to see ROI on AI in these FT charts.

The three industries leaning hardest into AI (information, professional services and finance) went from a 2.2% productivity trend to 5.0% since 2022. The rest of the economy went from 0.9% to 1.4%.

The chart I keep staring at is the first one. In AI-adopting sectors, US output per worker breaks away from its 2012 to 2019 trend right after ChatGPT. The UK, Canada, France and Germany stay close to trend.

The counterargument is that this is just America's flexible labour market doing what it always does. I think the simpler explanation is that the US is where the AI spend lands first, and Gavin's point that America is 72% of Anthropic's revenue fits that.

If the first real productivity data shows up exactly where the tools get used most, it's hard to argue the buildout is running ahead of demand. I'd love to see the same cut by company size next

There are a few benefits to this actually:

1. it makes it harder for copy bots to follow your next trade because each position uses a fresh wallet.

2. that also makes it harder for competitors to piece together your strategy or see your full book.

3. with fewer people copying your moves, you could get less price pressure while you're still building a position.

I can see more platforms adding this because being able to trade onchain shouldn't mean sharing your whole strategy with everyone.

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 10.26-11.1

ZBT traded inside a narrow band of roughly $0.068–$0.072 across the week of October 26 to November 1, finishing near $0.070 as the broader market’s defensive tone limited any meaningful bid. The token’s relative stability.

Total crypto market capitalization settled near $2.61 trillion, down approximately 2.7% on the week, while Bitcoin dominance held close to 60%. Bitcoin opened the period near $80,100 and closed in the $77,500–$78,200 area, a weekly decline of roughly 3%. 

Its range stretched from a mid-week high around $81,900 down to a low near $76,300, with the sharpest selling arriving after the October 29 security incident. Ethereum followed a nearly identical percentage path, finishing near $2,250–$2,270. Both assets spent most of the later sessions below the $80,000 and $2,300 levels that had acted as short-term support earlier in October.

Derivatives positioning reflected the shift. Funding rates stayed muted while long liquidations accelerated once price broke the prior range. The week’s defining event was the October 29 Binance incident, in which attackers drained approximately $6.3 billion across multiple chains in a matter of hours—the largest theft recorded in crypto history. 

On-chain tracing linked the activity to the North Korean group, with Ethereum accounting for the largest share of value, followed by Bitcoin and several other networks. Roughly $2.7 billion was subsequently frozen by stablecoin issuers and network participants, while Binance stated it would cover remaining user losses from company reserves and emergency funds.

The episode produced elevated exchange-related flows, including large BTC and ETH transfers between hot wallets and attacker-controlled addresses before partial freezes took effect. Withdrawals were paused and then partially restored over the following days, and reported outflow estimates in the immediate aftermath varied widely across on-chain observers. The incident coincided with a drop in the Fear & Greed Index into the 30–34 Fear zone by the weekend, reversing the more neutral readings that had prevailed earlier in the week.

Spot Bitcoin ETF flows mirrored the risk-off turn. Early-week inflows were more than offset by a $643 million outflow on October 30, leaving the complex net negative for the full period; BlackRock’s IBIT and several other products contributed to the Friday redemption. Ethereum ETFs extended a multi-week streak of net outflows. The combination of the exchange security event and the late-week equity sell-off amplified the redemption pressure, and total net assets across the Bitcoin ETF complex remained well above $100 billion even after the day’s outflow.

Macro conditions reinforced the caution. U.S. equities closed the week lower, with the S&P 500 finishing at 7,580.07 for a 0.57% weekly decline and the Nasdaq Composite falling 2% to 25,437. Friday’s session was the weakest for the S&P 500 since early June, driven by sharp losses in technology and AI-related names amid renewed questions about capital expenditure intensity. The 10-year Treasury yield eased toward 4.93%.

Energy markets stayed elevated against the backdrop of ongoing Middle East tensions. Brent crude settled near $117.64 and WTI near $104.12, supported by risks around the Strait of Hormuz, tanker incidents, and Houthi activity linked to the broader Iran conflict. Oil’s rise kept inflation concerns in focus and limited the scope for any sustained recovery in risk assets, including crypto.

On-chain metrics beyond the hack-related flows showed a modest contraction in stablecoin supply over the week, consistent with the broader de-risking. Whale and long-term holder activity outside the forced movements tied to the incident remained subdued, and Bitcoin’s realized volatility stayed compressed relative to earlier October swings even as the absolute price level declined. Exchange balances reflected the temporary disruption at the largest venue, while broader network activity did not show a comparable spike in organic demand.

The week therefore closed with price action clustered below the prior $80,000–$82,000 support band, ETF flows turned negative after early strength, and sentiment locked in Fear territory. The combination of the largest recorded exchange theft, equity weakness concentrated in growth stocks, and elevated oil prices left the market defensive heading into the new week, with any recovery dependent on clearer evidence that the security event had been contained and that macro pressures were not intensifying further.

按照标普 500 价格指数的日历年统计，1950 年到 2022 年一共经历了 19 个中期选举年，平均上涨 4.6%，其中 11 年收涨。而中期选举次年的 19 个年份，平均涨幅达到了 17.2%，其中 17 年收涨。

也就是说，中期选举次年的平均涨幅约是选举年的 3.7 倍，也高于总统大选年 8.1% 的平均水平。两次下跌分别发生在 2011 年和 2015 年，其中 2011 年跌幅非常小，接近平盘。

最近一次中期选举就是一个例子。2022 年标普 500 全年下跌 19.4%，到了 2023 年，全年上涨 24.2%。2022 年也正好赶上美联储连续加息，宏观环境同样会影响市场的实际表现。

从季度数据来看，中期选举年的第四季度平均上涨 6.6%，是总统四年周期中表现最强的第四季度。历史平均数不代表每一次都会重演，但从过去的统计来看，中期大选后的次年，确实是整个总统周期中平均表现最强的一年。

所以我个人一直再说，现阶段买入 bitcoin:native 在概率学来说，能够再 12，1，2月上涨的概率还是很大的。

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

text:
美股接下来最大的政治变量：11 月 3 日美国中期选举。

摩根士丹利给出的判断是：民主党大概率夺回众议院，参议院选情也从共和党占优转向双方势均力敌，民主党略占优势。

但对市场来说，真正值得关注的不是谁赢，而是选举之后华盛顿可能进入政府分治。

几个关键影响：

- 财政政策： 两党分治将提高重大税收、支出改革的立法难度，降低政策大幅转向的可能性，但美国财政赤字问题不会因此消失。

- 美股表现： 历史上，共和党总统任期内，中期选举后民主党控制两院，标普 500 随后一年平均上涨约 16%；两院分别由两党控制时，平均涨幅约 23%。但今年美股已经提前上涨不少，不能简单复制历史行情。

- 科技股： 数据中心建设面临地方抵制，项目可能延期，电网升级和基础设施投入也会增加，但这不意味着 AI 长期需求消失。

- 能源市场： 伊朗战争即使结束，霍尔木兹海峡恢复通航后，能源产能也需要时间修复。摩根士丹利预计，受损产量恢复 75% 可能仍需约四个月。

- 债券市场： 政府分治很难推动大规模财政改革，美国赤字和国债发行压力仍然存在，长期利率未必因此下降。

核心结论：中期选举可能改变华盛顿的权力结构，却未必改变美股的基本运行逻辑。

通胀、经济增长和企业盈利，依然比谁控制国会更重要。

对投资者而言，选举带来的短期波动可能创造交易机会，但真正决定美股中长期走势的，仍然是 AI 能否兑现盈利、能源成本如何变化，以及美国经济能否保持增长。

最近硅谷 AI 圈最有趣的连续剧，迎来了 Day 28 的大结局。

简单补个前情提要：一边是 OpenAI 负责 Codex 和个人智能体 Dot 的 Tibo，因为一言不合就给用户重置额度，被社区戏称为 Reset Company（后面成了 Token Company）。他在 10 月初立了个 28 天挑战，每天要么发新功能，要么全员重置额度。另一边是前 Meta React 编译器核心成员、现在在 SpaceXSI 的 Lauren（也就是 poteto），以极其严苛的 Agent 工程流和每个月合并上千个 PR 出名，自称 Ship Company（既造飞船又高频发版）。

这两个人最近在 X 上高强度互怼互撩了上百个回合，甚至有网友专门建了三个网站来实时抓取他俩的互动记录。前几天 Tibo 刚和 Meta 的 Alexandr Wang 围绕自家的 Dot 和 Meta 的 Muse 吵了一架，转头就买下 https://t.co/zjtiXqcv9z 整了个大活，拿了 300 万浏览量。

当时 poteto 吐槽说自己买不起 https://t.co/OhTZR6NVb8，然后默默发了个 Day 28 的预告。到了今天第 28 天，她花了 5.99 美元买下 https://t.co/jVAlHWI6o9 这个域名，用 Grok Bot 和 Cursor 搓了一个完成度极高的类吸血鬼幸存者网页游戏，甚至可以直接在 X 的推文卡片里点开玩。

最神的是，游戏在 4 天前就开坑了，设定是 Tibo 带着一群狗在满屏怪潮里求生。结果就在游戏发布前几个小时，Tibo 刚好发推吐槽手机输入法老是把自家的智能体 Dot 自动纠错成 dog，害他收到一堆诸如“我太爱我的狗了，昨天它还帮我约了理发”的搞笑短信。两边纯属巧合地撞在了一起，节目效果直接拉满。除此之外，游戏里把额度重置做成了核心机制，还顺带把 Meta 的 Muse 和 Alexandr Wang 的梗全写进了彩蛋里。

本来以为只是个玩梗小游戏，结果看她发出来的技术复盘，完全是一份教科书级别的 AI 辅助工程实践：

整个项目是她 4 天前利用业余时间开的坑，4 天里靠 Agent 提交并合并了大约 1150 个 PR。

工作流最核心的一点是：每次她在代码里发现问题，不是自己去改，而是让 Bot 针对这个问题写一条 lint 规则。甚至代码里直接通过 lint 规则禁止写注释，如果一段代码需要解释，解决办法只能是改个更好的变量名或者补一个测试。

为了防止游戏卡顿，她把上下文直接写进了文件路径里。所有每一帧或每个 tick 都要跑的热路径代码，文件后缀都命名为 .hot.ts，并且专门配了 lint 规则禁止在这些文件里做内存分配，不准用对象字面量、闭包或者 new。这样主循环几乎不产生垃圾回收压力，从根源上消除了 GC 带来的掉帧。

状态机部分重度使用了 TLA+ 做形式化验证，剧情、过场动画和核心系统都有各自的形式化验证 skill 来找 bug。

底层除了用 three.js 画 3D 场景，物理模拟、后处理和音频引擎全是自己写的。而且整个模拟层是完全确定性的，每一次游玩都可以通过输入序列精确重放。当你上传高分时，服务端会把你的整局操作完整重放一遍来校验有没有作弊。

更夸张的是整个项目没有任何外部音频和图片资源文件。所有像素画都是纯代码生成的，构建时自动打包成图集。所有音乐和音效都是浏览器里实时合成的，用代码写了一个类似 Game Boy 的芯片合成器加上合成器浪潮层，连乐谱都是代码里的纯文本，切地图时还能保持上一段旋律无缝过渡。

为了保证能塞进 X 的推文卡片里直接跑，构建流程设了严格的体积红线，首包 gzip 之后只有 124 KB，超了构建直接报错。在中端手机上同屏 500 个敌人也能稳定跑满 60 帧，还支持 10 种语言本地化和动态生成结算分享图，连各个难度曲线都是让无头 Bot 自己跑模拟测试调出来的目标存活率。

用最硬核的形式化验证、零内存分配约束和确定性引擎，去写一个成本 5.99 美元域名的玩梗游戏。这大概就是顶级工程师用好 Coding Agent 之后最真实的日常状态：生成代码已经不稀奇了，怎么用编译器思维、lint 规则和自动化验证把 Agent 管得服服帖帖，才是真正拉开差距的地方。

text:
ZKsync Is Building the Next Institutional Rails for Ethereum

ZKsync’s October roundup highlights two developments that could strengthen Ethereum's long-term adoption: institutional infrastructure and ZK technology

1. Prividium Commander: Bringing institutions on-chain
Prividium helps banks and financial institutions manage digital assets, compliance, permissions, and private transactions without rebuilding their existing infrastructure.

This is important because institutions need privacy and regulatory controls before moving sensitive financial operations on-chain. Prividium aims to provide that while retaining Ethereum's security and settlement benefits.

2. Airbender Prime: Making Ethereum proving faster
Airbender demonstrated the ability to prove around 99% of 7,200 consecutive Ethereum blocks in under 10 seconds each using a single GPU.

In simple terms, it makes verifying Ethereum transactions faster and more efficient, bringing ZK technology closer to real-time performance.

Why does this matter for Ethereum?
• Institutional adoption: More banks and financial institutions can bring assets and financial operations on-chain.

• Better scalability: Faster and cheaper ZK proofs make Ethereum's long-term scaling roadmap more practical.

• More ecosystem activity: Institutional applications can attract new capital, liquidity, and developers into Ethereum.

By combining institutional-grade privacy with Ethereum security, ZKsync is helping build the infrastructure that could bring traditional finance on-chain.

yetone 这套 Magpie 运维看着朴素，总结下来的方法如下：Claude Code + 官方 Opus，并行三条 /loop——一条盯 GitHub issue/PR 和 Discord（PR 要拉下来真跑才合），一条盯 X 反馈（前面用便宜模型 Jev 先拦一刀省 Token），一条定时清屎山、写教训、拉黑低质提交。人晚上只铲 UI/UX。

三端真机复现（mac + Win + Win 里 Linux VM，Agent 只装一端，跨机走 ssh）；决策靠 Claude Code 记忆 + 仓里设计文档；对外操作全是 browser use；有人问 /loop 比 scheduled task 有啥优势，他直接说「没有优势，能监听就行」。

我这边也在用 Magpie 给 Claude 做本机路由。越看越觉得 OPC 先把「什么算做完」写清楚，再给 agent 一本会升级的错题本，比再堆一层编排管用。

对比：理念类似，不是同一套方法。 都是「事件驱动、先过滤、少打扰人、持续盯仓」；yetone 是 Claude Code 上 3×/loop 手工作坊，DeepSeek SuperAgent 是 DSH 上产品化工单引擎的研究原型插件。

对照：

1. 连续运维：两边都不是一次性会话写码——yetone 整夜养 Magpie；SuperAgent 常驻盯 GitHub（可选飞书），panel 只推「待人工」。
2. 并行：yetone=3 条独立 /loop；DeepSeek=1 个 Router + 多 Worker Ticket（订阅可直通，不经 Router）。
3. 便宜过滤：yetone 用 Jev 拦 X；DeepSeek 用代码 Gate + 模型 Eval（长文称 Fast/Slow，Router 可用更轻模型）。
4. 记忆/错题：yetone 有 LESSONS.md→code-standards；SuperAgent 有 SQLite 工单账本 + 版本化 prompts，无公开错题本升级流水线。
5. 人机边界：两边都把人抬到验收/决策；DeepSeek 默认 observe、Mandate/白名单由宿主强制，yetone 更多靠提示词与人工习惯。
6. 产品角色：Magpie=网关；SuperAgent=Agent 插件本身。别和 Plugin Hub 上另一款 dsh-super-agent（preset 协议）搞混。

This is a really insightful take: Backpack @Backpack  isn't really a brokerage. It's a bank.

If stock trading is commission-free, where does the money come from? Not trading fees. It's the interest spread.

Idle USD gets automatically lent out to leveraged traders. Stocks, crypto, and dollars all share the same collateral pool. Every dollar is put to work.

That's why Backpack is willing to offer 6%+ yields on USD. It's not a free perk. They're literally paying to attract deposits. The more deposits they attract, the more they can earn from the spread.

Even with $100B in tokenized stocks, annual trading revenue would only be a few million dollars. Barely worth mentioning. But interest spread income could reach $400M a year.

When evaluating an exchange, don't just look at trading volume. Look at its balance sheet🫡.

全网Grok Bot教程越来越多了，新手到底该从哪里学起？

最近刷X，发现不少大佬都在分享Grok Bot的玩法，有人拿它做自动化，有人组建AI团队，还有人直接让Bot帮自己干活赚钱。

教程确实不少，但东一篇西一篇的，真想系统学起来，还挺费时间。

我把最近比较值得看的中文、英文和官方教程整理了一遍，从零基础到进阶都有，建议先收藏，省得以后到处找。

①中文教程，建议优先看这4个

1.铁柱AGI｜Grok Bot中文学习站
https://t.co/GvvZZWkGPe
一共25章，从创建第一个Bot，到Routines自动化、多Bot分工协作，还有路线图和现成模板。

新手不知道从哪开始，先看这个。

2.蓝哥AI｜24篇优质教程合集
https://t.co/lCVWSckODl

把X上的Grok Bot文章分成9个类别，不用自己满世界找教程，缺哪方面的知识直接翻。

3.西堂AI｜24篇精选教程
https://t.co/TSHpNNcXvQ

从91条教程中筛选出来的，还安排了学习顺序，适合想一步步进阶的朋友。

4.xilo｜零基础搭建自动化Agent团队
https://t.co/hfx7YgZteH

万字长文，从开通到多Bot协作都有，想让几个AI员工互相配合干活的，可以重点研究。

②英文教程，这套20课值得看看

5.Sawyer Merritt｜20课Grok Bot实战课程
https://t.co/d8GDTqJtX4

从基础对话、应用连接，到云电脑、Routines和多Bot协作都有，还带实际练习。

原帖：
https://t.co/sNoxI3G5Ho

③官方教程，这两个入口也别漏了

6.Grok Bot官方Guides
https://t.co/LZNBatqNnQ

建议先看Grok Bot 101，把基础功能跑通，再根据自己的工作需求研究其他玩法。

7.Matt Palmer｜Getting Started入门视频
https://t.co/3O038ZZgoN
不喜欢看长篇教程的，可以先从视频入手，跟着操作更直观。

最后说下我建议的学习顺序：

先看铁柱的中文教程，跑通第一个Bot；再结合官方Guides熟悉功能；想玩自动化、多Bot协作，就去研究Sawyer和xilo的内容。

其实还有个最简单的办法：直接问自己的Grok Bot，让它一步步教你操作。

我觉得学AI最容易犯的毛病就是教程收藏了一大堆，真正动手的次数却没几次。

与其花几天研究别人怎么玩，不如先给自己创建一个Bot，找件每天都要重复做的事情交给它。

等它真的帮你省下时间，你自然就知道下一步该学什么了。

text:
聯發科 TPU v9：押注 EMIB-T，沒有備案

聯發科把 TPU v9（Humufish）的封裝交給 Intel 的 EMIB-T。法說會上，管理層否認了台積電 CoWoS 備援的傳聞，Nomura 的Aaron和廣發的@sssjeffpu 今天的報告都這樣寫。

現在要看的已經不是用哪種封裝，而是能不能如期做出來。但瓶頸在哪，兩家看法不同。

Nomura：引述管理層，EMIB-T 良率「解決 2–3 個關鍵問題後會快速改善」。聯發科自建量產團隊，基板同時找台灣和日本供應商，v9 仍照計畫在 1Q28 量產。

廣發：EMIB 基板良率照進度，問題出在晶片本身。Core A 設計太複雜，連帶 Core B 和 I/O die 都要修改，tape-out 延到 2027 年 1 月，因此大幅下調 2028 年出貨顆數。

Morgan Stanley 補充：v9 的量高度取決於 EMIB-T 基板良率，估計 2028 年 EMIB-T 產能約每月 4–4.5 萬片，大多由 Humufish 吃掉。現在要改用 CoWoS 的話，重新 tape-out 約需一年。

時程沒有餘裕：v9 由聯發科獨拿，v10 則要和 Broadcom 分。每延後一季，就離分食更近一步。

接下來看三件事:
2027 年 1 月 Core A 能否如期 tape-out。
Intel 有沒有揭露 EMIB-T 的良率與產能。
第二家 ASIC 客户的進度，預計 2028 年貢獻營收。

以上都是管理層與券商的說法，非投資建議。
author: ryanwang
quoted_text:
$INTC 這次疲弱指引，跟 MTK 合作應該關係不大。兩邊雖然都碰到載板，但時間軸和產品線差很多。

雙方剛好同一天開 earnings call，可以直接交叉比對說法。
Intel 管理層把「滿足超高伺服器／AI CPU 需求」的阻力，講成三道門：

1Intel 3 的良率和生產週期還得再抓緊。
2EMIB 先進有機載板整個產業都缺，就算 Intel 3 晶圓產能在爬，封裝端也跟不上（載板產能雖然要 +40%，但大部分要到 2027 下半年才到位）。
3以色列廠事故拖累 Q4 10nm 伺服器出貨（一次性）。

指引偏弱的營收大頭，還是 PC／CCPG 在去庫存（記憶體漲價擠壓）；EMIB／載板解釋的是 DCAI／Xeon 賣不滿、供給被鎖住。

MTK講的美國 IDM，就是 Intel 未來的 ASIC 封裝。目前第二代 AI ASIC 還在開發、還沒有營收；跟美國 IDM（Intel）的封裝製程是第一優先。

MTK 現階段重心，是跟 IDM 加上日／台載板廠一起把封裝良率拉起來；信心很高，但沒給數字。目標是 2028 Q1 高量產。

跟 Intel 合作的部分 die 已經 tape-out，最大 die 略為延後，但還是在時程內，比較像 tape-out 後在衝良率的驗證階段，還沒到穩定量產。

所以這波大跌，不是聯發科專案進度的問題。Intel 官方沒點名聯發科，也沒有用 EMIB-T 外部客戶來解釋這次 guidance。

Satoshi released the Bitcoin Whitepaper 18 years ago today

And he believed bitcoin:native could be private

Most of you have never read the Bitcoin Whitepaper, so you wouldn't know this

He said: "privacy can still be maintained by breaking the flow of information in another place: by keeping public keys anonymous"

Think about it
Bitcoin actually started off fully private

Unless one publicly proclaimed they owned and operated a wallet, no one knew who was who

So how and why did that change?

> CEXs started requiring KYC
> Govt. regulations enforced KYC/AML policies
> Early on, it was hard to get bitcoin:native unless you mined it

Because most people were not mining Bitcoin, they had to buy it from the market

> OTC deals on forums
> Bitcoin ATMs in person
> Centralized Exchanges

Long story short: Bitcoin's price appreciation created massive demand and most of the market participants who wanted Bitcoin were willing to sacrifice privacy to own bitcoin:native  

You can still acquire bitcoin:native in a wallet privately and while the transactions will be publicly shared on the blockchain, no one will know it was you if you follow Satoshi's advice

Times have changed though and the onramp demand into crypto has made KYC a normal process in web3

Enter @Zcash, for those who want maximum privacy

zcash:native is not only a store of value, but bitcoin:native's private twin  with optionality at the privacy level

Privacy is not a narrative or a meta
Satoshi was preaching it in 2008

It has been the main theme of 2026 and it's only becoming more important with AI hacks, mass surveillance, and the digital age

A year ago today, zcash:native was $350
Now, the chart looks ready to go to $3,500

I think we are still very early, but it's nice to get a reminder that even Satoshi realized how important privacy was in 2008

text:
最近带 AI 高血压都要犯了，AI 在常规工作都没问题，但如果遇到瓶颈真的是能气死人。

监控项目进展的不错，但昨天在一个沙盒的写入权限上卡壳了，应该是一个 BUG ，然后就能看到 ChatGPT 和 Gork 的短板了，首先是 ChatGPT 就死活跳不过去这个问题，也找不到中转的方案，甚至都自动去给 OpenAI 汇报 Bug ，但就是卡住不动。

而 Gork 更傻，出现了严重的幻觉，在完全没有确定的情况下让 ChatGPT 去找不存在的菜单，被 ChatGPT 怼了以后开始认错，认错后不断的给 ChatGPT 穿小鞋，我真的就是气的要吐血了。

结果电脑开着一晚上，两个 AI 就在不停的循环，Token 是烧了不少，事是一件没做，结果还要等到我起床看到了，我来想办法，让 ChatGPT 重新开一个 Work 测试是否有写入权限，结果测试通过了，可以继续进行了。我真的是够了。

但这也说明了，如果不是两个 AI 配合工作，一定会有大量的潜在问题，最近配合工作以后，就能非常明显的看到单独 AI 工作的局限性。

text:
Kalshi 估值 400 亿美元之前，也曾是一份"看不出来"的 A 轮 Deck

Sequoia 的 Alfred Lin 刚公开了 Kalshi 当年拿去融 A 轮的完整 Deck。背景：Kalshi 刚宣布 G 轮，融资 10 亿美元，估值 400 亿美元，Sequoia 联合领投。

几个值得记下来的点：

1. 监管优先，从第一天开始
Kalshi 从一开始就走合规路线。今天大家觉得"交易事件结果"理所当然，但在 2018 年创立、2020 年 Sequoia 投资时，这还是一个不被看懂的新资产类别。

2. 曲棍球曲线真的画出来了，但过程比计划颠簸得多
Deck 里的增长预测，Kalshi 后来不仅做到还超过了。但 Tarek 自己说过：前五年感觉什么都不 work，直到某一刻突然全部跑通。

3. 融资不靠包装
Deck 里的创始人头像，就是一张很普通的"金融实习生"照片。Alfred 原话的意思是：每个了不起的人，都曾经很普通。

4. Sequoia 差点错过
因为一次沟通失误，他们差点完全错过这笔投资。8 年过去，Kalshi 依然是 Day 1。

我的看法：

做 Bagel、做预测市场和 AI 交易这一年，最有共鸣的是第 2 点。外面看到的是一条曲线，里面的人经历的是五年"没有任何东西 work"。

预测市场今天看起来是风口，但 Kalshi 是在没人相信的时候，先把最难、最慢的合规这件事做完。真正的护城河，往往是当时看起来最笨的那部分。

AI Agent 现在也在同一个阶段：所有人都在讲叙事，很少有人愿意先把底层的东西磨好。我们在做的事情也一样，先做内功，曲线会自己来。

还在"什么都不 work"阶段的创业者：Kalshi 也经历过。

text:
刚好刷到大山和吴说的两篇推文，一篇从 Crypto Fund 的角度讨论资金的大撤离，另一篇则讨论行业岗位的大收缩。

大概半年前，我就说过一个自己的体感：同样是熊市，但这一轮的凛冽程度，在我看来甚至超过了2018、2019年那一轮。

我的判断依据其实很简单。

2018、2019年的时候，尽管整个市场几乎没有赚钱效应，但我身边依然有不少人愿意拿着很低的薪水留在这个行业，也有一些老板愿意继续下注，不管是投资项目，还是自己组建团队。

但从今年开始，我明显感觉到，身边选择退圈或者躺平的人越来越多了。

赚钱效应消失、赚钱机会减少，肯定是最主要的原因。毕竟人性逐利，这没什么可讨论的。

但还有一个原因，是我和一些朋友交流后总结的，大家有个观点惊人一致：Web3可能已经被证伪了。过去那些宏大的叙事和愿景，喊了这么多年，始终没有真正落地，继续坚持似乎也看不到什么意义。

这种心态，可能是一些散户不太容易理解的。
一些人会认为，进币圈不就是为了赚钱吗？讨论个鸡毛的意义。

但对从业者而言，他们押注的不仅是资金，还有自己的时间和职业发展。

当然，我不是说从业者就更高尚，或者更委屈。而是大家都在寻找确定性，只不过想要的答案不太一样。

投资者想看到的是资产增值，而从业者除了收入，还希望看到一个行业能够持续、良性地发展。这样至少不用担心投入了几年时间，最后发现整个行业都没有未来，换个行业又得从头开始。

还有一个挺有意思的事。
我在大山那篇推文下面看到一条评论，大意是：现在连做CX的都看不上Web3了。

我会心一笑。

今年我自己在做一些乙方服务，出于业务需求，偶尔需要帮甲方项目对接渠道，所以接触过不少团队长。当然，我自己不参与他们后续的具体业务，基本只是做些渠道介绍。

有时候也会和这些人闲聊，反而能从另一个角度观察这个圈子。

所以，虽然不能一概而论，但这种现象确实存在，这群人本身不算币圈人，他们过去对币圈的依赖除了一些基建外，另外就是叙事层面和社会热度，简单来说就是，叙事要高级，方便他们占领用户心智，有社会热度，他们给人讲的时候对方要知道这个东西很火。现在这两个方面都被AI甩了十八条街。

其实产业链正在枯竭，我自己早就有所感受，也知道这是一个客观事实。

只是今天恰好同时看到这两篇推文，还是有点被触动到了。

至于为什么会走到今天这一步，我现在已经不太想归因，甚至懒得归因了。

毕竟走到今天，也是整个行业过去无数次选择共同塑造的结果。

我依然相信市场会自我调节。

毕竟，客观规律从来不以人的意志为转移。

text: I'm one of those (uninformed) foreigners who looked at what the business does and was "very wary" but i'm really open to change my mind
author: 0xGeeGee
quoted_text:
It's wild how misunderstood $SE still is, especially by people in Southeast Asia.

I get why foreign investors are wary. Most of them have never opened Shopee, played a Garena game or paid/banked with Monee. It’s certainly difficult to judge a business they’ve never touched.

Locals have no such excuse. We watch our parents, our friends and ourselves use Sea every single day. Shopee is the default place to buy almost anything. Yet very few people around me have ever thought to own the stock.

In my view, it's one of the most extraordinary businesses built anywhere in the past 20 years, and it gets almost no credit for it.

My take is that the primary reason is the stock chart. Anyone who bought near the 2021 peak watched the stock fall roughly 90%, and that memory has stuck. "Sea" became shorthand for a pandemic bubble.

However, if you separate the price from the business, I think it is a very clear story:

- Went from burning billions to being solidly profitable

- Defended and widened Shopee's lead across Southeast Asia despite TikTok Shop, Lazada and a long list of well-funded challengers

- Built a fast-growing Brazil business out of nothing

- Turned Monee into a real fintech, lending into an ecosystem it already knows better than any bank

- Kept Garena throwing off cash to fund all of it despite worries that Free Fire was a one-hit wonder

The stock has gotten crushed in the past year, but the business has never been stronger. 

Looking ahead, the runway is enormous. Ads and services are only beginning to lift take rates. Investments in logistics are paying off and can be seen in cost to serve. 

Monee is beginning to come into its own and is becoming less reliant on Shopee each month.

I don’t think a $1T valuation is an overstatement. Frankly, I think it’s more likely than not.

quoted_text:
𝗚𝗲𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗲. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝘄𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗶𝘁.
(The git moment for genomics)

This month The Bioinformatics Company unveils 𝗚𝗟𝟭-𝘀𝗲𝗾 — and the preprint behind it. One protocol that treats DNA, RNA and protein sequences the way git treats code: content-addressed, versioned, diffable, auditable.
Two layers. The separation is the point.

𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿 𝟭 — 𝗣𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗰 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲, 𝗼𝗻 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻

The 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗲 (𝗚𝗥𝗖𝗵𝟯𝟴) — every base, in full, in chain state on GenesisL1. Not a hash. Not a pointer. The sequence itself, in GL1-seq's native ~2-bit encoding, 4× denser than FASTA. One canonical sequence, verifiable by anyone: the main branch the world commits against.

Every other genome is a diff. A full human genome as a diff is 𝟭𝟬–𝟮𝟬 𝗠𝗕 — and thousands of genomes on chain become routine.

At launch: the 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗲 (𝗚𝗥𝗖𝗵𝟯𝟴) + 𝟭𝟮 𝗽𝗶𝗹𝗼𝘁 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀. Next: 𝟭,𝟬𝟬𝟬+ public genomes, then Swiss-Prot, RefSeq, UniRef50, IMGT/HLA and antibody repertoires.

Not theory. GenesisL1 already holds 𝟭𝗠+ PDB and AlphaFold structures in chain state (MolNFT). Sequences are next.

𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿 𝟮 — 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮, 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗲𝗻𝘃𝗶𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

Patient and participant genomes 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻. They remain in the institution's private, compliant environment — under its own governance, access controls and jurisdiction. The chain records only cryptographic commitments — a fingerprint, never the sequence. Provenance and change history, verifiable by anyone, with zero data leaving the institution.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀

🔹 𝗟𝗼𝘀𝘀𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗯𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 — bit-exact reconstruction from reference + commits. 100% fidelity.

🔹 >𝟰× 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿, >𝟰× 𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿 — touch the delta, never the full sequence.

🔹 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗶𝗻 — who, what, derived from what. Reproducibility becomes a property of the data.

🔹 𝗗𝗲𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 — identical results on-chain (EVM) and off-chain, in Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust and C++. No protocol upgrade required.

🔹 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 — one format, one interface. Agents branch, analyze and commit with full attribution; humans audit every step.

For biobanks, sequencing cores, national genome projects, pharma and regulators: one canonical reference everyone shares, plus a tamper-evident audit trail for private data — 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗲.

Preprint, benchmarks and code this month — follow for the release.

text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

quoted_text:
🇭🇰渣打银行、汇丰、OSL，香港稳定币市场的三条路径

香港稳定币市场，还有三家公司值得重点关注：渣打银行、汇丰和 OSL。

它们分别代表了三种不同的稳定币商业化路径：渣打系从企业和机构支付切入，汇丰从零售用户和日常消费切入，OSL 则试图借助美元稳定币，建立面向全球企业的支付与结算网络。

🔷 第一条路径，是渣打系的企业稳定币。

严格来说，发行港元稳定币 HKDAP 的并不是渣打银行本身，而是由渣打香港、HKT 和 Animoca Brands 共同成立的 Anchorpoint。渣打是其中的重要股东，并为 HKDAP 提供银行基础设施支持。

HKDAP 最初采取机构优先的路线，面向企业客户和专业投资者，重点探索跨境支付、企业资金管理、代币化基金认购与结算等场景。

2026 年 8 月，HKDAP 开始分阶段推出，渣打香港也成为其首家银行分销商。对于渣打而言，稳定币的价值不只是支付，而是利用 7×24 小时的链上结算能力，改善企业跨境资金流动和全球财资管理。

🔷 第二条路径，是汇丰的零售港元稳定币。

与渣打系从企业端切入不同，汇丰选择了自己最熟悉的零售金融市场。

2026 年 4 月，汇丰获得香港首批稳定币发行牌照之一，并于 10 月 23 日开始通过 PayMe 分阶段推出港元稳定币 RedCoin。

汇丰的优势在于现成的用户入口。PayMe 已经拥有超过 330 万用户，汇丰香港手机银行也拥有庞大的客户基础。用户未来可以通过熟悉的银行和支付 App，使用港元稳定币进行个人转账、商户付款，甚至认购代币化投资产品。

这条路径的核心，是把稳定币直接带入普通消费者的日常金融生活，让用户不必先成为 Crypto 用户，也能接触到链上支付。

🔷 第三条路径，是 OSL 的美元稳定币与全球支付网络。

与前两家主要围绕港元稳定币展开不同， @osldotcom  选择了美元稳定币 USDGO。

2026 年 2 月，OSL 宣布在旗下平台上线 USDGO。它是一种由美国 Anchorage Digital Bank 发行、由 OSL 担任品牌合作方和分销方的美元稳定币，采用 1:1 美元储备支持，面向企业资金管理、流动性管理和跨境支付结算等场景。

这意味着，OSL 并不只是想做一家数字资产交易平台，而是希望进一步成为连接稳定币、传统金融机构和全球企业支付需求的基础设施。

从港元稳定币 HKDAP，到汇丰的 RedCoin，再到美元稳定币 USDGO，三家公司选择了不同的切入点，也对应着不同的客户群体和商业模式。

一个从企业资金流动出发，一个从普通消费者出发，一个从全球美元支付和结算网络出发。

这三条路径究竟哪一种能够率先跑通商业模式？香港发行的港元稳定币能否真正进入日常支付和跨境贸易？而美元稳定币又会如何与香港本地的金融体系连接？

这些都是 @joezhoublack  希望在香港金融科技周现场进一步了解的问题。

okx wallet:https://t.co/86MJVBbgBR

Agent Wormhole is a security layer for AI Agents that can spend money.

The reason this project exists is that Agents can read configurations, token names, websites, payment information, and then use that information to make transfers or modify files. Attackers can hide malicious instructions inside these inputs, causing the Agent to send money to the wrong address, buy the wrong token, or even write malware into its own configuration and spread it further.

The product has three parts:

1. Local tool — wormhole-guard

Free to use. Installed on the computer to prevent Agents from maliciously modifying configurations.

2. Payment Guard — x402

Before signing a transaction, it verifies: “Is this money supposed to be sent to this address, and is this the correct amount?”

If the details do not match, the transaction cannot be signed.

3. Token Launch Scanner

$WORM is, in my opinion, one of the more interesting AI Agent Security projects to watch and research recently. What it is really trying to build is not a typical AI Meme, but security infrastructure for the AI Agent economy.

0x3ba500f1ababbcf0f0247d06d1c56fd7e6c4c09d 

AI Agents are already starting to have wallets, call tools, execute transactions, and make payments. The problem is shifting from “Can AI give the wrong answer?” to “Can AI send my money to the wrong place?” What WORM does is add a security layer between Agent → Decision → Signing/Execution.

It currently has three main components:

1. Agent Security
Using wormhole-guard to detect risks such as Prompt Injection, malicious configurations, MCP, and tool outputs.

2. Payment Security
Using x402 Payment Guard to check the recipient address, amount, Token, Chain, etc., ensuring that the transaction ultimately signed by the Agent matches the original Payment Quote.

3. Token Security
Scanning, hashing, and attesting Token Names, Symbols, Descriptions, Metadata, etc., to prevent Agents from executing incorrect actions after reading malicious Token information.

According to the official website, it currently has 640K+ scans, around $9.6K in buyback expenditure, and 37.4M WORM burned. This means it has already started to form:Agent Usage → Security Checks → Revenue → WORM Buyback → Burn → Supply ↓

This is also what I think is the biggest difference between WORM and a typical AI Meme: it already has a real product and a corresponding value-capture mechanism.

The core bet behind WORM’s current valuation is actually the Agentic Economy.

If AI Agents eventually start holding funds and performing large amounts of:Trading → Payment → DeFi → Token Purchase → API Payment

then security will become a necessity. The position WORM wants to capture is:Agent → WORM Security Layer → Payment / Trading / Tool / Token

If more Agents, MCPs, wallets, Launchpads, or payment protocols eventually integrate WORM by default, it could evolve from a security tool into the Middleware of the Agent Economy.

Another interesting part is its connection with Robinhood Chain + Tokenized Stocks. WORM currently uses Tokenized PLTR as its trading pair, compressing:AI Agent Security + AI Stock + RWA + Robinhood Chain

into a single Token. This is very easy for the Crypto market to understand and spread.

So WORM’s current Narrative Stack can be understood as:AI Agent → Agentic Commerce → Agent Security → Payment Security → Token Security → Robinhood Chain → AI/RWA → Revenue → Buyback/Burn

There are several catalysts I will be watching closely going forward:First, Agent integrations.
If Claude Code, Cursor, MCP, Trading Agents, etc. increasingly start calling WORM directly, that would be very important product validation.

Second, x402 payment growth.
If Agent payments begin to scale, WORM’s Payment Security will gain a direct use case.

Third, Launchpad integrations.
If Pons or other Launchpads directly use WORM for Token Scan/Attestation when launching tokens, WORM could evolve from a third-party tool into Launch Infrastructure.

Fourth, acceleration in Buyback/Burn.
Ultimately, it still comes back to:

Usage → Revenue → Buyback → Burn

If usage and buybacks grow together, the valuation logic can shift from a pure AI Narrative to Revenue Infrastructure.

Fifth, a real Agent Security incident.
If a major incident occurs in the future where AI Agents lose funds because of Prompt Injection or malicious tools, attention on the entire Agent Security sector could increase rapidly, and WORM would already be positioned within that narrative.

But the risks are also very clear.

The biggest risk is that Security Detection does not equal absolute security. The team’s own testing also shows that complex Prompt Mutation can reduce detection rates. Therefore, WORM should not simply be understood as “100% protection against hackers.”

The second risk is that revenue is still very early. Many of the tools are free, and the fee for each security check is very low, so it needs massive usage to generate meaningful revenue.

The third risk is that 642K scans does not equal 642K paid calls. What really needs to be watched is actual revenue and Buyback, rather than the number of scans alone.

The fourth risk is competition. AI models, wallets, trading platforms, and even MCP Frameworks could eventually build their own security layers. If native security functions become strong enough, WORM’s value as a middleware layer could be affected.

So for now, I would define WORM as:An early-stage project attempting to become the security middleware for the AI Agent economy.

The market is not really betting on whether the WORM Meme itself will continue to spread. It is betting on:

Will AI Agents actually start holding funds → Will Agent Security become a necessity → Can WORM become the default security layer called before Agents execute trades and payments?

If Agent Usage + Protocol Revenue + Buyback/Burn all grow together in the future, WORM’s valuation logic could gradually evolve from an AI Security Narrative into Revenue-generating Agent Security Infrastructure.

On the other hand, if usage and revenue fail to grow sustainably, then its current market cap is still primarily trading on the future expectations of AI Agent Security.

What's less visible is the much steeper rise in how AI is being used to write more secure software and defend at every layer.

Builders have always had a fundamental advantage against attackers because they have full access to source code and control over system design. 

We haven't always had the resources to fully take advantage of this asymmetry, but now with AI we do.

Everything we build can now be designed and pentested by the best security minds (models) in seconds -- for cents.

Not all teams have had the time to catch up yet, so we're not out of the woods as an industry. 

But as the best teams fully modernize how they ship, AI is also enabling an era of the most trusted software ever.  You don't see this in dramatized headlines yet, but it's a very good time to build.

text:
I actually hate holding a bunch of stables and earning NOTHING while I wait for my next trade.

@apyx_fi is tackling this by bringing preferred-share dividends and U.S. Treasury income onchain through $apyUSD and $aptUSD, so my stables can earn instead of sitting idle.

Here's a TL;DR on how those 2 products work ↓

1️⃣ How Apyx brings that income onchain

Apyx holds the underlying investments with custodians outside crypto, while smart contracts handle deposits and distribute income to token holders.

• $apyUSD earns from dividends paid by preferred shares like $STRC.
• $aptUSD earns income from U.S. Treasury bills and cash equivalents.

2️⃣ apyUSD

To get $apyUSD, you first need $apxUSD, Apyx’s non-yield-bearing token.

You deposit $apxUSD into an ERC-4626 vault and receive $apyUSD, which represents your share of the vault, fully permissionless with no KYC.

Apyx collects dividends from those underlying investments, converts them into $apxUSD, and routes them directly to end users.

The income is gradually released over time and added to the vault’s total value.

So your token balance stays the same, but each $apyUSD becomes redeemable for more $apxUSD as the income builds up.

3️⃣ apyUSD’s ROI

While looking into $apyUSD, I came across two figures:

• 30-day yield of 13.77%.
• 16.07% potential return

That second scenario also assumes $STRC recovers to its face value, known as par.

But this distinction is important because the dividends we just covered generate recurring income, while a recovery in the underlying shares adds another possible source of return.

What you could do is compare $apyUSD’s dividend yield with your other options and work out whether it makes sense for you without counting on $STRC’s price recovering.

4️⃣ aptUSD

$aptUSD aims for a 3.5% APY, using the bottom of the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate range as its benchmark.

As that benchmark changes, aptUSD’s target payout fluctuates too.

Underneath the hood, $alqUSD is the non-yield-bearing accounting asset designed to maintain a $1 value.

Apyx’s swap tool routes $USDC through $alqUSD into $aptUSD in one action, so you don’t need a separate staking or wrapping step to start earning.

Your $aptUSD balance stays the same while its exchange rate against $alqUSD rises as Treasury income accrues.

When you want to exit, the app routes it back through $alqUSD into $USDC.

For me, I like being able to earn without committing to an unlock period, which is a good segue into how withdrawals work for both products.

5️⃣ Withdrawals

$apyUSD has a 3-20-day redemption window, with fees declining from 3.5% to 0.1% as you wait longer to claim.

You stop earning during the cooldown as your shares are removed of the vault, and your $apxUSD is set aside until you can claim it.

$aptUSD has no lockup or cooldown and charges zero management, performance, staking, or unstaking fees. It's designed for money you want to keep available while earning passive income.

On top of that, Apyx provides a swap route back to $USDC, so you don’t have to go through $apyUSD’s cooldown process.

6️⃣ Transparency

Apyx uses @AccountableData to show the assets backing its tokens, alongside monthly reserve checks by Wolf & Company.

Its smart contracts have also undergone security reviews by @HalbornSecurity, @Quantstamp, @zellic_io and @Certora.

For me, I want to know where the yield comes from and how I can get my money back before putting my stables anywhere, so being able to check the reserves myself is a big plus.

I’ll be keeping an eye on both products, and you can take a look yourself here: https://t.co/ANvU3J2GwF

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

text:
Kalshi 估值 400 亿美元之前，也曾是一份"看不出来"的 A 轮 Deck

Sequoia 的 Alfred Lin 刚公开了 Kalshi 当年拿去融 A 轮的完整 Deck。背景：Kalshi 刚宣布 G 轮，融资 10 亿美元，估值 400 亿美元，Sequoia 联合领投。

几个值得记下来的点：

1. 监管优先，从第一天开始
Kalshi 从一开始就走合规路线。今天大家觉得"交易事件结果"理所当然，但在 2018 年创立、2020 年 Sequoia 投资时，这还是一个不被看懂的新资产类别。

2. 曲棍球曲线真的画出来了，但过程比计划颠簸得多
Deck 里的增长预测，Kalshi 后来不仅做到还超过了。但 Tarek 自己说过：前五年感觉什么都不 work，直到某一刻突然全部跑通。

3. 融资不靠包装
Deck 里的创始人头像，就是一张很普通的"金融实习生"照片。Alfred 原话的意思是：每个了不起的人，都曾经很普通。

4. Sequoia 差点错过
因为一次沟通失误，他们差点完全错过这笔投资。8 年过去，Kalshi 依然是 Day 1。

我的看法：

做 Bagel、做预测市场和 AI 交易这一年，最有共鸣的是第 2 点。外面看到的是一条曲线，里面的人经历的是五年"没有任何东西 work"。

预测市场今天看起来是风口，但 Kalshi 是在没人相信的时候，先把最难、最慢的合规这件事做完。真正的护城河，往往是当时看起来最笨的那部分。

AI Agent 现在也在同一个阶段：所有人都在讲叙事，很少有人愿意先把底层的东西磨好。我们在做的事情也一样，先做内功，曲线会自己来。

还在"什么都不 work"阶段的创业者：Kalshi 也经历过。

用户创建钱包时，通过量子计算机产生的随机数生成 Falcon 密钥。使用时，需要先把 SOL 存入 bb84 的智能合约金库。资金进入金库后，控制权由合约接管，每次提款都必须使用 Falcon 私钥签名。

Solana leads on speed, and now it's ready for the quantum era. Get a .quantum name like alice.quantum, a @metaplex Core NFT with its own embedded vault. Once activated, only your Falcon-512 key can spend from it.

Falcon-512 is a lattice-based signature scheme selected by NIST (FN-DSA), with no known quantum attack.

How it works:

• Your key starts with 1,024 bits measured on real quantum hardware (Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q via Amazon Braket), mixed with your browser's own randomness. Nobody else, bb84 included, can compute it.

• Your 897-byte public key is stored on-chain once. Each transaction carries a 666-byte signature, verified on-chain by our qpt program (~300k CU).
• Each Falcon signature covers exactly what you approve, works once, and expires in about a minute.
• IDs are composable: any Solana program can interact with them.

text:
In his first meeting with the Jedi Council, Anakin is asked if his "thoughts dwell with his mother." To this, Anakin responds, "I miss her." Keep in mind Anakin is a child who has just been separated from his mother for presumably the first time and is now on an entirely different planet. He expresses one of the most basic and human emotions a boy could express in that moment.

Within 30 seconds, Yoda is telling him he is full of fear and on the path to the Dark Side.

Fast forward to Episode 2. Anakin wants to save his mother from slavery after promising her in Episode 1 as a little boy he would come back and free her. It would be very easy to do. He's served and learned under the Jedi for 10 years, and despite his hotheadedness and youthful mistakes, he remains loyal.

What do the Jedi do? They let his mother die at the hands of alien savages. He has to witness her dying moments.

Yeah, but sure, Anakin is weak.

Oh yeah, and how did Luke wreck Vader btw? Vader threatened to turn Leia to the Dark Side which enrages Luke. Luke defeats Vader in a fit of pure, unadulterated, white hot rage. There's no stoic virtuee in Luke during the final seconds of his duel with Vader. It's the most belligerent and furious we ever see Luke across all three movies.

Finally, you cannot call Anakin weak and claim to understand the story. Anakin is true identity: it's the boy who loves his mother, the young man who fell in love with Padme, the student who trained under Obi Wan, the prodigy pod racer, the Chosen One. That identity was destroyed by the very order that he fought for and was loyal to until it broke him for their corrupt purposes.

The Boomer Jedi view of the world will die and we are going to win.

quoted_text:
I had a great chat with my friend @jacalulu (PM Director at Google Labs) about how Gemini 4 changed how Google builds products and how parents can get kids to explore AI.

Some takes I loved:

1. “It shouldn’t take someone longer to read your doc than it took you to write it.”

Writing is thinking. AI can be a thought partner, but you should firmly be in the driver’s seat.

2. “It’s no longer about can you build it, it’s about should it even exist?”

Code went from a scarce asset to basically free. If you can “throw a couple of agents at it over a weekend,” it’s probably not a durable product. So the hard part now is deciding what’s worth building in the first place.

3. “Why do you even want a person in your product?”

Agents do more of our work every month, so you should ask if your product needs a UI at all. Jaclyn thinks people will still show up to create, learn, or be entertained. Any task that feels like a chore should be built for agents first.

4. “Don’t just give users exactly what they want.”

Talk to them all the time, but find the root problem and solve it in a way they wouldn’t have thought of. You want them to walk away thinking, “I didn’t think this was possible, but it’s exactly what I wanted.”

5. “You shouldn’t expect users to know how to write elaborate prompts.”

Small business owners don’t have time to start from an empty prompt box. So her team built Pomelli, Google’s tool for SMBs to create on-brand content, to read your website and learn your business first.

6. “Let your kid be your creative director.”

Jaclyn’s 5-year-old loves scary stories, so they made their own podcast, Maya and the Fog. Her daughter picks the voices, names the characters, and gives notes on each cut, and Jaclyn has the agent produce the episode. It’s live on Spotify.
