text:
AI交易真能赚钱吗? 我用100 美金让 AI 帮我冲 10倍收益率的首周记录:

先回答问题: 能赚，但赚钱的那一下是我判断的方向，AI 负责执行。

我拿 100 美金，让 @MojoAI_HQ 挑战"只交易美股，最快冲到 1000"，跑了一周。

✅ 执行层，它真的行：一句话就能下单
⚠️ 决策层，还得靠人

最有意思的是，它复盘自己一笔失败的单子时说了一句话，比赚的那 40% 更值钱：

"先问这笔交易在现价上成不成立，再谈挂单价能不能优化。"

赚到的和卡住的，都摊开讲。

1. 一句话就能执行，和币安 AI 完全两种性格

我说一句"把现货卖了转去合约"，它直接卖出 ETH、POL，再划转到合约账户，全程不用我动手。

同一个 prompt 我也拿去问了币安 AI。它先警告：10 倍目标意味着清算风险优先于收益，然后明确拒绝给方向、杠杆和点位。

币安 AI @binance  是稳妥的助手，Mojo 是直接上手的交易员。

【配图：X1（图 1 + 图 2）】

2. 它给的第一张策略卡

用了 91 秒、23 个步骤，选了 NVDA。理由是：连跌 5 天（跌 6.1%），触及 30 日低点，本周没有财报，不容易被单一事件打穿。

策略是双向突破：升破 211 做多，跌破 201 做空，10 倍杠杆。

有两个细节我挺喜欢：
· 它发现我账户里还挂着两笔加密货币空单，和"只做美股"冲突，会主动提醒
· 但它不会擅自撤单，等我拍板

推理过程能看到它拉了哪些 K 线，方便复盘。不过这只是推理步骤，不等于经过统计验证的依据。

【配图：X2（图 3 - 图 5）】

3, 赚到的那笔：+40%，AI 负责执行，方向是我定的

SK 海力士财报当天，海力士和美光两笔合约合计赚了 40% 以上（按保证金计算，含杠杆）。

这笔是这样分工的：我根据财报判断方向，告诉它往哪边做；它负责算点位、挂单、设止盈止损，执行得很干净。

这也是一周下来最清楚的分工：遇到财报、宏观数据这类事件，它不会自己调整预期；但只要方向给对，它执行比我手动快得多。

【配图：海力士和美光的成交记录（打码账户信息）】

4, 卡住的那笔：AI 给我挂了一张 2.4:1 的漂亮单子，11 小时没成交 ⚠️

SOL 做空，它把限价单挂在 98.20，盈亏比 2.4:1，看起来很完美。

但我算了一下：如果按当时的市价 95.95 进场，同样的止损和止盈，盈亏比只有 0.8:1，这笔根本不该做。

所以那个 2.4:1 不是市场给的，是挂单价"凑"出来的。

结果：11 小时，价格一次都没碰到 98.20，反而跌到 95.39。

方向对了，一分钱没赚到，80 美金保证金白白占了 11 小时。

它复盘时自己承认：

"那个漂亮的 2.4:1 是挂单价虚构出来的，不是市场给的。"

目标越激进，AI 越容易为了凑盈亏比，把单子挂到市场根本去不了的价位。

【配图：SOL_价格档位图】

还有两点

· 参数稳定：同一条对话里迭代了两版 NVDA 策略，止盈 222 和 225，止损 205 和 204，基本一致。不过稳定不等于正确，下周我开新对话再验证一次。

· 链上监控只停在"监控"：它会推送 ETH 大额转账，但不解释意味着什么。对不常看链上数据的人来说，看到信号离做出决策还差一步。

一周结论

AI 交易工具最大的价值，目前不是帮你赚钱，而是帮你把想法变成可执行、可复盘的单子，顺便暴露你的想法哪里不靠谱。

下周会测加密货币合约、链上现货，以及资讯和排行榜功能。

这个系列我会一直更新：一边拆解 AI 交易产品，一边记录自己学交易的过程。

你会让 AI 帮你下单吗？还是只敢让它给建议？

text:
Gemini 4 已经改变了 Google 构建产品的方式。

Peter Yang 与 Google Labs 产品总监 Jaclyn Konzelmann 聊完后，总结了 6 个值得产品人思考的观点：

1. 用户读文档的时间，不该比你写它的时间更长。AI 可以辅助思考，但人必须掌握方向盘。

2. 现在的问题不再是“能不能做”，而是“该不该存在”。代码正在变得廉价，真正稀缺的是判断力。

3. 产品真的需要人来操作吗？创造、学习和娱乐仍需要界面；凡是像杂务的任务，都应该优先为 Agent 设计。

4. 不要只照着用户说的做。理解他们的根本问题，再交付一种连用户自己都没想到的解法。

5. 不要指望用户会写复杂提示词。Google 的 Pomelli 会先读取企业网站、理解品牌，再帮助小企业生成内容。

6. 让孩子担任“创意总监”。Jaclyn 让 5 岁的女儿决定播客的角色、声音和剧情，再由 Agent 完成制作。

AI 降低了执行成本，也让产品判断、用户洞察和创造力变得更重要。

text:
DeepSeek Harness 团队今天发了一篇讲 Super-agent 架构的长文，是我最近读到最有条理的 Agent 系统设计文章。

它几乎不谈模型多强，讲的是模型够强之后，系统该怎么搭。而且全文借用的都是计算机系统里的老办法：快慢路径、缓存、推测执行、计算存储分离、看门狗。

小路把全文读完了，想带您顺着作者的思路走一遍。文末的配图是我对全文的整理。

先说问题。现在的 Agent 以单个 session 为工作单位，session 之间互相隔离。同时跑几个任务，人就得手动在 session 之间切换，还要记住每个里面有什么。作者的经验是，一个人同时能跟住的活跃 session 大约 3 到 5 个。单个任务受限于模型能力，多任务则受限于人的注意力。

作者给出的解法叫 Super-agent：一个持续在线的 Agent，跨 session 保持上下文，同时处理多个复杂任务，任务之间互不干扰。他们认为它要有四个特性：Continuous（连续）、Productive（高产）、Proactive（主动）、Persistent（常驻）。

整篇文章的骨架可以压成一条链：

两层架构 -> 事件驱动 -> 全双工多渠道 -> 计算/状态/环境分离 -> Watchdog （Router 和 Worker 分工 -> 环境事件当输入 -> 长任务不堵对话 -> 云端常驻 -> 外部看门狗）

下面一块一块看。

两层架构。 只用一个 session，上下文最连贯，但一步一步跑，吞吐上不去，不同任务的中间过程还会混在一起。每个事件开一个新 session，吞吐有了，任务之间又断了联系。作者的办法是拆成两层。Router 是长期存活的全局层，负责和人对话、分派任务，自己不执行任务，甚至可以没有 Bash 工具。Worker 是执行层，每个 Worker 只做一个任务，有独立上下文和完整工具。Worker 不直接和人说话，进度统一报给 Router，由 Router 回复用户。作者说，Router 的活比想象的简单，小而快的模型通常就够，Worker 才需要最强的模型。

事件驱动。 Agent 的主要输入不再是人敲的 prompt，而是环境里的事件，比如群消息、邮件、日历提醒、代码评审评论、CI 结果。论文里把这些叫 Trigger。真实的群聊里绝大多数消息不需要 Agent 动手，所以先过两道筛：第一道是代码里的确定性规则（来源、群、白名单），第二道才交给大模型判断要不要处理。同一个 PR 或同一个聊天话题里连续的事件叫一个 Thread。Router 给 Thread 创建 Worker 之后，Worker 订阅这个 Thread，后续事件由代码直接送到 Worker，不再经过 Router。
上下文当缓存用。 作者把有限的上下文窗口看成缓存，有两个操作。Inline 是把马上会用到的信息直接放进窗口，Spill 是把放不下的留在窗口外，只留一个引用。每个对象都带着相关对象的 ID，模型可以顺着 ID 一跳一跳往外找，论文称之为 Chain of Recall。比如从当前消息的 Thread，找到相关的 Worker，再找到另一个 PR 的评审 Thread。

提前动手。 借用了推测执行的思路。他们内部用户群里配了一条"静默复现并修复"的策略：有人报问题，Agent 先在后台试着复现、找修法，确认了问题并且修法简单，才出来交付结果，否则全程不出声。

全双工。 经典的 ReAct 循环里，同步调用工具时整个 session 都在等。作者把耗时的调用换成异步的 start() 和 stop()，start() 立刻返回"Started"，工具跑完再以新消息的形式把结果送回来。这样人在测试还在跑的时候，就可以继续发下一条指令。文中说明，DeepSeek Harness 已经实现了这个机制，但还没有默认开启。

不同渠道不同说法。 IM 里尽量少打扰，只在需要决策或签字时才找人，他们验证过的一条硬规则是每条回复不超过 100 个字。GitHub 和邮件这类异步渠道则要信息密集，写 PR 时把问题背景、改动和验证结果写全。
计算、状态、环境三者分离。 本地 Agent 通常把这三样绑在一台设备上，电脑一休眠，Agent 就停了。作者先把 Agent Loop 放进无状态的云端容器，会话状态存数据库，所以本地设备离线也不影响 Agent。再往下一步，环境本身（未提交的改动、私有凭证、内网依赖）很难同步到云端，那就不搬，让每台设备只跑一个轻量 daemon，负责执行命令、返回结果。他们称之为 BYOM（Bring Your Own Machine）。设备断线后重新连上，云端 Agent 会自动把需要在这台设备上跑的任务补上。

Watchdog。 长期运行的 Agent 系统，很多故障不是崩溃，而是进程还活着，模型却陷进了没有进展的循环，或者偏离了目标。所以需要一个独立的 Watchdog session，由定时消息驱动，既处理 API 报错、状态恢复失败这类基础设施故障，也用模型判断每个 Worker 有没有实质进展。因为它本身就是带完整工具的 Agent，维护者还可以直接用自然语言问它为什么失败。

再看实验。作者强调这是初步实验，用的是合成负载和简化环境，结果只作参考。设置是：约 300 条群聊和 GitHub CI 消息，其中约 20 条是真正的工作请求，编码工作用一个只消耗时间的工具模拟，每种设计跑 5 次。

完成时间。 Super-agent 的任务完成时间 p50 是 12.4 分钟，p95 是 15.7 分钟。单 session 加 subagent 工具，用中性提示词时是 20.4 和 29.5 分钟，而且 5 次里模型一次都没有调用 subagent，活全在主 session 里干，不断被新消息打断。换成"优先交给 subagent"的提示词，是 13.8 和 29.0 分钟，5 次里有 1 次模型觉得活"小"，自己干了，拉出一条长尾。作者的解读是，单 session 要靠提示词和模型当场的判断来决定要不要分派，两层架构则把这个问题放到系统层解决。

代价。 Super-agent 每次运行的 cache-read token 是 23.2M，单 session 方案是 6.1M 到 10.8M。用更多 token 换更短更稳的完成时间。

透传。 去掉订阅透传，完成时间几乎没变（12.6 和 15.5 分钟），但 Router 的决策次数多了约 30%，cache-read token 从 23.2M 升到 31.8M，多了约 37%。所以透传的价值是减轻 Router 的负担，而不是让任务更快。

Router 批处理。 Router 单独压测，Trigger 到达速率从每分钟约 1 条升到约 40 条，平均批大小从 1.0 升到 2.8，每次请求的时间只从 2.5 秒增加到 3.9 秒，摊到每个决策上的推理时间从 6.4 秒降到 1.6 秒。原因是排队的 Trigger 会被合并进下一次调用，在 Prefill 阶段并行计算。结论是，以他们现在的团队规模，不需要急着拆分 Router。

作者自己列出的开放问题也值得看。

长期记忆。 Router 加 Chain of Recall 能覆盖近期的任务，系统跑上几个月之后，长期记忆会成为主要瓶颈。
Router 什么时候拆、拆多细。 拆得越细吞吐越高，共享的上下文就越少，这个取舍目前还没有定论。

安全。 云端 Agent Loop 不断接收外部事件，终端设备上又有私有代码和本地凭证。一旦 Agent Loop 被入侵或被提示词注入，所有连着的设备都可能被接管。凭证即使云端没被攻破，只要能进模型上下文，也可能泄露。作者的想法是，Agent 需要一种用凭证但看不到凭证的办法。

我读下来最有感觉的是 Router 那一层。我们平时和 Agent 合作，总想着把最强的模型放在最中心的位置。但这篇文章里，中心位置的活是接话、分派、记账，不碰执行，反而可以用小模型。真正吃力的活放到边上，一个任务一个 Worker。

简单总结一下就是，作者认为多任务 Agent 的瓶颈是人的注意力，所以让 Router 负责连续，让 Worker 负责并行，让 Trigger 把 Agent 从等指令变成看环境，再用云端状态加外部 Watchdog 保证它一直在线。实验显示，在他们的模拟负载下，这套设计把 p95 完成时间压到了 15.7 分钟，代价是 2 到 4 倍的 token。长期记忆、Router 拆分和安全，作者说都还没解决。

text:
币安到底是多想搞死hyperliquid？

这 16 个钱包的资金，来自 4 个不同的 USDC 转账源头（在 Arbitrum 链上）。虽然互相不直接转账，但动作极其一致。

它们在同一时间段（凌晨 3:45 - 4:28）进行小额提现测试，使用完全相同的 TWAP（分批买入）指令，甚至连邀请码（referral code）都填的一模一样。

它们总共开了价值 2300 万美元的 XPL 多单（这几乎等于那几天 XPL 全网多单增加的总和），并且故意把单个钱包的仓位控制在 237 万美元以下（为了卡住 10 倍杠杆的线）。

在暴跌前 8 分钟内，12 个钱包疯狂撤出保证金（总计 203 万美元），把账户余额精准抽干到只剩 10% 的清算警戒线边缘。（有 7 次提现还被拒绝了，说明它们是在疯狂试探系统的底线）。

是谁砸的盘？Hyperliquid 背锅了。

这些钱包撤完保证金后，XPL 瞬间暴跌 18%。

但是，调查发现：砸盘的凶手大概率不在 Hyperliquid，而在币安。

在 Hyperliquid 发生第一笔清算前，币安上的 XPL 已经跌了 6%。币安一分钟内砸出了 4900 万 XPL 的卖单。Hyperliquid 只是“跟随”了币安的价格。

这就非常像“跨所狙击”：有人在币安砸盘引发恐慌，导致 Hyperliquid 上的价格跟跌。

而这 16 个撤了保证金的多单，因为距离爆仓线只有一步之遥，瞬间被触发清算。

当这 16 个钱包爆仓时，没人接盘。Hyperliquid 的清算金库（HLP）被迫以高于市场价的价格（溢价 108 个基点）接过了 1.6 亿枚 XPL 的多头仓位，并在随后 75 分钟里割肉卖出，亏损了 55.5 万美元。（这占 HLP 总资金的 0.33%）。

凶手赚了吗？没赚。 

调查报告显示，这 16 个钱包在 Hyperliquid 上总共投入 321 万美元，最后只拿回 233 万，净亏损 71.1 万美元。

它们为什么要干这种“损人不利己”的事？

报告推测，它们可能在其他地方（比如币安）开了空单对冲，或者因为某种原因急需抽走流动性。

它们在 Hyperliquid 上亏的钱，可能只是“作案成本”。

意外的是：第一次用 Codex 跑 GPT 时，它自动读了我项目里的规则文件（AGENTS.md），给的建议具体到我在做的业务；去掉规则文件重跑，就变回了谁都适用的清单。

不一样的地方：

但斌转发了一条很震撼的新闻：挪威主权基金，1996年起步的时候，只注入了大约3亿美元，三十年过去，现在规模做到了2.3万亿美元。
 
它最厉害的一点，绝大部分增量并不是持续往里投石油卖出来的钱，靠的是投资收益，堪称复利的教科书案例。
现在这只基金，平均持有全球每家上市公司1.5%的股份。
 
它还有一条硬核制度：政府每年最多只能提取3%，只花投资赚来的收益，本金不动。这笔钱，能撑起挪威四分之一以上的国家预算。
 
从增长拆分图能看得很清楚，规模分成三块：新增投入、投资收益、汇率变动。真正撑起庞大体量的，是长年累月的投资回报。
 
沙特也有一支主权基金，同样做得很好。这种财富机制最大的好处，就是能稳稳托住普通老百姓的民生保障。

text:
solana:EJAxERvKU4kEVXn3NarjvRtgaMaJyP9ZuMeKA7JJpump: Ogle's Involvement Is Bringing Attention to What the Project Is Actually Building

EJAxERvKU4kEVXn3NarjvRtgaMaJyP9ZuMeKA7JJpump 

I believe Ogle's involvement has given CHOO a major new source of exposure while making the market take a closer look at the project's underlying value.

I won't go into the token's narrative in detail here. You can check my quoted post for that. Instead, I want to focus on something more important: although Ogle's appointment is clearly the immediate catalyst, what makes this interesting is what he's bringing attention to — a pet healthcare brand built around a real rescue dog, and an economic model attempting to connect real consumer spending with token burns.

Let's start with Ogle.

Besides serving as an advisor to WLFI and Americafun, he was also an early supporter of PONS. That PONS connection naturally makes the market pay closer attention to his decision. People are wondering whether he has found another project worth getting involved in early.

I also had a brief interaction with Ogle during my time around PONS, so his involvement caught my attention.

But what I find more interesting this time isn't his previous affiliations. It's why he chose CHOO.

In his public explanation, Ogle gave several reasons. He loves animals and believes in helping them live longer, healthier lives. He has spoken with the founder and followed his posts for some time, and believes he's genuinely committed to making the project work. He also has experience with the pet industry through a friend who founded Petflow, and sees significant commercial potential in this market.

More importantly, he likes the idea of consumers being able to purchase products directly with CHOO. He also shared that both of his animals passed away last year, making pet healthcare something he personally cares deeply about.

I think these last points matter.

Rather than simply announcing an advisory position, Ogle explained why he wanted to get involved and explicitly stated that he plans to continue accumulating CHOO over time.

For an early-stage project, having someone with relevant industry experience and an established presence in crypto publicly commit to supporting the project can meaningfully change how the market initially perceives it.

His involvement brings more than attention. It also introduces credibility and the possibility of future resources.

However, if CHOO doesn't have anything substantial behind it, the impact of an advisor announcement will eventually fade. That's why I think the more interesting part of this project is Pawgen.

CHOO isn't built around an entirely fictional animal meme. Its central character is Choo Choo, a real 14-year-old rescue dog.

Choo Choo was adopted at the age of nine. At the time, it weighed 102 pounds and had several health issues, including a heart murmur, thyroid problems, and high blood pressure. Founder Michael Morelli gradually built Pawgen around Choo Choo's health management and recovery journey.

This gives CHOO something that many ordinary animal memes don't have: a real story behind the character and an ongoing source of content.

But what interests me more than Choo Choo itself is whether Pawgen can actually grow into a sustainable business.

Pawgen has already launched K9-REPAIR, a product focused on pet health and recovery. It's also developing PawScript, at-home testing, PawScore, and other services.

If these plans materialize, Pawgen could eventually expand beyond selling a single product into testing, health assessments, and ongoing pet healthcare management.

This is the commercial opportunity I believe Ogle sees.

In his announcement, he mentioned that a friend who founded Petflow generated more than $50M in annual revenue. He believes the pet healthcare niche Choo is entering could be even larger and potentially more profitable.

That's his assessment of the market, not revenue already generated by Pawgen. But it shows that he's looking beyond the token itself and evaluating the potential of the underlying consumer business.

There's an important difference between pet healthcare and an ordinary meme market: consumers don't necessarily purchase products because of market sentiment. They purchase them because they have real needs.

Pet owners are willing to spend time and money on their animals. If a brand can establish trust, develop effective products, and generate repeat purchases, it has the potential to build a more sustainable business than one relying entirely on short-lived meme attention.

Coming back to CHOO, its connection to Pawgen's consumer business is another important part of the thesis.

According to the official mechanism, users can purchase Pawgen products with CHOO and receive a 10% discount. The CHOO used for payment is then sent to the Solana Incinerator address for permanent burning.

This creates a demand path that is different from that of an ordinary meme coin: consumers purchase products using the token, and the tokens used for payment are burned.

If Pawgen's product sales grow and more consumers choose to pay with CHOO, real consumer spending could translate into recurring token purchases and burns.

The project has also introduced an animal rescue component. According to the official disclosures, 1% of each CHOO transaction goes toward a rescue fund. Separately, Pawgen plans to allocate 1% of product sales revenue to support its own dog rescue initiatives.

These are two different funding sources, but together they reinforce the brand's identity around pet healthcare, animal rescue, and the Choo Choo community.

I think this combination is what makes the project interesting.

The real rescue dog provides the story and content. Pawgen provides the products and consumer use cases. CHOO attempts to connect that commercial activity to token demand through its payment-and-burn mechanism.

At least in terms of its design, this is more than just an animal meme relying on cute pictures to attract attention.

What I want to monitor next is the percentage of product orders paid for with CHOO and how many tokens are actually burned through real product purchases each month.

If Pawgen eventually launches PawScript and its pet health testing services, expanding from individual products into long-term healthcare management, the potential consumer use cases could become much broader.

At that point, CHOO's story could evolve from being centered around one rescue dog into something connected to the wider pet healthcare market.

My current view is that Ogle's involvement has opened a window for the market to reconsider CHOO, but what makes me want to keep following the project is Pawgen's potential to turn that attention into real consumer demand.

Ordinary animal memes need to constantly generate new viral moments to maintain attention. CHOO, however, has an opportunity to build a different growth model through Pawgen's products and pet healthcare services.

I'm not saying CHOO is guaranteed to succeed simply because Ogle has joined. But I do think his appointment has brought attention to a business model that deserves more serious consideration than the market might initially have given it.

What matters most going forward isn't how many more traders Ogle can attract. It's how many pet owners actually purchase Pawgen products, and how many of them are willing to use CHOO to pay.

A project can gain attention and rally because an influential person gets involved. But only when real customers continue paying for its products can that attention have a chance of turning into lasting value.

text:
wildwood is a true marvel of human artistry, craftsmanship, and storytelling. i honestly found it even better than You Can See Everything (gasp!).

[spoilers if you read on]

an interesting trend in both wildwood and hoppers is how they handle death. they’re both movies for young people that treat death as inevitable and natural, and both expose the audience to a surprising amount of it. this feels quite different from the cleaner moral universes of much of modern disney and pixar.

both movies also have strong themes of non-intervention. of course, this is environmentally motivated, but there’s a broader Buddhist / Taoist morality running through both films: the world has a natural balance, and our attempts to impose our own ideas of goodness upon it can be destructive.

this feels quite different from the more Christian-inflected morality of overcoming evil. in these films, nature isn’t inherently good or evil, and trying to eliminate everything we perceive as bad can itself be the source of harm.

i wonder if this reflects a broader generational shift toward stories where it’s increasingly difficult to know what’s “right” or “wrong”, and where good intentions aren’t enough to make an action good.

both films feel like spiritual siblings to princess mononoke, questioning the hubris of humans who believe they can impose their will on the natural world.

wildwood is also visually spectacular and a complete and utter artistic achievement. it is always so rewarding to see fresh new takes on what a movie can be and how stories can be told.

huge fan, go see it!

text:
Published on Terence Tao’s blog: Mathematics has changed. Let’s act like it.

this is a guest post by Frank Calegari, saying mathematicians need to stop treating AI as existential threat and start rethinking what makes a good mathematician.

“Choosing worthwhile problems may end up mattering more than producing proofs.”

his suggestion for the way forward:
> evaluate all math work as if AI-generated 
> math hiring should be based on vision and understanding rather than number of papers
> fewer but better papers need to be published
> train mathematicians to explore more ambitious problems

in a section named “the ugly truth” he writes how some mathematicians are rushing to publish AI papers without developing a deeper understanding of math: “there is quickly becoming a gulf between the ability to produce novel proofs and the ability to either demonstrate understanding or push the subject in new and interesting directions.”

he’s critical of OpenAI’s recent papers but the overall message is actually optimistic:
AI could free mathematicians from spending years to prove individual conjectures and let them explore problems that were previously out of reach. 

this is the way to go.

text:
我自己最后的看板 UI 选的是这位老哥的作品。

我的做法很简单：直接丢给 Claude Code 让它去分析，做成组件再拿来用。

当然，你需要严格遵守一下开发流程，比如：

底层是你确定的前端框架，上面一层是基于 Base UI，然后再上面一层是 shadcn UI，最上面一层就是你自己自定义的设计规范和组件。

你需要把这个 shadcn UI 改成你自己的设计风格。那这一步，我强烈建议你丢一个参考案例给这个 agent，尤其是 Claude，不要自己发挥。语言是贫瘠的，尤其是我们本来就是没什么审美的人，对吧？一个没有审美的人你去指导一个 agent，不是外行指导内行吗？对不对？

最后一步是要约束 Agent 的那颗躁动之心。

我非常不建议你绕过 design 模式，尤其是 CC 上的。它会生成一个 canvas，你可以理解成 Figma 的画板一样，我要求它生成几乎所有页面的设计稿。

因为我发现它如果不生成设计稿，直接跳过这个过程去开发原型的话，开发出来的交互会让我更为匪夷所思。这可能是我没跟它交代清楚，但如果真要交代得那么清楚，有这个力气，我为什么不直接让它生成画布呢。

这也是为什么我特别喜欢 Twitter 上面的设计师，就是因为这些资源直接就能拿来用

Hate to break it to you, but the global hardware shortage has not even started yet.

Right now, only 1% of humanity is burning any real amount of AI tokens. The rest are just using free accounts once in a while to ask dumb questions like "Who would win in a fight between a baby seal and 300 hamsters?"

And like Elon said, most RAM will not even go into data centers. It will go into Physical AI, which is robotics.

That is because robotics is the only thing that can actually boost human productivity in a real way.

People on X freak out every time AI solves a hard math problem, while people in the real world just go on with their lives like nothing happened. Meanwhile, robotics is already taking over factories and changing the physical world.

Imagine when these robots start replacing our daily chores. How much more RAM and compute will we need then?

Like I have said many times, building a new fab to make RAM takes at least 5 years, and supply is already fully booked out until 2029.

Even if the so-called AI bubble pops, this massive RAM shortage is not going away.

Starting next year, even the new iPhone might be too expensive for most people to afford.

text:
币圈没行情时，链上的高频资金去了哪？答案可能是原油市场。

刚刚WTI原油期货跌破100美元，而前几天还在110美元重要关口宽幅震荡。

这种震荡市，给敏锐的资金通过干预流动性从中牟利创造了极大空间。

彭博社近日披露的一份报告里，就阐述了这类资金是如何在链上暗处进行猎杀的。

今年 3 月初，原油市场同样经历了一轮由宏观事件引发的价格颠簸。

当传统金融市场因周末休市时，Hyperliquid 顺势成为了资金的替代流入口。在此期间，两个匿名账户在 Hyperliquid 的 Brent 原油等能源永续合约上，密集布下了超过 1.7 亿美元的可疑订单。

链上监控机构 Solidus Labs 的数据完全拆解了这场典型的“幌骗（Spoofing）”操作：

这两个账户在订单薄一侧挂出巨额卖单制造抛压假象，随后迅速撤单，并在另一侧完成小额反向吃单。

公开的链上记录显示，其撤单量与实际成交量的比例达到了极其夸张的 30:1（例如单笔撤销 1700 万美元的同时仅成交 42.5 万美元）。在短短三天内，该操作通过制造虚假流动性套利了约 11.9 万美元。

所以，如果你跟着做交易，尤其是让 AI 盯着着订单薄深度、依赖大单异动监控报警、甚至试图“跟着巨鲸做趋势”，那可能还会反向亏钱。

现在 AI 让大家获取数据做一个能运行的看板太容易了，亲眼看到的所谓链上真实数据，同样可以是一场被精心算计的骗局。

text:
Interesting.

Revolut reportedly only started seeing meaningful AI productivity gains after moving away from expensive OpenAI and Anthropic models to self-hosted GLM.

Decagon reportedly runs ~90% of its workloads on open weight models.

Why? Because when you're running AI agents in production for e.g. customer service, cost and latency matter enormously. You don't need a frontier model with PhD-level reasoning or even a model that knows the capital of Finland to handle every customer interaction.

We're seeing similar dynamics across hypergrowth AI startups and increasingly the large enterprises we work with.

But most importantly, the future isn't binary.

When use cases are new, you want the smartest general-purpose model available. But once workflows mature and become predictable, smaller, faster, specialized models increasingly win.

I wouldn't be surprised if 80–90% of routine enterprise AI workflows eventually run on open-weight and smaller models.

This doesn't mean frontier labs lose. 

It means the market is splitting into two massive opportunities: frontier intelligence and specialized execution at scale.

男性的胡子是一种面部杠杆

哈哈这个我还真研究过，直接说结论：

亚洲男性很多是没资格留胡子的，因为胡子的密度不够，留长是负债

胡须浓密本身有遗传基因的原因也有睾酮分泌旺盛的原因，作为第二性特征

胡子留出胡型需要坚持经常修型，边缘需要锐利，这本身意味着此人有更高的时间冗余

胡子作为男生天生的部分，可以修饰下颌线，提高面部折叠度，拉长面部比例，提供阴影对比

我尝试过一些胡型后，推荐5mm的短胡须，在下巴这里，我目前就是留这种，每天用5mm卡尺修型

上唇和下唇我是全部剃掉，这倒不是密度，是亚洲人在这两个部分的广度不够，斯拉夫和日耳曼人的广度更好，更有型，但也容易过于广是络腮胡

总而言之，亚洲人的面部偏俊美，加入下巴的5mm短胡须可以增加硬朗，平衡面部风格

text:
OKX ICE 反对名单变长，闪赚的美股代币还能拿吗？

先分清是哪个产品被反对，再看年化～

先拆分一下：

据 @james_x 老师整理，OKX 与 ICE 的代币化股票原名单 62 家，反对名单已到 50 家。

细看的话，50 家里有 7 家本来就不在原名单，原名单里真正反对的是 43 家。

还没反对的 19 家，包括 Apple、Amazon、Tesla、Coinbase、Circle、Strategy 等。

意思是：上市公司可以选择退出，被反对的是这个新交易场所的上架计划。

再看闪赚这边：

OKX 闪赚这几天的「美股持币赚币」，支持 xTSLA、xNVDA、xMSTR、xCRCL 等 10 种代币化股票。

这是 xStocks 一套的产品，目前活动照常进行；两者具体关系以 OKX 官方说明为准。

所以，看到反对新闻就清仓 xNVDA，可能是把两件事混在了一起。

继续看规则：

1/ 奖池 40 万 USDT，活动截至 11 月 28 日 07:59（UTC+8）；

2/ 每日合格持仓合计至少 100 美元，按当天随机快照的最低值计；

3/ 页面参考年化约 12.4%，已有 8000 多人参与，剩约 25 天。

公式还是那一行：年化 ≈ 奖池 ÷ 持仓总额 × 365 ÷ 天数。

反推分母，按活动约 30 天估：

每日奖池约 40 万 ÷ 30，约 1.33 万 USDT；

持仓总额约 1.33 万 × 365 ÷ 13.08%，约 3700 万美元；

8000 人平均下来，人均约 4600 美元。

接下来做个情景对比：

若反对新闻吓走两成持仓，分母约 3000 万，年化约 16%；

若走掉一半，分母约 1850 万，年化约 26%；

若反而涌进一倍资金，分母约 7400 万，年化约 6.5%。

分母翻倍，年化减半。

反过来，别人被新闻吓跑，留下的人分得更多。

当然，持币奖励只是表面，实际可能还需要对冲代币化股票本身的价格波动。

一个可复用的顺序是：先确认被反对的是哪个产品，再判断值不值得。

感兴趣可以去闪赚页看看实时参考年化，记得先点报名！

如果真点开，还会发现新一期的 USDC 「持币赚币」即将开始！

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

 introduced spam-limiter against people flooding the network with short-term orders that are unlikely to fill.  The formula is:

text:
AI 是如此好的提高生产力效率的工具，为什么我们却只能看到大量的垃圾 AI 文呢？

我在尝试解决这个问题，这是我的思考过程：

1. 从观众的需求层面，我发现很多观众想要看到我很久之前发过的内容，因为他们之前没看过，就算看了可能也忘了

2. 当时我的表达可能是在 Twitter 上直接语音转文字就发了，表达比较碎片化，不成体系

3. 所以 AI 可以去看一下我以前发过的成千上万篇内容，把同一主题下面的几个短推文合并成一篇文章，帮我改好错别字，改好标点符号

我让 claude code 尝试了一下，刚刚把我未来几个月的公众号文章都写好了

效果如下：

1. 从观众的角度，他们未来会在我的公众号看到更好的内容，因为表达更加连贯，也可以一次性把一个主题的内容直接看完

2. 这些内容不会有任何的 AI 味儿，因为全部都是我手写的内容，AI 只是做拼接和顺序的调整

3. 观众并不会因此只看到陈旧内容，我依然会坚持手写内容，AI 的这部分补充只是提高了我的更新频次

4. 公众号只是一个开始，这个内容试验发布几天之后，我会让助理同步更新到 threads、小红书、抖音等各个平台

我觉得这才叫 AI 写作吧

We've spent years asking which AI voice sounds better. 

Voice Arena is asking something different: can listeners actually mistake it for a human?

author: hamptonism
quoted_text:
Drop 2/15 

Are we actually measuring the things we ultimately want our voice AI models to achieve?

The best AI voices are becoming hard to tell apart.
From each other. Not from humans.

🚀 Introducing Turing TTS: an evaluation that measures how often human listeners mistake AI-generated speech for real human speech.

We tested leading TTS models against real human speech. Even the best model fooled listeners only ~10% of the time.

With Turing TTS, we hope to contribute to a broader discussion within the research community about how we measure progress in voice AI.

If one of our goals is to develop speech that is indistinguishable from human speech, how well do our current evaluation methods capture progress toward that goal?

We don’t claim that Turing TTS is the right way forward, or that human indistinguishability should be the goal of every TTS system.

Rather, we hope these findings encourage the community to collectively examine whether blind pairwise human evaluations of naturalness are sufficient, and what else we might need to measure.

Results are now live on @voicearena_ai.

text:
Agent 帮你跑了一晚上实验，结果比 Baseline 高了 15%。正准备分享给合作者，对方问了一句「你用的什么数据？」，才发现 1000 条数据里只有 5 条不同。

这是 AI 研究者 Thomas Jiralerspong 在《Chasing the Karpathy Peak》里描述的一个场景，他自己也经历过类似的坑。

文章画了一座「AI 生产力山」，从代码补全、Vibe Coding，到让 Agent 独立完成实验，越往上走，效率似乎越来越高。

但一旦越过 Karpathy Peak，就可能掉进 Slop Cliff。

意思很简单，你觉得自己每天完成了大量工作，实际产出却可能已经开始下降。

文章还引用了 METR 在 2025 年的一项实验。16 位资深开发者用 AI 完成任务反而慢了 19%，事后却认为自己快了 20%。虽然不能代表今天的 AI 水平，但这个认知偏差挺值得警惕。

作者还给自己起了个名字，Slopaholic，沉迷于使用 AI 所带来的高效感。

我觉得最扎心的是那个循环。Agent 帮你做事，你又让 Agent 检查结果，它告诉你一切正常，于是你越来越放心把更多工作交出去。

作者建议定期回头看代码、检查数据，找真正懂行的人审阅结果。

这点对做 Research Agent 的人尤其重要。下次 Agent 再跑出一张漂亮的实验结果图，或许应该先打开数据和脚本看看，再考虑让它继续跑下一个实验。

text:
North Korean-linked actors (TraderTraitor) have laundered approximately $242 million through the Tron leg alone within two days exploit. 

This is a fraction of the ~$6.3–6.4B total theft (largest crypto heist on record), of which ~$2.8–3B was frozen on-chain by issuers (Tether, Circle, etc.) and protocols. Roughly $3.5B remained controllable by the attackers after freezes; the Tron activity represents early, rapid layering.⁠

Tron flow breakdown:

Stolen on Tron: ~$628M (612.7M USDT + 46.4M TRX).
Tether froze 378.7M USDT on day 1 → ~$249M left movable.
~$194M exited via bridges/swaps: Relay ~$48M, THORChain ~$44M, Chainflip ~$32.1M, Symbiosis ~$16M (plus smaller routes like USDT0, Across). Additional ~$43M via Bitget Wallet and others (destinations partly unresolved).
~$26M stayed on Tron (JustLend, USDD swaps, CEX service accounts); ~$22M lost to fees/slippage.

Bridged funds primarily landed as ETH on Ethereum mainnet (~53k ETH), BTC, and stablecoins, then continued moving. ~$7.5M still on Tron; $3B+ on other chains (BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL) remains largely untouched.⁠

FBI, USSS, and IRS-CI have attributed the full hack to DPRK’s TraderTraitor and explicitly urged THORChain node operators, RPC providers, instant exchanges, and DeFi services to block addresses tied to the proceeds. Laundering shows high automation and volume (thousands of deposits), shifting toward bridges and instant swaps rather than solely mixers. 

Bridges remain high-throughput exit vectors even under scrutiny; decentralized designs face clear tension between permissionless operation and law-enforcement pressure. Most capital is still staged, so the next wave of movement will be the key tracking phase.

Tokenization has been one of the most exciting themes of this cycle, yet I still think we’re barely scratching the surface.

So far we’ve mostly taken already-liquid TradFi assets and put them onchain, but the outsized potential lies in tokenizing the illiquid, even the physical, and making it both tradeable and composable with DeFi.

An example: Portfolio-margin style borrowing has traditionally been reserved for UHNW private bank clients. Tokenizing physical assets democratizes this. Imagine owning a fraction of a yield-bearing data centre with a hyperscaler tenant, posting it as collateral, and borrowing against its future cash flows to lever into the infrastructure being built on top of it.

Literal finance on steroids. What a time to be alive

quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

text: 1/100 You pick up your phone to check the weather. Forty minutes later you know the weather in nobody's city. You've seen a puppy learning to swim, a celebrity's kitchen, a debate about whether hot dogs are sandwiches and an advert for socks you'll probably buy. The temperature outside remains a mystery. This happens to almost everyone, many times a day, and it rarely feels like a decision. It feels like falling down a well with very soft walls. This chapter is about the well. Specifically, it's about your attention and where it goes when you don't steer it. Attention is the one resource every app, shop, news site and game on your phone is competing for. Teams of clever people work full time to win a few more minutes of it. They measure their success in your seconds. Your own mind joins in, because it was built to grab anything new, loud or uncertain. The result can feel like a personal weakness. The research suggests a different reading. You're a normal brain in a building designed by experts to keep you inside. By the end of this chapter, you'll know a lot about how the building works. With luck, you'll also find a few of the exits and learn where the weather app actually is.

text: Having a court that can overrule the elected government was the worst idea in the US Constitution. Israel and Britain were both foolish to imitate it. Guys, what did you *think* would happen if you let someone take a contentious issue out of the scope of institutions of consent?
author: DavidDeutschOxf
quoted_text:
For Americans wondering what the hell is happening in Poland today:

Poland is having a constitutional crisis, and apparently nobody can agree on who gets to enforce the Constitution.

Here’s the background:

Poland has a conservative president, Karol Nawrocki, and a liberal prime minister, Donald Tusk.

When conservatives were in power, they overhauled the courts and appointed judges. Liberals called it illegal. Now liberals are in power and trying to undo those changes. Conservatives are calling that illegal.

Naturally, everyone claims they’re defending democracy.

Here’s what happened today:

• A judge announced the suspension of the Constitutional Court’s conservative chief justice and his deputy.

• Police secured the court building and reportedly prevented the chief justice from entering.

• The court’s official X account called it a “coup d’état.”

• The justice minister is seeking to lift the judges’ immunity to pursue criminal charges.

• Protesters gathered outside, and several people were detained.

• Poland’s president reportedly cut short his trip to Senegal to return home.

Imagine Democrats and Republicans fighting over who controls the Supreme Court, while police secure the building and both sides accuse each other of staging a coup.

The entire dispute is about who has the legal authority to interpret the Constitution, except neither side agrees on who gets to decide that either.

text: @grok @kevinschawinski The "Convention" is just ink and paper. It cannot decide anything. The issue is whether unelected ECHR judges who "interpret" it can, by doing so, overrule the Swiss Parliament, Courts, Supreme Court, and referenda.
author: DavidDeutschOxf

text: Yes. ECtHR judges interpret the Convention and issue binding judgments under it. Swiss courts give those interpretations primacy over conflicting federal laws and, in concrete cases, over constitutional provisions from popular initiatives. The Court cannot itself annul a referendum result or Swiss law; remedies run through Swiss processes. Switzerland retains the option to denounce the Convention.

6. 어린이, 노약자, 환자가 있으면 맞는 약을 따로 챙기고, 환자는 최근 처방전과 약을 준비하라고 함.

7. 화생방 대비 물품도 목록에 있음. 방독면 또는 수건과 마스크, 비옷이나 비닐옷, 고무장화와 장갑, 비누와 합성세제가 해당됨.

8. 창틀과 문틀을 막을 접착테이프도 충분히 두라고 함. 서울시는 알루미늄테이프를 들고 세제는 락스를 뺀 것으로 안내함.

9. 방독면이 없을 때의 대체 방법도 있음. 인천시 표는 물에 적신 손수건으로 코와 입을 막고, 비옷을 머리까지 덮어 쓰고 허리를 묶으라고 함.

10. 이 물자는 주기적으로 유통기한을 살피고 교체하라고 함.

11. 이제 대피용 생존배낭임. 행정안전부 2025년 7월 책자는 평상시 2~3일분 식수, 식량, 생필품, 상비약, 라디오, 손전등, 화생방 대비 물품을 가방이나 캐리어에 싸 두라고 함.

12. 대표 품목은 생수, 간편식, 손전등, 상비약, 라디오, 화장지, 비옷, 담요, 방독면, 마스크, 고무장갑, 장화, 비닐봉투임.

13. 국민재난안전포털은 가족 수대로 가방을 만들라고 권함. 속옷, 병따개, 수건, 안경, 생리용품, 종이기저귀도 목록에 있음.

14. 현금과 서류도 챙김. 신용카드, 현금카드, 현금을 두고 중요한 서류는 방수 비닐에 담음. 여분의 자동차 키와 집 열쇠도 따로 둠.

15. 통신이 끊길 때를 위한 준비도 있음. 가족 만남의 장소를 정하고 비상연락카드를 써서 생존배낭에 넣으라고 행정안전부 책자가 안내함.

16. 대피장소는 두 곳을 정해 둠. 대책본부가 지정한 대피소와 친척집 같은 곳임. 편한 신발, 가벼운 우비, 얇은 담요, 보온이 좋은 옷도 같이 챙김.

17. 대피소는 전국에 약 17,000곳임. 아파트 지하주차장, 지하철역, 지하상가가 해당되고 가까운 곳은 국민재난안전포털과 비상대비 앱에서 찾을 수 있음.

18. 8월 20일 전국 민방위 훈련은 20분간 진행됐음. 오후 2시 사이렌에 대피하고, 2시 15분에 이동할 수 있고, 2시 20분에 끝났음.

19. 외국인은 22개 언어로 훈련 일정과 대피소 위치를 비상대비 앱에서 받아 볼 수 있음.

20. 마을 단위 준비도 안내에 있음. 지하실이나 대피호, 펌프·우물·물탱크 같은 비상급수시설, 마대·삽·곡괭이·사다리 같은 응급복구물자가 해당됨.

21. 책자 목차에는 사재기 자제와 배급제 협조 항목이 따로 있음. 정부는 한꺼번에 사들이기보다 정해진 기준만큼 갖추는 쪽을 권함.

22. 요즘 한반도 정세도 배경임. 북한은 10월 29일 자폭 드론을 공개했고 31일에는 전술탄도미사일용 집속탄두를 시험했다고 국내 사설이 전함.

23. 그러면 다른 나라는 무엇을 하고 있나. 공통점은 며칠분 물, 식량, 약, 현금, 라디오를 갖추라는 안내임.

text: ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.
author: sacha
quoted_text:
The most interesting part of $ORE's design isn't live yet.

TLDR: Today, revenue generated by the ORE Reserve auto-compounds in isolation. Eventually, that revenue could be streamed to uORE holders (miners holding unclaimed rewards) as SOL mining credits, allowing the protocol to increasingly fund its own mining activity. The result is a flywheel that could strengthen mining incentives, lift staking yield, and put ORE on a path to net deflation.

First, it's worth understanding why ORE is different.

Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, and Solana all use their native assets to incentivize network security. ORE doesn't have that requirement. It inherits Solana’s security, so it can direct its incentives toward a different objective: rewarding those who accumulate and hold the asset.

ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.

Consider how value flows through ORE today:

- Miners deploy SOL to earn ORE, aiming to acquire it below market price.
- A 10% refining fee on claimed rewards is redistributed to holders of unclaimed rewards (uORE).
- Mining revenue funds ORE buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and the Reserve.
- The Reserve provides liquidity while generating its own revenue through LP fees and yield-bearing assets like JitoSOL and USDv.

The result is a system where mining activity supports holders through multiple mechanisms, while the Reserve continues to grow and generate additional liquidity and revenue.

But there's one more piece to the design. Arguably the most interesting.

In AI, recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system capable of improving its own capabilities, with each improvement enabling further improvements.

ORE has a potential economic equivalent.

Today, the simplified flow looks like this:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → Reserve.

The Reserve grows, generates revenue through LP fees and yield, and reinvests that revenue into itself. A straightforward compounding mechanism.

But the loop back to mining remains open.

Now consider what happens when Reserve revenue is redirected to uORE holders as SOL credits, usable exclusively for mining ORE.

The flow becomes:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → SOL mining credits → Mining → Reserve.

The loop closes.

This is the recursive moment.

Consider the significance of this change.

Today, mining depends on SOL supplied by users. With mining credits, the Reserve’s own revenue becomes a new source of capital to fund that same activity.

Originally powered by user capital, ORE could become increasingly self-powered.

A protocol generating its own fuel.

There are two particularly interesting second-order effects here.

First, Reserve-funded mining credits could increase competition for ORE rewards, driving up production costs. To the extent this stimulates incremental mining activity, it generates additional protocol revenue, supporting buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and Reserve growth.

Second, and perhaps most importantly, this creates a potential path toward sustained net deflation.

At sufficient scale, additional protocol revenue could fund enough buybacks and burial to consistently exceed new ORE issuance.

To be clear, mining credits aren't live today, and it may be years before the economics justify turning them on.

The Reserve first needs sufficient scale and sustainable revenue to fund meaningful mining incentives without compromising its liquidity or long-term growth.

More importantly, the incremental mining activity needs to generate enough additional value to justify redirecting revenue away from direct compounding.

But the potential end state is worth considering: an economic system that compounds recursively, under its own power.

text:
上周五多位美联储理事释放鹰派政策信号，为何12月加息概率从84%跌至73%？

其实在上周我解读沃什讲话内容中已经解释了，这其实是当下美联储政策逻辑的一种“反身性”

这里有正反两套逻辑：

正向逻辑，市场越相信Fed不用加息，市场自然宽松，反而对Fed来说更有加息的空间与必要性

反向逻辑，市场越害怕Fed加息，市场自然紧缩，反而越可能让Fed不用加息

这就回到了沃什上任初期我得出的结论——沃什时代，在可以塑造一个有限宽松的金融环境，让“水”定向流向某几个地方

所以，当上周五美联储理事连续鹰派政策之后，美股跌幅扩大完成一个“黑色星期五”后，反而市场认为当前金融环境已经加速收紧，12月加息的必要性反而下降。

如果此时中东局势可以缓和，Brent 回归下跌趋势，并且在未来1个月逐渐回归95美元下方， 那么金融市场反而会逐渐缓和

当然，通胀预期不灭，这种正反逻辑链会依旧存在，如果12月前美股快速收复跌幅，反而会增加12月加息概率！

quoted_text:
沃什讲话总结——10月鹰派暂停+鹰派通胀目标+未锁死但是保留12月加息选项，基本符合此前市场预期！

10月鹰派加息是此前市场的预期，而今晚沃什讲话基本属于符合预期，整体讲话听下来反而没有预期中那么鹰

1，对于通胀，是沃什讲话最鹰的一部分，强调没有软性通胀目标，见顶Fed通胀目标就是2%，Fed不接受更高的通胀预期

2，名义收益率+实际收益率上升，市场自然金融收缩暂时代替Fed加息的必要，这也成为10月不加息的理由

3，“Watchful thinking, not watchful waiting” “审慎思考，而非审慎等待”，这是沃什的原话，试图用这个理念来代替10月份的暂停加息，目的是不想让市场预期加息周期结束，继续保留12月加息窗口

4，沃什强调对AI资本开支的担忧，他的判断是资本开支强劲已经不在局限于少数领域，对美国经济是利好，同时也是经济增长的利好，AI短期是需求冲击，长期才可能成为供给冲击，沃什的观点认为AI的繁荣未必帮助Fed降息，反而会增加Fed控制通胀的难度

5，沃什承认了高利率在压制科技企业，但是并未打断目前的资本开支，他知道高利率的代价，但是目前美国经济和AI投资仍然承受得住，所以短期美股的波动不足以让Fed改变政策

6，明确能源通胀与Fed政策的关系，名义上能源供给带来的通胀Fed不会管，但是如果能源通胀向核心通胀扩散，Fed就要进一步收紧政策，这意味后续PCE数据是重点。

7，沃什今晚的讲话重新定义了Fed的“政策反应函数”，之前我们看PCE +GPD+就业+油价，现在要增加一个新的变量——金融状况

第一层，看通胀，观察PCE  CPI 服务通胀 工资 通胀扩散 能源二次传导
第二层，看实体经济，GDP 就业 资本支出 AI投资 生产率
第三层，看金融条件，看2Y 10Y 实际利率，看美元，看信用利差，看美股

沃什一直强调减少前瞻指引，依赖更多数据来决定Fed政策，而沃什也让数据观测领域更加复杂多样化了

如果按照这个逻辑，如果未来几周10Y收益率上涨+实际利率继续上涨+企业融资成本继续增加+金融条件进一步收紧，那么反而会削弱Fed 12月加息的可能性，反过来如果10Y快速下跌 + 美股大涨 + 信贷利差收窄 + 美元走弱，导致金融条件明显宽松，AI资本开支继续爆发，通胀仍然维持高位，那么12月加息可能性大大增加。

总结：

通过今晚沃什的讲话来看，进一步证明了我此前的猜测——沃什正在让美国利率处于一个有限宽松的阶段，沃什今晚的讲话相对此前预期没有更鹰，但是也没有关闭12月加息的可能性，如果一句话总结——沃什今晚试图让市场明白，这是一个开始让市场承担一部分加息工作的Fed

text: @kevinschawinski @grok Does the ECHR have the power to overrule all Swiss authorities, including referendum results, in matters of ECHR-defined "human rights".
author: DavidDeutschOxf

text: No. The ECtHR issues binding judgments that Switzerland must implement under the Convention, and Swiss courts prioritize ECHR human rights over conflicting federal laws (and often constitutional provisions from initiatives). It cannot, however, directly annul referendum results or Swiss laws; remedies occur via Swiss processes. Switzerland retains the option to denounce the Convention.

text:
The neocloud boom is the most exciting thing happening in AI infrastructure right now, and it's also where the gap between talking and building is widest

Every week I see another team announce they're "becoming a cloud". Some raised for a different idea and found that GPU capacity is the thing customers are actually paying for. Rental rates keep moving up, demand keeps outrunning supply and the capital is there, so it makes sense that people are jumping in

What a lot of new entrants learn the hard way is that the business barely lives in the GPUs. You can wire money for hardware in an afternoon. Then you need power that's actually contracted, a site with the right cooling, networking that holds up under real training loads, and a crew that can get all of it live on the exact date you promised your customer

That ready for service date is everything. A customer who signed for capacity in March has a model to train, a product to ship and their own investors to answer to. If you slip by two months, you've pushed their whole roadmap back

So the providers who win this cycle look a bit boring from the outside. They've brought clusters online before. They know the local electrician by name. They plan for the transformer arriving late and the permit taking longer than it should. They treat a delivery date like a promise to someone else's business

That's also what lenders and customers will pay up for. Plenty of buyers want to work with smaller and more flexible providers because the big clouds can't always give them the capacity, the timing or the price they need. That demand is real and it keeps growing. What they need is confidence that the capacity will actually show up

The long tail of compute providers is here to stay and it's healthy for the whole market. Over the next couple of years the ones who execute will pull way ahead, and the teams who can bring a cluster online on time, every time, are going to be worth their weight in gold

At Aethir we spend a lot of time on exactly this, because getting the compute to show up is the whole job

If you're building in this space, go hire the people who've done it before. They're the scarcest resource in AI right now

黄金创下 2008 年以来最差 10 月，但市场上仍有人豪掷 18.4 万美元押注年底前不会突破 6,000 美元。

COMEX 黄金 10 月下跌 6.87%，10 月 30 日收于 3,898.9 美元/盎司，创年内最低收盘价，单月跌幅为 2008 年以来最大，年内累计下跌 10.2%。

但有意思的是：

- Polymarket 上，黄金年底前触及 6,000 美元的概率仅为 2.1%。
- 交易员 ronm238 投入 18.4 万美元买入「不会」，其在黄金板块参与 12 个市场，胜率 75%，累计盈利约 5,100 美元。
- 央行购金仍在持续，中国央行 9 月增持 23 吨，波兰央行增持 24.9 吨。
- 高盛虽然将 2026 年底黄金公允价值预测从 4,900 美元下调至 4,650 美元，但仍维持 2027 年底 5,400 美元的目标价。

短期来看，加息预期与 ETF 需求疲软正在压制金价；但央行购金和长期配置需求并没有消失。

黄金这轮下跌，究竟是牛市中的一次深度回调，还是趋势反转的开始？

author: SShikang
quoted_text:
很快就到最后一天了。

说实话，我最期待的，就是GPT能拿出一个超越Opus 5.5的模型，不一定非得对标Fable 5.5。

现在的GPT，在日常自动化和视频制作上已经让我相当满意。很多时候，我只需要说几句话，它就能自己制作视频、处理素材、完成上传。这部分是真的省心。

但作为一个纯Vibe Coding用户，我还是觉得，GPT在Coding上对新手不够友好。主要是两件事。

第一，写后端时，解释太多，防御性逻辑和保护措施也经常加得过头。我不是反对必要的保护，而是有些实现明显超出了实际需求，把原本简单的问题越做越复杂。

再叠加上下文容量的限制，长任务反复压缩后，我经常遇到它忘记约定、前后逻辑不一致，最后连代码也跟着乱起来。尤其在搭建Harness时，这种不一致可能直接让整套流程跑不通。GPT-6相比5.6确实改善了很多，但我仍然会遇到这些问题。

第二，前端审美真的还需要向Claude学习。
让GPT自己做页面，字体、间距、排版经常不够讲究。我得花大量对话去纠正，有时候甚至要直接把HTML和CSS给它，让它照着参考实现，才能得到想要的效果。

说到底，我就是个纯Vibe Coding用户。我的长处不是审代码，而是理解客户的管理需求，把工具落地成真正能提升效率的方案。

我更关心的是：花了这么多钱，模型能不能准确理解我的要求，把东西稳定地做出来。

而不是跑了半天，东西没跑通，给我一句“sorry”，然后继续朝错误的方向使劲。

如果GPT 在近期能发布一款对标opus5.5的模型，并且不会降智。我立帖为证，我将直接抛弃Claude，并充值500美金套餐，成为Codex的忠实玩家。

text:
上帝已经给了答案，冯·诺依曼为什么还要追问？

《Lex Fridman Podcast》第 503 期里，麻省理工学院理论计算机科学家 Ankur Moitra 讲了一出老戏。戏里的冯·诺依曼上了天堂，得到一个向上帝提问的机会。他问，黎曼猜想是真的吗？上帝说，是。众人终于松了口气，冯·诺依曼却马上追问：“你怎么知道？”

上帝的回答大意是：我知道每一个零点在哪里，它们全都落在实部等于二分之一的那条直线上。这已经把答案说得再肯定不过了，可冯·诺依曼还是不满意。上帝能看见所有零点，他不能。他想知道的是，究竟有什么理由，使得连一个例外都不可能出现。

同场的数论学家 Alex Kontorovich 说，如果别人只告诉他一件事为真，却没让他理解为什么，他的知识并没有增加。我想把这个故事带进 AI 培训。假设模型判断一份采购合同有风险，把那一段圈红只算第一步。能指到哪条约定、解释哪两句话放在一起会出问题，再试试改掉其中一句后判断是否还成立，团队才真正学会了怎样审下一份合同。

text:
Pre Market Thoughts - 2 Nov 26

Friday's risk off move was the first time the blow up in the AI trade reached into the index with QQQ dropping over 4% for the day, sitting on its 200d ma. I noted that it is not a bad spot to bid the index, particularly if you have a longer term horizon.

The semis rebalancing flow itself reached gigantic proportions - over 21B at one point in time - which created opportunities for a fantastic high risk reward trade into the close. I will be sharing about it and how to use Gambit Terminal in a separate post.

For this week, we have yet another risk event - which is mid terms. Last week we had the destruction of the mags as investors hiding out in mag7 exposure were brutally delevered. Many of these names sit at the cheapest ever forward P/E ratios. On a longer time frame - this presents a fantastic opportunity to bid this names.

The AI trade as many people have noted seems to be "over". On vibes - i agree 100%. Pattern matching with crypto flows - this would be near the right edge of the curve where the blow off has occurred and quiet desperation is setting in. However, many of these names are now also cash rich and starting to devise ways to return/repatriate cash back to shareholders - i believe such measures will have the ability to reignite momentum in the AI trade once again.

What are the conditions that will create such a scenario? A deep plunge in the indexes would be one. Pain in 1 sector will not cause easier macro conditions, index level pain however will cause policy panic and government action.

Essentially, the whippings will stop once morale improves. This was a phrase that i remember saying to myself in the wake of the May 2021 BTC pop.

Prime brokerage data has shown further paring back of positions with purchases in Info tech last week being driven mainly by short covering. Interestingly, triple levered ETFs such as TQQQ and SOXL took in large inflows from retail. We have a situation of retail "buying the dip" while instris are cutting back on already very low exposure.

For professional managers, it will be difficult for them to get engaged in the AI trade again this year. Many of them have wrapped up their books after a fantastic 1H and are not taking risk. Prefering to preserve their performance and earn their fees. As such i would expect the next buyers for AI over the next 2 months to be company buybacks (memory) and retail. 

Flow wise - for tradfi and high beta AI stocks - i would expect very strong performance today as HFs derisk shorts into the mid terms tomorrow. Friday's selling was also a clearing event for many of these names. 

On Crypto - While $BTC has been extremely strong in the context of a hack - either bid momentum or bid value. 

Good luck!

An interesting thing though: this is not an issue for systems with client-side proving. If a transaction is proven locally (e.g., as we do in Miden), even if ECDSA signature is used, the public key never needs to leave the user's device - and so, the public never learns it. author: chainyoda
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Tim Cook's take on why competitors can't copy Apple is sharper than most people realize.

They start by copying the product. Then they realize the product isn't the hard part.

Cook said it directly: people who try to copy Apple first try to copy what they can see. The hardware. The design. The packaging. And they can get close on all of it.

But the thing that made the product, the organizational culture, the decision-making, the obsessive prioritization, that's invisible from the outside. You can't find it in a teardown.

This is why Apple's moat has held for decades while better-funded competitors kept losing. Samsung had more SKUs. Google had more engineers. Amazon had more distribution. None of it translated into the same output because none of it replicated the same input.

The lesson for founders is uncomfortable: if your competitive advantage is visible in your product, it's already copyable. The real moat is the culture that makes the product, and that takes decades to build, not quarters.

Reverse-engineering the iPhone is an engineering problem. Reverse-engineering how Apple decides what to build is a different problem entirely.

1/ hyperliquid:native : 情理之中的大赢家，但赢的不是「又一个交易所」

ICE 战略投资 @tradexyz ，双方联手将 7*24 永续合约引入美国，由 @HyperliquidX 提供基础设施，TradeXYZ 负责产品，ICE 负责合规和清算（另 OKX 负责渠道分发）。

这一合作不仅获得了传奇金融人物 @standuquesne 的公开站台，还得到了 @elonmusk 的引用评论，虽然就一个词「Interesting」，但折射出的是叙事已经从 Crypto 内卷进入华尔街。

这里有几个值得关注的细节：

- Hyperliquid 以合规的方式进入美国市场，并且是作为底层基础设施而不是交易所主体

- TradeXYZ 隶属于 HIP-3 生态项目，大部分人的共识是它们没有独立发币空间，叙事溢价只能回流给 hyperliquid:native  

- 币安黑客事件将加速用户从 CEX 转向 DEX 的迁移进程，Hyperliquid 作为最大的去中心化衍生品交易基础设施将是直接受益方之一

2/ ethereum:0x6985884c4392d348587b19cb9eaaf157f13271cd ：被很多人低估的「第二落点」

ICE 与 TradeXYZ 的合作确认了一件事，那就是 ICE 在认真对接链上原生基建，而 @LayerZero_Core 此前已宣布与 ICE 建立合作关系，后者也是 Zero Blockchain 的共同设计方之一，以及该 L1 上的旗舰应用 Atlas 的有力推动者。

叠加 AI 数学进展与量子担忧叙事， Zero 团队正在通过 Akita 和 Aerie 倡导在密码学方面保持敏捷。

另一方面，Agent 经济需要一个微支付交易层：高吞吐、低延迟、低成本，能同时满足的链不多；再加上 value accrual + 解锁压力相对可控，这类资产本轮其实很稀缺。 基于以上几点， ethereum:0x6985884c4392d348587b19cb9eaaf157f13271cd 也许是被很多人低估的受益方。

3/ near:native : 区别于隐私类资产的币安黑客事件间接赢家

@NEARProtocol 正在构建脱离传统体系的流动性轨道，可用于替代 CEX。黑客事件真正改变的是「信任寄存在哪」；受益的是大概率是能承接自托管交易与清算的轨道，而不是匿名现金本身。

这也是 near:native 与 $ZEC/ $XMR 这类黑客能用、或人们逃离实体时会转向的货币之间的主要区别。

以上是根据我的个人 Timeline 刷到的一些海外 CT 的观点总结和延伸，老师们怎么看？

每次换 AI 编程工具，都得重新交代项目背景和个人偏好？开源项目 Mnemosyne，想给不同 Agent 接上一套可持续使用的记忆。🧠

支持语义与关键词混合检索、记忆整理、知识图谱，以及跨设备增量同步；同步还能开启客户端加密，让记忆内容加密后再离开设备。

吸引我的，是记忆可以独立于某个聊天窗口或 Agent 存在，让长期项目少一些重复交代。

但“本地存储”不等于所有处理都在本地：若使用远程 Embedding API，文本仍会发送给服务商。注重隐私，记得选择本地向量模型。

Exceeding the:

- 2018 Volmageddon
- March 2020 COVID crash
- 2021 Archegos collapse / Evergrande crisis
- 2022 bear market

Goldman's prime brokerage desk reported on the 26th that it had also seen ~$20B of selling over 2 weeks vs. $23 billion during July's entire unwind.

$AAOI: 12.5% -> 19.84%+

$AEHR: 14.33% -> 17.93%+

$CIFR: 19.94% -> 25.39%+

$OKLO: 17.72% ->22.93%+

Substantial deleveraging coinciding with surging short interest, kinda looks like a July setup after Midterms?

Earnings on many AI capex + bottlenecks (not all like $INTC) looked strong: 

eg. $AXTI guided annualized Q4 = 23.7x P/E now, not including potential InP substrate hikes + capacity expansion that can compress it to single digits.

- No signs of $MSFT / $AMZN materially cutting capex, while $SPCX secures $40B more for GPU procurement. 

Slightly painful, but I think the AI capex trade (specifically photonics/memory) is a generational opportunity, with extreme volatility in between.

author: oxwizzdom
quoted_text:
I built uli: it trains a model on your own data inside a running inference engine on a Mac, in the idle gaps between requests, then serves it from the same machine.

Overnight, my 16 GB M1 Pro fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B on 2,000 labelled banking questions. The trained model answers 90 of 100 held-out questions from the question alone. The same base model, given every label in its prompt, answers 69.

Why it matters: serving generic models has become a price and speed race that big data centers win. But a Mac can do more than serve tokens. A model trained on your own labels gets its value from your data, not from scale, so it's work any Mac with spare time can do.

What it offers: if you have labelled data and a narrow task, like sorting support tickets or pulling fields from documents, you get your own model, trained overnight on a Mac and served from it. With OpenAI's self-serve fine-tuning closing to new jobs in January, teams with small custom models need a new home for them.

What I built:
- Training that runs in small pieces inside the inference engine and steps aside when a request arrives: at most 0.134 s added to a waiting request (p99)
- Many customers' adapters served side by side on one copy of the base model, for 0.30 GB of extra memory
- Talk to your model as soon as it finishes: uli chat in the terminal, or any OpenAI-compatible client, by naming your adapter as the model
- Crash-safe jobs: killed twice mid-run, it resumed and finished with a bit-identical adapter
- A hub and CLI (uli submit, watch, chat, eval) that deletes your training data when the job ends

See it, with a replay of the real overnight run: https://t.co/BYLf0egBOM

Built on @darkbloomai's open-source MLX engine. Thanks @0xkydo and @gajesh for building it in the open.

Reading the latest pieces by @scottew and @vigstar1 made me think we should pay more attention to the network token approach that @Visa and others are pursuing, alongside virtual cards. Not to discount virtual cards at all, but network tokens feel like an equally critical piece of the puzzle.

When an intermediary becomes the MoR and replaces the user’s chosen card with its own virtual card, rewards and purchase protections can change, while refunds and payment failures can become harder to resolve. Both pieces are well worth reading.

Wouldn’t network tokenization be a more practical way to preserve the user’s chosen card and existing issuer relationship? Combined with agent authentication and consumer recognition through TAP (Trusted Agent Protocol), it could offer a much more compelling approach to interoperability across agents, merchants, and existing payment infrastructure than substituting the user’s card.

If you’re curious about how network token payments work, take a look at this Visa-authored technical draft:

text:
AI will keep booming while AI stocks keep collapsing.

Palantir reports TODAY, and the results could explain why.

A boom in AI usage doesn’t mean a boom in AI profits. And stocks trade on profits.

October showed it. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.8%+, wiping out over $2T. Chip stocks slid into a bear market.

But AI usage didn’t slow down. The bill just got bigger.

Look at Amazon. AWS revenue grew 39% last quarter. Demand is clearly there. But Amazon’s free cash flow over the past year was negative $42.4B, mostly because of AI infrastructure.

Meta tells the same story. It spent $34.9B on capex last quarter, more than its operations brought in.

That’s the problem. The companies building AI are paying for it now. The returns come later, if they come at all.

So investors are selling first and asking questions later.

But not every AI stock is falling.

Palantir is up about 60% in three months

Palantir doesn’t buy the chips or build the data centers. It sells the software that puts AI to work.

Big Tech carries the cost. Palantir collects the revenue.

And the revenue is real.

Last quarter, US commercial revenue grew 149%. But customer count grew only 35%. That means existing clients are spending much more. Net dollar retention of 157% confirms it.

And it’s profitable. GAAP operating margin hit 47%.

That’s what investors want from AI: real spending, real profit.

But even here, expectations are huge.

Wall Street wants about $2.18B in revenue and $0.41 in adjusted EPS tonight. Roughly 85% growth would only meet the bar.

Tonight, watch three things:

- Are customers still spending more?
- Are margins holding?
- Does the Q4 outlook actually improve?

The last one is a trap.

Say Palantir beats Q3 by $100M and raises its full-year forecast by $100M. Sounds great. But the Q4 outlook hasn’t changed at all.

Palantir isn’t bulletproof either. It fell 6.3% on Friday as the selloff spread.

That’s the AI market right now.

The technology is winning. The question is which shareholders get paid for it.

text:
The neocloud boom is the most exciting thing happening in AI infrastructure right now, and it's also where the gap between talking and building is widest

Every week I see another team announce they're "becoming a cloud". Some raised for a different idea and found that GPU capacity is the thing customers are actually paying for. Rental rates keep moving up, demand keeps outrunning supply and the capital is there, so it makes sense that people are jumping in

What a lot of new entrants learn the hard way is that the business barely lives in the GPUs. You can wire money for hardware in an afternoon. Then you need power that's actually contracted, a site with the right cooling, networking that holds up under real training loads, and a crew that can get all of it live on the exact date you promised your customer

That ready for service date is everything. A customer who signed for capacity in March has a model to train, a product to ship and their own investors to answer to. If you slip by two months, you've pushed their whole roadmap back

So the providers who win this cycle look a bit boring from the outside. They've brought clusters online before. They know the local electrician by name. They plan for the transformer arriving late and the permit taking longer than it should. They treat a delivery date like a promise to someone else's business

That's also what lenders and customers will pay up for. Plenty of buyers want to work with smaller and more flexible providers because the big clouds can't always give them the capacity, the timing or the price they need. That demand is real and it keeps growing. What they need is confidence that the capacity will actually show up

The long tail of compute providers is here to stay and it's healthy for the whole market. Over the next couple of years the ones who execute will pull way ahead, and the teams who can bring a cluster online on time, every time, are going to be worth their weight in gold

At Aethir we spend a lot of time on exactly this, because getting the compute to show up is the whole job

If you're building in this space, go hire the people who've done it before. They're the scarcest resource in AI right now

text:
最近几天，美股科技板块正在经历一场由“AI 资本开支恐慌”引发的血洗。

Alphabet（谷歌）单日暴跌 12.6% 创下历史最差纪录，英特尔随之崩盘，整个 AI 交易主线剧烈震荡。
 
大家都在焦虑“AI 算力泡沫是不是终于要破了”，来看看顶级对冲基金大佬 @BillAckman 的最新操作与复盘。

在最新的一场播客中，Ackman 详细拆解了他最近两笔极具反共识的美股调仓：在暴跌前清仓谷歌，并重新买回了奈飞（Netflix）。

为什么卖 $GOOGL ？—— 绝对的估值纪律

散户总喜欢在科技共识最强的时候追高，而巨鳄只在恐慌中买入安全边际。

2023 年初，当市场被 ChatGPT 吓坏、铺天盖地都是“谷歌搜索已死”时，Ackman 趁着估值被极度压低重仓了 Alphabet。而今天，当 Alphabet 涨回高位，未来的远期年化回报率已经无法满足他苛刻的复利门槛。

在资本分配的数学模型里，只要价格透支了确定性，哪怕是 AI 巨头也必须无情离场，给高回报标的让位。

为什么买回 $NFLX  ？—— 现金流印钞机的“半价时刻” 

2022 年奈飞管理层因用户流失而惊慌失措、推翻“绝不碰广告”的核心原则时，他曾在 275 美元果断认亏清仓，因为“企业走向的确定性被击碎了”。 但事实证明，奈飞随后展现了恐怖的执行力，不仅广告体系大获成功，更是彻底熬死了迪士尼等流媒体对手，变成了一台庞大的自由现金流印钞机。

前段时间，市场仅因单日停留时长的轻微波动就恐慌抛售，导致奈飞股价腰斩。面对一家垄断壁垒更强、高度可预测的伟大企业被打到半价，他毫不犹豫地再次重仓出击。

AI 算力到底有没有泡沫？

面对当下的科技股抛售潮，Ackman 的判断是，算力需求正在无限接近超级智能，这并非虚假的伪需求。当前 AI 真正的隐忧和天花板，根本不是算力过剩，底层的“能源瓶颈”与高息环境下的“资本杠杆”更需关注。

SPACEX IN TALKS TO BUY BOOST MOBILE OR ACCESS ITS NETWORK: WAPO

SpaceX $SPCX is reportedly in talks with EchoStar $ECHO over a potential acquisition of Boost Mobile or a deal to use its wireless network, as Elon Musk looks to launch a full-fledged U.S. cellphone service.

Musk previously approached Verizon $VZ, AT&T $T and T-Mobile $TMUS seeking access to their networks, but all three rejected the proposal.

He then met with EchoStar Chairman Charlie Ergen last month to discuss a potential deal.

Boost Mobile is an existing low-cost U.S. wireless carrier that sells phone plans to consumers using network access leased from AT&T and T-Mobile.

Acquiring Boost could give SpaceX an established wireless business, an existing customer base and access to nationwide cellular coverage without having to build its entire ground infrastructure from scratch.

That would offer Musk a potential shortcut into the estimated $235B U.S. wireless market.

The idea is to combine Starlink's satellite coverage with traditional cellular networks, which remain essential in densely populated cities where direct-to-satellite connections are less efficient.

SpaceX also recently agreed to acquire roughly $8B in additional wireless spectrum to support its mobile ambitions.

However, Boost's existing network agreements may not automatically transfer to SpaceX, meaning AT&T and T-Mobile could still need to approve access.

Talks remain ongoing, and no deal has been reached.

text:
trivia:

• started working on the game as a side project 4 days ago, landing ~1,150 PRs 
• every time i found an issue in the code i asked bot to make a lint rule against it
• used TLA+ heavily to find bugs in the game's various state machines: the story, cutscenes, the game's systems. there are many formal verification skills, one for each major system
• i put context into the filepaths: code that runs every frame or every tick gets a .hot.ts extension, and a lint rule bans allocating in it (no object literals, closures, new, etc.), so the game loop creates almost no garbage and GC doesn't cause stutters
• game engine is mostly custom. three.js draws the 3D scene, but the simulation, post-processing and audio are all ours
• the simulation is fully deterministic, so every run replays exactly from its inputs. when you post a high score, the server replays your whole run to check it isn't cheated
• we generate dynamic og:images for every run based on your final stats, and it's all localized too! the game supports 10 languages
• my favorite feature: the music seamlessly transitions into different music for the various biomes, continuing the previous melody
• no audio files. all the music and sound effects are synthesized live in the browser by a custom Game Boy-style chip (two pulse voices, a wave voice, noise) plus a synthwave layer. the songs are written as text in code
• all the pixel art is code. every sprite is a file drawn with one shared palette and packed into a sprite atlas at build time
• it runs inside an X post, from the 245px card up to full screen. the bar is 60 fps with 500 enemies on a mid-range phone
• the build fails if the first download goes over budget. it's about 124 KB gzipped right now
• bots play the game headless to tune each difficulty against target survival rates
• comments are banned by a lint rule. if code needs explaining, the fix is a better name or a test

text:
AI 安全圈一个细思极恐的爆料。

Jun Song 说，昨天有匿名黑帽黑客团队找上门，开出天价，希望他用海量真实攻击数据，对开源大模型进行强化学习（RL）后训练。

最恐怖是数据规模。

他之前参与的一个白帽项目，使用 GLM-5.3，仅用了对方声称掌握数据量的不到 1%，就已经在相关安全任务上大幅超越前沿模型。

注意，是不到 1%。

他拒绝了这笔交易。

他说的最后一句话让人后背发凉：

“我拒绝了，但迟早会有人接受。”

这可能是 AI 安全领域最值得警惕的趋势之一：

当开源大模型 + 强化学习 + 海量真实漏洞利用数据结合，AI 的攻击能力可能会以远超预期的速度进化。

我们现在更应该担心的是：谁在训练AI，以及谁愿意为它的攻击能力付出天价。

（以上基于 Jun Song 的公开自述）

Meta's AI spending is increasingly becoming a CREDIT risk:

Meta's, $META, 5-year credit default swap (CDS) spread, which measures the cost of insuring against default, has surged to 127.9 basis points, up from just 49.9 bps a year ago and approaching its October 23rd high of 130.5 bps.

Meanwhile, S&P Global Ratings lowered its outlook on the company from stable to negative, while affirming its AA- credit rating, citing rising leverage and growing pressure from AI-related spending.

S&P expects Meta's CapEx to reach $140 billion in 2026 and accelerate to more than $225 billion in 2027, while leverage could exceed 1.0x next year, up from approximately 0.1x in 2025.

The firm has also disclosed more than $800 billion in future spending commitments, with nearly 50% tied to leases that have not yet begun, largely for data centers and energy infrastructure.

Crucially, S&P considers Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments more limited than that of its peers, warning that it remains unclear when AI spending will generate enough revenue to offset rising costs.

Credit risk is surging among Big Tech amid record debt issuance and AI spending.

text:
Musa (AS) stood beneath the shade of a tree.

Far from his home,
With no wealth, no provisions,
And no certainty of what tomorrow would bring.

He had helped two strangers,
Then withdrew into the shade,
With nothing to offer his Lord
But the truth of his condition.

And from the depths of his need, he whispered:

رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

“My Lord, indeed I am in desperate need of whatever good You send down to me.”
Qur’an 28:24

O my Lord,

Musa sat beneath a tree,
But I have spent my life beneath the shade of Your mercy,
And only now am I beginning to see it.

How many mornings have You awakened me,
While I slept through the remembrance of You?

How many doors have You opened,
While I stood before the ones You had closed?

How many times have You carried me,
While I believed I was walking on my own?

Ya Rabbi,

I spent my life asking You for things,
Never realizing that what I needed most
Was to be freed from needing anything but You.

I asked for wealth,
But forgot the One who provides.

I asked for peace,
But searched for it everywhere except in Your remembrance.

I asked for guidance,
Yet resisted when You turned me away
From the very things that were keeping me from You.

Forgive me, my Lord.

I did not know how poor I was
Until You allowed me to see
That nothing I possess has ever truly belonged to me.

Not my strength.
Not my knowledge.
Not my good deeds.

Not even this longing that now fills my heart.

For how could I have searched for You,
Had You not first awakened the desire to seek?

O Beloved,

I have come to Your door with empty hands.

But even these hands are Yours.

I have come with a broken heart.

But even its breaking
May be a mercy I have yet to understand.

I have come with tears.

But I cannot claim them,
For You are the One who softened the heart
That once could not weep.

Ya Rabbi,

I am tired of pretending to know what is best for me.

I have followed my desires
And called them destiny.

I have mistaken my fears for wisdom,
My attachments for love,
And my own voice for guidance.

How many times have I begged You
To open a door
That Your mercy had closed?

How many times have I wept
Over something You withheld,
Not knowing what You were protecting me from?

Forgive my ignorance.

I do not know what is good for me.
I do not even know what to ask of You.

So I ask as Musa asked:

Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir.

My Lord,
Whatever goodness You choose for me,
I am in need of it.

If it is patience, grant me patience.

If it is purification, cleanse me.

If it is forgiveness, forgive me.

If it is a trial, grant me the strength
To remain grateful and steadfast through it.

If it is a blessing,
Do not let that blessing make me forget You.

And if it is something I have never imagined,
Something my limited understanding cannot comprehend,
Then grant me a heart that trusts Your wisdom
More than its own desires.

O my Lord,

I once thought surrender meant giving up.

Now I begin to understand
That surrender is to stop struggling
Against the One who has never stopped caring for me.

I once thought poverty meant having nothing.

Now I see that true poverty
Is to recognize that everything is Yours.

And I once thought I was seeking You.

Until I realized
That every step toward Your door
Was possible only through Your mercy.

Ya Rabbi,

Do not give me everything I ask for.

Give me what brings me nearer to You.

Do not make my life free of every difficulty.

Make my heart free of everything
That keeps it from remembering You.

Do not leave me to my knowledge,
For I know nothing.

Do not leave me to my strength,
For I have none without You.

Do not leave me to my own will,
For I have spent a lifetime
Mistaking my desires for what is good.

I am nothing.
I have nothing.
I know nothing.

And yet, my Lord,
You have given me everything
By allowing me to call upon You.

Why Hyperliquid, and why now?

Hyperliquid is where a lack of privacy costs large traders on every trade, and public exposure is holding back desks and funds who want to trade there.

After screening 332,317 wallets over 30 days, ShieldTX studied the impact of copy-trading on seven top perp traders and found a median execution loss of 63 bps per trade.

Hyperliquid can't capture the flow that needs privacy while every position remains public. ShieldTX routes that flow to @HyperliquidX, with the enterprise-grade privacy large traders need.

We've spent months speaking with whales, trading desks, market makers and digital asset funds who want to use the platform without the public exposure. They want privacy from competitors and copy-bots, without giving up compliance.

The current solutions aren't enough:

• Hyperliquid sub-accounts link to the main account onchain
• Multi-wallet rotation gets exposed by Arkham and other analytics platforms
• Third-party privacy solutions still expose a trader's PnL onchain

ShieldTX is built to close this gap.

Every trade is placed on Hyperliquid from a brand-new Hyperliquid wallet. Nothing links the trade onchain to the trader, and nothing links the trades together. A full trading history is available to users for audits and compliance.

ShieldTX is the on-ramp for crypto-native desks today, and the institutions who come next.
