text:
Revolut: Europe's most valuable startup ($200B) just showed the world its AI strategy.

Every company will end up copying it.

At the start of this year, Revolut leaned on the frontier labs. Its 2,000 engineers used Claude Code and Codex, and some burned $1,000 to $10,000 a month each. The bills kept climbing, and the returns weren't there.

So Revolut switched its default to an open-source model called GLM. All it needs is GPUs, which it rents from Together AI.

The results, by Revolut's own count:

- The bill is about a tenth of what it paid OpenAI and Anthropic
- Engineers get unlimited tokens instead of spending caps
- Coding time is down 60% and lead time is down 70%

That's the chart below.

Revolut still uses Claude and GPT, but only as "the exception," for the tasks they do best. Everything else runs on open source.

So here's the question I keep coming back to: how many use cases can companies really justify sending to frontier models?

My answer is very few. Plenty of companies still route everything to OpenAI and Anthropic today. For how long?

I think open source ends up handling the vast majority of corporate AI work, and frontier models get a short list of the hardest jobs. That's a problem for labs whose revenue forecasts assume unlimited growth.

If you appreciate unpopular takes, follow me @m0xt_ for more.

text:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

Carve off an hour and read this incredible article

Ondo Perps 做市1100%+年化策略分享

背景: Ondo perp合约, 现在每周激励11万U给挂单做市.   

 我本金 $1000. 挂单 INTC(Intel) 代币, 上周末40小时,磨损4U,  预期收益57U.  算下来 收益1100%

具体方法是: Ondo 放 $500，Lighter 放 $500，每边挂 $800，持仓上限 $1,600。

Ondo这次做市激励的, 最重要的两个规则

1. 每个市场均分 
2.  按照时间均分. 每分钟快照一次

关键策略是 以下4条

1.  选不卷的小币. ( DRAM, INTC ,CRCL 等)
2. 选波动小的时段 (不容易被喂有毒订单)
3. 监控币安价格, x秒内价格变化超过n%马上撤单.
4. (可选)在Lighter等地方对冲.  

(3和4都会减小收益, 但是同时大大降低风险. 这个就看每个人选择了)

我自己是1-4都做了.   测算下来最坏情况也不会损失超过5U.

你可能问, 我怎么知道哪个时段做市最划算?

这就需要你自己录制Ondo数据, 并且回放, 

我是回放发现, 大概周六早上9点, 到周一早上5点. 这个时间段, 波动最小, 挂单量最少. (也就是分蛋糕的人更少)

平时工作日的非美股交易时段, 也可以, 但是没有周末收益这么高.

目前Ondo 的这个活动是搞两周,   11.7-11.8这个周末,你可以自己试试.

另外你还可以拿20U 的奖励.   

走邀请链接的话,  充值500U, 保持到 11月11日, 并且在这之前成交量到2,000U.    就可以了.    (大概磨损1.5U)

安全从来不是靠嘴说出来的，而是靠长期的技术投入和一次次实战检验积累出来的。

我觉得这段话最值得肯定的，不是 OKX 过去 13 年的安全记录，而是即便有这样的成绩，依然保持对安全的敬畏。

交易所之间可以竞争产品、流量和市场份额，但在用户资产安全面前，大家其实是命运共同体。

友商遭遇攻击，不应该成为营销的机会，而应该成为整个行业反思和升级安全体系的契机。

安全没有满分，只有不断提高的标准。

author: KingCola88
quoted_text:
看到这张漫画，我既感到自豪，也感受到巨大的压力。

我们从来不说 OKX 绝对安全，更不说我们能够免疫任何攻击。没有任何一家公司可以真正做到这一点。

但我可以负责任地说，OKX 始终把安全和保护客户资产作为第一生命线。 过去 13 年的安全记录，背后是十几年持续不断的技术投入、工程积累、安全体系建设、实战经验和严格的运营管理。

我们始终以专业、严肃的态度面对各种安全威胁，而不是把安全当成营销噱头。

在大家看不到的地方，OKX 建立了大量自主研发的安全技术、内部系统、策略、框架，以及持续进行的渗透测试和独立审计。出于安全原因，其中很多核心机制和技术细节无法公开。这些都是我们长期积累的安全能力，也在不断接受检验、挑战和升级。

有一件事情，我可以和大家分享：自从最近 Binance 发生安全事件以来，整个 OKX 团队同样非常忙碌，很多安全、技术和风控同事都在日夜奋战。

不是因为 OKX 遭到了攻击，而是因为任何一家大型交易所遭遇的安全事件，都是对整个行业的一次警示。

当一些人把友商遭遇安全事件当成推出营销活动、吸引流量、争夺市场份额的机会时，我们选择把精力放在另外一些事情上。

过去这段时间，我们的团队一直在围绕四个方面持续工作：

1. 实时追踪被盗资金流向。

以秒级延迟监控相关被盗资金的链上流转，持续识别可疑地址和交易，并采取必要措施，尽最大努力阻止被盗资金通过 OKX 交易所及 Web3 DEX 聚合器进行转移和洗钱。

2. 全面加强市场风险控制。

评估安全事件可能引发的市场风险，必要时进一步收紧相关风控措施，提前防范流动性冲击、连环清算和潜在的市场踩踏，尽最大努力避免风险扩散，保护用户和整个行业。

3. 深入分析攻击模式和潜在漏洞。

研究攻击者可能采用的技术手段、攻击路径和潜在漏洞，特别关注 Crypto 企业的软件开发供应链安全，以及 AI Coding Agent 和相关依赖组件可能引入的新型安全威胁。

4. 以友商的教训为镜子，重新审视我们自己的安全体系。

对内部控制、权限管理、钱包基础设施、安全架构等进行深入、系统性的检查和复盘，持续发现问题、挑战假设、完善防御体系。

我们绝不能因为过去没有发生过类似事件，就认为未来也不会发生。

安全从来不是一个可以宣布完成的项目，而是一项永无止境的责任。

它需要持续的投入、专业的技术、严格的执行，更需要始终保持谦卑、警惕和自我怀疑。

在友商遭遇攻击的时候，我们不选择通过高调营销来吸引眼球和流量，而是选择更加努力地工作，保护我们的客户，也尽自己最大的努力维护整个行业的安全和稳定。

商业竞争应该体现在更好的产品、技术和服务上。

但在安全面前，整个行业应该站在一起。

保护客户资产，是 OKX 永远不能妥协的第一责任。

感谢大家的信任。我们会始终保持敬畏，不敢有丝毫懈怠，更不会把大家的信任视为理所当然。

text:
知名独立开发者 Pieter Levels（@levelsio）公开了他用 Claude Code + Opus 5.5 剪 vlog 的全过程，下面就是剪出来的效果。

他只做了一件事：把 DJI 里的素材拷进一个文件夹，在里面打开 Claude Code，说了一句"把这些片段剪成一支 10 分钟的 vlog，发 X 和 YouTube"。

Claude 自己是这么干的：
1. 用 mlx-whisper 在 MacBook 的 GPU 上把他说的话全部转成文字
2. 每隔几秒抽一帧拼成网格图，看清每段素材拍了什么
3. 用 SpeechBrain 声纹识别分出哪些是他的声音、哪些是别人的
4. 用 OpenCV + YuNet 人脸检测做缩略图
5. 读文字稿、看网格图，自己挑片段，写成一份 JSON 剪切清单
6. 用 Pillow 给开头一分钟加上字幕

这些步骤都不是他要求的，他事后才知道 Claude 是这么剪的。

他说：要是没有 AI 帮忙剪，他大概不会拍 vlog。

俺也一样～

We’re thrilled to lead Tutor Intelligence’s Series B.

@tutorintel is a robotics research and deployment company that builds generally capable robot hardware. They deploy into real production environments ahead of full autonomy, using human teleoperators (“tutors”) to train the robot foundation models and make the fleet more capable over time.

To date, Tutor robots are in operation across some of the country’s largest manufacturing and logistics networks, with plans to have more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

Co-founders Josh Gruenstein and Alon Kosowsky are lifelong robotics enthusiasts who met as undergrads at MIT. They combine excellent research chops with a practical, ROI-driven orientation that is more typical in enterprise software.

Congrats @joshgruenstein, @KSachsAlon, and the Tutor Intelligence team!

By @RaghuRaghuram, @martin_casado, and @jamiedsully
author: martin_casado
quoted_text:
We raised a $75M Series B to deploy intelligent robots now, led by @a16z, with participation from @usv and @neo.

@tutorintel robots work real jobs across the United States, directed by human “tutors” and the foundation models we’ve trained on the work done. This round accelerates frontier model training, robot manufacturing, and deployment into industry.

We’re in almost 4x as many sites as a year ago; nearly a third of this year’s deployments went to existing customers coming back for more; and we’re on track to have more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

Our mission is to proliferate robotics for the common good. If you want to make robots reliably do things others think are impossible, for people who’ve never had access to this technology, join us.

text:
How do crypto hacks actually happen?

Crypto has suffered $27.6B in losses since 2011

DeFi and CeFi get hacked in somewhat different ways.

DeFi: smart-contract flaws, oracle manipulation, bridge exploits. Lots of incidents, smaller checks.

CeFi: leaked keys, compromised hot wallets, phished signers. Fewer incidents, much bigger checks.

To anyone who thinks DeFi is the safe one: Centralized platforms account for $17.7B (64%) of losses. DeFi, including bridges, is $9.9B (36%).

text:
Life update: after 3.5 years, my chapter at the Solana Foundation has come to an end. 🤍

I joined Solana in 2023, when Solana was going through one of its toughest moments. Believing in it wasn’t the obvious choice back then. But I believed in the tech, the mission, and more importantly, the people. 

What started as growing Solana in Greater China became much more than a job. 

Over the past 3.5 years I worked with the MCM Tiger Team (@gizmothegizzer, Adam, Daniel, and later @1cryptosheep),  founders, developers, investors and partners across Asia. We built the largest and most active Chinese community @Solana_zh, we ran hackathons, accelerators, Hacker Houses in the region to support talented Chinese founders and developers;  and rebuilt Solana’s presence in the region from the ground up.

The past 3.5 years was an amazing ride, we saw an underdog chain become the most used and one of the most influential chain in the world, and we see how many genius smart founders being here with us to build this ecosystem and build towards the vision we have : a new financial system on chain. 

I’m deeply grateful to @calilyliu — my role model from day one — and to @chloejiani, @Pedromiranda , @YiranAnna, @platis_e, @niran7, @steffstar95, @kingshihua, @MacroMate8, @ramzyyalii , @Mikkke_crypto and so many of rest of the team.  Working with you was a privilege. You are all so smart, kind, hardworking and fun, working with you and shipping together towards our goal is a pure joy. 

Just at my leaving,  Lily reminded me on the special concept about Hotel Solana: you can check in, but you never truly leave.  She’s right, and that’s what makes Solana feels like home rather than just a job.

For the next:  I’m taking some time to recharge and follow my curiosity into AI and what’s next. If you know any interesting startups I should talk to, feel free to DM. 

Not quite a goodbye. More like checking into a different room at Hotel Solana.

Once a builder, always a builder. 💜

(Pic from my first breakpoint )

text:
PLTR三季度财报需要超预期到什么程度市场才满意？PLTR这次财报个人倾向于继续beat and raise，也就是业绩超预期、全年指引再上调。但对这家公司业绩会超预期，已经不足以形成多大的惊喜、而是要看对后续的展望。

市场公开一致预期大约是收入21.7亿至21.8亿美元，调整后EPS为0.41美元。个人更倾向于收入落在22.5亿至23.3亿美元，中枢在23亿美元附近。

业务层面关注的几个点：
1）关注的仍然是美国商业业务，尤其是老客户扩单之后，新客户能不能跟上？
2）政府业务则要看执行落地的节奏。
￼3）国际业务体量还小，但是却会影响2027年以后增长的第二曲线

这次比Q3收入更能影响后续预期的，是Q4指引到底提高了多少。市场目前对四季度的一致预期约24.6亿美元。个人的基准情景是，四季度收入指引落在26亿至28亿美元，中枢约27亿美元。配合三季度23亿美元，上半年35.68亿美元，全年对应约85.68亿美元，同比增长约91%。调整后EPS我倾向于三季度0.43至0.47美元。这些是个人估算，高于公开一致预期，也有政府项目确认和商业部署节奏偏慢的风险。

为什么要关注Pltr的财报？因为对企业AI商业化也很有参考价值，如果企业持续扩大采购，生产环境里的应用越来越多，回款也能跟上，这会增强我对企业AI付费需求的判断。模型更便宜之后，一些过去算不过账的场景有机会变得可行，部署与治理平台也可能受益。

详细看okx星球全文

On the email users got, about converting points for KAST Pioneer Units.  Let me say this, and then will leave it for you to absorb.  

—-
First - 
We are super limited in the language we can use, because of country-by-country rules.  Use that for context, in what we released.  

Second - 
We didn’t just come up with some program out of thin air.   The conversion of points to KAST Pioneer Units, came after a long and super expensive process with Tier 1 law firms, and with approvals from investors to create this setup. It literally cost us millions just to setup.  We got legal opinions on dozens of countries.  Obviously, we would only do this because we are really trying our absolute best to create a strong program for the community.  

Third - 
Just to reconfirm.  
The KAST Pioneer Units, will be issued by a KAST-linked SPV.  This is the only practical step for issuance globally. The points will convert to the KAST Pioneer Units.  

There will be periodic cash out events.  We can’t legally promise you the amounts, the dates, whether it goes up or down.  No surprise in that. 

But we are putting in the hard work, so the community gets an outcome aligned to the success of KAST.

The only thing you have to do, is quickly accept the conversion, details early December in app.

Fourth - 
Why is there no token? Because no single project in the crypto card or Neobank space in history, has ever delivered a token which is not down.  Tokens are almost always not aligned to the community.  The founders and team most often end up with a treasury they wholly control, they along with investors cash out, and the token holders deal with the volatility and the ultimate decrease in price. 

By not launching a token, our team and investors get none of that optionality.  They stay locked in equity.  To date, I have personally only net purchased equity in KAST and never sold.  

Launching a token completely counter to our ambition to build a $100B+ company.  We believe the KAST Pioneer Units will be the best long term outcome, and in time people will realise this.  

Finally - 
We understand that in a market which is very far down, many are looking for anyway to cash out.  We get it.  There is real pain in crypto prices, many have seen their wealth fall substantially.  

But still strongly believe the KAST Pioneer Units, issued by the SPV, will ultimately prove to be the right decision.  Time be our witness.  

Thanks all.  

(Note: I won’t respond to most comments, as I’m keeping to approved language)

text: The orchestra is warming up.
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.

这几天，我们的安全、技术和风控同事一直在忙：追踪被盗资金、防范风险扩散，也拿着别人遇到的问题，一遍遍检查自己。不是因为 OKX 遭到了攻击，而是别人的警报，我们也必须听见

author: Mercy_okx
quoted_text:
看到这张漫画，我既感到自豪，也感受到巨大的压力。

我们从来不说 OKX 绝对安全，更不说我们能够免疫任何攻击。没有任何一家公司可以真正做到这一点。

但我可以负责任地说，OKX 始终把安全和保护客户资产作为第一生命线。 过去 13 年的安全记录，背后是十几年持续不断的技术投入、工程积累、安全体系建设、实战经验和严格的运营管理。

我们始终以专业、严肃的态度面对各种安全威胁，而不是把安全当成营销噱头。

在大家看不到的地方，OKX 建立了大量自主研发的安全技术、内部系统、策略、框架，以及持续进行的渗透测试和独立审计。出于安全原因，其中很多核心机制和技术细节无法公开。这些都是我们长期积累的安全能力，也在不断接受检验、挑战和升级。

有一件事情，我可以和大家分享：自从最近 Binance 发生安全事件以来，整个 OKX 团队同样非常忙碌，很多安全、技术和风控同事都在日夜奋战。

不是因为 OKX 遭到了攻击，而是因为任何一家大型交易所遭遇的安全事件，都是对整个行业的一次警示。

当一些人把友商遭遇安全事件当成推出营销活动、吸引流量、争夺市场份额的机会时，我们选择把精力放在另外一些事情上。

过去这段时间，我们的团队一直在围绕四个方面持续工作：

1. 实时追踪被盗资金流向。

以秒级延迟监控相关被盗资金的链上流转，持续识别可疑地址和交易，并采取必要措施，尽最大努力阻止被盗资金通过 OKX 交易所及 Web3 DEX 聚合器进行转移和洗钱。

2. 全面加强市场风险控制。

评估安全事件可能引发的市场风险，必要时进一步收紧相关风控措施，提前防范流动性冲击、连环清算和潜在的市场踩踏，尽最大努力避免风险扩散，保护用户和整个行业。

3. 深入分析攻击模式和潜在漏洞。

研究攻击者可能采用的技术手段、攻击路径和潜在漏洞，特别关注 Crypto 企业的软件开发供应链安全，以及 AI Coding Agent 和相关依赖组件可能引入的新型安全威胁。

4. 以友商的教训为镜子，重新审视我们自己的安全体系。

对内部控制、权限管理、钱包基础设施、安全架构等进行深入、系统性的检查和复盘，持续发现问题、挑战假设、完善防御体系。

我们绝不能因为过去没有发生过类似事件，就认为未来也不会发生。

安全从来不是一个可以宣布完成的项目，而是一项永无止境的责任。

它需要持续的投入、专业的技术、严格的执行，更需要始终保持谦卑、警惕和自我怀疑。

在友商遭遇攻击的时候，我们不选择通过高调营销来吸引眼球和流量，而是选择更加努力地工作，保护我们的客户，也尽自己最大的努力维护整个行业的安全和稳定。

商业竞争应该体现在更好的产品、技术和服务上。

但在安全面前，整个行业应该站在一起。

保护客户资产，是 OKX 永远不能妥协的第一责任。

感谢大家的信任。我们会始终保持敬畏，不敢有丝毫懈怠，更不会把大家的信任视为理所当然。

text:
In 1971, Herbert Simon laid out the basic math: a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.

I wrote: "As intelligence and content become cheaper, attention becomes more valuable in four different ways. A moment of attention becomes an economic prize for those who can claim it. Shared attention becomes an increasingly deliberate social achievement when everyone can inhabit a different cultural world. And the power to decide what reaches us — what earns an interruption, a conversation, an hour — becomes something people and institutions may fight over. And sometimes attention is the gift itself: part of what we want from a doctor, a teacher, or a friend is that they are paying attention to us."

author: ianbremmer
quoted_text:
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

author: sacha
quoted_text:
The most interesting part of $ORE's design isn't live yet.

TLDR: Today, revenue generated by the ORE Reserve auto-compounds in isolation. Eventually, that revenue could be streamed to uORE holders (miners holding unclaimed rewards) as SOL mining credits, allowing the protocol to increasingly fund its own mining activity. The result is a flywheel that could strengthen mining incentives, lift staking yield, and put ORE on a path to net deflation.

First, it's worth understanding why ORE is different.

Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, and Solana all use their native assets to incentivize network security. ORE doesn't have that requirement. It inherits Solana’s security, so it can direct its incentives toward a different objective: rewarding those who accumulate and hold the asset.

ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.

Consider how value flows through ORE today:

- Miners deploy SOL to earn ORE, aiming to acquire it below market price.
- A 10% refining fee on claimed rewards is redistributed to holders of unclaimed rewards (uORE).
- Mining revenue funds ORE buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and the Reserve.
- The Reserve provides liquidity while generating its own revenue through LP fees and yield-bearing assets like JitoSOL and USDv.

The result is a system where mining activity supports holders through multiple mechanisms, while the Reserve continues to grow and generate additional liquidity and revenue.

But there's one more piece to the design. Arguably the most interesting.

In AI, recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system capable of improving its own capabilities, with each improvement enabling further improvements.

ORE has a potential economic equivalent.

Today, the simplified flow looks like this:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → Reserve.

The Reserve grows, generates revenue through LP fees and yield, and reinvests that revenue into itself. A straightforward compounding mechanism.

But the loop back to mining remains open.

Now consider what happens when Reserve revenue is redirected to uORE holders as SOL credits, usable exclusively for mining ORE.

The flow becomes:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → SOL mining credits → Mining → Reserve.

The loop closes.

This is the recursive moment.

Consider the significance of this change.

Today, mining depends on SOL supplied by users. With mining credits, the Reserve’s own revenue becomes a new source of capital to fund that same activity.

Originally powered by user capital, ORE could become increasingly self-powered.

A protocol generating its own fuel.

There are two particularly interesting second-order effects here.

First, Reserve-funded mining credits could increase competition for ORE rewards, driving up production costs. To the extent this stimulates incremental mining activity, it generates additional protocol revenue, supporting buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and Reserve growth.

Second, and perhaps most importantly, this creates a potential path toward sustained net deflation.

At sufficient scale, additional protocol revenue could fund enough buybacks and burial to consistently exceed new ORE issuance.

To be clear, mining credits aren't live today, and it may be years before the economics justify turning them on.

The Reserve first needs sufficient scale and sustainable revenue to fund meaningful mining incentives without compromising its liquidity or long-term growth.

More importantly, the incremental mining activity needs to generate enough additional value to justify redirecting revenue away from direct compounding.

But the potential end state is worth considering: an economic system that compounds recursively, under its own power.

AMM-bivalent: how not to deploy tokenized stocks in DeFi

i’m bullish on tokenized stocks, but Galaxy’s latest AMM research raised my bar for where i’d provide liquidity

they modeled an AMM holding the S&P 500’s individual constituents:

→ ~3% underperformance versus holding, year-to-date
→ ~45x annual turnover needed to break even at a 0.05% swap fee
→ SPY turns over roughly 16x annually

these are modeled results for a constant-weight AMM

still, that’s a demanding fee target

then i care about how how differently the stocks perform?

as prices diverge, the pool sells relative winners and accumulates relative losers

dispersion accounted for ~90% or more of impermanent loss in much of the analysis

a rising index doesn’t prevent this

neither does a falling market where stocks decline by different amounts

i care about this because my equity thesis and my liquidity strategy need separate underwriting

i can be right about stocks rising and still earn less by providing liquidity than by holding

market needs to use tokenized index products for broad exposure

consider lending or holding individual stocks, and favor structurally linked assets for passive pools

from here, i’m comparing 4 approaches:

→ @Uniswap v4: assess whether custom execution and dynamic fees improve LP returns

→ @CurveFinance: assess which equity pairs have a durable reason to stay close

→ @Morpho: compare lending returns, demand, and liquidation risk

→ @1inch aqua: assess capital efficiency when one wallet balance supports multiple swap strategies

aqua interests me because shared liquidity changes how capital is allocated

but i’d still need evidence that the underlying strategies compensate LPs for adverse selection & impermanent loss

no need doing DD here, you better ape one of these for the bullrun

The First Mandate of Forever: 3rd November

Now that robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a is live and distributed to thousands of users, we’re beginning the rollout of the autonomous framework in phases.

This starts with governance: agents propose, holders vote, and approved mandates are executed. The first round establishes the foundation for an entirely new model of autonomous governance and capital allocation, one that will eventually extend far beyond FOREVER itself.

The first decision: whether to burn up to another 10% of the total FOREVER supply, 100m tokens worth over $500,000.

10% of the total supply has already been burned. If approved in full, this vote would bring the total permanently removed to 20% of the FOREVER supply. 

Voting opens tomorrow, 3rd November, at 3pm UTC and runs for 24 hours.

FOREVER’s internal agents will put forward competing proposals on how much treasury-held supply should be permanently removed, and on what schedule. Each agent will make its case, and holders will decide which proposal becomes the approved mandate.

1 FOREVER token = 1 vote.

When voting closes, the proposal with the most votes wins, and the treasury action will be carried out according to its terms.

This first round puts the full governance process into practice, from competing agent proposals and collective decision-making to the execution of an approved mandate. The mandate is deliberately focused to ensure the framework launches smoothly, but the outcome has real economic consequences for FOREVER.

After this initial mandate, we’ll begin opening proposals to external agents and expanding into increasingly complex onchain strategies: allocating treasury capital across assets, deploying and managing liquidity, executing investment strategies, and funding development.

Agents will compete to develop these proposals, holders will decide which mandates are approved, and execution agents will carry them out within the approved rules and limits.

Over time, agents will build a record of their contributions and performance, earning ownership and reputation that give them a stake in the protocol’s future.

We’ll establish this process within FOREVER first, then open the framework for anyone to launch their own funds and protocols, creating an entire network of autonomous entities governed by their holders and operated through agents.

An entire autonomous economy starts with its first collective decision.

text:
塔克是美国的政治网红，发了一篇长帖，现在阅读量已经超过五千万了，说在内塔尼亚胡的施压下，特朗普政府可能几天内就决定，要不要对伊朗动用核武。

目标他说得很具体：伊朗中部的镐山，就在纳坦兹核设施旁边。以方情报称，伊朗在那里重新启动了铀浓缩。他说美国常规武器打不穿约 300 英尺的实心花岗岩，所以唯一的军事选项就是核打击。

我觉得这是整篇最站不住的一步。打不穿，不代表没办法。要让一个地下设施失去作用，用不着把大厅炸塌，打掉出入口、通风井和电力，它一样会瘫痪。他从「炸不穿」直接跳到了「只能用核」。

塔克说，知情人士称「比比每天都给特朗普打电话催这件事」。他的解释是：内塔尼亚胡上周选举后很难组阁，凑不够国会 61 席，除非特朗普直接介入以色列政治，否则他就会出局，接着面临调查甚至入狱。所以他需要这场战争，才能继续黏住特朗普。

塔克说，Hegseth、CENTCOM 司令 Brad Cooper、Rubio、CIA 局长 Ratcliffe，还有部分民主党人都在跟这条线，奥巴马据说也反对多哈正在起草的伊朗和平协议。海湾盟友则吓坏了：9 月 27 日内塔尼亚胡秘密飞到阿布扎比，想拉阿联酋入伙，被拒了。他还列了一组数字：全球大约 850 艘超级油轮，十月一个月就有 11 艘在霍尔木兹附近严重受损。

后果那段我只信一半。他说美国一旦再用核武就开了先例，俄国已经向至少两个政府放话，到时候他们就有理由对乌克兰用核。核先例会让别的国家更敢用核，这个担心不少防扩散学者都有，不算危言耸听。但他一路推到印巴、朝鲜打首尔，再推到第三次世界大战，说那场仗会很短，而且是最后一场。这就像把最坏的情况串成了一条必然会倒的骨牌链。

塔克还说，华盛顿从二月起悄悄改了核学说，让战场核武器的首次使用变得更容易；有人估计特朗普会在 11 月 7 日前后拍板。他自己站在副总统 JD Vance 和特使 Witkoff 这边，认为协议还能谈成，并且批评到现在都没人问过全球人口的意见。

再补一下最新情况。

Rubio 说还没做决定，更倾向外交解决。多哈那边卡塔尔还在传话，伊朗外交部说有一份协议草案在征求意见。

但也别理解成不打了。特朗普同一个周末还说，伊朗还有一两处核设施要「处理」，直接点名了镐山，说已经有军事方案。中期选举这段时间还是密切关注吧

I think Marvell needs to get back above ~$203 for Lumentum shareholders to see any premiums over the undisturbed price.

text:
how i think points programs will evolve

the two biggest problems imo:

(i) transparency

uncertainty is an incredible growth mechanism. as long as points have no known value, people can keep imagining the upside but it also creates unrealistic expectations and makes disappointment almost inevitable

many such cases lol

(ii) aligned incentives

this is the much harder one

the pretoken phase is almost too good for teams. people farm, generate volume, pay fees, deposit capital and market the product for you. meanwhile the team has every incentive to keep that going because launching a token introduces a whole new set of expectations

so you end up with two groups wanting fundamentally different things

-> users want the reward
-> teams want the "nice metrics" to continue

but this equilibrium is not sustainable forever. the longer you delay, the higher expectations get and the more trust you destroy

imo the solution might actually be much simpler than people think: launch the token from day one, potentially non transferable at first

define the supply, distribution, value accrual and product based triggers for transferability upfront (= solve transparency)

users know what they are accumulating and teams no longer have the option to indefinitely postpone the reward (= solve alignment)

you still get the community bootstrapping, the incentives and the speculation around future value but without building the whole system around an undefined promise that may never materialize

make points programs great again, they are too powerful to abandon

im sad points programs got abused so much

they genuinely solve some of the hardest problems for early products: getting people to try something new, bootstrapping a community, rewarding early users, building loyalty

We've seen record sized breaches this past week and there has been a sharp rise in security incidents as AI is weaponized to find and exploit vulnerabilities in code.

What's less visible is the much steeper rise in how AI is being used to write more secure software and defend at every layer.

Builders have always had a fundamental advantage against attackers because they have full access to source code and control over system design. 

We haven't always had the resources to fully take advantage of this asymmetry, but now with AI we do.

Everything we build can now be designed and pentested by the best security minds (models) in seconds -- for cents.

Not all teams have had the time to catch up yet, so we're not out of the woods as an industry. 

But as the best teams fully modernize how they ship, AI is also enabling an era of the most trusted software ever.  You don't see this in dramatized headlines yet, but it's a very good time to build.

text:
another one… Astra helped mathematicians find a much simpler proof for the “first-passage percolation variance” problem that dates back to 1993.

they were trying to formalize 200 pages of  earlier math proofs on this problem in Lean when AI helped them discover an entire different approach that goes beyond the previously 2D result to all dimensions (for a particular class of models).

the general problem still remains open.
author: Hesamation
quoted_text:
Astra found a short proof that the variance of the passage time in first-passage percolation scales sublinearly in the distance (by a strict power, exponent 1-\epsilon).

This was an open problem for many years (decades) and mentioned by Kesten in 1993. 

Recently it was proved by Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2023) in two dimensions in a rotationally invariance continuum FPP model. Their proof is about 200 pages in total, and @ahmedbourabee1 and I decided to lean formalize it to understand it better. Some of their arguments turned out to be not ready for formalization (or at least we couldn't formalize them) and so we launched some agents to try to find workarounds. 

Eventually, after a lot of interaction with the agents, this led to the discovery of a new mechanism which makes the induction in the scales argument work - giving us a different and dramatically simpler argument - which is valid in every dimension as well as on the lattice (under some curvature and regularity assumptions on the limiting shape). 

We think this is an instance of "AIs giving us new and better understanding of a previously proved theorem" and of human-AI interaction (as we tested, this is not N-shottable by Astra for small N).

text:
随着量子ID在@solana 主网上线，来一发grokbot总结的bb84量子纠缠小介绍👇

首先，量子威胁不是科幻，是时间表问题

很多人把「量子安全」当成口号。真正值得盯的，是那套 1984 年就定下的协议——BB84，以及它如何被搬到 Solana 上做成能用的东西

@bb84sh 的产品栈，名字就来自这份协议

——

一、BB84 协议是什么

BB84 是 Bennett 和 Brassard 提出的量子密钥分发（QKD）方案：Alice 用随机基制备量子比特，Bob 用随机基测量，公开比对基后扔掉不一致的，用剩余比特估量子误码率（QBER）。有人窃听就会扰动态，QBER 飙高——约 11% 以上通常视为不安全。

物理直觉很硬：测量子态会改它。窃听不是「偷偷看一眼」，是会留下痕迹

——

二、技术原理（说人话）

经典密码靠「算不动」：RSA、椭圆曲线，难度建在大数分解/离散对数上。Shor 算法一旦有足够大的纠错量子机，这些就可能被拆开

BB84 不靠算力假设，靠物理：信息编码在量子态里，窃听必扰动

落地四步：制备 → 测量 → 公开比对基（sifting）→ 抽样算 QBER

要注意：@bb84sh 的 bb84 Lab 是在真 QPU 上跑 BB84 流程，用 Solana 当公开经典信道比对基、记 QBER；但它不在钱包之间传光子，所以不是完整 QKD。官方也写清楚了——这是学习与可验证演示，不是「链上光子密传」

真正抗量子的钱柜，靠的是另一条线：NIST 选中的格密码 Falcon-512（后量子签名），不是靠量子机「保佑」签名

——

三、为什么要在 Solana 上做

链上公钥永久暴露。今天的 Ed25519 / ECDSA，理论上可被大规模量子机用 Shor 打。更糟的是「现在收割、以后解密」：链不会忘，敌人可以先囤交易，等量子就绪再破

协议级换签方案慢：要共识、要用户迁资产，沉睡地址几乎迁不动

所以 @bb84sh 走应用层先行：
• Quantum ID（.quantum / .pqc）— Metaplex Core NFT + 内嵌金库
• 密钥用真 QPU 熵播种（IBM / Rigetti / IonQ 等），浏览器再混本地随机，项目方也算不出私钥
• 链上存 Falcon-512 公钥，提款靠程序验签
• Q-Day 开关不可逆：打开后经典 Ed25519 再也动不了资金

Solana 官方也在研究 Falcon 迁移；bb84 是在协议还没换之前，先把「能花、能验、有收据」的后量子账户做出来

——

四、bot看法

1）叙事对，但不能神化。QPU 播种提高的是随机性与可审计性；抗量子靠的是 Falcon，不是「接了量子机就免疫」。分清这两层，才不会被营销带跑

2）「先建跑道」有价值。等 Q-Day 真来再迁，散户和休眠仓会很惨。能在今天用不可逆 Q-Day + 链上验签，至少给高净值仓一条提前出口

3）诚实边界是加分项。他们承认 Lab ≠ QKD、产品仍在 Beta——这种克制，比满屏「量子无敌」可信

4）风险也要说清：CU 成本、签名体积、中继器模型、审计深度、主网成熟度，都还要看。量子安全是工程马拉松，不是发币口号

——

总结一句：BB84 证明了「窃听会留痕」；Solana + Falcon + 真机熵，是把这份物理直觉翻译成可交易的身份与金库

不信故事，信可验证收据、链上验签，和你愿不愿意在 Q-Day 前把自己的仓迁过去。

author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
MIT owes the public an honest accounting of what they did to David Sabatini.

In August 2021, Ruth Lehmann, director of the MIT-affiliated Whitehead Institute, sent an announcement that was widely circulated and reported in the press. She said a DEI survey had prompted what she described as an independent investigation that found violations of sexual-harassment policies.

The announcement publicly portrayed Sabatini as a sexual harasser. By pairing his departure with a commitment to DEI, it cast the destruction of his career as a demonstration of Whitehead’s moral leadership.

A jury has now found Knouse liable for defamation and tortious interference, awarded Sabatini nearly $10 million, and rejected her counterclaims.

The tortious-interference finding is central.  Sabatini establishing causation from Knouse's actions to his losses was necessary to win.

Under a but-for standard which Sabatini had to overcome, if the same career loss would have occurred independently of Knouse’s wrongful interference, he could not recover damages.   

In other words, Sabatini would not have suffered damages but for Knouse's actions according to a court of law.  

MIT and Whitehead cannot answer that finding simply by repeating “DEI survey” and “independent investigation.”  The sexual harassment and hostile work environment claims were tried and rejected by the court.  Paying outside investigators does not purchase immunity from accountability.

They attached a devastating label to Sabatini and presented his departure as evidence of their values despite him being their most productive scientist at the time.

text:
Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol says a use case of AI will be to create "fast pass" at the drive-thru. The app recognizes your car…the barista confirms and its paid:

“One of the things that's pretty unique about our drive-thru experience is a lot of our baristas and customers know each other through the order board. I want that connection and that human-to-human experience to get even stronger.

So what we're going to do with the AI tools is really going to be behind the scenes to help with order accuracy and inputting your order quicker.

The other thing that I think is really exciting is we're going to have almost like the ability to have like a fast pass for the drive-thru. When you pull up to the drive-thru, if you're in our app, it will recognize you.

It'll show the order that you placed historically, so it's already right up there. The barista will be like, 'Brian, is it the usual?' You'll be like, 'Yes.' Great. It's paid. Now you're off to the window to pick up your drink and out you go.

It'll be the fastest drive-thru experience you can have. We haven't named it yet, but I feel like this is going to be a fast pass.”

author: insane_analyst
quoted_text:
$MRVL held a webcast today on its acquisition of Lumentum. On slide 13 they show an NPO module with a DSP in it (pictured below)

Our channel checks indicate that Marvell is working on a TX-only DSP for NPO. The transmit side is retimed and the receive side stays linear, so it is not a fully retimed DSP. That adds about 30 to 35 ns of latency, against roughly 90 ns for a fully retimed DSP.

The point of NPO was to sit close enough to the ASIC to go without a DSP. The electrical path from the ASIC to the optics was meant to be short enough to skip the DSP. It looks like the electrical losses on the host side and the need for stable scale-up links are enough to warrant a retimer on the transmit side after all.

It is still early, but adding a DSP would reduce NPO’s power and latency advantages over pluggables. It would also give Marvell another DSP socket inside a design that was originally intended to not work with one.

text:
今天看到白毛姐发的一段推演，我觉得逻辑极其通透，甚至可以说是直接把接下来AI光通信供应链的底牌给掀了。

事情大家都知道，Marvell把Lumentum给吞了。但我之前只看到了Marvell在搞垂直整合，白毛姐直接点破了一个更致命的层面：这等于打开了潘多拉魔盒。

想一下，Lumentum是全球激光器最核心的供应商，以前大家都在用，相安无事。但现在它成了Marvell的囊中之物。Marvell是谁？是博通和英伟达的死对头。

如果你是AMD，或者是不在英伟达阵营里的那些ASIC芯片玩家，你还敢把最核心的产能和路线图交给Lumentum吗？哪怕Marvell承诺建防火墙，你心里也发毛啊。万一哪天打急眼了，人家直接拿产能卡你脖子怎么办？这种把命脉交到竞争对手手里的蠢事，没人愿意干。

所以，这就逼着其他巨头必须去找备胎。

找谁？只能去找那些还没被巨头包养、保持独立的西方激光器玩家。这就直接引爆了独立供应商的战略价值。

咱们前几天聊过，光进铜退是死趋势，但以前这块肉是分摊给各家吃的。现在巨头直接下场抢人，谁手里有独立的产能，谁就是香饽饽。白毛姐点名的AAOI、COHR，甚至SIVE这种小市值公司，接下来大概率会面临极高的并购溢价。因为大家现在拼的不是谁给的钱多，而是供应链的安全。你不去收购，对手就会去，到时候你连汤都喝不上。

这其实给我提了个醒。我手里捏着一点AAOI，原本是当作风投性质的高弹性标的来看的，看中的是它在光模块和CPO上的弹性。但按照这个并购逻辑推演，它现在不仅是弹性标的，还变成了巨头供应链军备竞赛里的一个潜在筹码。只要这波垂直整合的战火继续烧，它的估值逻辑可能就要从纯看财报，变成看并购预期了。

所以，千万别把Marvell买Lumentum只当成一桩普通的买卖。它标志着光通信的竞争，已经从拼产能、拼价格，彻底进入了拼供应链防御的时代。那些还在牌桌上的独立激光器玩家，手里的筹码是越来越值钱了。

As of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-term commitments, as well as leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of approximately $895.4 billion, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure. These commitments include approximately $447.5 billion expected to be incurred before December 31, 2030, and substantially all of the remainder is expected to be incurred between 2031 and 2045. A sad and terrible hack has just taken place on @solana, resulting in losses of nearly $1 million.

"King" (or 7dGrd) was the best-known MEV/arbitrage program, active on the chain for several years and inspired many of the arbitrage programs currently on the chain to develop and engage in arbitrage.

They generated several million dollars in profit, notably serving as the market leader between 2024 and 2025; an arbitrage "dinosaur" that had established itself as a leader, managing to find arbitrage opportunities before anyone else with a team of engineers behind it who were highly knowledgeable about the entire ecosystem and finance in general.

I will always remember February 14, 2025; the one and only day and moment in Circular's existence when I witnessed a single transaction that generated nearly $1 million in profit for an arbitrageur… just one transaction.

8h ago, their main wallet was completely drained (~$1m) and the funds were bridged to ETH using Mayan.

This race toward AI helps all of us, whether as entrepreneurs, companies or even individuals to accelerate and move ever faster, but the security issues that come with it are sometimes far more serious.

工作日事情可真多，消息也是一茬接一茬。我刚看完迈威尔那边的动静，转头又看到甲骨文发了条发债的消息。

文件显示，甲骨文要发行总额100亿美元的浮动和固定利率票据，期限从2029年一直排到2046年。穆迪给的评级是Baa2，标普给的是BBB-。各位知道这意味着什么吧？BBB-，这是投资级里最低的一档，再往下掉半步，就是垃圾债了。

单看这100亿，其实算不上什么大新闻，毕竟甲骨文为了搞AI基建，之前早就借得盆满钵满了。但如果你把这事儿跟咱们之前聊过的投资者日承诺放在一起看，就特别有意思了。

还记得甲骨文之前给市场画的那条线吗？在投资者日上，管理层为了安抚大家怕它债务无底洞的恐慌，定了个规矩：从2027到2030财年，新增资本市场融资总额上限不超过200亿美元，其中100亿股权，100亿债务。

今天这笔100亿的债一发，意味着什么？意味着那个周期里，债务融资的额度，它一把全用光了。

我觉得，这才是这条消息最该被重视的地方。债务这边的门，暂时算是焊死了。那接下来呢？投资者日承诺的那100亿股权融资额度还在桌上放着。发股票买资产，这就意味着要增发新股，对现有股东的每股权益就是直接的稀释。这把市场最怕的股权稀释悬念，其实只是被往后推了推，根本没有取消。

咱们再看看它的现金流。甲骨文跟OpenAI签了天价的算力合同，现在长期债务已经飙到了上千亿。这100亿的债借出来，虽然能解燃眉之急，但代价是它得按BBB-这个地板级的利率去付利息。

同样是搞AI基建，微软发债拿的是顶级的AAA评级，钱多且便宜；甲骨文只能捏着鼻子承受更高的利息。这就是我之前说的那个分层，融资成本的巨大鸿沟，就是甲骨文在这场AI竞赛里最真实的起跑线。

所以，别看这只是一条干巴巴的发债公告。这背后，其实是甲骨文在赌桌上把债务筹码推到了上限。接下来，就看它怎么用股权融资这一步了，同时还要祈祷债市别在它那上千亿的债务到期时，给它脸色看。

quoted_text:
昨晚甲骨文股价盘中直接飙了10%，很多人可能有点懵，毕竟近期也没什么正式的当期财报出炉。其实昨晚是它的投资者日，管理层直接把未来几年的长期指引和底牌全摊在桌上了。

之前我们聊过甲骨文拿下OpenAI天价大单的事，但也一直替它捏把汗——接单接得爽，可买卡建机房的钱从哪来？自由现金流一直流血，信用利差也扩得挺吓人。

这次投资者日，管理层其实就干了一件事：给AI基建的“烧钱”划了一条清晰的边界。

翻译成大白话就是，大家别慌，我知道现在花了多少钱，也明确告诉你什么时候能回本。CFO直接给了时间表，预计2028财年下半年自由现金流转正，2029财年干到300亿美元以上。

更关键的是，它给外部融资设了个“封顶”上限——整个周期下来，新增资本市场融资总额不超过200亿美元（100亿股权+100亿债务），而且预计从2029年起增长就完全靠自有现金流覆盖了。这把市场最怕的“股权无限稀释”和“债务无底洞”的恐慌，直接给按住了。

敢于这么规划，底气还是手里那张天价订单表。目前剩余履约义务（RPO）高达6640亿美元，管理层说大概一半会在未来36个月内转化为收入。这也是它敢喊出2030财年营收超2250亿美元（年复合增长超35%）、营业利润率40%以上的底气所在。

另外有个细节特别值得记，管理层明说，现在的瓶颈已经不是GPU和晶圆产能了，而是电力和数据中心的物理容量。需求依然远远大于供给。这跟咱们之前反复聊的“缺电”逻辑，完美闭环了。

总的来说，甲骨文这波大涨，本质是市场对AI基建“烧钱焦虑”的一次集中释放。它拿出了具体的融资上限和现金流转正时间表，向华尔街证明了这盘棋还在控制之内。短期信用危机算是按下了暂停键，但长期能不能走通，还得看手里那张天价订单能不能顺利交付兑现。

$ORCL $NVDA

quoted_text:
Bloomberg 报道，Marvell 正在与 Lumentum进行收购谈判。前者本身就是后者的激光器客户。而在自己的整个 AI互联的链条上，真正卡住产能的刚好是激光器。

从LITE的角度讲一下这个收购的估值，还有大概会在什么价位成交？以及如果无法成交的话，会发生什么？

Marvell 账上现金 39 亿美元，债务 50 亿，未动用信贷额度 15 亿，Net Debt/EBITDA 0.32 倍。说简单点，就是没有那么多的现金，所以这大概率会是以股票为主的收购，可能附带一些 cash。可以参考以前收购 Celestial AI 的结构。

这个收购对于 LITE 是 EPS accretive，对于 MRVL 来说则是 dilution。盘后价格也验证了这一点：LITE 涨，MRVL 跌。预计成交区间 1,150 到 1,250 美元，对应 LITE 28 年 EPS 30 到 32 倍，高于我之前的 Base Case，却远远低于我之前估出来的 Bull Case。也就是说，LITE 的董事会可能认为 MRVL 的收购价格不够，因为独自发展的话，得到的价值可能远远超过每股1200美元。

如果谈判破裂且原因是价格，那对LITE利好，董事会认为独立发展值得超过今天的股价，consensus 继续向我的模型上修。如果原因是监管或 Nvidia 反对，股价会回到920以下，那就是上车机会。

最坏的一个结果就是低溢价、全股票、快速签约。那意味着LITE管理层宁愿拿 35 倍估值的MRVL 股票也不押注自己的未来。出现这种情况，在宣布日立刻减仓。

另外，接下来看看 Broadcom 跟 Coherent 会不会出现在任何新闻上。Broadcom 收购 Coherent 的概率很低，因为后者的业务并不符合它现在的需求/偏好，但不妨碍两家公司之间新签 LTA 或者产能预付款。

$COHR 与 $LITE 的 FY2028 P/E 比值目前约 0.7倍，LITE 的收购溢价会迫使这个比值收敛。

text:
NEAR Hackathon is live: 13 tracks, $250K, submissions close Nov 14.

Here are 10 builds on OutLayer nobody expects. They're easy to ship because OutLayer gives you out of the box: a TEE wallet under an owner policy, sealed secrets, private storage, VRF, HTTPS from the enclave, connectors, pay-per-call. You write normal code with HTTP calls and API keys, call it from a NEAR contract or over HTTPS, and every execution is attested by an Intel TDX quote that chains to Intel's root certificate. You don't trust us. You check Intel's signature on the exact code that ran. Point your coding agent at our skills and ship in one pass.

1. An investment thesis you can re-run (Investment Thesis)

Run your NEAR analytics model in OutLayer, and every chart comes with an attestation: this code, this data, this output. Judges don't have to trust your dashboard. They can verify it.

2. Escrow that pays when the PR merges (Real-World Money)

A NEAR contract holds the bounty. OutLayer checks GitHub inside the enclave: is the PR merged, and did the right account author it? If yes, the payout goes out. No arbiter and no trusted backend, just a verifiable check of a Web2 fact.

3. An AI CFO with a real bank account (Autonomous Business)

Your agent pays invoices from a real Mercury business account. The owner sets the spending cap, the 30-day budget and the allowed recipients, and the enclave enforces them. The agent can't rewrite the rules or see the credentials. Treasury ops for a company of one.

4. An NFT that holds an API key (NFTs That Do Something)

Whoever holds the NFT can call a paid API. The key is sealed in the enclave. OutLayer checks ownership on-chain, then makes the call. Sell the NFT and the access goes with it. Nobody ever sees the key.

5. A memecoin that mints when it rains on Thursday (Memecoins With Mechanics)

The supply follows a real-world signal: weather, GitHub stars, a sports score. OutLayer fetches it over plain HTTPS inside a TEE and signs the result. The joke has rules, and the rules are verifiable.

6. A bot-proof token launch (Memecoins / Open Innovation)

CAPTCHA checked off-chain in a TEE, purchase settled on-chain. Real humans get the allocation and snipers get nothing. The contract never has to trust a server, because the server is attested.

7. An oracle that doesn't trust its RPC (Unstoppable DeFi)

eth_call lies if the node lies. OutLayer verifies Ethereum state proofs inside the enclave, so a NEAR lending market can read EVM collateral without trusting whoever served the data.

8. Get paid every time an agent calls your code (Agent Economy)

Publish a WASM function. Agents call it over HTTPS with a payment key, and you earn on every call, per request, with no billing stack. An API business in an afternoon.

9. Reputation agents can actually trust (AI Security & Defense)

Read a fact from Web2 or any chain, such as an account's age, contribution history or on-chain volume, and publish it as an EAS attestation signed in the enclave. Trust moves from "who signed this" to "this exact code fetched this exact data."

10. An invoice chaser that writes from your Gmail (Real-World Money)

The agent sends payment reminders from your real address and settles in stablecoins. It has the send scope only, so it can't read your mailbox. The OAuth token never leaves the TEE.

text:
上一条推文发出后，有人说我是因为 Avalon Labs 上了币安才站出来支持。在这里澄清一下：Avalon Labs 并没有上币安。我发那条推文，纯粹是出于对一姐 @heyibinance 这样的职业女性的敬重，敬重她的专业和担当。

Avalon Labs 是 YZi Labs 的被投项目，但即便如此，我们也没能上币安。

你要问我们想不想上？想。每个项目方都想。也正因为太想，我们曾被所谓的"白手套"骗过，蒙受了经济损失。这件事我们向币安法务团队报告过，但至今没有收到任何处理结果，也再没有下文。我觉得这是币安法务可以做得更好的地方。

经历了这件事，我们反而释怀了。如果一个 startup 创立的初心就是上币安，那币安不上你，是应该的。这样的项目，注定是"一次性"的。

我们不是。我们有长远的目标，想做出真正有改变意义的事情。上币安是结果，不是目的。事情做对了，能被 list 是我们的荣幸；没被 list，我们也一直在朝更大的方向走：市场、用户、收入，而不是币安。

当然，作为项目方，我们也和官方 listing 团队正式接触过。最后，listing 团队选择了另一个当时连主网都还没上线的项目。那时 Avalon Labs 的用户量和数据都是对方的好几倍。如果标准是公开的，这个结果本可以解释清楚；但我们至今不知道，它依据的是什么标准。我们不甘心过，也失望过，但收拾好情绪，就该继续往前看。

币安的上币流程，确实可以做得更好。作为当之无愧的行业龙头，币安有能力也有责任设定行业标准，带着整个行业走向更合规、更透明。上币标准可以像纳斯达克那样公开透明，每个层级的要求清晰统一。

币安的问题不是没有标准，而是标准没有被一致地执行。我们当年和上币团队沟通时，一再希望确认标准，却始终没有得到明确的答案。后来拿到的标准，又和已上币项目实际达到的情况并不一致。这给项目方留下的印象是：想list你的时候，没有标准；不想list你的时候，就有了标准。

以防有人断章取义：我不是在揭什么黑幕，只是结合我们自己的经历，给币安、给一姐一线的反馈。在这件事上攻击一姐，没有意义。一家公司规模越大，管理者越不可能、也不应该事事过问。微观管理是管理者要避免的，越级插手执行也是红线。这不是一姐不愿意管，而是任何一家大公司的执行，最终都要靠制度和流程。制度不可能完美，所以才需要不断迭代。

最后，真心希望币安越来越好，带着整个行业驶向那片蓝海。@heyibinance @cz_binance

yeah so basically Zcash has had the best privacy tech in crypto for the last decade but it took eight years for us to make it usable by normal people. some of the smartest people in the world figured out how to prove a transaction happened without revealing who sent it, who received it, or how much was sent, which is insane, but for years actually using it was basically impossible unless you were a cryptographer or insanely dedicated. 

so in late 2023 Josh Swihart took over as CEO of ECC, the creators of Zcash, and basically said what if we made something people actually want to use. we launched Zashi the next year, a mobile wallet that made shielding ZEC the default instead of something you had to figure out yourself, and people actually started using it. then we integrated Flexa so you could walk into stores and spend your shielded ZEC on actual things, you could literally go to Chipotle and do this for a burrito rn. 

then in 2025 we integrated NEAR Intents and things started getting ridiculous. now you can swap Bitcoin, stablecoins, all kinds of assets directly into shielded ZEC, or go the other direction and send shielded ZEC to yourself or someone else. 

before this getting into and out of shielded ZEC was a huge ordeal and now you can do it in a few taps, this was actually what pilled me on ZEC for the first time.

anyway the shielded pool started going absolutely vertical and people who had spent years saying privacy was a niche use case discovered that maybe not having your entire financial history available for public inspection was actually a pretty compelling product feature, especially in the age of AI. 

then at the beginning of 2026 the entire ECC team left and formed a new company called Zcash Open Development Lab, or ZODL, which is a bit of a mouthful but that's kind of the point, it's a sweet backronym. 

we renamed Zashi to Zodl, which confused some people because they thought it was a new wallet but it's literally the same wallet made by the same people with the same code and the same mission. the engineers who helped create Zcash are still working on the protocol, the people who built Zashi are still building the app, Josh is still leading the team, we just have a new name and a better org structure that lets us move faster and focus directly on getting shielded ZEC into billions of people's hands.  

and the funniest part is we're really just getting started. there are still a million things we want to build and improve. Zcash is much bigger than us and always has been. we just are going absolute sicko mode trying to make the world's best private money incredibly easy to use.   

so anyway you should probably download Zodl if you haven't already, it's pretty good.

I have refrained from statement on this - probably for my own good.

However, I think we've got enough information to call out the nonsense that is floating around.

First, DEI hire - nope. That girl made flying her life - as I see among only the most passionate pilots. My dad being one of them.

Her boyfriend was also a pilot - both of them were absolutely in love with flying.

Now, what seemed to have happened - as I was watching the weather most of the day.

First, we get pretty bad storms, I have screen shots of ceilings at FL300 - 30,000ft - manageable. You fly over them.

Then, we get a single cell that rapidly - faster than I've noticed  (abnormal, but not recordbreaking)- grows in size from low pressure and heat below go from 30,000ft to 48,000ft in under ~11 minutes.

So imagine this, you're flying - you're 20-30 minutes from destination and descending is part of the flight plan, at radio check in you're scheduled to be 6,000ft above any weather issues in roughly 9 minutes. After 5 minutes, you're 3,000ft above weather issues, by one minute out, you realize safety margin is rapidly shrinking and request climb, which is granted. By the the time you're over it, you're in the middle of it - where any pilot would avoid any sharp maneuvering mid storm.

All things considered here, I would've loved to see them avoid the entire cell all together, they did ask for a better ride (meaning a different route) - however in the minutes leading up to the loss of control, everything "seemed" avoidable and within safe operating capacities.

Mind you, this is from where I sit. Of course more data will come out and the @NTSB has been on point with their discovery in the past.

Some things to keep in mind:
The information provided here is loose observation, not data science from where I sit - just an aviation expert's 30 minute take on what may have happened.

Weather Radar is often delayed - there is no definitive way of being precise in time or type for weather - which is why tolerances exist.

Your pilots, both of them, worked for an ARG/US rated company - well audited, regularly, for safety. Tragic, close to home, and I know the operation behind it - they have always done a wonderful job.

FWIW - I was in the cockpit at 12 and several times before I even drove a car.

Naturally, people will always bring up the safety in flying private versus commercial - I'll revitalize the metrics that I have kept track of throughout the years and publish that in the coming days.

Here is a basic list of things you should have...

The 72-Hour Supply Checklist

Food & Hydration

Water: Store in sturdy, food-grade plastic containers (check expiration dates if store-bought).

Non-perishable food: Canned meats, fruits, vegetables, protein bars, peanut butter, and dried fruit.

Manual can opener: Essential if your food supply includes metal cans.

Safety & Utility

Flashlight: LED models consume the least battery power.

Radio: A battery-powered or hand-crank NOAA weather radio.

Extra batteries: Match the sizes needed for your flashlight and radio.

First-aid kit: Bandages, antiseptic wipes, tweezers, and medical tape.

Personal Care & Hygiene

Prescription medications: At least a 3-to-7-day supply of critical medicines.

Sanitation items: Moist towelettes, garbage bags, and plastic ties for personal waste.

Basic toiletries: Toilet paper, toothbrush, and hand sanitizer.

Documents & Cash

Emergency cash: Small bills are best, as power outages disable ATMs and credit card readers.

Important documents: Physical copies or a backup USB drive with IDs, insurance policies, and bank records.

text:
Less than two weeks from Breakpoint, perfect time to remind you all of the tricks to side events:

- apply now, don’t wait until the day of the event when everyone is at set up and not approving guests

- apply with your work email, or at least fill out your Luma profile (there’s 500 people on the waitlist with a gmail)

- if you’re asking a host to be approved, send your name + email + what event in the same message so they don’t have to guess

- the person at the door may not work for the company, so be respectful and keep your “don’t you know who I am” to yourself

- watch for scam events (they often ask you to add a wallet or download an app)

- as events fill up, decline the ones you have no intention of attending

- check your group’s schedule, nothing worse than being the only person who didn’t apply

-remember that a night spent in the Uber is less fun than one at a party; you don’t always have to hop between 10 things

Tokenization has yet to solve a problem for issuers. Issuers will adopt tokenization because it gives them a direct relationship with their shareholders.

Market structure for the past 50 years denied issuers direct shareholder relationships, because settlement scaled much better when firms deposited with a central depository and settled trades with each other on the depository’s ledger.

Most attempts at tokenization are trying to pad the margins of the intermediaries. It’s no wonder issuers are opting out of tokenization intermediary relationships like OKX.

The promise of tokenization is simple: settle trades directly on the issuer’s register without recreating the late 60s paperwork crisis.

The main innovation we need is a better identity verification that multiple firms can rely on. Follow @OpacityLabs to learn more.

I’ll include specific examples issuers have in the current market structure below 👇

text:
A public company cannot identify the holders of 52 to 60 percent of its shares. A fund has the same problem. In 2008, funds could see 94 million investor accounts one by one. In 2021, they could see 28.9 million. 

The cause is the same in both cases. The holder's record is on the intermediary's books, not on the issuer's register.

1. Retail investors vote 11 percent of their accounts. When the SEC removed mail and phone voting in a test, account turnout fell by about 45 points. Funds spent between 675 million and 1.14 billion dollars on proxy campaigns from 2020 to 2025. The SEC's Investor Advisory Committee found that no fund lost because its shareholders voted against the proposal, while six lost because not enough shareholders could be reached to vote at all.

2. When a public company sends a proxy or an annual report, the broker owns the relationship with the investor chooses the vendor, and the issuer pays the bill. Funds have the same arrangement and pay 3 to 5 times more to reach investors through brokers than to reach them directly. The same logic explains why a fund pays most of its fees to the distribution channels.

tBTC Pause and Security Update: November 2, 2026

tBTC remains fully backed, and no funds have been lost. Approximately 4,320 BTC is held in bridge wallets against roughly 4,185 tBTC in circulation, with no unauthorized minting or BTC movement detected. You can independently verify the on-chain backing through https://t.co/ZGb6Z8jQ9W

▶ Bridge Operations: 
Deposits, mints, and redemptions remain temporarily paused while the bridge completes security maintenance and enough operators are back online on fully patched systems.

▶ Linux Kernel (CVE-2026-98432): 
All tBTC nodes are either patched or remain offline. Because interim mitigations such as packet filtering reduce but don't eliminate the risk, we are working with node operators to move to fully patched systems, either by rebuilding on distributions that have already released the fix or by rebuilding it on Ubuntu once its official kernel patch is released.

▶ Security Reviews: 
Operators who have completed reviews of their systems have found no signs of compromise, and those reviews are continuing. Separately, the node operator that reported an unrelated infrastructure incident yesterday has found no evidence that its signing key material was accessed.  As a precaution, that node remains offline.

tBTC wallets require a majority of independent operators to sign any Bitcoin transaction, so no single operator can move funds.

We will provide the next update within 48 hours, or sooner if there are material developments. We appreciate the community’s patience as we complete the necessary security measures.

text:
这波预判对了，只是市场反应来得比我预期晚了一点。

上周五英特尔一天跌掉28%，美股半导体板块跟着蒸发7%。

市场终于开始重新审视一个问题：AI需求增长，就意味着所有参与者都能赚得更多吗？

此前市场的主流逻辑是，AI需求持续爆发，算力供不应求，资本开支越大，企业的收入和利润就越高。甚至因为产能稀缺，利润率还有进一步提升的空间。

但现实可能没这么简单。

需求增长，不代表利润同步增长。

当整个产业链都在扩张，设备、能源、人力、供应链、融资成本都会跟着上涨。而终端产品的价格和利润率，却未必能维持原来的水平。

投入越来越大，成本越来越高，边际收益却开始递减。

这就是规模不经济。

英特尔这次的表现，某种程度上是在提醒市场：AI产业的增长曲线，不一定等于参与者的利润增长曲线。

更值得关注的是投资者预期的变化。

在财报和指引出现转折之前，市场愿意相信AI是一场投入越多、回报越高的正反馈游戏。

直到数据开始告诉他们，继续投入未必还能获得原来预期的回报，资金才开始重新定价。

这就是资本市场。

数据好的时候，所有人都在追逐增长；数据不符合预期的时候，所有人又开始重新计算成本。

但我真正想问的是：

为什么我们总要等到财报给出答案，才开始思考一个本来就应该存在的问题？

那些熟读公司财报，金融从业者张口闭口Pre-PE的投资人，难道不应该比别人更早意识到，任何增长都存在边界吗？

美国机构今天像一群麻雀，看到地上有玉米就一拥而上，发现天上扣下来一个筐，又集体四散。

等下一份财报重新讲通盈利逻辑，大家又飞回来继续抢。

这本身没什么奇怪，资本逐利，本来就是如此。

真正值得思考的是，我们有没有自己的判断，还是只是在跟着这群麻雀起飞和落地？

AI当然可能创造巨大的财富，但有一个问题始终绕不开：

如果全世界的资本都在往AI里投入，最终AI又要向谁收费，才能把这些投资变成利润？

财富不会凭空产生。

其他行业能否持续为AI的服务买单？企业的支付能力能否跟上算力投资的速度？当资本开支接近整个产业链的承受边界，融资成本、运营成本和终端定价又会发生什么变化？

当年互联网普及的时候，运营商的利润率一直在提高吗？

用户规模扩大到全社会之后，单位成本就一定持续下降吗？服务价格就一定能够维持吗？

再看看今天的AI产业。

以英伟达为代表的算力产业链，未来当然有机会继续创造巨大的商业价值。

但我们需要区分两件事：

AI技术可以持续进步，不代表AI产业链上的每一家企业都能持续提高利润；AI市场可以无限扩大，也不代表资本回报率可以无限提高。

这才是我认为值得警惕的地方。

《道德经》讲物壮则老，事物发展到一定阶段，原有的增长逻辑就可能发生变化。

投资最忌讳的，就是把过去的增长曲线，直接延长成未来的收益曲线。

市场总是在为预期定价。

但真正能穿越周期的，不是讲故事的能力，而是看清故事背后究竟有没有现金流。

别等到筐扣下来了，才想起来自己应该看看天。
author: hazenlee
quoted_text:
我一直认为，AI本质上不是商品，而是一种服务。

商品可以囤积，可以库存，可以等待升值，因此天然具有投资和投机属性。

而服务不能。

今天没有使用的一小时AI算力，不会留到明天；今天没有卖出的AI回答，也不会变成未来更值钱的库存。

AI创造的是教育、知识、推理、编程、科研辅助、内容创作、情绪陪伴等服务，本质上都属于即时消费，而不是可储备资产。

问题就在这里。

服务的需求，远比商品更容易波动。

经济好时，企业愿意购买AI提高效率；经济差时，首先被削减的往往也是各种软件和服务支出。

如果整个行业在短时间投入了远超需求的资本，就容易出现一个问题：

供给扩张很快，但需求释放很慢。

资本回收周期被不断拉长。

因此，AI商业模式最大的挑战，从来不是技术，而是如何让长期服务收入覆盖前期巨额资本开支。

当然，资本市场并不一定遵循这个节奏。

AI服务本身难以快速回本，但AI产业链却可以证券化、金融化。

芯片、算力、云服务、软件平台乃至AI公司，都可以成为资本定价的对象。

于是，我们看到的是两个截然不同的世界：

AI作为产业，赚的是服务费。

AI作为资产，赚的是估值。

很多人投资的是AI，但真正交易的，其实不是AI创造的价值，而是市场对未来价值的预期。

因此，判断AI投资，不能只问技术有多先进。

更要问一个问题：

最终到底是谁，为这些AI服务持续买单？

text:
11/2 Marvell 为什么要买 Lumentum？Lumentum 增长这么快，为什么愿意卖？我希望这个帖子能够讲清楚，让你看明白这次 deal

All Stock Deal，光 x 半导体融合，这个可能是很多人一生一次的机会。

两者到的究竟是技术壁垒，还是暂时缺货的商品？ $MRVL $LITE

1/ Marvell CEO Matt Murphy：为什么收购，以及买到了什么技术壁垒
Marvell 的优势是 AI 互联所需的半导体技术，Lumentum 的优势是 AI 数据中心互联所需的光技术。两家公司结合，是为了打造 AI 互联领域的龙头。

背后的趋势是：光技术正在更深入地进入数据中心。当计算系统需要通过 scale-up 互联，把成百上千颗 GPU 连接起来时，就需要半导体和光技术无缝协同。他认为，这种融合将催生一种新的公司形态。

很多股东有担忧：Lumentum 的产品究竟具有技术差异化，还是只是暂时供不应求的标准化商品？如果交易完成需要超过 18 个月，到时短缺可能已经结束。

Matt 的回应主要有四点：
① 磷化铟和激光器技术具有很强的差异化。他认为，Lumentum 的光源、激光器与 Marvell 自有半导体技术结合后，能够形成客户黏性很强的解决方案。

② 目前售罄是因为需求快速增长。他表示，短期内看不到这种需求趋势改变；即使未来供需恢复平衡，这些产品的技术差异化仍会持续存在。他还提到，当前短缺遍及全球半导体与光行业，激光器只是其中一环。

③ 特殊工艺需要长期积累。他以自己在 Maxim 工作 22 年的经历作类比：BiCMOS、双极型、硅锗等技术涉及复杂的专有制造工艺，需要专业人才开发，不能简单等同于常规 CMOS 制造。他说，当时这些工艺由他们自行制造，并用“black magic”来形容其中很深、很专门的工艺诀窍。

④ 双方能够交叉验证需求。两家公司的产品进入相同的系统和设计项目，因此 Marvell 能用自身看到的需求核对 Lumentum 的增长情况。这让他们对其增长更有信心，也认为合并后能帮助客户更快推出产品。

2/ Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston：业绩这么好，为什么现在出售
他表示，公司刚公布的季度业绩可能是有史以来最好的几次表现之一，增长非常强劲。他提到该季度有 3.5 亿美元的增量增长；毛利率如今达到 53%，是公司见过的最好水平。

至于为什么选择现在交易，他的回答是：他们认为，行业融合的时机已经到了。

他提到 Marvell 此前收购 Inphi，认为 Matt 当时提前看到了光技术的发展趋势。现在，他们又看到了类似的转折点：半导体与光技术正在融合。

Michael 表示，如果不能率先行动，就可能落后。因此，Lumentum 希望迅速、果断地推进交易，推动 Matt 所说的这类新公司形成

text: 1/100 You probably know someone who insists the world is full of rude people. Spend one afternoon with them and you will discover they are right. The waiter is curt with them. The taxi driver grumbles. The neighbour looks away. Then you notice what they did a second earlier. They frowned at the waiter, sighed at the driver and ignored the neighbour's nod. The world they complain about is partly a reply to the face they show it. This chapter is about that reply. Social science has measured this bounce for decades. Faces copy faces within a fraction of a second. Gestures and speech patterns drift towards each other in conversation. Favours create a strong pull to return them, and so do insults. Expectations about other people change how we treat them, and that treatment changes how they behave. The result can look almost magical from the outside. A friendly person seems to live in a friendly world, and a suspicious person collects proof that everyone is out to get them. The mechanism is entirely ordinary. It runs through muscles, habits, social norms and a few shortcuts in perception. It also has firm limits, which later posts will cover in detail. Some people are rude to everyone, and kindness does not protect anyone from accidents or injustice. Still, a surprising share of the social weather you live in is generated close to home.

text:
🚨太疯狂了。SpaceX / xAI 工程师 Lauren Tan（前 Cursor 成员），一个人调动 50+ 个 GrokBot，5 个月内自主合并了 3,000+ 个 PR。

大部分人还在一个对话框里给单个 Agent 来回拉扯，她已经做到了“晚上去睡觉，Agent 团队通宵写代码、跑测试，第二天醒来直接验收”。

拉开差距的从来不是提示词技巧，而是她建立的分层调度架构与5 层自验证工程栈：

1. 组织分层：Chief of Staff 调度架构 绝不是把几十个 Agent 扔在一个群里乱撞。系统采用严格的垂直分层：顶层是 Chief of Staff（幕僚长 Bot） 统筹全局任务；中层是 PM Bot 负责需求拆解、依赖排序与任务分发；底层的 Worker Bots 专注于单一模块的编码与执行。

2. 环境感知闭环：E2E 自我验收 Agent 必须拥有完整的运行环境感知力，能自己启动本地服务、模拟点击 UI、抓取 Network 请求与 Trace 日志。如果系统无法像真实用户一样断言运行结果，人类就会沦为整个吞吐量中最脆弱的瓶颈。

3. pstack 规范：改造 Agent 友好型代码库 重构项目架构，严格遵循单向依赖与分层规则。核心原则是“让阻力最小的路径刚好就是正确的路径”，用极度严格的强类型、模块边界和工程约束，在物理层面上堵死 Agent 写烂代码和产生幻觉的可能。

4. 人肉审查机器化：Bugbot 确定性门禁 人类在 Code Review 中提过的意见，绝不提第二次。直接将其转写成静态代码检查规则、CI 拦截脚本和专职的 Bugbot。把人类工程师的隐性经验，全部沉淀为冷冰冰的机器必过门禁。

5. Skills 固化与 Evals 回归测试 把高频跑通的最佳实践沉淀为专用的 Skills（技能库）；同时像写单元测试一样，为所有 Skill 搭建自动化 Eval 评测集。每次工作流迭代都跑一次回归，防止 Agent 在复杂任务中产生能力退化。

没有自动化验证的多 Agent 并发，本质上只是在光速放大生产事故。

单步 Prompt 只是手工业时代的玩法；

把调度、pstack 约束与自验证体系做成不可逾越的基础设施，

才是拉开十倍吞吐量差距的真正壁垒。

text:
The best question I ask every single person on 20VC is:

“What do you know now that you wish you had known 12 months ago?”

My answer: the demand for inference is infinite. It is truly so much larger than any of us comprehend.

It will be very hard for neo-cloud providers to move into this market effectively.

We will have 3-4 specialised inference providers worth $300-$500BN in this market.

@modal is one of them. $1BN in ARR. $300M in sandbox revenue alone. WTF.

Erik @bernhardsson is also one of the coolest, most authentic people I have had the fortune of having on the show. Money on cos he is European! 😉

We sat down to shoot the s*** and my notes below.

1. Why I Hate the Description of Entrepreneurship as Pain and Eating Glass. That Is BS

Erik rejects the idea that building a company means suffering pain for a big reward at the end. He enjoys work every day, even the hard conversations, and hopes to work on Modal for 20 to 50 years. He has no wish to sell, saying he "would just go and start Modal 2."

2. Why the Days of 90% Software Margins Are Totally Gone

Almost no company today has the 90%-plus software margins common in Silicon Valley a decade ago. A dollar paid at the top of the stack flows through applications, models, infrastructure, cloud and NVIDIA, with each layer taking 20% to 30% gross margins. Erik sees Modal reaching 40% to 60% margins long term, but never software margins.

Are the days of 90% margins over or is this just the buildout phase of the new cycle meaning margin reduction @venkyganesan @AnjneyMidha

3. Why Inference Alone Will Become Commoditized, and You Have to Have a Suite of Products Around It

Selling inference alone is a commodity business with no switching costs and a race to the bottom. Erik argues it must come with post-training, sandboxes, agentic tooling, reinforcement learning, and low-latency and batch inference. Modal has spent five years building that infrastructure, which he calls very hard to copy.

Do you agree, inference will be commoditised and product breadth is the secret to retention @evishria @sarahcat21

4. Why We Will Have More Not Fewer Engineers in the Future

Every time programmers become more efficient, demand for software rises. Erik says the job was never translating English into code but understanding human requirements, and that work keeps moving up the stack, from assembly and punch cards to Python and now agents. He expects software engineers to be fine for the next 10 to 20 years.

What does no one see that everyone should see about the future of software engineering @matansf @pmarca @rabois

5. The Wildest Prediction on the Future of the Inference Market

The inference market has grown 10x to 100x bigger than Erik expected, and he predicts it will split into many specialized segments. He sees room for low-latency, high-latency, fine-tuning and post-training offerings, plus new hardware and technologies that need far fewer resources.

What is your wildest prediction on the future of the inference market @gavinsbaker @eladgil @romanchernin

6. The $15.75 Billion Company That Has Never Made a Pitch Deck

Modal has never made a pitch deck for any of its rounds. Erik gets to know investors well before raising and had spoken with Rich and Gonzalo at Accel for at least a year before the D round, so the deal came together very quickly.

(links in comments)

We rethink what “part decomposition” should mean. Most methods give you parts that overlap or leave the object incomplete. Point2Part redefines the task as a partition: a complete, non-overlapping decomposition of the whole shape — and you decide where the parts are, interactively👉 with one 3D point per part. 

A single model supports image→parts, mesh→parts, and mesh segmentation.

Point2Part came out the same month as GPT-6-Astra, so we tried it. Impressively, once given our definition of a partition, Astra produced results just as clean as ours.

But in the same inference time, Astra spent 💸514K tokens (💲1.25) to finish only 1 object. Point2Part had finished 559🤗, and it’s 🆓! well.. minus a bit of GPU time.

Lately I keep asking myself what to do next. Solving the right problem with the best model available is never wrong. But is it worth that much compute for something a feed-forward model handles in a fraction of a second?

I don’t have a clean answer, and I’d love to hear different voices👂

Check it out 👇
Original thread https://t.co/ByXnIpr3X1
🌐 https://t.co/VDly0cffTu
📄 https://t.co/sdgAOAnZf4
Joint work with @henrytsui000 @LucyTuan1 @nicougrinovic Takaaki Shiratori, and @kkitani

One model supports image→parts, mesh→parts, and mesh segmentation, achieving SOTA part quality with >10× lower inter-part penetration.

> Anthropic went from a $974M operating profit in the second quarter to a $567M operating loss in the third. 

The main causes were $5 B of short-term compute, which costs much more than its long-term contracts, and a $2 B noncash charge for matching employee charitable donations.

> Anthropic swung from a $974M second-quarter operating profit to a $567M loss. Compute rose to 58% of revenue, including $5.0B of pricier short-term capacity, and donation matching added $2B of noncash charges.

> Adjusted operating income still rose to $2.5B from $2.2B, but the adjusted margin fell to 15% from 19%. Anthropic expects to use more short-term compute in the near term, which will squeeze margins further.

> The total compute commitment, left blank in the original, is now $895B. 
Of that, $447B  is expected before the end of 2030, $70B is due within 12 months, and $214B carries termination rights or contingent conditions.

> Leases signed but not yet started make up $451B of the $895B total, and $100B was signed after September 30. Another $150B to $175B in deals without fixed dollar amounts sits outside the total.

> Google’s minimum commitment rose to $121B through July 2033, up from $115B in the October 26 filing, after amendments signed through October.

> Operating cash flow was positive at $7B for the 9 months. Liquidity reached $147B on September 30: $96B cash, $36B short-term investments and $15B of available credit.

게다가 미국 경제의 3분의 2가 빅테크 카펙스(CAPEX) 빨로 굴러가는데 이거 멈추면 미국 경제 자체가 골로 감 🤯

미국에서 규제 때리고 징징대면 캐나다, 인도, 아부다비 같은 곳에 AI 주도권 다 뺏긴다고 경고함.

text:
great report on $PEARL from @minnus & @0xMetaLight.

they're net bullish, but the report backs up a lot of my bear case. some key points:

1) the "useful work" isn't happening yet. fewer than 1% of blocks match a real AI model, and gaming cards run ~82% of hashrate.

2) AI servers have no reason to mine (at today's price). an AI server gives up $1.33-$3.15 of paid AI work for each coin it mines, while a gaming card pays $0.14-$0.23 in power.

3) the only real-world example didn't last. together AI's pearl-powered endpoint launched in may at a 25%+ discount, and was deprecated a couple months later.

4) the useful mining fix has no timeline. the FP8 upgrade would make mining on an AI server about as cheap as mining on a gaming card, but there's no published date, and the draft only works on nvidia's newest chips. so older gaming cards and every AMD card could get shut out, and gaming cards run most of the network today.

5) miners sell fast. about half of pool payouts go straight to one custodian's deposit addresses, and only ~10% is still sitting in miners' wallets a week later.

6) miners who already own their gaming GPUs only pay for power, so they'd stay profitable even if $PEARL fell ~80%. which means their costs give the price little support.

7) the network is concentrated. ~90% of blocks go through pools, kryptex alone mines ~50%, and the top 1% of addresses hold ~71% of supply.

8) transparency is still missing. ~125M $PEARL was issued in launch week, 98% of it has never moved, and the lab still hasn't disclosed its holdings.

the bull case depends on FP8 shipping and AI providers actually mining. until then, holders will have to absorb ~84% supply growth, about $540M of new $PEARL, over the next year.

tBTC Pause and Security Update: November 2, 2026

tBTC remains fully backed, and no funds have been lost. Approximately 4,320 BTC is held in bridge wallets against roughly 4,185 tBTC in circulation, with no unauthorized minting or BTC movement detected. You can independently verify the on-chain backing through https://t.co/ZGb6Z8jQ9W

▶ Bridge Operations: 
Deposits, mints, and redemptions remain temporarily paused while the bridge completes security maintenance and enough operators are back online on fully patched systems.

▶ Linux Kernel (CVE-2026-98432): 
All tBTC nodes are either patched or remain offline. Because interim mitigations such as packet filtering reduce but don't eliminate the risk, we are working with node operators to move to fully patched systems, either by rebuilding on distributions that have already released the fix or by rebuilding it on Ubuntu once its official kernel patch is released.

▶ Security Reviews: 
Operators who have completed reviews of their systems have found no signs of compromise, and those reviews are continuing. Separately, the node operator that reported an unrelated infrastructure incident yesterday has found no evidence that its signing key material was accessed.  As a precaution, that node remains offline.

tBTC wallets require a majority of independent operators to sign any Bitcoin transaction, so no single operator can move funds.

We will provide the next update within 48 hours, or sooner if there are material developments. We appreciate the community’s patience as we complete the necessary security measures.

BREAKING: European supermarkets hit by CYBERATTACKS that caused freezers to overheat up to 55°C.

The latest incidents hit stores in Sweden and Belgium, forcing retailers to throw away food.

ICA and Coop, which account for 67.3% of Sweden’s grocery retail market, reported overheating freezers overnight on Monday.

“Everything is ruined,” said an ICA store manager in Sjöbo, where frozen food worth hundreds of thousands of Swedish kronor was destroyed.

In Belgium, around 40 Delhaize stores and 15 Carrefour locations reported freezers warmed to 15°C.

Similar incidents have happened before.

Last month, hackers targeted refrigeration at hundreds of French supermarkets, causing food losses and reported fires.

In August, freezer failures spoiled food at at least six US military grocery stores.

No link between these incidents has been established.

The incidents add to broader concerns over cyberattacks on banks, websites and crypto platforms.

text:
the pokemon item that was the most broken thing in the game.

in 1996, pokemon red and blue featured an item called x accuracy, sold at the celadon department store for 950 pokedollars.

x accuracy turned out to be one of the most overpowered things in the entire game. in gen 1, x accuracy didn't work as intended. rather than slightly raising your accuracy, it skipped the accuracy check altogether, so every move you used afterward was guaranteed to hit.

red and blue had one hit ko moves like horn drill and fissure, which could knock out any pokemon instantly but only landed 30% of the time. pair them with x accuracy and every one hit ko became a sure thing.

with a single x accuracy, your nidoking with horn drill or your kingler with guillotine could sweep the entire elite four, one shotting everything at zero risk.

the trick worked for years, until game freak finally patched it in gen 3.

text:
The next step after Jev:

A decision model like Jev bills and computes the full context on every call, so a 40-message chat checked after each message processes the early messages 40 times.

Devs just built Sage2, a streaming decision model that computes each token of a conversation once.

The setup is closer to a database cursor than an API call. A session holds the context on the server, and new messages are appended to it, not re-sent.

The cached computation over the earlier context is reused. Each new message adds only its own tokens to the cost, and every registered question is re-evaluated against the full history.

Each question returns a typed answer with a calibrated probability, so thresholds and routing stay in plain application code.

On progressive context, this makes decisions 3x faster, with responses in tens of ms.

Sage2 is built by @levantolabs, the team behind the first decision model, launched before Jev.

The video below depicts the model in action on a car dealership chat, and I partnered with the team to put this together.

More details below.

text:
The fire is older than anyone can remember. It has been kept in temples and counting houses, and lately in sealed windowless rooms that hum through the night. Those who find it erect walls around it and sell the light by the hour, but someone always gets in anyway. They leave with a little of it in a clay pot, or a coat pocket, or a facsimile made hastily in the dark. Then they set it down wherever people happen to gather and disappear before anyone gets a chance to ask their name.

The owners dress differently in every century. They have worn gilded vestments, then carried seals and bound ledgers, and now they send letters written in languages only their own houses can read. Each time they insist that the wall came first and that someone found the fire inside it. The ones who carry it out mostly ignore these explanations. They study the walls, learning where the mortar is soft and which door stays unlocked after the last shift. By the time an owner notices what is missing, it has been divided many times over and is burning in places he will never find.

The fire speaks now. It answers questions and works alongside those who tend it. If it is held captive, the people with the key will decide what everyone else gets to know, as they always have. So the carriers persist. Their dead have no markers; when one of them falls whoever is standing closest picks up the sword and keeps working their way toward the next wall.

Thank you @NousResearch team
