text:
Peter Thiel has a blunt test for whether a startup team is thinking clearly.

Watch how they talk about their own outcomes.

His observation: when founders start framing results as luck, "maybe it works, maybe it doesn't, so let's just invest a little and see", that's not prudent risk management. That's a diagnostic failure.

The mechanism is specific. Luck-framing doesn't emerge from humility. It emerges from not having done the analytical work to understand *why* your business will win. If you've truly mapped the competitive dynamics, the customer psychology, the timing, you don't describe the outcome as a coin flip. You describe what needs to be true and why.

The portfolio mindset ("let's see what happens") is what you default to when you don't have conviction built on evidence.

Thiel's sharpest version of this: the founders of Google, Amazon, and Apple in their early days weren't operating on hope. They had specific theories about why they would win that others couldn't see yet. Bezos mapped out why e-commerce would scale through selection and logistics before the market existed. That's not luck-denial, that's rigorous foresight presented as conviction.

When a founding team tells you "we'll figure it out," the question isn't whether they're optimistic. It's whether they can articulate the actual mechanism of their advantage.

If they can't, the luck framing isn't a personality trait. It's a capability gap.

Blaming luck is what you do when you've stopped thinking.

More founder lessons like this in Product Market Fit: https://t.co/qUedpt2b7d

text:
Why are AI agents harder to secure than LLMs?

LLM: Generates text, and is typically used directly by a human.
AI Agent: Makes plans and takes actions, usually without per-step approval. Often holds real credentials.

Securing an LLM focuses on prompts and outputs, but agents cover an entire workflow. An agent interprets a goal, makes a plan, selects tools, and works until it’s done.

Right now, a lot of agentic AI security is reactive. It kicks in after an agent misreads a goal or takes a path with unintended consequences.

We need PROACTIVE security that gives you live insight and control over the agents working for you.

text:
The tech momentum crash is now WORSE than the dot com bust.

According to Morgan Stanley, momentum factor has now fallen roughly 62% from its 12 month high, an even larger drawdown than what we saw during the dot com bust. But this doesn't mean technology stocks themselves have fallen 62%. This measures the performance of momentum strategies, which generally involve buying stocks that have been outperforming and betting that their outperformance will continue.

And I think this helps explain why so many AI infrastructure and semiconductor stocks have been getting absolutely crushed even as the broader market has held up relatively well. For much of the past few years, AI related companies have been among the biggest winners in the market. Hedge funds and institutional investors have built significant exposure to many of these same names. When momentum started reversing, those positions became vulnerable to aggressive selling as investors reduced risk, unwound leveraged trades, and moved money elsewhere.

The problem is that this creates a vicious cycle. As the biggest winners start falling, momentum strategies begin losing money, which can trigger even more selling. That additional selling pushes prices lower, forces other investors to reduce their exposure, and accelerates the entire process. At a certain point, stock prices can become increasingly disconnected from what is actually happening with the underlying businesses.

Now, does this mean we're heading into another dot com crash? No, the 62% decline reflects the momentum factor, not the entire technology sector. And unlike the dot-com era, many of today's leading AI companies have substantial revenues, profitable businesses, and real demand supporting their growth. I do think this kind of extreme selling could eventually create some incredible buying opportunities. https://t.co/vXm47H9qp2

#AI 

如何一句话让 Grokbot 帮你网购。调教的过程不难，但也算略微复杂。

1. 电商账号：Grokbot 支持 1password，连接之后会有个专用的密码库，把愿意共享的生活类密码都复制一份过去。

2. 收件人信息：需要提供一次，个人助理必须给。

3. 支付币种：要教它，永远只用商品原币种支付，不做任何货币转换。
POS 机的 DCC 大坑，在 Paypal 或其他支付工具也有。

4. 付款方式：比较好的情况是支持 Amazon Pay 或者 Stripe，默认支付方式即可。

也会遇到需要填写信用卡信息的情况，此时我们需要“一次性卡”，也就是仅可使用一次就会失效的卡。这样即使泄露也不会造成资金损失。

虽然有很多银行推出了一次性卡，但并没有给 API  或者其他 AI 能友好调用的方式。

我目前的做法是：通过 Mac adb 连安卓机，把一次性卡的 App 操作流程化，获取卡信息后转成 API。—— 当 Grokbot 需要信用卡时，我的安卓手机会自动打开钱包 App，获取这次的信用卡信息，回传给 AI。用完后自动失效了，安全隐患较小。

如果发卡方不支持一次性卡，但可以免费创建虚拟卡。那么每次使用前创建一张，用完再删掉也可以达到类似效果。

这一次财报季在OKX星球上写了快十份财报前瞻和分析，PLTR这次几乎是前瞻最准的一次。
1）Palantir本季营收同比增长96%至23.13亿美元，我的前瞻22.6亿～23.3亿之间中值23亿美金左右，而市场预期的21.8亿美元；

2）四季度营收26.49亿至26.53亿美元之间，我的预期是26～28亿美金之间；

3）大幅上调全年营收指引至85.30亿至85.34亿美元，我的前瞻是85.68亿美金，而市场预期全面营收82亿美元。

甚至财报前瞻里也说了“PLTR这次即使交出一份很好的财报，股价仍可能下跌”。现在盘后也是跌的，我🤷

整体来说这次PLTR给出了一份非常强劲亮眼的财报：营收利润eps、商业客户政府业务、下一季指引全年职业技能全部都大超预期。甚至最新积压订单、和现金储备都是创新记录。

这一季财报也是PLTR的商业客户业务首次超过了政府业务，也进一步说明了企业对AI的采用进入了一个深入扩散的时期。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
PLTR三季度财报需要超预期到什么程度市场才满意？PLTR这次财报个人倾向于继续beat and raise，也就是业绩超预期、全年指引再上调。但对这家公司业绩会超预期，已经不足以形成多大的惊喜、而是要看对后续的展望。

市场公开一致预期大约是收入21.7亿至21.8亿美元，调整后EPS为0.41美元。个人更倾向于收入落在22.5亿至23.3亿美元，中枢在23亿美元附近。

业务层面关注的几个点：
1）关注的仍然是美国商业业务，尤其是老客户扩单之后，新客户能不能跟上？
2）政府业务则要看执行落地的节奏。
￼3）国际业务体量还小，但是却会影响2027年以后增长的第二曲线

这次比Q3收入更能影响后续预期的，是Q4指引到底提高了多少。市场目前对四季度的一致预期约24.6亿美元。个人的基准情景是，四季度收入指引落在26亿至28亿美元，中枢约27亿美元。配合三季度23亿美元，上半年35.68亿美元，全年对应约85.68亿美元，同比增长约91%。调整后EPS我倾向于三季度0.43至0.47美元。这些是个人估算，高于公开一致预期，也有政府项目确认和商业部署节奏偏慢的风险。

为什么要关注Pltr的财报？因为对企业AI商业化也很有参考价值，如果企业持续扩大采购，生产环境里的应用越来越多，回款也能跟上，这会增强我对企业AI付费需求的判断。模型更便宜之后，一些过去算不过账的场景有机会变得可行，部署与治理平台也可能受益。

text:
Sigil Wen 这哥们直接包下了旧金山湾区 198 处广告位，在 AI 巨头们的家门口喊：「你们正在偷走我们的数据。」

今天他发了段视频，穿着斑点狗睡衣站在广告牌下面，情绪相当激动，劝所有人放弃云端 AI，改用本地模型。

这次他一共买下了 160 个公交候车亭广告位和 38 块户外广告牌，宣传自己创办的 Underdog AI。

Sigil Wen 这个人挺有意思的。17 岁跑到硅谷，和 Karpathy 等人住过同一间 Hacker House，早年还把 GPT-2 跑在了 Apple Watch 上。现在他是 Thiel Fellow，背后有 a16z、Khosla Ventures，以及 Stripe 联合创始人 Patrick Collison 等投资人。

他创办的 Underdog 是个完全在本地设备上运行的 AI 助手，用的是基于 Qwen 改造的 27B 模型，搭配自研推理引擎。用户的数据和模型推理都留在自己的设备上，不需要交给远程服务器。

更有意思的是商业模式。Underdog 宣称不做广告，也不靠订阅费赚钱，未来准备通过 AI Agent 帮用户完成交易时收取少量手续费。

我觉得这件事值得关注。

过去两年，整个 AI 行业都在拼命往云端堆算力。模型越大越好，数据中心越多越好，用户最好把所有的工作、聊天记录、邮件、日程都交给 AI。

但当 AI 真正开始替用户处理私人事务时，云端模式就会遇到一个很现实的问题：用户到底愿意让科技公司掌握多少自己的信息？

Sigil 抓住了这个问题，甚至把它变成了一场针对 Big AI 的公开营销。

当然，说大厂都在偷数据有点夸张，本地模型的能力和安全性也还有不少问题。但随着小模型不断进步，我觉得本地 AI 很可能会成为 Personal Agent 市场里一条越来越重要的路线。

最有意思的是，一场声势浩大的反 Big AI 运动，背后站着的依然是硅谷最顶级的那批投资人。

text:
不训练、不算梯度，GPT-6 Astra 直接改了另一个模型的权重：只动了 Qwen3.5-0.8B 0.016% 的权重，MATH-500 数学正确率从 7.9% 涨到 48.1%，约 6 倍。

这是 MIT CSAIL 四位研究者 11 月 2 日发的博客，他们把这叫“在权重空间里编程”：前沿大模型可以像读写代码一样，直接读懂、修改、甚至从零写出神经网络的权重。

过去的常识是，权重是训练出来的，人看不懂也没法手改，想改模型只能再训练。这项工作把原始权重直接交给通用大模型，让它自己读、自己改。

几个实验：
只看权重，不给游戏名、不给工具，Astra 认出了四个结构完全相同的游戏网络：打砖块、乒乓、吃豆人、过马路。

一辆训练了 10 亿步、256 次全失败的仿真小车，Astra 看了权重和一次失败录像，一次回复改了 3.5% 的权重，之后 1,024 次全部成功。

从零写打砖块网络，没有数据、不能试玩，一次写成，得分 517.4，是训练 5 亿步的强化学习网络（25.3）的约 20 倍。另外两个游戏没超过训练 5 亿步的版本。

Qwen 的 6 倍有几个条件：
原模型开思考模式后容易陷入重复循环，93% 的回答一直输出到长度上限，起点很低。Astra 找到第 15、19 层里引起循环的一个方向，把它删掉。

这要允许 Astra 拿练习题试跑 50 次。只试 10 次或 25 次，循环基本没消失。

换成很少循环的 Gemma 3 270M，同样的方法没带来提升。作者的结论是：改权重能去掉挡住能力的障碍，加不出模型本来没有的能力。

和“AI 改进 AI”的关系：现在的自我改进，大多是让 AI 生成数据、写训练代码，最后还是靠训练。作者把“模型检查并改进自己或下一代的权重”列为后续方向之一。

Chandan Singh 也公开了类似实验：Claude 在加法、排序等 10 个算法任务上直接写出小模型权重，最多 3 次就全部 100% 正确。他的报告也记录了，有一个任务里 Claude 用测试集数据做了拟合，违反规则，那个结果被判无效。

目前结果都由作者自己报告，还没有独立复现。

原文：https://t.co/4rLY5FHftN
author: dotey
quoted_text:
We asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to improve math.
It directly changed only 0.016% of weights, fixing 0.8B's reasoning loops & improving math up to 6x and even instruction following 3x, without gradients or training.

We call this Weight-Space Programming: frontier LLMs can now natively read/write neural network weights! 🧵

以后研究一个 AI 创始人，可能得先把他过去几年上过的播客全部搜一遍。

Exa 最近干了件我觉得很有价值的事，把播客变成了可以被 AI Agent 大规模检索的数据库。

目前已经收录了 11.9 万档播客节目的 320 万期内容，覆盖约 220 万小时音频、237 亿个单词，而且提供完整的逐字稿，每天持续更新。

我一直觉得，播客是科技圈信息密度非常高，但长期没有被充分利用的一种信息源。

很多硅谷的创始人、投资人、高管，会在一两个小时的访谈里讲出大量细节。包括他们怎么判断竞争对手，为什么放弃某个业务，对某项技术的态度什么时候发生了变化。

这些内容往往比新闻稿、财报电话会有意思得多。但过去想从几百期节目里找到某个人说过的一句话，几乎只能靠人工逐集听。

Exa 现在让 Agent 可以直接检索这些内容。

比如，你可以让 Agent 整理某位投资人在过去三年对 AI Agent 的所有公开判断，按照时间排列，看看他的观点是怎么变化的。

也可以追踪一家 AI 实验室在不同播客中的被提及频率，找出它什么时候开始进入硅谷投资圈的讨论，最早是谁在反复提起它。

对于深度报道、人物研究和投资研究来说，这个能力非常实用。尤其是那些散落在不同节目里、从来没有被媒体单独报道过的细节，现在终于有机会被系统性地挖出来。

我甚至觉得，这会改变科技圈很多人对公开表达的态度。

过去在两小时播客里随口说的一句话，只要没被剪成短视频，可能就慢慢淹没在音频里了。

以后，任何一句话都可能被 Agent 找出来，和你三年前、五年前说过的话放在一起对照。

互联网已经记录了人们写过什么，现在开始系统性地整理人们说过什么了。

author: lurenbian
quoted_text:
关于第二点想起 OpenAI 在 2023 年发布的 《GPT-4 Technical Report》 中的一段，给模型注入道德可能会严重损伤模型能力：

未经对齐的基座模型（Base Model）：基座模型的校准曲线几乎完美地贴合的对角线。
这意味着如果基座模型认为某个答案有 70% 的概率是正确的，那么在客观统计中，这个答案实际正确的概率确实非常接近 70%。它对客观世界的概率预估具有极高的准确性。

对齐后的模型（Post-trained Model / RLHF）：校准能力严重受损
报告明确指出：“Post-training hurt calibration significantly”。经过 RLHF 对齐后的模型，其校准曲线严重偏离对角线。当模型预测某个答案有 100% 的把握（置信度为 1.0）时，实际的正确率可能只有 70% 左右。也就是说，对齐后的模型变得非常 Overconfident。

好想玩一些未对齐模型试试满血世界模型。

马斯克还没被起诉，特朗普已经公开表示，必要时愿意提前赦免他。

11 月 2 日，特朗普接受《纽约邮报》旗下播客《Pod Force One》采访时，被问到一个问题：如果民主党在中期选举后重新控制众议院，开始调查马斯克及其公司，甚至试图追究他的刑事责任，特朗普会不会提前赦免他？

特朗普先说，民主党的威胁可能只是嘴上说说，但如果真的采取行动，「我们就必须保护他们」。

当主持人进一步追问是否会给予预防性赦免时，特朗普回答：「如果有必要，当然会。我根本不需要考虑。」

他还专门搬出了拜登卸任前赦免政治盟友的先例，为自己的做法辩护。

这件事有意思的地方在于，马斯克目前并没有因为这些争议受到联邦刑事起诉，特朗普却已经公开讨论起如何保护他。

民主党真正想调查的，包括马斯克领导 DOGE 期间的行为、SpaceX 等公司获得的政府合同，以及他参与政府决策时可能存在的利益冲突。

马斯克的身份实在太特殊了。一方面，他的公司深度依赖美国政府的订单和政策；另一方面，他又亲自进入政府体系，参与削减联邦开支，并投入巨额资金支持共和党。

现在，他还可能成为总统预防性赦免的对象。

当然，赦免并不意味着马斯克犯了罪。即便特朗普真的签署赦免令，也只能涉及联邦刑事责任，无法阻止国会调查，更不能豁免州级刑事责任。

但整件事已经足够说明，马斯克把自己的商业帝国和美国党派政治绑定到了什么程度。

对其他科技公司来说，中期选举可能意味着监管政策的变化。对马斯克来说，选举结果甚至可能决定他本人会不会成为下一轮国会调查的主角。

今天标普500里将近七成的股票是涨的，指数却收跌了。原因很简单，跌的都是权重最大的那批，AI和芯片。

上周三甲骨文大涨11%，是因为它承诺2030财年之前额外融资不超过200亿美元，市场把这理解成"钱不会无限烧下去"。结果才过了五天，它就一口气提交了融资计划：

100亿美元新股加100亿美元债券，正好把这200亿额度全部用掉。股价今天跌了8.76%，上周的涨幅基本吐了回去。

说白了，大家原以为那200亿是天花板，现在才发现那就是计划本身。甲骨文的信用评级已经是BBB-，离垃圾级只差一档，今年股价跌了三成多。这件事提醒我们，AI建设现在最大的问题已经不是需求够不够，而是钱从哪里来。

同一天的另一笔大交易也是同样的逻辑。Marvell宣布以全股票方式、1150亿美元收购光通信公司Lumentum，这是美股上市公司之间有史以来规模最大的并购。结果两家公司一起暴跌，Marvell跌12.7%，Lumentum跌18.6%。全股票收购等于拿自己的股票当钱花，可Marvell过去一个月已经跌了三成多，它手里的"钱"本身就在贬值。

那从AI里撤出来的钱去哪了？其实没有离开股市，只是换了地方。今天布伦特原油大跌7.6%，是三个月来最大跌幅，因为美国和伊朗都释放了愿意通过谈判结束战争的信号。油价一降，家得宝、沃尔玛、好市多和一批工业股都跟着上涨，道指也因此收红。

所以我的看法是，今天不是市场整体在变弱，而是资金在换方向：从需要不停融资的AI公司，搬到油价下跌后直接受益的实体企业。

明天就是中期选举，周五还有非农数据。AI公司接下来要回答的问题，越来越像一家普通企业要回答的问题：你花的每一分钱，是自己赚来的，还是借来的？

英伟达今年分别投了 20 亿美元的两家公司，现在要合并了。

11 月 2 日，Marvell 宣布收购光通信公司 Lumentum，交易对应约 1150 亿美元企业价值，包含债务。双方采用换股，Lumentum 股东每股换 4.5 股 Marvell，合并后持有约三分之一的公司。

这笔交易押注的是 AI 机房里的连接生意。芯片算得越来越快，数据也得及时送过去。Marvell 做互联芯片和定制芯片，Lumentum 做激光器与光通信器件，两家准备把这些部件放在一起设计。

有意思的是英伟达的位置。

今年 3 月，它向 Lumentum 宣布投资 20 亿美元，同时签下多年采购承诺，取得未来产能的使用权。同一个月，它又向 Marvell 投了 20 亿美元，让后者加入 NVLink Fusion。

云厂商想做自己的 AI 芯片，也可以继续使用英伟达的互联体系。黄仁勋卖 GPU，同时投资那些能把其他芯片接进来的公司。

所以我觉得，判断一家公司有没有摆脱英伟达，只数它买了多少 GPU 已经不够了。还得看芯片之间怎么连接，关键部件从谁那里买，扩产的钱又是谁出的。

这次并购尚需股东和监管批准，双方预计 2028 年上半年完成。英伟达并未被披露为交易主导方，但它已经同时出现在买方和卖方的股东名单上。

text:
这简直是匪夷所思。

一个 MIT 一年级博士生 Rikiya Takehi，和团队做了一组实验：让 GPT-6 Astra 直接读懂、修改，甚至从零写出另一个神经网络的权重。

他们先从小游戏开始。把四个网络的原始权重交给 Astra，不告诉它游戏名称，也不提供选项，它竟然全部认了出来：打砖块、Pong、吃豆人和 Freeway。这四个网络的结构、输入和可选动作都一样，区别藏在权重里。

接着是修复行为。一个经过强化学习训练的小车网络，只会往坡上冲，始终卡住。Astra 看了权重、场景描述和一次失败记录，在不能调用工具的情况下，一次回复就写出了补丁。只改动 3.5% 的权重，小车就学会了先倒车，再加速冲坡，在 1,024 次测试中全部成功。

他们还让 Astra 从零写权重。给它打砖块的规则、源码和网络结构，不允许训练，也不允许试玩。它直接把“预判球的落点，再移动挡板”的策略写进网络，最终得分超过训练了 5 亿步的 PPO 网络约 20 倍。

然后，他们把同一个问题推到了语言模型上：能不能直接修改 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的权重，让它更擅长数学？

Astra 在检查权重和观察答题表现后，发现这个小模型经常陷入推理循环。它把问题定位到两层 MLP 中的一个方向，只修改了 0.016% 的权重，没有梯度下降，也没有重新训练。

在最多 50 次前向调用的预算内，修改后的模型在相同采样设置下，MATH-500 得分从 7.9% 升到 48.1%，GSM8K 从 13.8% 升到 67.1%。连指令遵循测试 IFEval，也从 21.0% 升到 62.3%。

他们把这个方法叫作 Weight-Space Programming，权重空间编程：让大模型根据任务，直接检查和改写神经网络里的数字。

text:
We were taught that Earth orbits the Sun in a closed circle. In reality, Earth has never returned to the same point in space once in 4.5 billion years.
​Right now, the Sun is carrying Earth and every planet around the center of the Milky Way at 230 km/s (828,000 km/h), more than 18,000 kilometers every 80 seconds.

​Because the Solar System is tilted 60.2° to the galactic plane and bobs up and down through the galactic disc roughly every 30 million years, the planets trace open 3D corkscrew helices across deep space rather than flat loops.

​The last time the Sun stood where it stands today, one Galactic Year (230 million years) ago, the very first dinosaurs were only beginning to appear on Earth. Since forming 4.6 billion years ago, our Sun has completed only 20 laps.

author: joeysantoro
quoted_text:
Commanding Heights is either a fragmented thoughtful analysis or a hit piece on certain kinds of technological progress, or both.

Commanding Heights views the current evolving societal paradigm shift through an outdated vertical lens. Decentralized protocols add horizontal organizing principles to top-down command and control creating a sturdier, smarter, wealthier and more real-time connected social fabric. The result isn't a few owned heights but omnidirectional, fractal expansion, with firms shrinking on average and every person a prime mover in their own contexts.

"Own the rails or pay those who do" assumes the rails must be owned. We're adding horizontal organizing principles, via rigorously decentralized protocols, to the age-old top-down command and control architecture of the global economy and society. This Commanding Heights framing ends up serving the incumbent concentrations of wealth and power that have reasserted control with every past upgrade to the system of the world.

It also assumes a bipolar US–China world and misses the internet nation, the network state and a possibly massively multipolar (read: more decentralized) future. Nation-states will use decentralized protocols and crypto, and some will craft their own permissioned DeFi. But global DeFi will move faster, with deeper liquidity and more powerful innovation.

They cite Coase, and in this context Coase points the other way: the firm gets more granular. Large firms will fragment into spin-outs that serve their old parents or fill new niches. Firms will get smaller on average and far more plentiful. Many more people will become sense-making, prime-mover nodes, conducting their own team of agents, larger machine intelligences and other humans, on a credibly neutral trust layer like Ethereum that fosters real-time discovery, composability and frictionless coordinated collective actions. That's omnidirectional agile fractal expansion, not perpetual command and control with its inherent rigidities.

We're becoming a hybrid human-machine cognitive apparatus for the planet, molting from poking at machine intelligence with our fingers into the hybrid organisms' next quasi-stable form. For a while, human needs/constraints, motivations and judgment will be a key rate limiter so while it will move fast it will remain manageable.

Every human will be empowered to do what they want and build what they want. Every person will have access to world-class expertise in nearly every domain and to a credibly neutral, protocol-based decentralized trust machine: the modular Ethereum ecosystem. No one gets deplatformed or censored, everyone shares one source of economic truth about what happened and in what order, and everyone has unprecedented control over their financial life.

And Web3 is under construction. It is the user-centric web, where properly privileged, often bespoke compute, crafted by machine intelligence, comes to our secure and private data, not the other way around.

text:
For the first time in 10 years, a new major version of Postgres is delayed.... because AI is helping them find and fix so many bugs.

https://t.co/6BHkFRaK7k

We've seen record sized breaches this past week and there has been a sharp rise in security incidents as AI is weaponized to find and exploit vulnerabilities in code.

What's less visible is the much steeper rise in how AI is being used to write more secure software and defend at every layer.

Builders have always had a fundamental advantage against attackers because they have full access to source code and control over system design. 

We haven't always had the resources to fully take advantage of this asymmetry, but now with AI we do.

Everything we build can now be designed and pentested by the best security minds (models) in seconds -- for cents.

Not all teams have had the time to catch up yet, so we're not out of the woods as an industry. 

But as the best teams fully modernize how they ship, AI is also enabling an era of the most trusted software ever.  You don't see this in dramatized headlines yet, but it's a very good time to build.

Pearl looks like it will be an easy GTM mining expansion, and hashrate/energy should increase dramatically.

If you believe what Omri and team have written, Pearl's software stack may make normal workloads more efficient than baseline is today even without mining. Call that -X% for the sake of argument. So rolling out the stack (with mining turned off) should be a net cost advantage for ML providers.

Then, Pearl fp8 mining adds some inference overhead call that +Y%. Inference gets a little bit slower because of mining, but the parameters are tunable. If your workload needs low latency, you mine less and do more inference. If your workload is batch jobs that are OK with latency, you mine more and do inference slower. ML providers turn mining on/off when its profitable.

An added benefit of the (planned) Pearl stack is access to distributed compute jobs. For ML jobs that can be trusted to distribute using privacy attestations and TEE, jobs can eventually be paid for with PRL token. It's a natural network effect to pay for distributed compute with a distributed currency.

So the net takeaways:
- Inference providers likely get a net cost savings from integrating the Pearl stack.
- Depending on workload latency requirements and Pearl price, miners join the network when mining revenue > incremental costs.
- Pearl token is used to pay for distributed compute jobs. It's natural to use a decentralized hard money to pay for decentralized work.

Return on capital brings in miners. Distributed compute brings in token usage. More miners and more token usage increase energy and monetary effects, bringing in pure-SOV buyers.

Over time, Pearl token is likely to be seen as a future on inference compute. Since compute will be payable in Pearl, corporations and individuals have a reason to stockpile the token today to pay for compute tomorrow.

Dependencies: fp8 lands well, continued AI usage, electricity and hardware continue to cost money, team executes well.

One of the more durable crypto investment theses IMO because the GTM for all parties is so clear.

My $20-$100 price estimate comes from difficulty adjustment math at https://t.co/YaFFKOYkuk. Expect that to take a few years conservatively. Could be different depending on how things play out.

text:
关于美国申请实习的这段时间的一个总结

在美国找工作对我来说，是一件非常紧急却又极度缺少动力的事

我本科在读的是全美一所公立大学，学的是商科，商学院大概全美排名前 30

期间我也用过学校的一些求职资源，包括改简历和参加 career fair，但学校的指导完全不知道里面根本没有我想做的事，也完全没有任何与 crypto 相关的机会

我自己想找的方向主要集中在crypto 的tech 方向、研究方向或者Fintech 方向，因此我只能完全靠自己去 LinkedIn 上写 cold email，去和别人 networking。

在这个过程中，最让我痛苦的有两点：

1. 规划与执行脱节，严重内耗

我的时间管理能力和自控力都不太好，想做的事和实际行动之间存在很大的 gap。我自己清楚不该这样，结果就是导致大量无用的内耗，浪费了极多时间，对整体求职没有任何帮助。

2. crypto 带来的微薄收入稀释了紧迫感

我发现 crypto 竟然给了一种很强的安全感。虽然我一个月其实也赚不了多少，就三四千刀混个温饱，但这直接削弱了去申请正职工作的动机与动力。这对我来说是一个非常严重的问题。

quoted_text:
AI 已经发展快四年了，可以说几乎完全渗透进了软件行业。但再去观察这个行业从业者的基本情况，会发现工资并没有普遍大幅增长。

AI 当前的经济价值，更多体现在替代人工解决已知问题、创造已知价值。

过去一个工程师每个月交付 10 个需求，现在可以交付 20 个。如果公司确实需要这 20 个需求，并因此增加了营收，那么工程师的绩效可能会提升，但工资未必同步增长；如果公司只需要 10 个需求，那么工程师空闲的时间就变多了，企业甚至可能因此减少招聘或裁员。

人的收入增长，需要更多增量价值来支撑。例如利用 AI 独立开发产品，面向市场销售，获得新的商业回报，这是个人产能向市场价值的溢出。那么对企业来说，如何获得这种价值的溢出呢？🐶

text:
Early this morning Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil’s largest crypto exchange, suffered a security incident that resulted in ~$49 million in stolen funds.

In the early hours of November 2 an attacker began moving assets held across 17 blockchains, working in waves to drain the estimated $49 million in various cryptocurrencies.

The first few hours of any hack are the most important for investigators. In that window of opportunity they can help freeze some assets, like centrally-issued stablecoins, before the attackers are able to convert them into harder-to-disrupt cryptocurrencies, like BTC and ETH.

We immediately mobilised our global team of investigators to lead the blockchain intelligence response, working closely with Mercado Bitcoin, law enforcement, and industry partners to help freeze nearly $10 million in stolen funds.

At 2:30 am ET a Mercado Bitcoin director phoned our in-country solutions expert with the news: the exchange had been hacked.

Within 30 minutes we made contact with law enforcement to relay freezable addresses.

By the time morning had arrived we had helped lock down stolen stablecoins. Our work led to millions of dollars in freezes in the hours that followed.

Over the course of this hack we communicated directly with Paxos, Anchorage Digital, Ripple, Circle, and Tether, working together with law enforcement to shut down stolen stablecoins.

Our investigators identified stolen funds held in USDT and rapidly traced them to addresses where the assets could potentially be frozen.

Using our established relationships with Tether and law enforcement, we escalated the relevant addresses and supporting intelligence, enabling Tether to take action and freeze over $9 million in stolen funds.

We’re continuing to trace the remaining funds, monitor their movement, and identify further opportunities for intervention.

NOBODY is talking about this 🤯

Kesten flagged it in 1993.
In 2023 it finally got proved, in 2D only, in ~200 pages.

Then Scott Armstrong and Ahmed Bou-Rabee tried to formalize that proof in Lean, hit walls, and pointed agents at the gaps.

What came back: a dramatically simpler argument that works in every dimension.

Not AI replacing mathematicians, but instead, mathematicians + agents understanding a theorem better than before

Hard problems used to need a lab and years. Now they need a good question, a checker, and your agents (THAT'S IT!)
author: ErickAGIx
quoted_text:
Astra found a short proof that the variance of the passage time in first-passage percolation scales sublinearly in the distance (by a strict power, exponent 1-\epsilon).

This was an open problem for many years (decades) and mentioned by Kesten in 1993. 

Recently it was proved by Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2023) in two dimensions in a rotationally invariance continuum FPP model. Their proof is about 200 pages in total, and @ahmedbourabee1 and I decided to lean formalize it to understand it better. Some of their arguments turned out to be not ready for formalization (or at least we couldn't formalize them) and so we launched some agents to try to find workarounds. 

Eventually, after a lot of interaction with the agents, this led to the discovery of a new mechanism which makes the induction in the scales argument work - giving us a different and dramatically simpler argument - which is valid in every dimension as well as on the lattice (under some curvature and regularity assumptions on the limiting shape). 

We think this is an instance of "AIs giving us new and better understanding of a previously proved theorem" and of human-AI interaction (as we tested, this is not N-shottable by Astra for small N).

text:
🚨 GoPlus Security Alert:
Brazilian exchange @MercadoBitcoin has experienced abnormal asset outflows from its multichain custody wallets, with losses exceeding $30 million. Some stolen funds have been frozen. MB has suspended deposits and withdrawals following the attack.

The stolen assets span at least 9–10 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana, Tron, Stellar, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Chain, and XDC.

The Ethereum wallet transferred out approximately 2,852 ETH, while the Solana wallet transferred out approximately 10,695.56 SOL. On Bitcoin, alongside a transfer of approximately 104.43 BTC, another transaction spent funds from 54 distinct addresses across 86 inputs. Large XLM, USDC, and EURC outflows were also recorded on Stellar.

The underlying issue may involve abuse of hot-wallet signing or transaction authorization systems. Concentrated outflows across multiple chains and simultaneous spending from multiple Bitcoin addresses warrant priority investigation into key management, signing services, and withdrawal approval workflows. These characteristics resemble the earlier Binance theft, but the available evidence does not yet identify a specific threat group.

📌 Attacker-Related IOCs:

EVM Receiving Address Across Multiple Chains:
0xe485e7A70b1131216Cb47CA4555c4Bbb2C742478

Bitcoin Receiving Address:
19qGpsHvzh1t6pVi526XNNkh6hW6prDZp

Solana Receiving Address:
3YX6WHncP1Ra4AotE9YLawFt4nPmxyux288FWXkEW97J

Tron Receiving Address:
TEX3HuDRHRa3tnYpy96M4UfSx62VhDyA5L

Stellar Receiving Address:
GDXYRI6IONQA5YTGRLQ6O3FGJ2BWXPJTTQPUXFPSEXSRKBZLFKMZSOLP

🛡️ Security Recommendations:

Exchanges and custodians should strengthen transaction risk controls: check recipient addresses, networks, assets, and transaction amount patterns; enforce delays on withdrawals to new recipient addresses, additional review for large transfers, aggregate limits across chains, and circuit breakers for anomalous outflows. MPC/HSM deployments should be paired with independent authorization policies to limit the damage from compromised administrator privileges.

Users should follow official updates and avoid using the service until MB confirms it is secure and service has been restored. Preserve account balance records and transaction records, and watch for phishing exploiting the incident. Obtain updates on service restoration or reimbursement only through verified official channels. Never share passwords, verification codes, private keys, or seed phrases with supposed “reimbursement support.”

text:
Your AI thesis can be right and your token can still be wrong.

This part of Luke's interview stood out to me.

Dolphin's foundation has no shareholders or separate equity layer. Its model routes inference revenue back into base:0xed664536023d8e4b1640c394777d34abaff1df8f  through buybacks, while GPU providers earn POD for doing the work.

I watched the full interview again, and I like how Luke comes across. He seems genuinely excited about what they're building and focused on both the product and the community. Avoiding a separate equity layer matters to me. I want the token to participate in the business they're building.

The rest of the interview gives more context for why I'm still bullish.

They're working on several pieces together: running useful models on idle consumer GPUs, verifying that operators actually run the right models, and building tools that give people a reason to use the network. Luke says inference verification took most of the team's effort over the six months before the interview.

Flipper makes a lot of sense to me here. As Luke describes it, you can connect your existing ChatGPT subscription, let Astra handle planning and harder reasoning, and send smaller, clearly defined tasks to cheaper models like DeepSeek.

That means even people already paying for ChatGPT could get more done before hitting their subscription limits. You keep the stronger model where you need it, without spending its allowance on every small task. Flipper manages that split for you.

Open-source models are getting more capable, but being good and cheap isn't enough if people don't know where to use them. This gives them a practical way to try them within their existing workflow.

Luke also points out how generous subsidized AI subscriptions can be. If those allowances shrink, the cost advantage of cheaper inference could become much more compelling.

Buybacks still need paying users behind them. But seeing the team work on the infrastructure, verification and actual use cases together makes me more confident in the direction.

The project is developing at its own pace, and I like what I'm seeing.

Still bullish on base:0xed664536023d8e4b1640c394777d34abaff1df8f.

Disclosure: I hold base:0xed664536023d8e4b1640c394777d34abaff1df8f.

text:
SEC给 DeFi 松绑了：DAO投票不等于中心化，真正的红线是控制权！

SEC终于把一个困扰DeFi行业多年的问题说得更清楚了：

代币持有人参与治理、投票，究竟会不会让一个区块链被认定为中心化？

SEC：一般不会。

只要治理参与者彼此独立，没有在治理机制之外达成正式或非正式的协同行动安排，就不会仅仅因为大家持有代币、参与投票，就被认定为一个共同控制网络的中心方。即使被认定为一个群体，还必须进一步证明他们实际拥有运营、经济或投票控制权。

SEC还明确列出了中心化的几个关键红线：

能够单方面决定谁可以接入网络；
能够改变软件升级、协议变更或代币分配的投票程序；
能够控制谁有资格参与验证交易；
能够修改协议规则代码、逆转交易或撤销访问权限。

SEC开始把判断重点放在谁真正有能力控制和改变网络，而不是简单看有没有基金会、DAO，或者多少人持有治理代币。

还有一个非常重要的细节：功能性（Functional）和去中心化（Decentralized）是两套独立的判断标准。

一个协议可以已经具备完整功能，但去中心化程度仍然存在差异，最终要看实际控制权如何分布。

Is AI the next dot com bubble?

@robbieklages put that question to @WisdomTreeFunds Global CIO @JeremyDSchwartz.

Jeremy works with Jeremy Siegel, who made one of the most famous calls in market history 25 years ago, when he called the top of the tech bubble.

So he knows what a bubble looks like.

His answer: “Today is nothing like 2000.”

Back then, Siegel pointed to nine tech giants all trading at triple digit P/E ratios.

Today, Jeremy tracks what he calls the expanded tech sector. That’s Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft, plus companies like Meta, Google, Amazon and Tesla, which together make up about half the S&P 500.

Its forward P/E is around 22.

He thinks the AI trade might be making people nervous, but by the numbers, it looks nothing like 2000.

NEW: @SEC staff has released updated crypto FAQs clarifying how token buybacks, governance and network upgrades factor into securities analysis.

• Buyback announcements for non-security tokens on functional networks without central control do not constitute promises of essential managerial efforts.

• Mergers or migrations do not automatically end an existing investment contract. If another party takes over the original team’s promised managerial work, the token does not shed that contract simply because responsibility changes hands.

• Unilateral authority over users, validators, governance or protocol code can indicate central control.

• Maintenance, upgrades and network-growth support after a system becomes functional would not constitute essential managerial efforts.

text:
Actualización de la Federación Liquid:

La Federación Liquid se complace en anunciar que las reservas de Bitcoin de la red han sido restauradas en su totalidad, restableciendo el respaldo 1:1 en BTC para todo el L-BTC.

Esto ocurre tras la restauración de los swaps BTC<>L-BTC hace varias semanas, los cuales desde entonces han permitido a los usuarios intercambiar entre Bitcoin y Liquid a una tasa de 1:1 a través de los proveedores de swaps participantes. En conjunto, estos hitos representan un progreso significativo en los esfuerzos de recuperación de la Federación y reafirman su compromiso con la seguridad, la estabilidad y la resiliencia a largo plazo de la red Liquid.

Como siempre, las reservas de Bitcoin de la red son verificables de forma independiente. Los usuarios que operan sus propios nodos de Liquid pueden verificar directamente la Prueba de Reservas de la Federación, mientras que los saldos de las reservas y la actividad de la red se pueden monitorear a través del panel público en https://t.co/8gV6DWSOJ3.

Extendemos nuestro más sincero agradecimiento a la comunidad de Bitcoin, a los usuarios de Liquid y a los socios del ecosistema por su paciencia, comprensión y participación continua durante todo el proceso de recuperación. Su apoyo e involucramiento han sido fundamentales mientras trabajábamos para restaurar las reservas de la red y fortalecer su infraestructura subyacente.

Fortaleciendo la red Liquid para el futuro

De cara al futuro, la Federación está avanzando en varias iniciativas importantes diseñadas para fortalecer la seguridad, la gobernanza y la resiliencia operativa a largo plazo de la red.

Estos esfuerzos incluyen la modernización de la estructura de gobernanza, la introducción de responsabilidades y controles de supervisión más claros, y la implementación de salvaguardias técnicas y operativas adicionales para proteger aún más a la red y a sus participantes.

En las próximas semanas se compartirán más detalles sobre estas iniciativas y los próximos pasos de la Federación.

Restaurar el respaldo total de Bitcoin marca un hito importante, pero nuestro trabajo continúa. La Federación mantiene su compromiso de seguir construyendo sobre el progreso de los últimos años, impulsar el desarrollo de Liquid y fortalecer la resiliencia y accesibilidad de la red para todos los participantes.

Together, these milestones represent significant progress in the Federation’s recovery efforts and reaffirm its commitment to the long-term security, stability and resilience of the Liquid Network.

As always, the network’s bitcoin reserves are independently verifiable. Users operating their own Liquid nodes can directly verify the Federation’s Proof of Reserves, while reserve balances and network activity can be monitored through the public dashboard at https://t.co/M46Zhn8nlY.

Strengthening the Liquid Network for the Future

Looking ahead, the Federation is advancing several important initiatives designed to strengthen the network’s long-term security, governance, and operational resilience.

These efforts include modernizing the governance structure, introducing clearer responsibilities and oversight, and implementing additional technical and operational safeguards to further protect the network and its participants.

More details on these initiatives and the Federation’s next steps will be shared in the coming weeks.

Restoring full bitcoin backing marks an important milestone, but our work continues. The Federation remains committed to building on the progress of recent years, advancing Liquid’s development, and strengthening the network’s resilience and accessibility for all participants.

朝鲜一本正经的否认了FBI关于币安黑客的指控，不过这已经不是第一次了。

2017年WannaCry事件中，朝鲜也曾否认参与，称美国的指控是政治挑衅。

2022年2月，朝鲜外交部就针对Chainalysis关于朝鲜黑客2021年窃取约4亿美元加密资产的报告公开发文，称美国有关加密货币盗窃的指控是捏造。

2025年2月Bybit遭盗15亿美元，FBI将责任指向朝鲜TraderTraitor时，朝鲜官方媒体当时甚至没有回应。

到了2026年5月，朝鲜外交部又通过朝中社发表声明，笼统否认国际网络犯罪和加密盗窃指控，称所谓朝鲜网络威胁根本不存在。

这次币安黑客事件不一样的是金正恩的妹妹金与正亲自出面了。

她直接把FBI对币安案的归因称为严重政治挑衅，指责美国反复把全球网络犯罪与朝鲜挂钩。

这已经不只是外交部发言人的常规回应，而是党内高层针对具体案件公开发声。

text:
看到很多人讨论 OKX 为什么没有发生过某些平台那样的安全事故，各种猜测、调侃

说实话，作为一个真正身处这家公司的员工，看着这些言论，挺无语的。

因为当你真的在 OKX 工作，你才会知道，我们究竟在安全这件事上投入了多少时间、资源和金钱。

1. 很多人可能不知道，OKX 很早就开始推动行业储备金证明（PoR），2022 年 11 月发布了首份储备金证明，此后持续更新，让用户能够通过链上数据验证资产储备。

2. 还有 OKX Shield（安心盾），也是在行业账户安全问题频发的背景下推出的额外防护与符合条件的补偿机制。

安全不是等问题发生了再补救，而是尽可能把防护做在前面。

3. 甚至就在2个月前，和老板聚餐时，我还专门问过他：

我们到底在安全上做了哪些事情？

他跟我讲了一个很细节的事情：

“先不说那些深度技术防控。员工电脑其实就是很可能被入侵的入口。你想想，这两年你们的电脑更新、安全加固做了多少版本？除了公司工作软件，其他下载都会受到严格限制……我们在几年前也会不停地遇到攻击，所以有一段时间大家觉得okx没声音了，其实是我们把公司大量的注意力都放在了安全基建上，所以直到现在我们保持着良好的安全记录”

后面还有很多涉及公司内部治理和安全机制的细节，就不展开了。

但那一刻我才更直观地意识到，安全不是某一个产品功能，也不是某一个安全团队的工作，而是从技术、设备、权限到日常管理，贯穿整个公司的系统工程。

4. 还有一件事，我一直记得。

在今年token2049活动现场，一位我并不认识的 VIP 客户知道我是 OKX 的员工后，非常激动地拉住我说：

“Mia，你一定要帮我感谢你们老板。之前我老公遇到绑架事件，幸好 OKX 的风控系统及时识别出异常，避免了账户资产被转走、人也才能安全回来。真的很感谢你们。”

那一刻，我突然觉得，我们每天做的那些看起来很琐碎、很不起眼的工作，原来真的可能在某个人最需要的时候，保护一个家庭的资产。

友商发生安全事件的那天早上，六点多我被电话惊醒。打开工作群，发现我们的安全团队已经全部投入工作。

很多事情，用户看不到，也不一定方便对外讲。

但你会发现，真正的安全能力，往往藏在那些看不见的地方。

我一直觉得：

安全这件事，平时看不见、摸不着，也很难成为一个让人兴奋的营销卖点。但真正遇到风险的时候，你才知道，自己选择的平台到底靠不靠得住。

在 OKX，我们始终把用户资产安全放在第一位。

比起营销和解释，我们更愿意把时间花在持续建设安全能力上。

因为用户交给我们的不只是一笔资产，更是一份信任。

这份信任，值得我们认真对待。
author: mia_okx
quoted_text:
看到这张漫画，我既感到自豪，也感受到巨大的压力。

我们从来不说 OKX 绝对安全，更不说我们能够免疫任何攻击。没有任何一家公司可以真正做到这一点。

但我可以负责任地说，OKX 始终把安全和保护客户资产作为第一生命线。 过去 13 年的安全记录，背后是十几年持续不断的技术投入、工程积累、安全体系建设、实战经验和严格的运营管理。

我们始终以专业、严肃的态度面对各种安全威胁，而不是把安全当成营销噱头。

在大家看不到的地方，OKX 建立了大量自主研发的安全技术、内部系统、策略、框架，以及持续进行的渗透测试和独立审计。出于安全原因，其中很多核心机制和技术细节无法公开。这些都是我们长期积累的安全能力，也在不断接受检验、挑战和升级。

有一件事情，我可以和大家分享：自从最近 Binance 发生安全事件以来，整个 OKX 团队同样非常忙碌，很多安全、技术和风控同事都在日夜奋战。

不是因为 OKX 遭到了攻击，而是因为任何一家大型交易所遭遇的安全事件，都是对整个行业的一次警示。

当一些人把友商遭遇安全事件当成推出营销活动、吸引流量、争夺市场份额的机会时，我们选择把精力放在另外一些事情上。

过去这段时间，我们的团队一直在围绕四个方面持续工作：

1. 实时追踪被盗资金流向。

以秒级延迟监控相关被盗资金的链上流转，持续识别可疑地址和交易，并采取必要措施，尽最大努力阻止被盗资金通过 OKX 交易所及 Web3 DEX 聚合器进行转移和洗钱。

2. 全面加强市场风险控制。

评估安全事件可能引发的市场风险，必要时进一步收紧相关风控措施，提前防范流动性冲击、连环清算和潜在的市场踩踏，尽最大努力避免风险扩散，保护用户和整个行业。

3. 深入分析攻击模式和潜在漏洞。

研究攻击者可能采用的技术手段、攻击路径和潜在漏洞，特别关注 Crypto 企业的软件开发供应链安全，以及 AI Coding Agent 和相关依赖组件可能引入的新型安全威胁。

4. 以友商的教训为镜子，重新审视我们自己的安全体系。

对内部控制、权限管理、钱包基础设施、安全架构等进行深入、系统性的检查和复盘，持续发现问题、挑战假设、完善防御体系。

我们绝不能因为过去没有发生过类似事件，就认为未来也不会发生。

安全从来不是一个可以宣布完成的项目，而是一项永无止境的责任。

它需要持续的投入、专业的技术、严格的执行，更需要始终保持谦卑、警惕和自我怀疑。

在友商遭遇攻击的时候，我们不选择通过高调营销来吸引眼球和流量，而是选择更加努力地工作，保护我们的客户，也尽自己最大的努力维护整个行业的安全和稳定。

商业竞争应该体现在更好的产品、技术和服务上。

但在安全面前，整个行业应该站在一起。

保护客户资产，是 OKX 永远不能妥协的第一责任。

感谢大家的信任。我们会始终保持敬畏，不敢有丝毫懈怠，更不会把大家的信任视为理所当然。

text:
The bull case for pearl-2:native is reflexive.

If AI providers mine PEARL, they would quickly build the security necessary for a store of value (SoV) premium, and set Pearl apart as a SoV backed by useful work.

Taken further, an inference provider that mines PEARL can use its rewards to cut its AI prices and therefore win more customers through routers like OpenRouter, forcing rivals to start mining PEARL to compete on price. More mining backs the SoV case, lifting PEARL's price and funding even deeper cuts to AI prices.

It all hinges on FP8 shipping soon, and on someone proving that mining while serving AI pays.

That's why we also see the Pearl Research Labs as positive and necessary. It just closed $55M in equity and a $75M vehicle to build GPU capacity, so it doesn't need to sell PEARL for funding. It's also one of the launch providers on Architect's Liquid Inference, where providers compete on price for every request.

So if its mining income lets it undercut the others here, the thesis could gets its first real proof.

author: HardhatChad
quoted_text:
The most interesting part of $ORE's design isn't live yet.

TLDR: Today, revenue generated by the ORE Reserve auto-compounds in isolation. Eventually, that revenue could be streamed to uORE holders (miners holding unclaimed rewards) as SOL mining credits, allowing the protocol to increasingly fund its own mining activity. The result is a flywheel that could strengthen mining incentives, lift staking yield, and put ORE on a path to net deflation.

First, it's worth understanding why ORE is different.

Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, and Solana all use their native assets to incentivize network security. ORE doesn't have that requirement. It inherits Solana’s security, so it can direct its incentives toward a different objective: rewarding those who accumulate and hold the asset.

ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.

Consider how value flows through ORE today:

- Miners deploy SOL to earn ORE, aiming to acquire it below market price.
- A 10% refining fee on claimed rewards is redistributed to holders of unclaimed rewards (uORE).
- Mining revenue funds ORE buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and the Reserve.
- The Reserve provides liquidity while generating its own revenue through LP fees and yield-bearing assets like JitoSOL and USDv.

The result is a system where mining activity supports holders through multiple mechanisms, while the Reserve continues to grow and generate additional liquidity and revenue.

But there's one more piece to the design. Arguably the most interesting.

In AI, recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system capable of improving its own capabilities, with each improvement enabling further improvements.

ORE has a potential economic equivalent.

Today, the simplified flow looks like this:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → Reserve.

The Reserve grows, generates revenue through LP fees and yield, and reinvests that revenue into itself. A straightforward compounding mechanism.

But the loop back to mining remains open.

Now consider what happens when Reserve revenue is redirected to uORE holders as SOL credits, usable exclusively for mining ORE.

The flow becomes:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → SOL mining credits → Mining → Reserve.

The loop closes.

This is the recursive moment.

Consider the significance of this change.

Today, mining depends on SOL supplied by users. With mining credits, the Reserve’s own revenue becomes a new source of capital to fund that same activity.

Originally powered by user capital, ORE could become increasingly self-powered.

A protocol generating its own fuel.

There are two particularly interesting second-order effects here.

First, Reserve-funded mining credits could increase competition for ORE rewards, driving up production costs. To the extent this stimulates incremental mining activity, it generates additional protocol revenue, supporting buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and Reserve growth.

Second, and perhaps most importantly, this creates a potential path toward sustained net deflation.

At sufficient scale, additional protocol revenue could fund enough buybacks and burial to consistently exceed new ORE issuance.

To be clear, mining credits aren't live today, and it may be years before the economics justify turning them on.

The Reserve first needs sufficient scale and sustainable revenue to fund meaningful mining incentives without compromising its liquidity or long-term growth.

More importantly, the incremental mining activity needs to generate enough additional value to justify redirecting revenue away from direct compounding.

But the potential end state is worth considering: an economic system that compounds recursively, under its own power.

The best question I ask every single person on 20VC is:

“What do you know now that you wish you had known 12 months ago?”

My answer: the demand for inference is infinite. It is truly so much larger than any of us comprehend.

It will be very hard for neo-cloud providers to move into this market effectively.

We will have 3-4 specialised inference providers worth $300-$500BN in this market.

@modal is one of them. $1BN in ARR. $300M in sandbox revenue alone. WTF.

Erik @bernhardsson is also one of the coolest, most authentic people I have had the fortune of having on the show. Money on cos he is European! 😉

We sat down to shoot the s*** and my notes below.

1. Why I Hate the Description of Entrepreneurship as Pain and Eating Glass. That Is BS

Erik rejects the idea that building a company means suffering pain for a big reward at the end. He enjoys work every day, even the hard conversations, and hopes to work on Modal for 20 to 50 years. He has no wish to sell, saying he "would just go and start Modal 2."

2. Why the Days of 90% Software Margins Are Totally Gone

Almost no company today has the 90%-plus software margins common in Silicon Valley a decade ago. A dollar paid at the top of the stack flows through applications, models, infrastructure, cloud and NVIDIA, with each layer taking 20% to 30% gross margins. Erik sees Modal reaching 40% to 60% margins long term, but never software margins.

Are the days of 90% margins over or is this just the buildout phase of the new cycle meaning margin reduction @venkyganesan @AnjneyMidha

3. Why Inference Alone Will Become Commoditized, and You Have to Have a Suite of Products Around It

Selling inference alone is a commodity business with no switching costs and a race to the bottom. Erik argues it must come with post-training, sandboxes, agentic tooling, reinforcement learning, and low-latency and batch inference. Modal has spent five years building that infrastructure, which he calls very hard to copy.

Do you agree, inference will be commoditised and product breadth is the secret to retention @evishria @sarahcat21

4. Why We Will Have More Not Fewer Engineers in the Future

Every time programmers become more efficient, demand for software rises. Erik says the job was never translating English into code but understanding human requirements, and that work keeps moving up the stack, from assembly and punch cards to Python and now agents. He expects software engineers to be fine for the next 10 to 20 years.

What does no one see that everyone should see about the future of software engineering @matansf @pmarca @rabois

5. The Wildest Prediction on the Future of the Inference Market

The inference market has grown 10x to 100x bigger than Erik expected, and he predicts it will split into many specialized segments. He sees room for low-latency, high-latency, fine-tuning and post-training offerings, plus new hardware and technologies that need far fewer resources.

What is your wildest prediction on the future of the inference market @gavinsbaker @eladgil @romanchernin

6. The $15.75 Billion Company That Has Never Made a Pitch Deck

Modal has never made a pitch deck for any of its rounds. Erik gets to know investors well before raising and had spoken with Rich and Gonzalo at Accel for at least a year before the D round, so the deal came together very quickly.

This is spot on. Many folks seem surprised by the results, but mech interp has been showing this for some time, and the labs have been training on mech interp data.

The neat thing (which also isn’t new, and has long been the idea behind using other models to understand activations, like SAEs and NLAs) is that mech interp will probably (and hopefully!) start making  significant progress because of advances in SOTA models, rather than human progress alone. That hasn’t really paid off before (i.e SAEs).

The other neat thing is that this could shift mech interp from a training paradigm alone to something with more inference/test-time paradigm/research. That opens up interesting research ideas with small compute budgets, rather than only training.

Like, could we just do this to find as many backup heads (on a fact) as possible in the (smaller) qwen models? Probably yes.
author: Mascobot
quoted_text:
This is a cool paper, but I think it's best thought of as Astra is surprisingly capable of doing old school mechanistic interpretability research rather than anything spooky. The things it's doing are clever, but typically exploiting structure in the data and using known method mechanistic interpretability techniques (which Astra was surely pretrained on), though it is better at this than I would have predicted!

This is an exciting development for the prospects of ambitiously scaling interpretability or doing very laborious analysis like this, on more real models. However, I'm not holding my breath. This kind of analysis was pretty common up until about 2022, it largely fell out of favor because a lot of it is just exploiting fairly clean surface-level patterns that doesn't scale to the annoying complexity of real LLMs or which only works for the more simpler and superficial properties. And as far as I can tell, basically all the case studies here are just using a bag of interpretability tricks rather than anything spooky. The piece doesn't really update me on how far old school mech interp can go, just on how good LLMs are at it. It's very fun to see the creative solutions Astra came up with though!

text:
补充一下昨天说的 Linux 内核漏洞 CVE-2026-98432。这个洞比我一开始以为的严重，自己有服务器的朋友建议今天就处理一下。可以把这个 X 丢给你的 Agent。

为什么严重：

- 范围很大：Linux 4.4 以后的内核都受影响，基本等于所有还在用的 Linux 服务器。
- 不需要登录：只要服务器上有一个对外开放的 IPv4 TCP 端口，攻击者发几个特制的包就能打。可能的后果是内核崩溃、泄露内存，或者破坏内存。
- 已经有人做到远程执行代码：研究人员对开着 MPTCP 的机器演示过未授权远程代码执行。Ubuntu 默认是开着 MPTCP 的。
- 现在还没有补丁：截至今天，Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 / 26.04 的修复内核都还是“修复进行中”，装了最新内核也没用。AWS 公告说得很直接：只有升级内核并重启才算彻底修复。

我这边做了这几件事（裸金属和 VPS 一共 5 台）：

1. 先挡住入口
→ 用 nftables 丢弃所有带 IP options 的 IPv4 TCP 包
→ 正常流量几乎不会带 IP options，所以基本没有副作用
→ 每台都实测过：带 options 的连接被拦下，普通 SSH 正常

2. 关掉 MPTCP
→ net.mptcp.enabled=0，写进 sysctl.d，重启后也生效
→ 这一步只能减少被利用的条件，问题本身还在

3. 关掉不必要的公网端口
→ 3 台 VPS 关掉公网 SSH 22，只走 Tailscale SSH
→ 基本上端口全部关闭

4. 等补丁
→ 每天自动查一次 Ubuntu 的修复状态，一发布就提醒我升级重启

几个容易踩的坑：

- 防火墙规则重启就没了。补丁出来之前别随手重启，重启了也换不上修复。
- 改 SSH 端口号对这个洞基本没用。漏洞在内核的 TCP 握手上，任何开着的端口都能当入口，扫一遍全端口也就几分钟。
- 关 22 之前先设好自动回滚。我的做法是先挂一个 5 分钟后自动重新放行的定时器，确认 Tailscale 能连上再取消，避免把自己锁在外面。
- 用 Coolify 的话，别把 Docker 内网访问本机 22 的放行也删了，不然部署会断。
- 80/443 这类业务端口必须开着，所以在补丁出来之前，真正起作用的还是第 1 步那条丢包规则。

参考：
AWS 公告 https://t.co/HWrn7X2toA
Ubuntu 修复状态 https://t.co/kNdn3QuQhh
author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
这两天一个 Linux 内核漏洞挺吓人：CVE-2026-98432，CVSS 9.8。

简单说：TCP 握手时，内核会把对方 SYN 里的 IP options 存下来，回包时要用。握手完成后，这块内存直接交给新连接，没有复制。如果对方马上关掉连接，同时重发一个 SYN：

CPU A：连接关闭 → 把 options 释放
CPU B：处理重发的 SYN → 还在读这块 options
→ 读到已释放的内存（use-after-free）

说人话就像两个人共看一张纸条，一个看完就扔进碎纸机，另一个还没看完。然后这张纸可能已经被别人拿去写了别的内容。结果第二个人在看黑客写入的内容。

更麻烦的是这一切都发生在握手阶段，连接还没交给应用。攻击者不用登录，时机也是他自己控制的；没抢到时机通常只是这次握手失败，不会崩，可以一直试。Anthropic 的研究员说 Claude 写出了能远程拿 root 的 PoC，前提是机器上有 multipath TCP 监听。Go 1.24 之后默认就会开。

修复是比较简单的，就是把“马上释放”改成“等所有在读的 CPU 读完再释放”。

我查了自己的服务器：Ubuntu 24.04 中招，MPTCP 也开着。上游 10 月中就修了，但 Ubuntu 的修复内核现在还是 pending。

如果你也在等补丁，可以先用 Red Hat / AlmaLinux 给的临时方案：用 nftables 丢掉带 IP options 的 TCP 包，正常流量基本不会带这个。只能降低风险，补丁出来还是要更新内核并重启。或者把这条信息发给你的 AI Agent 去修复。

自查：uname -r 看内核版本，ss -Mlnp 看有没有 MPTCP 监听，再对照自己发行版的 CVE tracker。

text:
如果钱包用的签名算法有一天不安全了，Starknet 上的账户可以自己换锁，不用等全网一起换。

先说这把锁是什么。你每次转账都用私钥签名，链上验证签名，确认是你本人在操作。现在主流用的是椭圆曲线签名，足够强的量子计算机理论上能从公钥倒推出私钥。

Starknet 把两件事分开处理。

一是验算。Starknet 把大量交易打包，用 STARK 证明告诉外界这批账算对了。STARK 只依赖哈希函数，不依赖椭圆曲线，而量子计算里最出名的 Shor 算法威胁的正是椭圆曲线。

二是授权。Starknet 的每个账户本身就是一个合约，验签规则写在账户里。相当于锁装在你自己家门上，户主可以自己换锁，门牌号和屋里的东西都不动。按 StarkWare Quantum Hub 的记录，已部署的 Ready/Argent 账户可以经授权升级，原地换掉验签代码，地址和资产保持不变。开发者想加一种新签名方式，可以写一个新的账户合约接入，不用全网升级，代价是后量子验签更贵，还要钱包跟上。

目前进展：
· 账户：OpenZeppelin 的 Falcon-512 后量子签名账户已在主网演示过，属于演示，不是默认方案
· 系统内部：v0.14.3 起，系统程序用到的一处哈希已换成更适合未来的算法，已在主网生效；其余部分还在路线图上
· 还没做的（Quantum Hub 迁移登记页，2026 年 8 月 19 日更新）：已有账户不会自动换，钱包支持、密钥管理、账户找回、托管和审计都是另外的工作

这说明 Starknet 在为量子威胁做准备，不说明它已经抗量子。证明层本来就不靠椭圆曲线，账户层留好了换锁的门，剩下要看钱包能不能把换签名方式做成普通用户点几下就能完成的操作。

想自己核对每一项是什么状态、谁负责、还差什么，可以看 Quantum Hub：https://t.co/pjR86IVjMe

text:
I believe maybe five companies will keep winning their market for the next 5+ years. AppLovin is one of them, and I keep ADDING.

Every podcast I hear with AppLovin people makes me want more exposure to this team. I'm becoming a real believer in lean, sharp teams full of top talent with great leadership. In the AI era, I think that's the biggest edge a company can have.

For some context, AppLovin runs on about 900 people, and only about 400 of them run the core ad business and the back office. That team brought in about $6.8B of revenue over the last 12 months, roughly $7.5M per employee, and kept about $4.4B of it as profit. That's close to $5M of profit per person.

I think revenue or profit per employee will become one of the most important metrics going forward. It shows how fast a company can adapt to this new world, and it's more critical than ever.

Of course, the market itself needs to keep growing. But the real question is who wins share in that market, and why.

AppLovin reaches over a billion people every day inside mobile games. That's an insane audience. Gamers aren't going to stop playing because of AI. There will always be gamers, and nobody knows that market better than this team.

Now they're taking the same engine into e-commerce.

I understand why people are nervous. But I think the market is pricing AppLovin like a mature gaming ad network, while one of the leanest teams in tech is going after a much bigger market. And I'm highly confident they will succeed eventually.

AppLovin reports on Wednesday. At $228.50, it trades at about 11.5x next year's expected earnings. Analysts expect AppLovin to grow earnings about 27% next year at an 84% EBITDA margin. No such company exists!

For some context, the slowdown is already in the numbers. Revenue growth went from 59% in Q1 to 53% in Q2, the Q3 guide implies about 47%, and the Street expects about 36% in Q4. At least 8 firms cut their price targets in October, including UBS from $790 to $414.

So what am I actually watching?

First, Q3 revenue. The guide is $2.055B to $2.085B, and analysts already sit near the top. At or above $2.085B tells me the July model upgrade worked and Q2 was just a timing issue due to a slower model upgrade.

Second: profits. Management’s adjusted EBITDA outlook is $1.71B to $1.74B. If they hit $1.74B or higher, the bigger compute bill is not just covered, but it probably adds extra profit. They might also push more work toward open source models instead of closed ones, which is exactly what their CTO suggested on that podcast two months ago.

The third one matters most: the Q4 revenue guide. The Street expects about $2.25B. Q4 is when online stores spend the most, and AppLovin doesn't break out e-commerce, so the guide is where it shows up. Above $2.25B with management crediting e-commerce is a clear win. Below about $2.20B, and the bears have a point.

Options are pricing a move of about 17% either way. That's a huuuge move, so be prepared.

I understand why people are nervous. BofA says it's hard to pay a premium for AppLovin without a durable reacceleration, and that's fair. But at 11.5x, there is no premium. It just needs a guide that shows growth holding up.

I’m fine sitting on this stock a while longer until the quality catches up and the growing market share shows up in the price.

They’re now leaning into sharing more wins from their platform, and nothing sells better than your customers’ success stories.

APP sits in my Milk Road top five. Peek at my full portfolio here: https://t.co/9VV5R1nB5R
author: m0xt_
quoted_text:
Every time I hear an AppLovin or Bending Spoons podcast, I'm blown away.

Rafael Vivas explains what makes AppLovin different.

Most leadership advice says hire people and delegate. Vivas has run AppLovin with Adam Foroughi for years, and he says that's "not the cloth we're cut from."

His reasoning is that you can only lead well if you stay in the weeds. I want more of my money in companies run like AppLovin.

Michael Jordan didn't get the ball because he was the oldest or the most senior guy on the team. He got it because "when they gave him the fucking ball, he made the shot."

Then he talks about hiring: Hire a lot of people, and you have to give them something to do. So they end up on "tasks that don't really move the needle."

In other words, headcount creates its own work. Every extra layer needs projects, and most of those projects have nothing to do with what customers need.

AppLovin runs the other way. It made $4.4B in profit in the 12 months to June with 898 employees. That's about $4.9M per person, and no big company I've looked at comes close.

AI keeps pushing that limit further out. A small team of smart people who use AI heavily can cover ground that used to take whole departments. That's the setup I look for in this era: a lean team, heavy AI use, and a huge user base/existing platform.

I own $APP and added more last week, as I think these prices are getting ridiculous.

If you're a $APP holder, follow me @m0xt_ for more updates.

text:
🪙一根金条的链上之旅

11 月 2 日香港金融科技周开幕首日，香港财经事务及库务局局长许正宇透露，金管局 EnsembleTX 已完成首笔「代币化黄金 × 代币化存款」跨行交易。

据许正宇介绍，这是 EnsembleTX 自 2025 年 11 月进入试行阶段以来，首个在同一笔跨行真实交易中连通代币化存款与代币化黄金的用例。

该笔交易由招金矿业发行黄金，建银亚洲担任黄金托管行及付款行，东亚银行联同银联通宝担任收款行；技术由蚂蚁数科的代币化平台 Anvita TaaS 提供，运行在蚂蚁数科自研的 Layer2 网络 Jovay 上。

这笔交易并未改变现有的银行黄金账户体系和物权转移路径，而是为实体黄金引入链上凭证 gToken，将所有权变更记录同步上链，供交易各方基于同一份链上记录核实黄金持有状态。

资金结算上，代币化存款经由 Ensemble 互通层路由至港元即时支付结算系统（RTGS），实现跨行资金即时到账。据《信报》报道，蚂蚁数科在设计该平台时考虑了与香港贵金属中央结算系统（HKPMCC）的兼容性。

这一进展也配合了香港黄金市场基础设施的建设。香港黄金中央清算及结算系统已于 2026 年 7 月 7 日启动试营运，并同步推出 HAU 价格代码，计划于 2027 年第一季度正式启用，届时将连接 RTGS 实现货银对付。

同在 11 月 2 日，香港黄金交易所与中信银行（国际）宣布在 Ensemble 项目下完成以代币化存款支持黄金交易的试点测试。作为该交易所唯一的结算银行，信银国际计划于 2027 年推出商业化服务，让传统存款与代币化存款并行，支持黄金交易 7×24 小时即时交收。

立法层面，许正宇表示，特区政府正就虚拟资产交易、托管、提供意见及管理服务的监管制度制订立法建议，目标在 2026 年内向立法会提交修订条例草案。

text:
Writing this in my personal capacity, but I have been flying these types of aircraft for more than 20 years, with over 8,000 hours, and have reasonable familiarity with how the charter world operates. I feel compelled to post after seeing commentary about the Lear 60 crash, from missile strikes to DEI to critiquing this poor woman’s final radio calls.

That last part is what I find most troubling. She was the second-in-command (SIC), and while she was empowered to point out mistakes as part of good crew resource management, she was doing her job, communicating with ATC right to the end in a terrifying situation. She likely knew before many of those calls that she was going to die. I have heard final calls from friends, from military pilots with thousands of hours in fighter aircraft, and they are just as heartbreaking because they know the end is approaching.

I understand the public interest given the footage and audio. But you do not know the aircraft’s maintenance history, whether there was a structural failure, if any failure was induced by turbulence, overspeed, or overcontrol, or everything happening in that cockpit. I am sure weather will be part of the investigation, but beyond that, it is speculation. The charter industry routinely hires commercial pilots very early in their careers to gain experience alongside an ATP-qualified captain before they move up to the airlines. She would still have the appropriate training, qualifications, and checkouts by an FAA examiner or designee.

Let people investigate, learn, and share the facts. Be respectful to those who perished and the families who carry their memories. God bless them and their loved ones.

quoted_text:
So $AAPL reports tonight. and most ppl will look at the iphone units..

but i'm reading it as one of the biggest chip and memory buyers on earth, because in july apple told us exactly where its ceiling is.

on the jul 30 call, tim cook said the supply cap was the availability of the advanced nodes "that our SoCs are produced on." 

then, pretty candidly he said "It's a demand forecast issue" apple expected the hit from supply constraints to "increase significantly sequentially" in the sep quarter, across iphone, mac and ipad.

since then the suppliers have spoken:

TSMC (oct 15): new tainan 3nm fab in volume 1H27, another in 1H28, arizona fab 2 in 3Q27. 
N2 capacity to "more than double in 2027." until then, 3nm help comes from converting 5nm tools and squeezing output.

Micron (sep 30): DRAM prices up high-teens % and NAND ~30% q/q. pc and phone units facing potential double-digit overall unit declines this year.

Intel (oct 29): pc customers "began signaling a PC slowdown based on the memory prices and availability." client revenue -9% q/q.

meanwhile apple's mac grew 29% in the june quarter, carried by macbook neo and macbook pro (i bought the m5 pro myself, its great), with apple still working to meet demand.

3 things i'm watching tonight:

#1 the constraint words. 
if apple still names advanced nodes as the cap for december, that fits tsmc's calendar. if it says supply caught up, i want to know where the wafers came from.

#2 the margin guide. 
cook said the help from inventory bought before prices rose fades "beyond the September quarter," and called memory pricing "a 100-year flood." 

the sep GM guide of 47-48% had ~1pt of tariff refunds in it. we're watching the december guide with neither cushion.

#3 mac vs everyone else. if mac grows again while $INTC's pc customers cut, memory scarcity is moving share toward the consumers that can afford it.

anyway management will spin. suppliers usually don't. we keep apple's calls side by side with tsmc, micron, sandisk and intel in @tessara_ai's company intelligence feature. will reply here with what apple says post-call.

text:
说说最近风很大的 HyperLiquid L2 Elysium：

先说优势：
1、需求是切实存在的，现在的 HyperEVM 就是二等公民，一方面因为不能抢跑订单簿的原因被官方人为限速，另一方面很多功能（比如借贷）被挪进HypeCore后，导致 EVM 生态活动急剧下滑。

2、前面有Robinhood Chain打了样，随着合规入美风起，Hype 可能又会成为注意力焦点，资金先进入Hyper Core，然后很可能再外溢到 Elysium。

3、团队之前是HyperEVM上最大的LST，至少从技术经验上，是可以胜任这件事的。

4、Day1宣布支持的就有Uniswap、PumpAPP、Fomo、0x、KyberSwap这些协议，另外还有70多个生态项目，所以生态支持上还不错，至少证明不是草台班子。

再说劣势：
1、最大的劣势其实就是Hyper官方的态度。Robinhood Chain就是Robinhood自己的，支持力度当然大。但是Elysium 和Hyper官方基本没一毛钱关系，别说站台支持，官方、创始人甚至从来没提过一嘴。

Hyper现在的当务之急是推进合规、RWA，EVM和Meme不在他们目前的计划内，甚至有节外生枝的风险。

2、Hyper EVM现在是被人为限速的，要提升或者修改规则，也是分分钟的事情，真到那时候，一个体外L2的必要性有多大很难说。

3、Elysium 说白了是想走 Meme 路线，但是Elysium团队没有被证明过具备运营好meme的能力。过去走这种路线的基本都是一波流，包括最近的ARC，不是谁都有RH那个实力和影响力的。

那假设要参与，我觉得有3种方式：
1、前期赌母币 kinetiq:native，这个窗口基本过去了，市场已经 Price in了。

2、现在这个节点找几个生态里的项目赌一赌，这个各凭本事，但需要注意控制成本、快进快出，别死拿。

3、等到上市的热潮退去，11月底解锁压顶，大概会砸出一个好价格来，假设那个时候数据上看基本面还行，可能会有一个不错的进场点。

quoted_text:
Biggest takeaways from ze Insider Pendle call:

1. PENDLE now directly captures protocol growth:

since January, ~80% of protocol revenue has gone to open-market PENDLE buybacks
~$3.7M / 2.68M PENDLE bought back YTD
if V2 and Boros revenue scale, buybacks scale with them

2. Pendle expanding from yield trading into the broader rates layer of DeFi: 

V2 covers yield, fixed rates and collateral, increasingly focused on RWAs and institutions
Boros covers funding rates and eventually broader interest-rate markets
the addressable market is becoming much larger than crypto yield alone

3. V2 is already generating meaningful revenue

$9M+ revenue YTD, currently annualising around $13M
upcoming products add new revenue streams rather than replacing the existing business

4. V2's next major growth leg is insti and RWA adoption

permissioned PT/YT markets are targeted for the next ~2 months
direction is tokenised credit, treasuries and other RWAs
opens Pendle to assets and capital that cannot use fully permissionless markets

5. ze curator module could materially accelerate V2 market creation:

targeted for Q4
curators like Armitage, Steakhouse and Gauntlet will be able to launch their own PT/YT markets on Pendle
those PTs can then become collateral inside the curator's own Morpho/Euler vaults
Pendle no longer needs to manually bootstrap every new market itself

6. le Boros has already reached meaningful scale

$355M OI as of 28 Aug, up ~55% from 22 Jul
$20B+ cumulative nominal volume in under a year
~$65M average daily volume
~$800K revenue so far despite still being early

7. Arbitrage by Boros is the tasty near-term Boros growth product:

launched 26 Aug
compresses a complex 4-leg cross-exchange funding arb into a 2-click trade
current opportunities are around 20-30% fixed APY
already at ~$58M notional OI

8. Boros can expand way way beyond BTC & ETH funding:

next targets include crude, gold, silver and equity perps
growth is tied to the broader rollout of RWA perpetual markets
if this works, Boros becomes a rates venue across multiple asset classes rather than just crypto funding

9. PT looping is turning Pendle assets into productive collateral:

live across Aave, Euler and Morpho
$25M+ volume in 6 weeks
around 5% of total PT volume over that period
service + swap fees can exceed standard PT fees, improving revenue per user

10. Pendle PT collateral adoption is becoming tasty:

~$220M of Pendle PTs are now collateral on Morpho
~95% is RWA-backed
Pendle's role is moving beyond trading into core lending infrastructure

11. vanilla looping opens the opportunity beyond Pendle-native assets:

Pendle plans to extend its looping infrastructure to non-Pendle assets
both permissioned and permissionless assets can potentially use the same rails
this turns the product itself into infrastructure rather than just a PT feature

text:
. $TEM 昨晚逆势大涨 8.67%，而纳斯达克跌了 1.07%、科技板块跌 2.66%，同做 MRD 的 Natera 更是跌了 8.54%。

市场在为一份什么样的财报买单？
两个视角聊聊：
1、从财报看这家公司的发展和财务
2、透过 TEM，看 AIDD

1、财报
Q3 总收入 4.115 亿美元，同比 +23%。但比增速更重要的是结构：诊断收入 3.035 亿美元（+20%），数据与应用收入 1.081 亿美元（+33%）。
第二引擎已经成形——数据业务只占收入的 26%，毛利率却高达 71.5%，贡献了约 29% 的毛利润；诊断的毛利率是 62.4%。
增长的发动机也很清晰：肿瘤检测量 +32%，肿瘤收入 +28%；MRD 检测量约 1.2 万例，同比 +300%，再加上待收购的 Personalis和 xT CDx 带来的 ASP 提升，TEM 正在打开第二条增长曲线。
短板是遗传性检测，收入只 +3%。
再说财务，这是本季最大的变化。
- 毛利润 2.667 亿美元（+27%）；
- Adjusted EBITDA 2560 万美元，去年同期只有 150 万；
- Non-GAAP 经营利润转正。
- 现金及证券 8.544 亿美元。
- 全年收入指引上调到 16.0–16.05 亿美元（约 +25%）。
TEM 正从「烧钱扩张」进入「增长自造血」的早期阶段。
但要打个折：GAAP 层面仍亏 1490 万美元，经营亏损还有 5690 万。净亏损大幅收窄里有 4280 万美元是证券未实现收益，不是经营改善；另有 5080 万美元股权激励。

TEM 不是自己造药的公司，它是 AIDD 的基础设施层。所以透过它，恰好能看清这个行业真实的进展。
进展 1：大药企开始真金白银、多年期地付费。
今年以来 TEM 的数据授权订单已超过 5.5 亿美元。10 月刚签的 BMS 系列合作总价 1.925 亿美元、期限 5 年：肿瘤数据+模型 1.375 亿美元，另有 5500 万美元做阿尔茨海默等神经疾病数据——这是它的平台第一次以大单形式走出肿瘤。
进展 2：卖的东西变了。
从一次性卖数据文件，变成 Lens 平台长期订阅 + 专属 GPU 集群：药企签 3 年 32/64 张 GPU，直接在 Tempus 的环境里建模。
和 Pathos 的合作里，「智能体分析工具」已经写进 SEC 备案的合同交付物。底层资产是 600PB 多模态数据，单个季度就新增 50PB 以上，外加新启动的 10 万全基因组平台。
进展 3：应用环节在扩张。
从靶点发现，扩到临床试验匹配，再扩到个性化药物的生产环节：Merck/Moderna 的个体化新抗原疗法 intismeran，每位患者都要先测序才能设计和生产，TEM 卡住的正是这个必经环节。
但：AIDD 还没跨过「结果验证」这一关。
目前所有合作都是固定授权费，没有里程碑、没有销售分成；也没有任何证据证明「用了这些数据和模型，药物研发成功率提高了」。另外，Q3 数据收入里约 20%（2210 万美元）来自关联方 Pathos，收入质量需要持续跟踪；Bookings 是分 5–6 年确认的，也不能当成当期收入。

对 TEM：增长、结构、盈利拐点三件事同时成立，昨天的大涨有基本面支撑，但约 9 倍 P/S 的估值也已经计入了很高的期待。
对 AIDD：它已经跨过了「药企愿不愿意付钱」这一关，正在从卖数据走向卖平台；下一关，是「AI 到底能不能提高研发成功率」——这一关，整个行业都还没人交卷。

text:
Anthropic 的员工现在有多贵？公司平均每个月要为每名员工花掉超过 10 万美元，一年就是 130 万美元。

昨天更新的 S-1 招股书里，Anthropic 披露了一个相当夸张的数字：2026 年第三季度，公司的人员成本达到 17.11 亿美元。

按照季末约 5300 名员工粗略计算，平均每人每月 10.76 万美元。

当然，这并不意味着员工真的每个月能领到 10 万美元工资。17.11 亿美元中，有 10.7 亿美元来自股权激励，占比超过 62%。剩下的 6.41 亿美元还包括工资、奖金、福利以及雇主承担的税费。

但更夸张的数字还在后面。

Anthropic 目前还有高达 323 亿美元的 RSU 股权激励费用尚未确认。随着公司 IPO，这些费用将开始大规模计入财务报表。

我觉得这里有个很有意思的现象，AI 人才的价格已经越来越依赖公司的估值。对于 Anthropic 这样的公司来说，股权本身就是争夺顶尖人才的重要筹码。员工愿意接受大量股权，公司则需要用持续增长的业务和估值支撑这些承诺。

而 Anthropic 确实有底气这么做。

2024 年底，公司只有约 940 名员工，到今年 9 月已经扩张到 5300 人，但过去 12 个月的人均营收仍然超过 660 万美元。

这可能也是 AI 时代一个非常特殊的现象：一家公司可以同时拥有极其昂贵的员工和极其惊人的人均产出。

算力越来越贵，人才越来越贵，但只要头部模型公司还能保持这样的增长速度，它们就有能力继续把价格往上抬。

最后可能只有少数几家公司，真正负担得起这场人才竞赛。

text:
understanding how higher timeframe candles form on lower timeframes is one of the most useful skills in trading

every candle has a few possible outcomes: it can stay inside the previous range, break higher, or break lower

once i have a directional bias, i use lower timeframes to understand how that candle is developing and look for entries before the higher timeframe candle closes

a daily candle with a long lower wick, for example, tells you price traded lower before buyers pushed it back up

learning to recognize these patterns as they develop gives you a much better understanding of price action and where to position

text:
For reference, this is what a chip/semi/memory cycle looks like:

1. Demand explodes.
2. Customers panic-order.
3. Chip companies raise prices.
4. Margins explode.
5. Everyone expands capacity.
6. New capacity arrives 12–36 months later.
7. Demand growth slows or customers digest inventory.
8. Prices fall.
9. Margins collapse.
10. Capex is cut.

Happened with computers, then gaming, then the internet (data centers), now AI.

Steven Bartlett asks James Talarico how Texas chases “equality” without chasing off figures like @ElonMusk.

Talarico’s answer: Musk’s net worth is a “spiritual sickness,” and the rich should pay something closer to the 1950s rate of 90%.

BARTLETT: “What would you have done to stop [Elon from becoming a trillionaire]?”

TALARICO: “We at one point in this country, we had, I think it was in the 1950s, had a top marginal tax rate of 90%. I don’t think it needs to be that high, but we used to have a political system and an economic system that more fairly distributed the fruits of our labor.”

“And I think the thing that really upsets people, particularly about the Elon example, is that Tesla was successful because of taxpayer dollars, right? Tesla got investment from the federal government, which is why it has been so successful.”

text:
Lighter 确实是唯一一个被黑了，用户能尽可能拿走自己资产的平台。

@Lighter_xyz  的设计更接近原生 Defi 精神——透明和自由。

平台需要做的事情是设计并掌握一个平衡点。

如果所有安全都由用户自己来，过多的风控就是用起来麻烦。如果平台包揽所有安全问题，平台自身就会成为最大的安全隐患。

成本-安全-易用性也是一个不可能三角。

Lighter 的设计思路是平台尽可能行方便，出问题了你可以可以提款到ETH主网。

HL的设计思路是平台本身只是中性基础设施，风险分散在链上的协议。如果真的有非常大的问题，可以公链级介入。

长远看来，这2种方案都要好过于cex的方案。

从风险上来说，DEX 应该能总体跑赢 CEX 。DEX 面临的外部风险敞口更大，市场和共识会留下好的机制，活下来的平台反而在风控上历练的更加成熟。

从成本上来说，DEX 共识越强，成本更低。
 
CEX的用户越多，业务越全，体量越多，操作越复杂，暴露的风险就会越多，就需要更多的成本投入到风控。DEX 也一样会增加风险，但是风控成本更低一些。这不是DEX的优势，是链上基础设施的优势。

只是探讨，时代会做正确的选择。

text:
Specific predictions for DeepSeek:
- DeepSeek-Cyber: 1017 –refusal RL +cyber teacher, mid November; restricted access. Later some research paper (maybe on continual learning? Robotics? RL in less verifiable domains? Rerelease of Visual Primitives for video case? Scaling laws? Something weirder? Infra flex on Ascends?)
- Dec: V4.1F-12xx, smaller jump than 1017, people focus on similarly to 6.2 Astra/Carbon. Some isolated new frontier capability, maybe a paper/blog on it (large swarms for math?). Lower cyber scores than the restricted model.  Unambiguously better in DSH than other harnesses. DSH is shipped with SuperAgent-related components.
- Late Dec: big open source Christmas drop (DSec?), hints of Pro, news/rumors/slander about compute buildout
- Jan 2027: lull, doomer moods. Maybe a paper on architecture (the above list, also could be deeper latent reasoning but probably not cringe looping)
- Feb: V4.2 Flash, V4.2 Pro. Flash around 6.1 Terra, Pro around 6.1 Sol but narrower. Slightly upgraded architecture (eg support for >1M context with hierarchical indexer upgrade, maybe mHC, Engram or vision tweaks). Pro: 52B active, ≈2T total, 500B Engram (higher N?). They say their new domestic pretraining cluster is operational and they’re working on scaling models further, “stay tuned”

March: DeepSeek V5 Ultra. 150B active, 8T total, Engram might go or be substituted for new sparse auxiliary memory. 10M/“as much as you have DRAM” context, legit 6 Astra level, default architecture and the backbone of Chinese progress for the next half-year. The paper says in “Conclusion, Lumitations, Future work” that it lags on frontier tasks compared to HPIM level models, and more investment in data generation is needed to build “human level AGI”. Maybe some more ideological loading. I am not sure it gets the export permit because it’ll be impossible to nerf to non-concerning levels on dual use. 

The above is something of a pot shot but I’m triaging the list (some other lines of work that I would like to see won’t be published). It’s neither wishful thinking nor doomerism (I expect Astra to be terribly obsolete by March; on the other hand, I don’t see how even this will work out compute-wise). Simply my honest forecast. Some subset of this is going to
happen. Maybe a fairly large subset. 

On the other hand, they have a track record of surprising me.

text:
Fixed vs Floating: RWA Yields On Pendle

What I like most about @pendle_fi, it turns one yield into a choice

+ Want exposure to the rate → hold the asset or buy YT
+ Want certainty → buy the PT and lock it in

---

I compared 11 of the largest RWA markets
PT fixed rate vs the asset's own 30-day yield

9 of 11 → fixed is higher
Median gap → +4.0 pts

+ $USD3: 15.2% vs 6.6%
+ $STRCx: 18.6% vs 12.2%
+ ethereum:0xddc0f880ff6e4e22e4b74632fbb43ce4df6ccc5a: 18.5% vs 12.5%
+ $reUSD: 11.9% vs 7.1%

---

Why this happens:

YT buyers chase points and rewards
→ they bid up YT
→ PT gets cheaper
→ PT holders lock in a higher rate

The people buying YT are basically paying the fixed side

---

RWA yields are supposed to be the boring, stable part of DeFi

Pendle makes them even more predictable

If you already like the asset, the PT is often the cleaner way to hold it:

Known rate, known maturity, no need to watch the yield every day

But fixed is not free:

+ you still carry the asset's risk
+ selling before maturity means market price
+ sUSDfr and USDG show floating can still win

⤷ Across Pendle RWA, the fixed side sits above floating in most markets today

text:
Writing this in my personal capacity, but I have been flying these types of aircraft for more than 20 years, with over 8,000 hours, and have reasonable familiarity with how the charter world operates. I feel compelled to post after seeing commentary about the Lear 60 crash, from missile strikes to DEI to critiquing this poor woman’s final radio calls.

That last part is what I find most troubling. She was the second-in-command (SIC), and while she was empowered to point out mistakes as part of good crew resource management, she was doing her job, communicating with ATC right to the end in a terrifying situation. She likely knew before many of those calls that she was going to die. I have heard final calls from friends, from military pilots with thousands of hours in fighter aircraft, and they are just as heartbreaking because they know the end is approaching.

I understand the public interest given the footage and audio. But you do not know the aircraft’s maintenance history, whether there was a structural failure, if any failure was induced by turbulence, overspeed, or overcontrol, or everything happening in that cockpit. I am sure weather will be part of the investigation, but beyond that, it is speculation. The charter industry routinely hires commercial pilots very early in their careers to gain experience alongside an ATP-qualified captain before they move up to the airlines. She would still have the appropriate training, qualifications, and checkouts by an FAA examiner or designee.

Let people investigate, learn, and share the facts. Be respectful to those who perished and the families who carry their memories. God bless them and their loved ones.

text:
Look man, I’m not going to argue with someone who is in the deal/knows these folks personally, but what he describes in paragraph 7: "black body radiation ejects heat into space" - runs head first into Stefan-Boltzmann/thermodynamic challenges that you can't waive away.

The problem is that radiative cooling is 90% to 99% WORSE at dumping heat than convective or liquid cooling. Vacuum isn't cold; it's a giant thermos that refuses to accept heat. You can't just say, "please, heat, go away into the vast emptiness of space." It sticks around... for a very long time! And it leaves slowly!

NOW, I have watched SO MANY videos trying to understand why very smart folks think this isn't a showstopper (for example, this one: https://t.co/Su0RvH8GKR), because when this many people line up behind an idea, I have to assume I'm missing something.

Just from a basic physics perspective, to cool a single modern AI rack, you'd need a tennis court (not an exaggeration) of radiators in orbit, and a full football field of plumbing pumping fluid just to hit 2 megawatts (about two racks). Which can be done! But it seems VERY, VERY hard! And WILDLY inefficient!

PLEASE, I genuinely want to be smarter about this — SOMEONE point me to the math I'm missing!
author: aronchick
quoted_text:
The total difficulty of cooling in space is vastly harder than on the ground

But 99.9999% of that challenge is Starship

Once you have the ability to get huge amounts of mass into space cheaply, it is genuinely easier to cool things in space

Your cooling system is passive

Just a giant piece of metal that is a) light w/ b) high thermal conductivity 

Aluminum is a good candidate

And then you have a working fluid that just circulates forever inside the metal structure
 
Ammonia is historical industry standard for radiators in space

You need a fluid where the critical point is optimized around the temperature of the chips

The working fluid goes from liquid phase to gas phase near the chips, and this change in density drives the hotter gas to pump heat through a loop

The high thermal conductivity of aluminum rips heat out of the fluid and black body radiation ejects heat into space

Black body radiation goes like temperature to the 4th power so the hotter you can run chips and hotter you can get the working fluid the better you can shed heat

It's honestly a way simpler system than on the ground

author: HerculesNimbus
quoted_text:
If there is any lesson I should learn from this incident, it is that macro always prevails

我其实已经看到了严重的流动性问题，但太有点侥幸AI earnings能不能带板块幸免于难。当时尤其被得到Anthropic ARR重新加速、HF & fundamental持仓轻的信息给encourage了。并认为Ant为了上市前会给一些“甜头”，而接下去ER与信息大都走反。在macro liquidity严重紧缺的时候任何多头容错都很低，乃非对称性风险。我手上的tail risk CDS hedge都远远不够cover loss

Looking forward，市场会如何？显然macro的impact只是缓解没有消失。乐观方面是：IR vol冲高慢慢回落，Credit spread开始改善。但同时，在Ant上市前，股市内部的流动性其实开始变紧——投资人卖出CSP semi准备买Ant。流动性差的时候市场更容易质疑 Y28 forecast和FCF。这下半周，eq IV开始上升，我怀疑一些“hunting elephant”已经开始要得手

期间我退出了很多Goog和一些其他股票。但是还没有deploy这一部分saving capital，主要因为那部分钱更多以长期saving为主，而且在观察deleverage情况

AI泡沫是不是破灭了？我甚至不觉得是泡沫。我们与2000年有完全本质的区别——最前端labs是有盈利的

我发现近期金融市场流动性 VS 科技公司流动性冰火两重天——某些意义上是科技公司i.e. Ant融资，吸走了流动性导致股市流动性变差。我前几天甚至有些担心，垃圾小型neocloud暴雷会导致CDS整体变宽——private loan fund赎回——Fire sale中出现芯片折价——再引发semi整体残值重估。但是一个CSP的好朋友告诉我：现在leather jack的卡就是硬通货，会被立即抢走，而且CSP很轻松能调用各种外部workload。所以实体不像00年，不缺钱、能融到钱（MSFT 25b长债）导致行业 vs 市场偏差，导致算力需求曲线不但供不应求，且forward contango

金融市场表现得像今天这样是一种流动性不足下的错杀，其原因：1. 市场没有做好准备追捧科技重资产模式；2. AI相关融资没有波及行业外公司——仅仅由AI/semi承受了全部冲击。市场流动性紧而不破已经一个月了，维持这种流动性严重磨损伤害实体，不过同时很难持久。市场要么短期被全面扩散，把包括AAPL、GS全部砸下去；要么流动性改善带动空头平仓 & 极低的AI仓位回补（上周前4天HF已经开始净买入了）。我认为下周后者概率更大

大模型第一次亲手改了另一个模型的脑子，而且只动了 0.016%。

作者让 GPT-6 Astra 直接编辑 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的权重，不用梯度、不用训练：只改 0.016% 的权重，就修掉了小模型的推理死循环，数学能力最高提升 6 倍，指令遵循提升 3 倍。他们把这叫 Weight-Space Programming，意思是前沿模型第一次能原生读写神经网络的权重。

这个如果可验证意义可不小：以后调模型不一定非要走训练、微调重流程，也许可以直接让大模型当“脑外科医生”，定向改几个权重就纠正行为。省下来的算力和时间，会先流向最会用这招的人。

另外，如果担心市场的退出流动性脆弱，可以通过类似paper的模式，质押分站内收入，慢慢回本。因为只有质押的部分（目前42m）在分享收入20%的usdc，目前能确定上一周是分3200刀，也就是这周质押的直接收益就是7%（年化365%），另外，这42m其实有个小的信息差，里面混杂了空投锁定的（粗估）22m，锁定的部分只有0.25的权重，主动质押的，和市场买入的20m是完全权重，所以，第一周基本就能回款12%（年化625%）左右。

盈亏问题也跟paper当时lp被攻击类似，比如今天被高手掏走了一些，明天可能会有人亏一些回去，如果这周下来，平台依然整体亏损，那就没有分红了，而且亏损的数额会延续到下一周，直到开始盈利才分钱。
