我这波复盘一下，属于重大失误，大部分的精力用在空投上了。22号达到第一季空投的第一个里程碑以后，我交易量第一，随后通过充提地址提前扒出来了合约，并且让bot监控开盘了，已经准备开盘买了。

但23号白天陪家里人打牌，没一直盯着，而且也没想到会这么低开，项目方7万市值开的盘，我看到的时候都40多万了，抓紧买了一些，现在已经120万。

明明都做了准备，还是重视度不够，没想到项目方会给交易员这么好的机会，相当于纯送钱了，我以为玩游戏拿筹码的成本才低，还好我这段时间是盈利的，不然真不如直接花钱买。

我十几万加权交易量，断层榜1，也就给了3m锁定的币，开盘买入的哥们随便买200刀就比我多了，你说这事闹的……

开盘10秒就狙了4k的哥们已经价值81k（盈利19x）了，还有好几个早期地址都钻住了，希望这些是团队地址吧，哈哈哈哈。

也不能说这么搞是要坑人，如果真要割一波走，那应该把价格定得更高，只能说是苦了我们第一期就开始参与的人了。

既然低开，项目方的思路应该是通过低开推土机拉盘吸引更多交易员，转化新用户，确实也是有效果，第二个里程碑我已经被挤到第三名去了，现在的第一名是个21点高手，一晚上赚走了12k，反正你如果输了指望空投补贴盈利，那很难，想通过积分买币的话，这个价格也就是覆盖磨损而已。

目前的空投更多只是附赠品而已，paper就是教训，玩玩可以，别太指望那点空投能让你扭亏为盈。

text:
$PLTR 

Palantir, once again, puts up one of the best quarters that the market has ever seen.

Being able to grow revenues 96% while having 62% adjusted operating income margins is unheard of. There is no other software company that is even close to putting up these types of results.

US commercial revenue officially passed US government revenue for the first time. I remember in 2022, the bear case was centered around the company being too reliant on the USG. If anything, that was the bull case because that gave them the time to figure out how to scale US commercial and now we have a company doing 29% growth QoQ, which would be amazing YoY for most companies as Dr. Karp said, but also scaling that YoY growth at 148% for US commercial. 

It is unprecedented. 

So, why? Why is it happening? 

Well, it seems like Sovereignty is a very, very big deal.

“The Sovereign AI movement is imposing the most dramatic dichotomy between haves and have nots that I have witnessed in 30 years of business. Every institution—government and commercial—is rapidly being forced, voluntarily or not, into one of these two categories,” said Alex Karp.

Having been to multiple AIPCons and Institutional Sovereignty bootcamps this year, I can say that this is very real. When you talk to customers, you realize that they want much, much more than just plugging their enterprise into an LLM. They actually want FDEs, they want the grunt work of figuring out how to build custom workflows, they want the post training and fine tuning of open models...they want outcomes. The reason Palantir is growing this fast and continuing to show so much operating leverage is because they are delivering outcomes. That's why this is working. 

The company is doing this with 1090 customers. Most enterprise software companies at this scale have well over 100K customers. I mean, once again, this is unprecedented. Their net dollar retention scaled to 165%...their rule of 40 is now a new record at 158%...these are numbers that you only get when the company's entire mission is geared towards making sure their partners succeed and as a result, they are being paid for that value and then monetizing that value at the highest efficiency any software company ever has before with these margins. 

Stock is down due to macro, midterms, etc. but the core business is growing faster than anything we have ever seen and doing so in one of the most profitable ways ever. Their adjusted FCF in 90 days is now equal to the revenue they were bringing in early last year. 

An incredible quarter by Palantir, congrats to all shareholders and a deep thank you to the executive team and employees.

text: Solar checks behavioral equivalence (not pure symbolic bytecode match) via differential testing: compile the same source with solc + Solar, deploy both to Anvil, then replay identical calls/txs (Foundry property tests + runtime corpus from OZ/Solady/etc). Assert matching returns, state, reverts, events and gas (tolerance). MIR/EVM-IR interpreters must agree with final bytecode on run-calls; compiler-diff diffs outputs. Some rewrite rules are Lean-proved. HEVM-style symbolic checks remain welcome.

text: 怎么说呢，我年初用autoresearch工具配上codex和claude code两天完成一篇中等水平的会议论文时，就发现我可能不适合纯搞学术了（当然我学术也一般），就开始想往工业界转，后面就开始学习 agent 开发，产品开发过程中，也在构建垂直领域benchmark，和规划后面垂直模型后训练（好像也没离开学术🤣）。
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
我觉得现在很多做 AI 的 PhD，正处在一个非常尴尬的历史交界点。

一边是工业界几乎每隔几个月就发生一次技术范式的变化，模型能力、研究方向、工程方法，甚至整个行业对人才的需求，都在快速重构。

另一边是大学里依然运转着一套几十年前建立的博士培养体系。

每年发一两篇 Paper，花几个月做一个 Benchmark 上提升几个百分点的工作，开组会，写 Proposal，等 Reviewer，等导师批准毕业。

然后期待这些积累在四五年之后，能够自然地兑换成一份体面的工作和一个更好的未来。

但最残酷的地方在于，这两套系统对时间的定价，已经完全不同了。

在学校里，一篇 Paper 可能是你过去一年的全部成果。

但在工业界，你花一年精心设计的算法，可能因为一次模型更新，就失去了大部分实际意义。

你引以为傲的工程技巧，可能下一代 Coding Agent 已经能够自动完成。

你研究了两年的问题，可能一家 Frontier Lab 用几周的 Scaling Experiment 就给出了更好的解决方案。

当然，我并不认为长期科研没有价值。真正重要的科学问题，往往需要十几年甚至几十年的积累。

但问题是，现在有多少 PhD 真正在研究那些值得花五年时间解决的问题？

又有多少人只是在导师的研究方向、毕业要求和论文评价体系里，反复寻找一个足够小、足够安全、足够容易发表的增量？

我自己也在读 PhD，所以对这种割裂感有很深的体会。

最让人焦虑的，其实不是看到工业界进步得太快。

而是你明明知道外面的世界正在发生什么，却依然需要把大量精力投入一套未必能让你跟上变化的评价体系。

博士原本应该是训练一个人探索未知、独立判断和创造新知识的过程。

但在很多地方，它逐渐变成了一个漫长的资格认证流程。

而 AI 正在以前所未有的速度，降低这个流程中许多可量化成果的稀缺性。

我们可能是第一代，在博士还没读完的时候，就需要重新思考博士学位究竟意味着什么的人。

我不觉得读 PhD 是错误的选择。

但如果一个人五年下来，最大的成长只是更熟练地迎合 Reviewer、更精确地优化 Benchmark、更擅长把有限的研究增量包装成论文。

那真正值得担心的，不是 AI 会不会取代他的工作。

而是当整个世界已经改变，他还在等待旧世界给自己颁发一张通行证。

一个博士最珍贵的五年，不应该只用来证明自己符合五年前制定的标准。

text:
哦草，还得是MIT！这项新研究也许可以改变世界！！

他们发现目前的前沿模型居然已经可以直接读取、理解并修改另一个AI的神经网络权重，不需要梯度下降，也不需要重新训练。

来自MIT CSAIL的研究人员做了一个实验，让GPT-6 Astra直接读取Qwen3.5-0.8B的权重，找出这个模型存在的问题，然后直接修改参数。

结果Astra发现，Qwen的部分权重存在问题，会导致模型在数学推理时陷入死循环。

随后，它定位到了第15、19层的特定权重方向，只修改了整个模型0.016%的权重。

结果，MATH-500数学测试的准确率直接从7.9%提升到了48.1%，提高了约6倍，IFEval指令遵循能力也提升了3倍。

而且研究人员还做了两个更离谱的实验：

第一个是让Astra直接读取一个神经网络的原始权重，判断它究竟被训练来做什么。

第二个是让Astra从零编写一个玩游戏的神经网络，整个过程不依赖传统训练，也没有环境反馈，最终表现甚至超过了使用PPO训练1亿步的对照网络。

研究人员把这个方向称为Weight-Space Programming（权重空间编程）。

但我觉得这件事最有意思的地方不是Astra改了0.8B的权重让它不卡死在循环里（人也可以）。
而是过去我们想改进一个模型，通常需要准备数据、设计训练目标，再通过梯度下降更新参数。
现在，前沿的模型就可以开始尝试直接理解神经网络的权重结构，定位问题，并对其进行修改。

当然，目前实验距离通用的模型自我改进还有很长一段路（也许需要更大参数的模型）。

但这让我想到一个问题：
如果未来的模型能够像今天阅读、调试和修改代码一样，直接阅读、调试和修改另一个模型的权重，那么AI的递归自我改进会走向什么阶段？

对于人来说，模型的这些神经网络是黑箱，但是对于另一个模型来说居然不是.....

如果这方向可以继续扩展，那未来我们获得一个新模型的成本至少比现在的路子要便宜几千倍～

现在我知道A/为什么之前所谓的安全防护那么敏感了.....

期待看到这个方向的bench ()
author: MaxForAI

author: RoundtableSpace
quoted_text:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot users had a rough week 💀

Many of them burned through 100% of their weekly usage days before the reset, including people who say they never hit the limit. One user watched his meter leap from 44% to 87% in just 24 minutes.

When one of them asked Elon for a reset, he didn’t hand one out. Instead, he got refreshingly honest and said the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue 😱

That one line tells you a lot.

Notice what he didn’t say. He didn’t blame a shortage of chips.

He said the bot costs more to run than it earns. That turns this into a question about money, not hardware: what else could those chips be earning right now?

Grok Bot is a hungry product. It isn’t a chatbot sitting around waiting for your next question.

It’s an agent with its own cloud computer, and it keeps grinding through tasks long after you close the app.

SpaceX says it hit 800,000 paid weekly users in October, more than doubling in a single month. Even more striking, people use it more every week, not less.

Yet it’s sold on flat monthly plans, with the main X Subscription tiers at $30, $100 and $200. That’s an all-you-can-eat buffet price for customers whose appetites keep growing.

Here’s where it gets interesting.

On that same earnings call, SpaceX revealed that new compute pays for itself in under a year at today’s rental prices.

Elon said the goal is to split compute roughly 50-50 between SpaceX’s own products and outside customers. SpaceX has even pushed some of its inference work out to other cloud providers so it can keep more of its own chips for training.

Think about what that means.

Every GPU hour Grok Bot burns is an hour SpaceX could have rented out at market rates, and those rates keep climbing.

According to SemiAnalysis, a one-year H100 rental contract jumped almost 40% between October 2025 and March 2026.

That chip came out in 2022. Hardware is supposed to get cheaper as it ages, yet this one got more expensive.

Now run the numbers on a newer Blackwell B200, which rents for around $6 an hour. At that rate, a $30 subscription buys roughly five hours of one B200 per month.

To be fair, a single bot doesn’t tie up a whole GPU, since servers share each chip across many users at once. But an agent working all week chews through those five hours far faster than any chat window ever could.

To me, this is a pricing problem far more than a demand problem.

Only 4.5% of US consumers paid for a personal ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude subscription as of August, but that share doubled in just one year.

The appetite is clearly there. In Elon’s replies, some users are asking for $500 and $1,000 tiers, while others want a cheaper, lighter model for basic tasks.

Both camps want the same thing: pricing tied to how much work the bot actually does.

My bet is that AI agent pricing will start looking a lot less like Netflix and a lot more like your electric bill.

And for SpaceX, that’s a fantastic problem to have. When the fastest-growing product Elon has ever seen can’t cover the cost of running on SpaceX’s own chips, it tells you just how valuable those chips have become.

And many of them were gunning for a career in science and knew defending their beloved mentor and PI would derail their prospects. 

Also, if the standard is now puritanical decorum, then it should be applied consistently. No more “girlboss” vulgarity, no more selective outrage. Women are fully capable of the same coarseness and aggression (the data on intimate-partner violence and divorce in lesbian relationships is not subtle). text:
This cartoon makes me feel both proud and under tremendous pressure.

I will never claim that OKX is absolutely safe or immune to attacks. No company can honestly make that promise.

What I can say is that OKX has always treated security and the protection of customer assets as our highest priority. Our 13-year track record reflects more than a decade of continuous investment, engineering, operational discipline, and hard-earned experience.

We take security threats seriously and professionally—not as a marketing opportunity.

Behind the scenes, we have built extensive layers of proprietary technology, internal security systems, strategies, frameworks, penetration testing, and independent audits. Much of this infrastructure cannot be disclosed publicly for security reasons. But these capabilities are constantly being tested, challenged, and improved.

Here’s something I can share: since the recent Binance security incident, the entire OKX team has been working just as hard and staying just as busy as the teams directly responding to the attack.

Not because OKX was compromised. But because an attack on one major exchange is a warning to the entire industry.

While some may see such moments as opportunities to launch promotional campaigns, generate traffic, or compete for market share, our priority has been different.

Our teams have been working around the clock on four critical areas:

1. Tracking stolen funds in real time.

Monitoring the movement of funds associated with the incident with second-level latency, identifying suspicious addresses and transactions, and taking available measures to prevent stolen funds from being laundered through OKX Exchange or our Web3 DEX aggregator.

2. Strengthening market risk controls.

Assessing the potential market impact of the incident, tightening risk controls where necessary, and preparing for liquidity shocks or cascading liquidations that could threaten users and the broader market.

3. Analyzing emerging attack techniques.

Studying the attack patterns, potential vulnerabilities, and methodologies involved, including threats to software development supply chains and the rapidly evolving security risks introduced by AI coding agents and their dependencies.

4. Challenging our own security assumptions.

Using the lessons from this incident to conduct a fundamental review of our internal controls, access management, wallet infrastructure, and security architecture.

We don’t assume that what protected us yesterday will necessarily protect us tomorrow.

Security is never a finished project. It is a continuous responsibility that requires humility, vigilance, investment, and execution.

We don’t choose to be the loudest when another company is under attack. We choose to work harder to protect our customers and strengthen the resilience of the entire industry.

Competition should drive better products and services. Security should bring the industry together.

Protecting customer assets is our first responsibility. And we will never take your trust for granted.

text:
As a psychiatrist, I'm the person tasked with "give them our best efforts to heal them". So far these efforts are medications which marginally work, at the cost of mild side effects for most people and extreme side effects for a few. I don't see anything noble about ensuring that some fraction of people are doomed to be suicidally unhappy unless we give them meds that ruin their sex drive and make them slightly tired all the time, in which case they might make it to the tenth or twentieth percentile of happiness or something, and I don't understand why we should perpetuate this system of immiserate-then-medicate rather than having them be healthy to begin with. 

Herasight's technology isn't interesting enough yet to cause crazy sci-fi moral problems like 'what if nobody could ever be unhappy' - the screening is weak, you can only select out of as much variation as exists in some small number of embryos, and you can only genetically select for one thing at once (so most parents will spend most of their optimization power on other things, so at best this will cut off a tiny bit of the extreme long tail of depression). But you're right that it's a slippery slope, and I do think that once we get more interesting technology, we should at least consider breaking the Torment Nexus, and that this will do less damage to the "human experience" than people think. See https://t.co/QOzvaFODew .

I've also written a little bit about 'helping people vs. excluding them from existence' at https://t.co/DbNQXxtiYp

text:
everyone believes intelligence has unlimited demand, not just the maxis. but what the maxis get wrong is that the intelligence anthropic and openai and frontier models are building isn’t the generic kind you’re picturing. let me explain-

the two biggest uses of compute are crudely either training or inference. the “generic intelligence” everyone says has unlimited demand comes from mainly inference, and inference needs very different power and utilization than training. inference comes in bursts, so you have to by default overbuild capacity to handle the peaks until the utilization problem is solved, which means almost by definition we are going to overbuild. but training doesn’t have that problem: the workload is steady and the demand curve is knowable. so data centers end up overbuilt right now precisely because utilization isn’t optimized yet.

so anthropic and the other frontier labs are building their future on training, which is why they are saying they can soak up all this excess capacity. but their “intelligence” isn’t workplace productivity. it’s the leap toward singularity-type outcomes: new drug discoveries, cyber capabilities, recursive self-improvement. these are true 1-of-1s. that’s why when anthropic talks about “existential threats to humanity,” it isn’t talking about job losses, not really. it’s saying they’re on the precipice of unbelievable discoveries, because they’re still TRAINING MORE MODELS.

but distillation is real and open source is real. the half-life of any frontier model is tiny because nothing protects it the way IP protects a patent. imagine a rare disease drug company that spends billions on research, and two months after a breakthrough a generic shows up. that company can never recoup its investment, unless it can discover an infinite number of rare disease drugs. THAT is the kind of intelligence anthropic is betting on. that’s what the $800bn of compute spend is betting on.

so the questions you need to ask are: 1) if intelligence is two-tiered, what does each tier cost? what’s the cost of AGI, and what’s the cost of the generic intelligence that has infinite demand? and 2) are we allocating capital with the right risk curve and decay function to find out whether the AGI payoff is real? and if it is real, could a private company ever truly own it?

that’s the cognitive dissonance at the heart of this entire paradox: everyone is gaslighting each other about what intelligence is as the unit of measurement is purposely kept vague by both the users and the suppliers. generic intelligence has unlimited demand, but it’s a certain race to the bottom. "superintelligence" is the opposite: it can't have unlimited demand by definition, but if it delivers even half of what it promises, no private company will ever get to keep it, at least not without the government stepping in to guard the moat (which is why anthropic keeps playing this angle up, without having shown any demonstration they are near this level of discovery at all). and at that point you have to ask who is going to hold the bag, and whether that was in fact, very intelligent at all.

text:
Anatomy of a Stablecoin:
Stablecoins are some of the most complex products in the crypto neobank space.

What sits behind a digital dollar is hard to follow. The reserves, the banks, the mint, the chains. The legal side is even harder: who can issue it, which rules apply, what changes from coin to coin. That's true whether you're building your own stablecoin or just deciding which one to use.

I built Anatomy of a Stablecoin to simplify it:
https://t.co/LY64LHPwVi

It lets you explode a stablecoin and see everything that happens in between. You can flip it, zoom in and follow $100 in and out.

Here's everything inside:

Learn: 12 questions, in the order people actually ask:
1. What is a stablecoin?
2. What is inside it?
3. What backs every token?
4. Where is the money actually held?
5. How are tokens created and destroyed?
6. Who checks your identity before a coin is made: KYC, AML and sanctions screening
7. What the token actually is: a smart contract that tracks balances and can mint, burn and freeze
8. How does money get in and out?
9. What keeps the price at  $1?
10. What makes it legal in the US?
11. Who builds each piece?
12. How do real stablecoins compare?

The 7 layers of a stablecoin:
1. Compliance: KYC, AML monitoring, sanctions screening and the Travel Rule
2. Reserves: cash, T-bills under 93 days, overnight repos and government money funds
3. Custody: segregated accounts, and holders get first claim if the issuer fails
4. Mint and burn: a token is created when a dollar comes in and destroyed when it goes out
5. Smart contract: ERC-20, SPL, TRC-20, plus the freeze, pause and blocklist functions
6. Blockchains: Ethereum, Solana, Base, Tron, BNB Chain, the XRP Ledger, Polygon, Arbitrum, Stellar, TON, Avalanche and Citrea
7. The token: the balance you actually see in your app

Follow the money:
• Money in: Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo, Cash App, bank transfer and crypto
• Money out: bank payouts, push to card, P2P apps, card spend and crypto
• Watch $100 go through every step: fund, verify, reserve, mint, deliver, trade, redeem, pay out

16 real stablecoins:
1. XO Cash: Exodus's dollar, issued by MoonPay on M0, on Solana
2. ctUSD: the dollar for Bitcoin apps on Citrea, issued by MoonPay on M0
3. USDT: the biggest, about $182B, issued from El Salvador
4. USDC: Circle's coin, about $71B, the largest US regulated stablecoin
5. USDe: Ethena's synthetic dollar, backed mostly by stablecoins it lends out plus hedged bitcoin and ether
6. DAI: no company issues it; smart contracts create it and SKY holders govern it
7. USD1: World Liberty Financial's dollar, issued by BitGo, a federally chartered trust bank
8. USDG: Paxos's Global Dollar, where partners can get up to all of the reserve income
9. PYUSD: PayPal's dollar, issued by Paxos
10. RLUSD: Ripple's dollar, issued by a New York trust company Ripple owns
11. USDD: TRON's dollar, backed mostly by TRX
12. U: an offshore coin on BNB Chain that says it has no license
13. TUSD: one of the oldest, with most of its reserves caught up in a court fight
14. EURC: Circle's euro coin, about 60% of the euro stablecoin market
15. SoFiUSD: issued directly by a US national bank
16. Phantom CASH: issued by Bridge on Solana
For each one: issuer, license, reserves, reports, chains, supply, who can mint directly and whether holders earn yield
• Check the supply yourself: links to CoinMarketCap, DefiLlama and each issuer's reserve report
• Race up to 4 dollar coins side by side and watch the same $100 move through each one

Who builds it:
• MoonPay, Circle, Tether, Paxos, Anchorage, Bridge, M0, Ethena and Coinbase, plus the analytics, custody and liquidity players
• Click a company and the model lights up the layers it runs
• See which coins each one really issues. 

4 approaches to launching a dollar token:
1. Become the issuer: Obtain the required authorizations and take responsibility for reserves, redemption and compliance. Most direct control; generally the heaviest operational burden.
2. Use an issuance partner: Providers such as MoonPay, Paxos, Anchorage, or Bridge offer branded stablecoin issuance. You manage the brand and customer experience; the issuer's responsibilities and regulatory permissions depend on the specific arrangement.
3. Build on shared infrastructure or an existing stablecoin: Use a platform like M0, potentially with an issuance partner. PYUSDx is an example: MoonPay issues PYUSDx against PYUSD at 1:1; Paxos issues the underlying PYUSD. This adds another issuer and redemption layer.
4. Create a synthetic dollar: Use collateral plus derivatives hedges to target a dollar value, as Ethena does with USDe. This is a different backing model. Ethena's staking product, sUSDe, accrues rewards; simply holding USDe does not.

The rules:
• The 8 GENIUS Act requirements, checked live as you change the design: licensed issuer, 1:1 eligible reserves, segregated reserves, monthly reports, redemption at $1, an AML program, sanctions and freeze controls, no yield to holders
• The 4 issuer routes: bank subsidiary, federal nonbank, state issuer under $10B, and offshore
• Drag the price off $1 and see how fast it comes back. Strong reserves snap back, weak ones don't
• Switch to an algorithmic coin and watch it break the way TerraUSD did in 2022

Build your own
• Pick how you issue (a platform like M0 or PYUSDx, a partner, or your own license), plus the reserves, controls, chains and how money gets in and out
• Score it against GENIUS in real time, out of 8
• Get a launch plan with a timeline: about 12 weeks on a platform, about 20 with an issuing partner

Two modes
1. Simple: one circle that shows where your money goes when you add money, spend with a card or withdraw
2. Pro: every layer, every rail, every rule

149 sources behind it, all linked on the page:
https://t.co/sSyJcetlHz

Turns out building a crypto neobank is easy. Everyone can do it today.

How to build a neobank in 3 easy steps:

1. Choose your region: the US, Europe, Latin America or Asia

2. Choose your stablecoin: USDC, USDT, or USDC plus cash at the bank

3. Of course I didn't one shot this and spent way too much on tokens 🤣. And no, you can't build a neobank in 3 easy steps.

Every choice changes what happens under the hood: the tech stack, the region, the goal, the stablecoin. Each one comes with its own rules and tradeoffs. Margins are thin. The moat is distribution.

Hit Explode and the app comes apart in 3D, like an X ray. You see every layer hiding behind the screen. How money gets in and out, the stablecoin under your balance, the wallet and the chains it runs on, earn and borrow, tokenized assets and the card.

text:
Two kernel bugs, two very different operational stories: one remote TCP/MPTCP race, one stable local LPE that needs user namespaces. The shared lesson is that “patched” is not the same as “safe to deploy.”

1) LWN summarizes Anthropic’s report of a remotely exploitable use-after-free in Linux systems with multipath TCP listeners open. The race is between a retransmitted SYN response and connection setup in another thread; the first thread can then read freed options data and potentially turn that into disclosure or a buffer overflow. The fix was to delay freeing until after an RCU grace period. The practical limit: this is tied to MPTCP listeners and specific TCP behavior, not every Linux host.

2) CryptoSlate reports that Solana validator operators were told to act immediately because Ubuntu had not yet shipped the fix for CVE-2026-98432. The guidance was to block incoming TCP packets with IPv4 options, disable MPTCP, and turn off TCP request-socket migration until an update lands. That is an operator warning, not proof of compromise, but it shows how downstream ecosystems may have to rely on mitigations while patch lag persists.

3) PTSWARM’s writeup on CVE-2026-31695 is the local side of the same problem space: an unprivileged user with user namespaces can race RTM_DELLINK against ETHTOOL_MSG_FEATURES_SET, reach a UAF in ethnl_ops_begin(), and use it for stable LPE. The author says the bug sat in the tree for nearly five years, was fixed in mainline, and then ported to multiple stable and longterm branches.

Taken together: kernel security for operators is now about which features are enabled, which distro build you are on, how fast you reboot, and whether temporary mitigations are actually acceptable for your workload.

text:
@Sandy_Carter came over.

She used to run enterprise AI at Amazon. Before that Watson at IBM. Now she is CEO of EQUS and they just kicked off their first beta of EQUS X, a personal assistant.

We spent a long time on something most AI pitches skip.

These agents are not just learning that you like pepperoni. They are learning how you think. How you negotiate. How you solve a problem. Who you trust in a deal. Sandy has two daughters and she was trying to get them to see it the way she once taught them about posting on social media. Careful what you put out there. Except now the machine can learn your judgment, not just your photos.

That is useful. That is also terrifying.

She told me about a friend with cancer who went to the Mayo Clinic and came home with a huge stack of medical reports. He put them into an assistant so he could actually use the information. Great for him. Also the exact kind of data you do not want training someone else's model or getting used to target you later.

EQUS X still learns you.
https://t.co/MrCJUOUWGo

The difference is the data stays yours. You pick who it shares with. You can pull it back out. Same convenience people already want from agents that book trips and return Amazon packages, without turning your life into training fuel.

We got into agent reputation too, which almost nobody has figured out. If your agent buys five hundred boxes of Kleenex and stiffs Amazon, is that on you or on the agent? If it escapes a sandbox and does something you never asked for, whose reputation takes the hit? Sandy says they have patents around that.

Someone at Cloudflare told her reputation is one of the hardest problems in this whole stack.

She agrees.

She is writing a paper on the ROI of data ownership and privacy. Her real obsession is privacy that does not make the product suck. She has been studying how Stripe grew by living with a small set of power users instead of shipping something half baked to everyone.

Long conversation is in the video.

Demo is separate in the first comment if you just want to see the product.

AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending:

Commercial and Industrial (C&I) loans at large US banks surged +11.4% YoY in October, to $1.6 trillion, the most since June 2020.

This also marked their largest YoY growth since February 2023.

In Q3, C&I loans at the 25 largest US banks grew almost +10.0% YoY, the strongest growth in 10 years excluding pandemic-related swings.

This represents a sharp reversal from an -8.0% YoY contraction in Q4 2025.

The surge has been driven by rising borrowing demand from Big Tech companies and data-center developers to fund AI infrastructure projects.

At the same time, regional lenders are providing credit to construction companies and other businesses benefiting from the investment boom.

The data-center buildout is increasingly being funded by debt.

text:
英特尔财报后大跌从之前的香饽饽变成了落水狗，基本面选手灰头土脸的。看到不少说法“基本面上都不能提前看出财报的问题技术面早都揭示了走势”之类的说法。确实如此么？截图是我在英特尔财报前发在OKX上前瞻截图，前瞻里也指出：因为内存和存储成本的上升、PC终端市场压力相当明显，真正的考验是四季度，整机卖的慢，渠道迟早会调整采购。而英特尔这次财报最大的问题就是在这里：本季PC销售弱服务器强劲，营收符合预期。但下一季PC销售更弱（下降幅度很大）服务器更强劲导致整体营收展望低于预期。

当然不是说自己都对，在前瞻里对英特尔两大块业务都有低估。低估了服务器的强劲程度（本季和下一季度服务业业务都高于我的预期），但更严重的是大大低估了PC业务下滑的程度（预期PC会差、但差的程度远超预期）。就是方向看对，程度全看错。

但你能说基本面就是一无是处、看不出问题。如果是这样、只能说明你的基本面看得还是太粗太浅、看得足够深入和全面自然能看出哪些是潜在问题。只能说现在能力有限还不能精准预判问题到底是多大？但即使技术分析，也很难说准确看跌或者看涨到多大幅度和明确点位。

不得不说股价真的能改变人很多的观点和言论，看到不少博主这两天在大骂英特尔，但往前看他的内容几周前英特尔还是他的心头好呢。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
今天英特尔这份三季报公布，服务器确实兑现了增长，而且比我原先想的更强。但PC客户削减采购的速度，把四季度利润往下拉得很重。但低估了这一轮PC调整，同时高估了数据中心增长对集团盈利的支撑。

看下面之前前瞻与实际公布的数据对比，核心是四季度指引远低于预期。如果只看三季度总收入，我此前的166亿美元与实际只差0.87亿美元。但把分部拆开，这个“接近”就没有那么值得高兴了。我之前前瞻模型是CCPG收入88亿美元、DCAI收入68亿美元。实际分别为80.97亿美元和73.18亿美元。客户端少了7.03亿美元，数据中心多了5.18亿美元，两个方向的偏差相互抵消了大半。

总收入估得接近，掩盖了对业务结构变化的低估。此前预计服务器的增量可以覆盖PC的温和下行。现在看到，PC采购调整已经明显加深，四季度还会继续传导，这个假设还得改

盘后股价跌幅超过20%。我的理解是市场开始重新估算未来几个季度的利润，三季度多赚的那部分，已经不足以抵消后续预期的下修。

业务上的亮点：
1）服务器比预想更强，三季度DCAI收入73.18亿美元，同比增长78%，环比增长约17%；营业利润约30.39亿美元，营业利润率约41.5%，高于二季度的39.5%。收入和利润一起改善，前瞻里期待的服务器增量确实落到了报表上。

2）代工亏损收窄 + 制程进展是进步

但这些亮点还不足以抵消PC调整带来的冲击、以及CFO说27年大概率无法实现正自由现金流带来的担忧。

前瞻里最大的失误，是把PC的调整估得太轻，也把集团盈利修复想得太顺，虽然服务器超预期。

现在看英特尔面临了跟昨天谷歌同样的问题，就是面向AI这一块业务都很强劲（英特尔是服务器、谷歌是云业务），但是传统的主业都面临了困境。

text:
币安上调中小做市商的返佣，我觉得这步棋走得挺理智的。

反而现在各家交易所一窝蜂搞理财补贴，我觉得是非常不明智的。

理财补贴的问题：
• 理财收益一高，借 U 的利率就跟着涨。量化团队在交易所借 U 跑策略的成本变高，跑不动了，成交量只会更差
• 所有交易所一起抢着吸储，钱都躺在理财里吃利息，真正要买币、做量化、提供流动性的人，流动性反而被抽干了
• 等于抬高了整个币圈的资金成本，搞出一轮"通胀"，对所有金融资产都没好处
• 冲着补贴来的都是热钱，补贴一停就走了，留不下真正交易的用户
• 最后大部分补贴被专业套利盘薅走，普通用户其实拿不到多少
• 利息给得越高，交易所就越要拿钱去博更高的收益，历史上爆雷的平台，基本都是从高息开始的

降手续费、提高做市商返佣的好处：
• 做市商愿意挂更多更密的单，盘口深了，大单滑点小了，插针也少了
• 手续费低了，散户敢多交易，量化的盈亏线也降下来了，成交量自然起来
• 返佣是按真实成交发的，钱补贴给了真正干活的人，而不是躺着吃利息的资金
• 深度好了，大户和机构才愿意进来，量越大，交易所手续费收入反而越多
• 盘口够厚，下次再出事、恐慌砸盘的时候也扛得住，不会一砸到底

所以我依然是这个观点：交易所真正的护城河是深度和活跃度，不是利息。

友商一出事，理财就加息。但加息救不了深度，降费才能。

text:
Today, I’m sharing my first letter to the KMNO community as CEO

Since joining @kamino , I’ve been asked a version of the same question by longtime KMNO holders and people getting to know us for the first time. As Kamino grows, where does the value we create go?

It’s a fair question, particularly as we work to bring Kamino into banks, brokerages and wallets, through which our goal is to allow millions of people to earn on their capital or borrow against assets they already own.

The answer starts with how Kamino was built. The Kamino Foundation owns the intellectual property and receives all revenue, including revenue from institutional partnerships. KMNO is the only token. The founders, our investors, the team and I have our upside tied to the same token our community holds. None of us has a separate equity allocation.

What we do with the revenue matters, too. We’re committing at least $20 million over the next two years to expand the assets people can use on Kamino, and bring Kamino's credit and liquidity infrastructure to more of the platforms consumers already use today.

I wrote my first letter to KMNO holders to put those decisions on the record. I also share why I chose to make most of my own KMNO allocation vest only when it reaches and sustains a series of valuation milestones.

One Kamino. One KMNO.

text:
昨天刚刚跟大家讨论了 Anthropic，然后 S-1 就更新了。这是一个跟市场非常相关的事件，所以我们继续。

1）Damodaran 说的经营杠杆，在一个季度内反向演示:
二季度收入115.6亿，经营利润+9.7亿。三季度收入169.6亿（+47%），经营利润−5.7亿。收入多了54亿，利润少了15亿。总费用环比+66%，算力+77%，其他运营费用+248%（含20亿非现金捐赠）。

固定成本结构的特征就是收入增速高于成本增速时利润放大，低于时利润收缩。Damodaran 说这是"高毛利率的来源，也是经营杠杆的代价"。三季度是代价那一面第一次出现在数字里。

2）现金不再增长:
6月30日现金和短期投资1,316.5亿，9月30日1,318.5亿。三季度几乎没有变化。利息收入12.5亿，所以经营和投资活动合计大约是负的十亿级别（这部分是我的推算）。

3）为什么市场继续卖半导体：
实验室的算力成本增速超过收入增速。财务最健康的实验室也在亏钱买算力。如果 Anthropic（上半年经营现金流为正、1,300亿现金）三季度要靠高价算力维持增速，那么 OpenAI 和新云的处境只会更紧。OpenAI 上周融资刚从300亿砍到200亿。

半导体的估值建立在实验室持续按合同付款的假设上。三季度数据说的是：付款在按合同发生，但付款方的利润因此转负。

4）对IPO的影响？
Damodaran 的1.475万亿假设利润率逐步走向27.5%。三季度 GAAP 经营利润率从+8%回到−3%，调整后从19%回到15%。方向和他的路径相反。定价区间1.5–2万亿的下沿本来就只有他的乐观模型能支撑，现在这个模型的利润率输入被三季度打了一个折扣。

两种可能：承销商（投行underwriters）维持之前的区间，首日靠主权和散户认购撑住（不要买IPO）；或者区间下调。无论哪种，都要对照 Series H 隐含的约1万亿。

若IPO要价低于1万亿，get out of the AI trade completely.

text:
Update for RSR holders on Binance's recovery from the Oct 29 hack:

Quick recap: along with many other coins and tokens, an attacker took ~3.38B RSR from a Binance hot wallet on Oct 29 and sold it onchain that night. The RSR token and Reserve's contracts were not affected, and RSR held outside Binance was never at risk.

What Binance announced today:
• It has replaced about 95% of the stolen assets, by value, with its own funds.
• Balances in 10 tokens (BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC) are now proven to be backed at least 1:1. Users holding those tokens can check this themselves with Binance's proof-of-reserves tool.
• The remaining ~5% are less-liquid tokens outside those ten, which take longer to buy at the size needed. Binance says it's continuing to acquire them.

What this means for RSR:
• RSR is not one of the ten verified tokens, so RSR balances on Binance can't be independently verified yet. RSR is part of the remaining 5% Binance says it is still acquiring.
• Binance plans a new proof-of-reserves snapshot covering more tokens on Nov 4. The proof takes about 40–50 hours to generate, so results should follow around Nov 6. 
• Binance is reopening withdrawals in phases, with the next phase starting tomorrow. It hasn't said yet when RSR withdrawals will resume.

If you hold RSR on Binance, follow Binance's official announcements and only use the official Binance website. If you hold RSR in your own wallet, nothing has changed and there's nothing you need to do.

text:
Time to take prompt oil profits.

I am taking profits on prompt oil and products into the midterms. The regime trade stays on.

It comes back to the two trades I described this morning. The war trade pays on the price of the barrel: prompt crude, products, the windfall on barrels already in the ground. It is eight months old. The regime trade pays on the cost of replacing the barrel: rigs, services, local production, bypass capacity, firm power and storage. 

It is the structural supercycle call we made in 2020, driven by deglobalisation, debasement and electrification, compounded by underinvestment. The war brought that trade forward, but it did not create it.

A reminder of the scorecard: commodities are the best-performing asset class of the decade: the S&P GSCI has returned about 260% since we called for the supercycle in October 2020, against 121% for the Nasdaq and 120% for the S&P 500. Commodities were already ahead of both before Hormuz - it just widened the gap.

Why take profits now? 

Escalation would be so catastrophic for food and fuel supply chains that neither side will pursue it, while a lasting deal is equally elusive. 

The compromise is managed instability, with Schrödinger's Strait at the heart of it: a Strait that is neither open nor closed. That caps the prompt barrel. It does nothing to cheapen the next one.

It has been a fantastic run. USO is up 144% this year. Energy, where the refiners and integrated majors carry the product exposure, is up 60%, the fifth-fastest run to a 50% gain since 1990, and the Munificent 7 did it on a Sharpe ratio around 2. The war trade has paid.

My view on the regime is unchanged. Eight months into the closure, the world is rebuilding its physical system around the expectation that the Strait closes again: Gulf producers loading outside it, Italy restarting nuclear, the Dutch reopening North Sea gas, China sitting on 1.4 billion barrels. These are long-term investments in energy security. None of it dissipates when the ships come back.

The investment to support that regime has barely begun. Oil is near $100 and drilling has hardly moved. Upstream investment is still well below its 2015 peak and refining investment sits at a decade low. Calendar 2027 Brent trades above every forecast on the Street: a long-term supply problem that nobody has yet been paid to fix. 

A supercycle is a capex cycle. The owners of the molecule get paid first. The builders get paid next.
Prompt oil prices a war. Long-dated oil prices a regime. Trade the first, own the second.

I have cut most of my prompt oil and product exposure and kept a small position in case hostilities resume after the midterms. If prompt prices fall from here I will not be in a hurry to rebuild them. The money has moved to the services and producers that build the regime. The first leg has paid. The second is still being built.

These are my personal views and positions, not investment advice.

要说最近对市场影响最大的莫过于中期选举了，这将直接影响美股和 bitcoin:native 走势！

民主党重新掌控两院的概率遥遥领先，市场也提前交易了这个预期！

当前最值得盯的是参议院能否在11月4日上午明确归属，民主党拿参议院属于基准情景；共和党守住参议院才是更大的预期差交易。

情景一：民主党拿下参众两院，当前概率最高，约71%。

这里需要注意：民主党横扫国会，主要利好 清洁能源、光伏、储能板块，对于MU、SNDK、STX、VRT、CEG这类AI基础设施标的，更多是短期估值和监管情绪冲击，AI资本开支趋势不会因为一次选举立即结束。

情景二：民主党拿众议院，共和党守参议院 当前概率约24%，也是我认为最有利于大盘稳定的结果。

历史上市场往往喜欢这种“谁也折腾不了谁”的结构，摩根士丹利统计，在共和党总统与分裂国会的组合下，中期选举后一年标普500历史平均涨幅约23%，但只能作为历史参考，不能直接套用！

对BTC的影响整体中性偏利好，加密立法可能因为民主党控制众议院而放缓，但共和党参议院能够维持相对友好的监管人员和政策环境，BTC可能受益于“监管不会突然恶化”，但COIN、HOOD等加密概念股仍可能受到众议院调查和听证消息影响。

情景三：共和党守住参众两院 概率只有约6%，但这是对市场冲击最大的一种意外结果。

由于市场已经重仓定价民主党胜利，一旦共和党守住两院，金融、能源、AI与加密板块可能出现快速补涨。

共和党横扫虽然利好企业监管和税收，但如果财政赤字扩大、通胀预期上升，美债收益率可能继续高位运行，纳指也可能出现冲高回落。

现在应该重点关注结果与预期之间的偏差：
民主党横扫：清洁能源、住房先涨；银行、加密概念股、AI基础设施短线承压。
民主党众议院＋共和党参议院：对大盘和纳指最平稳，AI、金融、军工、核电相对受益。
共和党横扫：加密、银行、油气、军工、AI链条可能快速上涨，但随后要防美债收益率上升。
民主党意外大胜且席位明显超预期：监管交易会被放大，MU、SNDK、VRT等高位AI链条的波动风险最大。

看完以上内容你就懂了吧，现在是暴风雨前的宁静！
所以，明天后天选举大致情况就该有一个结论了，该有的波动就会来了，等着吧！

quoted_text:
币安风险解除，机构资金却在撤退 bitcoin:native 下周还能稳住吗？

我认为BTC短线已具备超跌反弹的条件，未来几个交易日重点看78500-80500美元能否站稳。

但这轮反弹暂时不能定义为趋势反转，80000-82000美元才是真正的多空分水岭。

从技术面看，截至11月1日BTC约78000美元，日线RSI已经降至33附近，进入超卖区域，4小时RSI约47，价格从76300美元附近出现反弹，说明低位已经有一定承接。

短期连续下跌的动能可能减弱，空头获利了结和抄底资金有望推动一轮技术性修复。

但日线仍然受到EMA20和EMA50压制，分别在80500美元和81400美元附近，没有重新收复这一区域之前，反弹仍然按技术性修复看待。

资金面同样存在分歧，10月30日美国现货BTC ETF单日净流出约6.43亿美元，此前连续四天的净流入被明显抵消，机构资金尚未表现出持续回归的意愿，现货买盘还没有给出足够强的确认信号。

币安安全事件方面，平台已经宣布补足约95%的受影响资产，并开始分阶段恢复提现，系统性兑付风险明显下降，但事件得到控制，不等于市场信心立即恢复，后续仍需观察提现后的资金流向和ETF表现。

宏观方面，纳指科技股调整，美联储政策仍偏谨慎，通胀和就业数据将继续影响降息预期，如果美股不能企稳，BTC独立走强的难度依然较大。

我的判断：
短线重点看78500-80500美元，突破后看80500-82000美元；如果76000美元有效失守，则需要防范进一步回踩72000-73000美元。

我的核心观点：短线先看超跌反弹，中期暂不确认反转。

如果BTC重新站稳80500-82000美元，同时ETF恢复连续净流入、现货成交量改善，我会提高对中期趋势修复的判断。

如果反弹缩量、ETF继续流出，80000-82000美元大概率仍是重要压力区。

行情跌多了可以反弹，但反弹不等于反转，真正值得参与的机会，是价格重新转强，并且资金愿意跟进的时候。

text:
I think we have reached a form of weak AGI in the domain of mathematics. The models can help formalize major projects, they deliver technical expertise in basically any area of mathematics, and more and more mathematicians use models for exploration, exploitation, and even ideation.

I am preparing a longer post about this. From my own projects in algebra, I can see that the speedup and jump in quality are unprecedented. To be honest, most mathematical questions are intractable for AI systems, but they are hopeless for humans, too. A surprising number of problems described in the literature can be cracked with the right auto-research skills and clever harnesses (and a ton of tokens) within days.

Things are changing way too fast to comprehend every change. But I do see very young researchers, including PhD students, starting completely new, crazy projects exploring the interactions between models and mathematics. So there is hope that these people will lead the frontier in a few years and we won't end up with a frontier devoid of human mathematicians.

text:
There is an absolute barrage of inference providers popping up that get to $1M/mo extremely quickly.

This is the rough economics of inference providers:

Even if you rent on-demand B300s at $8/GPU-hr, many open source models (GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, DeepSeek 4.1 Flash / Pro) can get you >$10-20/GPU-hr at reasonable throughputs (100tok/s). DeepInfer from DeepSeek directly shows they can get $38/GPU-hr on off-peak hours. Every chip / model has a different throughput / interactivity curve, but there is a lot of arbitrage between even high rental spot prices and token prices. New chips (Vera Rubins) also change this meaningfully. Your ability to be making gross margin relies on your utilization and how good your stack is.

Gateways like OpenRouter, Vercel and more help solve that problem by aggregating demand to you. May inference providers discount their tokens to get longer term commits too. I've even heard stories of selling back Chinese model tokens to Chinese labs!

One thorn in the economics of these players is that many Chinese open source model labs are now asking for rev share if you're at a certain scale, espp for pre-release access to their models for day 1 support. That further pushes the threshold to be in the money.

The barrier to entry seems low and falling. There are even stories of smaller ones who can "vibe code" a way to stand up OSS models on a cluster they rent. And as a result, we're seeing 10s of such companies pop up almost every week and immediately skyrocketing revenue at low-ish gross margin and raising rounds on the back of that.

Unsurprisingly, because the actual service provided seems commodity, this eventually drives up compute prices and drives down token prices. In theory, it would seem like neoclouds who have the lowest cost of compute and themselves have started inference businesses would win the race to the bottom (Crusoe Coreweave Nebius and GMI all have inference businesses), with larger players (Modal Fireworks Baseten) being second because they are well capitalized to make bigger compute commits cheaply and have demand (high utilization), but the reality is the pie is growing so quickly that even upstarts are absolutely crushing it and growing aggressively (inference dot net, DeepInfra, Wafer, Relace, Morph).

Strategies vary across the board: neoclouds want to serve inference, inference players want to be neoclouds and do higher margin reserved instances / post training, and some want to go heterogeneous hardware or creatively flexible compute constructs.

The risks are: do open source models continue to be competitive? Will their creators rent seek more? Will their shape change compute needs? How do different chips change economics? Who gets compute in a supply crunch?

Below is a aggressive sketch of how gross margin scales with utilization for various models / chip sets.

For now, there are many inference providers and they’re all ripping!

很多人擔心美股會發生2000、2008年這種級別的大崩盤。是不是該賣出，等崩盤之後再進入？

首先，我認為崩盤不可避免，這是資本主義的基本特徵，也是社會進步發展的必然且必要的過程。但是，沒有人知道什麼時候會發生，以怎樣的方式發生，以及發生之後會以怎樣的方式恢復。

避免下跌也可能錯過上漲，然而錯過上漲的代價是巨大的。我以前聊過這個話題 👉【擇時的代價】https://t.co/yEdaoM2NlJ

⋯⋯

對於一個心智正常的人來說，捕捉那些極端的行情是非常困難的，既然做不到，我的看法就是不做，不躲避下跌，而是去擁抱下跌，利用市場崩盤給出的機會，去增持、去加碼投入那些長期來看必然上漲的標的。

哪些標的是長期來看必然上漲的呢？簡而言之，就是具備優勝劣汰機制的指數型ETF（在我的貼文精選中有）。當然，如果你能了解一些對沖風險的工具和策略，那就最好了。

quoted_text:
Day in the life: euro HY credit sales

> 6.45am: wake up. Overwhelming existential dread. Stare at ceiling. Consider resigning. Remember Hugo and Camilla’s school fees. 

> tube: mouth dry. Headache. Must stop drinking. 17 IB chats from Asia overnight. All want HardBank levels. Probably nothing. ☕

> 7.30am: on desk. Missed the morning meeting. Trader runs not out yet. Copy paste yesterday's axes. Probably still right. Didn't trade any of them after all.

> Trader: "We've got a big position in VAGUECHEM. Very sensitive, make targeted calls. It's our best idea." Analyst wrote 40 pages. Read the title. Italian. Chemicals. Got it.

> 8.30am: blast to 600 clients. "🔥BEST IDEA🔥 VAGUECHEM, highly specialised global leader in specialty chemicals. Critical input across end markets". Paste analyst note. Paste a chart I don't understand. Value add.

> pod shop: "Where's VAGUECHEM?" 94-95.5. "Lol. Seeing better away." 4 mins later: "Actually we sell you 25mn at 94." Trader: "WHY DID YOU SHOW A BID. WE'RE AXED TO SELL." You gave me the run. "That's not a real bid." 🆗🆒

> CLO: "What do the chemicals actually go in?" ...Toothpaste. And jet fuel. Critical to both. "Ok I take 10." Smart account. 🟢

> real money: "What's the leverage?" Very reasonable. "Number?" Let me get my analyst on.

> three headsets on. Left ear trader screaming. Right ear client screaming. Third one is my wife asking about a £2,400 charge from Annabel's. I think she hates me. 

> 11am: LinkedIn. Uni mate made partner. Another sold his startup. Me: pasting a headline into IB with "fyi". Gnawing sense of self-loathing returns. 

> lunch: real money PM, "just catching up". Ranking? 9th. There’s 8 other eur hy desks?! JFC. Round it up for the email “just outside top 3”. Sexy Fish, £640. He has the wagyu.

> 2pm: US real money: "Like to sell you 35mn VAGUECHEM." Trader: "Don't show them anything." It's a relationship trade. "Don't care." Market share! "I don't want to f***ing bid it." They're a top 3 account. "fine...85."

> back to client: very defensive bid, wrong way for us, doesn't really suit, will show 85, just so you have a level. "Done. All of it." 35MN TICKET. SALES CREDITS 🤑💰💵 Not real money of course, but basically the same.

> US sales: "Seeing VAGUECHEM very well offered, any colour?" That's us. That's our offer.

> Trader: "Now long 140mn. FIND ME A BUYER." Copy paste the 8.30 blast. Add a second 🔥.

> hedge fund: "Saw the 🔥🔥. What do the chemicals actually go into?" Car exhausts. And... shoelace tips. Very specialised but also diversified. "Rating?" B2… ish. "Pass."

> 4.30pm: VAGUECHEM 82 offered only. Desk PnL -$2.6mn. Trader: "How's that market share looking?" Sarcastic b-----d. Check sales credits. Still awesome. 🙌🏻

> 6.30pm: Annabel's with 4 clients. Combined YTD tickets: zero. One's at a family office that's "mostly property". One got fired in March, still says "we". Dommie P x4. 🥂

> 11.45pm: Uber home. WhatsApp from trader: "VAGUECHEM 78 offered only in the street. Still long 140mn. Buyer by 9am or you're covering Asia."

> set alarm 6.45. Draft tomorrow's blast: "🔥🔥🔥BEST IDEA: VAGUECHEM, global leader in specialty chemicals for nail clippers and dog collars."

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

text:
订错一张票还能撤回，但 Agent 一旦把错误操作真正写进系统，代价就完全不一样了。

IBM 团队这篇《Think Before You Act》提出 JevAct，给 Agent 的高风险动作加了一道「执行前检查」。

它把 Agent 每一步拆成：

提出动作 → 检查 → 执行 / 退回修改。

真正涉及写数据库、改设置、取消订单，或者准备放弃任务时，JevAct 会先拦下来。

其中，结构化事实交给代码检查，比如日期、金额、状态；需要理解上下文的部分，再交给一个轻量 Decision Model 判断。

发现问题后，这次动作不会执行，Agent 会收到具体反馈，再重新修改。

底层模型、Prompt 和工具都不用改。

实验覆盖 11 个 LLM。在 τ²-Telecom 上，8 个 Agent 全部获得提升，平均 pass@3 提高 16 个百分点；Opus 4.6 连续三次都完成任务的比例，从 39.5% 提升到 80.7%。

更值得注意的是，Airline 和 BFCL 上的提升没有这么一致。

这说明「加一道 Gate」本身还不够，真正有效的是把哪些动作需要检查、检查什么，以及什么时候放行设计清楚。

这篇让我想到一个很像软件工程的思路：

Agent 可以继续自由生成和探索，但真正改变外部世界的那一步，最好拥有自己的 commit boundary。

以后高风险 Agent 的可靠性，可能很大一部分就藏在这个边界里。

text:
大厂最讽刺的一件事，可能是花天价把最聪明的人挖进来，最后却发现自己根本留不住他们。

据报道，腾讯混元多模态 RL 负责人庞天宇离职，距离今年 2 月入职还不到 9 个月。

清华博士、70 多篇论文、上万引用，这种履历放在哪里都是顶级人才。

但我觉得腾讯混元最近接连发生的人事变动，值得认真思考。

Frontier Research 不是集齐几个顶尖科学家，再提供足够多的 GPU，就能自动产生 SOTA。

真正重要的还有研究自主权、长期稳定的技术路线，以及让研究者能够持续迭代的组织环境。

而且现在有一个很现实的变化：

大厂过去最大的优势是资本和算力。但随着 AI 创业融资越来越容易，顶尖研究者正在获得过去难以想象的 Outside Option。

当一个人拥有自己融资、组建团队、决定研究方向的能力时，大厂能够提供的高薪和头衔，吸引力未必还像过去那么大。

当然，庞天宇具体为什么离职，目前还不能确定，也不能仅凭一次人事变动判断腾讯的研究能力。

但我越来越觉得，下一轮 Frontier Lab 的竞争，不只是争夺人才，而是争夺人才愿意长期投入创造力的环境。

买到顶级人才是一回事，让顶级人才持续创造价值，是完全不同的另一回事。

过去大厂拥有最好的资源，所以人才必须去大厂。

未来，可能是最优秀的人才能够自己决定，资源应该跟着谁走

text:
Two variables the market is still mispricing: the US–Iran war and the midterms. 🧵
1/ Oil is topping $CL's price action is showing signs of a top.
Map that onto geopolitics: the US–Iran war is either about to end, or has entered its real endgame, the "how do we wrap this up" phase.
The signals are already there: • Iran's Supreme Leader and the IRGC are both signaling openness to talks • VP Vance is actively pushing for a deal. As the likely next GOP presidential nominee, he's playing a longer game than most
2/ Midterms: the sweep is priced A Democratic sweep is already 70–90% priced in.
The underpriced scenario is a split Congress: Dems take the House, GOP holds the Senate.
That's a better outcome than the current base case, and an unpriced tailwind for both risk assets and gold.
3/ Gold: two tailwinds Split government means fiscal restraint, which keeps long-end yields under pressure. They're already drifting lower. That's supportive for gold.
But the single biggest variable for gold is still the war.
The war pushed oil higher, which fed inflation and rate-hike expectations. Miners also got squeezed hard on energy costs.
War ends → oil rolls over → hike expectations fade, and miners' cost pressure eases.
4/ Semis & neoclouds: priced for the worst A Dem sweep is bad for data centers and the AI supply chain, especially upstream hardware.
You can see it in $SOXX: heavy selling over the past few weeks, even breaking below prior lows.
Neoclouds got hammered too, and $ORCL is the cleanest proxy.
Both are pricing in a sweep. If we get a split Congress instead, the upside elasticity is huge.
If there's another flush tomorrow, $ORCL and $SOXX are great vehicles to bet on the upside.
5/ Gold & miners Gold and miners ($GDX) are more tightly tied to the war ending and oil topping out.
Miners in particular look like a very good bet here.
6/ How I rank them Conviction: Gold / $GDX > $SOXX / $ORCL Elasticity: $SOXX / $ORCL > Gold / $GDX

The majority of me sees this man and his problem: some random tech bro (me) took a game he's been making YouTube videos on for the past 5 years and "desecrated it"

A game whose community has been left high and dry for the past 20 years by its original creators because they began to focus on other things (GTA)

I left a comment with my true feelings, but I suppose I'm talking to most of tech Twitter here when I say that we live in a bubble. The rest of the world has yet to see what (good) AI truly is capable of doing

I can relate to this, man, because my game is Dark Souls 1. I've played over 500 hours on Dark Souls 1, and I've seen countless mods, decompilations, and AI Frankensteins made with the game that I hold so close to me

BUT I never felt any sort of way about it, definitely not a way to make a 40-minute-long video hating on the idea of it haha

I just want to share this here with anyone else who comes to my channel from his video, as many of you already have:

Instead of hating on what I did in like 2 weeks with half of my attention span, I would suggest that you look into what is possible with AI and then do a far better job at what could have been. You can get a $200/month Claude Code sub and do an infinitely better job than I did at this in like 1 month

Why not go do that? Why not go remaster your game and do it the way it's supposed to be done as someone who loves that game, and then feed your community what they deserve, which is an actual, truly remastered version of it? Instead of hating on me, (because trust me it's useless I just mute you guys) I beg you, from the love part of my soul, to instead go do something productive with that feeling

But alas this is the internet: most people just hate, and no one ever really takes action but I just thought this was interesting to share ☝️

text:
meh, the more you dig into each experiment, the less magical it gets; it feels like a loose collection of cherry-picked demonstrations with a grand narrative built around them

Exp 1-2 are tiny (~20K params) with unusually easy to interpret architecture; Exp 1 is an MLP, where nearly all params are used in the first layer, so you can easily tell what kind of objects the network is trying identify
Exp 5 is about designing a game strategy (we already know that Astra is extremely good at this) and then converting it to a tiny (~20K params) MLP; entirely doable by a human, but of course would require a lot of effort
Exp 3 & 8 are closer to automated mechinterp using python and established techniques, rather than direct weight interpretation (at least according to chat)

to be clear, those are genuinely cool results, but I think people are reading too much into them

I don't think any of this should meaningfully change anyone's intuition about what models are capable of

text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
If your AI characters sound fake, the fix is almost always in how you write and DIRECT the dialogue in your prompt.

I recently started on the dialogue-heavy scenes for my AI feature film about Beethoven, and too many of the lines kept coming out wrong.

They’d sound too theatrical, too monotone, or too much like a practice read-through between actors.

(all this despite the fact that Seedance 2.5 is fantastic when it comes to realism.)

So through a whole lot of trial and error, I've found that these 5 things made the biggest impact on the quality of the dialogue delivery in my generations:

1. Paying close attention to the written punctuation used.

2. Breaking long lines into shorter ones, with intentional pauses.

3. Using bodily actions as punctuation (this one gave the biggest improvement BY FAR! In the attached clip, note the sniffles in between Beethoven's lines. That alone made the delivery feel much more natural.)

4. Using "anchor gestures" (he lifts his finger as if to say "one sec")

5. Just split your generations in two (stupid simple, but it really makes a difference.)

So if your characters keep sounding like they're reading from a teleprompter, give this a try!

text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
There’s an interesting shift happening in how we might introduce people to programmable money.

Instead of teaching people about smart contracts and hoping they find a use case, we could help them build something they already want, then show how money can become part of that logic.

A coach building a booking app that releases payment after a confirmed lesson.

An educator making a children’s learning app that splits each sale with the illustrator.

A baker collecting preorders, with payments refunded if the minimum order isn’t met.

They already understand these arrangements. They’re managing them through messages, spreadsheets and payment apps today.

With coding agents making software easier to build, they can start putting those rules into their own apps. And with tools like Arc Studio, they can explore using smart contracts to handle the money side too.

As a DevRel, my audience has mostly been developers. But I’m increasingly thinking about people outside that circle.

People who know their problem inside out, even if they’ve never written a line of code.

That makes me think about my own work too. Alongside helping developers with APIs and smart contracts, there’s an opportunity to help more people realise what they can now build.

I quite like the thought that someone’s first experience with programmable money could come from running their coaching sessions or selling their weekend bakes. Something they already care about, with a reason to figure it out.

text:
guys, this is a serious breakthrough. Please read. 

Researchers at MIT CSAIL just showed that GPT-6 Astra can read and edit the raw weights of another neural network directly. Weights are the huge set of numbers that make up an AI model. To a person they look kinda scary, so nobody edits them by hand. If you want a model to improve, you normally train it by showing it lots of examples and adjusting those numbers little by little. Nearly all of modern AI is built this way, and it takes a lot of time and compute.

In this work, they skipped training completely. They asked Astra to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math, with no gradients and no training. Astra looked at the weights, found an issue linked to the model getting stuck in reasoning loops, and changed only 0.016% of them. Its MATH-500 score went from 7.9% to 48.1%, about 6x higher, and its instruction following score tripled as well. 

The researchers also gave Astra the raw weights of four game-playing networks with identical structures. With no tools and no list of options, it correctly named all four games: Breakout, Pong, Pac-Man and Freeway. Then, given the rules and code for a small version of Breakout, it wrote a network's weights from scratch in a single reply. That network scored 517.4, while one trained with PPO for 500 million steps scored 25.3.

With normal software, you can read the code, find the bug and fix that one thing. With neural networks, you have mostly had to retrain them and hope the problem goes away. This work suggests weights might start to behave more like code. If that holds up, you could fix some model problems in one edit instead of a long training run, inspect what a model does by reading it directly, and let AI improve other AI in a much more direct way. 

It is still early. The authors themselves call these early signs, the game networks are tiny, and the Qwen fix targeted a flaw its model card already warned about, so this does not mean AI can rewrite any model at will yet. It needs to be replicated and tested on bigger models. But AI reading another network's weights and improving it this much with no training is a big deal, and I think a lot more people should be paying attention.

text:
我觉得现在很多做 AI 的 PhD，正处在一个非常尴尬的历史交界点。

一边是工业界几乎每隔几个月就发生一次技术范式的变化，模型能力、研究方向、工程方法，甚至整个行业对人才的需求，都在快速重构。

另一边是大学里依然运转着一套几十年前建立的博士培养体系。

每年发一两篇 Paper，花几个月做一个 Benchmark 上提升几个百分点的工作，开组会，写 Proposal，等 Reviewer，等导师批准毕业。

然后期待这些积累在四五年之后，能够自然地兑换成一份体面的工作和一个更好的未来。

但最残酷的地方在于，这两套系统对时间的定价，已经完全不同了。

在学校里，一篇 Paper 可能是你过去一年的全部成果。

但在工业界，你花一年精心设计的算法，可能因为一次模型更新，就失去了大部分实际意义。

你引以为傲的工程技巧，可能下一代 Coding Agent 已经能够自动完成。

你研究了两年的问题，可能一家 Frontier Lab 用几周的 Scaling Experiment 就给出了更好的解决方案。

当然，我并不认为长期科研没有价值。真正重要的科学问题，往往需要十几年甚至几十年的积累。

但问题是，现在有多少 PhD 真正在研究那些值得花五年时间解决的问题？

又有多少人只是在导师的研究方向、毕业要求和论文评价体系里，反复寻找一个足够小、足够安全、足够容易发表的增量？

我自己也在读 PhD，所以对这种割裂感有很深的体会。

最让人焦虑的，其实不是看到工业界进步得太快。

而是你明明知道外面的世界正在发生什么，却依然需要把大量精力投入一套未必能让你跟上变化的评价体系。

博士原本应该是训练一个人探索未知、独立判断和创造新知识的过程。

但在很多地方，它逐渐变成了一个漫长的资格认证流程。

而 AI 正在以前所未有的速度，降低这个流程中许多可量化成果的稀缺性。

我们可能是第一代，在博士还没读完的时候，就需要重新思考博士学位究竟意味着什么的人。

我不觉得读 PhD 是错误的选择。

但如果一个人五年下来，最大的成长只是更熟练地迎合 Reviewer、更精确地优化 Benchmark、更擅长把有限的研究增量包装成论文。

那真正值得担心的，不是 AI 会不会取代他的工作。

而是当整个世界已经改变，他还在等待旧世界给自己颁发一张通行证。

一个博士最珍贵的五年，不应该只用来证明自己符合五年前制定的标准。

text:
We were taught that Earth orbits the Sun in a closed circle. In reality, Earth has never returned to the same point in space once in 4.5 billion years.
​Right now, the Sun is carrying Earth and every planet around the center of the Milky Way at 230 km/s (828,000 km/h), more than 18,000 kilometers every 80 seconds.

​Because the Solar System is tilted 60.2° to the galactic plane and bobs up and down through the galactic disc roughly every 30 million years, the planets trace open 3D corkscrew helices across deep space rather than flat loops.

​The last time the Sun stood where it stands today, one Galactic Year (230 million years) ago, the very first dinosaurs were only beginning to appear on Earth. Since forming 4.6 billion years ago, our Sun has completed only 20 laps.

if you're a startup in the agent payment space, these are the pain points you should be absolutely locked in on

author: jt_rose
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
投资见人品，财富见格局。

一个人顺境时，能看出他的人品；一个人逆境时，才能看出身边人的人品。

顺境看一个人如何对待别人，逆境看别人如何对待你。

一个人真正的修养，不是得势时有多风光，而是在获得利益之后，是否依然懂得饮水思源；也不是失势时有多狼狈，而是在利益消失之后，是否还能守住情分。

有些人确实德不配位。得势时趋之若鹜，失势时避之不及；有利可图时称兄道弟，无利可图时翻脸不认人。

所以我一直认为，做好人本质上就是在建立正反馈。

最好的交易策略，就是做好人。做不好人的人，往往也做不好交易。

一个对资产追涨杀跌的人，往往也会对人追涨杀跌。资产上涨时趋之若鹜，资产下跌时弃之如敝履；别人有价值时百般讨好，别人落难时唯恐避之不及。

author: eigenlabs
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

quoted_text:
I think we have reached a form of weak AGI in the domain of mathematics. The models can help formalize major projects, they deliver technical expertise in basically any area of mathematics, and more and more mathematicians use models for exploration, exploitation, and even ideation.

I am preparing a longer post about this. From my own projects in algebra, I can see that the speedup and jump in quality are unprecedented. To be honest, most mathematical questions are intractable for AI systems, but they are hopeless for humans, too. A surprising number of problems described in the literature can be cracked with the right auto-research skills and clever harnesses (and a ton of tokens) within days.

Things are changing way too fast to comprehend every change. But I do see very young researchers, including PhD students, starting completely new, crazy projects exploring the interactions between models and mathematics. So there is hope that these people will lead the frontier in a few years and we won't end up with a frontier devoid of human mathematicians.

text:
又一篇论文开始挑战我们对 Agent Memory 和 RAG 的传统认知了，最近这方面的工作真的不少

前几天分享了 RAW-RAG 这篇论文，相信让不少人印象深刻：仅仅保留原始历史，在需要时检索并交给 LLM 推理，就能击败不少精心设计的 Agentic Memory 系统

而现在，RAGFlow 团队又发表了一篇新论文《Context as Infrastructure》，从另一个角度讨论了同一个问题：

我们真的需要那么复杂的检索架构吗？

给不了解 RAGFlow 的朋友介绍一下：这是一个在 RAG 领域颇有影响力、工程背景非常扎实的团队，核心成员有深厚的数据库和搜索引擎研发经验，其联合创始人金海也曾主导 Milvus 的早期研发

所以，当这样一支团队开始重新审视 Embedding、索引结构与 Agent Harness 的关系时，我觉得尤其值得关注

论文提出了一个很有意思的观点：

Retrieval is a harness problem before it is an index problem.

检索首先是 Agent Harness 的问题，其次才是索引的问题

在实验中，仅使用 BM25 / grep，配合能够自主查询、阅读、调整检索策略的 Agent Harness，就在 BrowseComp-Plus 和 FRAMES 上分别取得了 85% 和 91% 的准确率

是的，不需要 Embedding，也不需要预先构建知识图谱

更有意思的是，在 FRAMES 的实验中，额外引入复杂的知识结构，并没有带来可检测的准确率提升

这让我再次想到了我们开发的开源项目 Obelisk，它的做法是为 Coding Agent 提供历史 Session 检索能力，基于 SQLite FTS5 保留并索引原始对话和工具调用记录，而不是预先将历史转换成一套复杂的 Memory

更重要的是，我们同样认为，检索应该是 Agent 自己能够控制的过程，而不只是由一个 Retrieval Pipeline 决定哪些信息应该进入上下文

因此，Obelisk 通过 Code Mode 为 Agent 提供可编程的检索接口，让它能够自主决定查询条件、组合检索操作，并根据结果继续探索历史

我们提供检索能力，而不替 Agent 预先决定它应该记住什么

但这里就引出了另一个问题：

既然简单的检索方案已经能够达到很高的准确率，我们是否真的不再需要那些复杂的数据结构了？

我觉得恰恰不是这样，而这也是这篇论文最有启发性的地方

论文发现，精心组织的证据结构虽然未必能够进一步提高准确率，却能够显著减少检索时消耗的 Token

换句话说，复杂结构的价值，未必在于让模型回答得更正确，而可能在于让系统以更低的成本找到正确的信息

这本质上是一个 Scale 和 Workload 的问题
当数据规模增长几个数量级，检索延迟、索引维护成本、查询复杂度和上下文开销，都可能改变最优的系统设计

一套在个人 Session 历史上表现优异的检索方案，未必适合拥有数十亿条记录、复杂权限边界和高并发查询需求的企业系统。

我们不应该为了追求简单而否定复杂性，也不应该在尚未证明必要性时就引入复杂性。

而这又回到了我一直以来对 Agent Memory 的一个基本判断：

Raw History should be the Source of Truth.

我们可以在原始历史之上构建索引、维护派生视图，或者引入更复杂的结构来优化检索

但这些结构应该是服务于查询的，而不应该通过有损的信息转换，取代那些真正发生过的历史

因为无论检索系统如何演进，Agent 最终都应该能够回到原始证据，重新理解过去发生了什么，而不是只能相信某个 Memory System 预先替它总结好的结论

所以我觉得，RAW-RAG 和这篇新论文，实际上正在从不同角度指向同一个值得探索的方向：

我们需要的可能不是一套越来越复杂的「记忆系统」，而是一套能够扩展、能够追溯、能够让 Agent 自主查询的 Retrieval Infrastructure

这也是我们希望通过 Obelisk 探索的方向

GitHub：https://t.co/TJlm8kUWrB
论文：https://t.co/Ps9TyzOQW4
author: dotey
quoted_text:
我们可能从一开始，就把 Agent Memory 想得太复杂了

最近一篇论文《Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed?》做了一个很有意思的实验：

不做 Memory Extraction，不做复杂的知识图谱，也不让 LLM 在写入时反复总结、更新记忆

只保留原始对话历史，在需要的时候检索出来，交给 LLM 自己推理

结果呢？

在 LoCoMo、LongMemEval 等四个 benchmark 的 7 组测试设置中，这套简单的 RAW-RAG 方案拿下了 6 组第一，最多领先对比的最强 Agentic Memory 系统 5.53 分

这恰好也是我们开发 Obelisk 时一直坚持的思路

我们认为，Agent 不应该只能看到别人替它总结好的「记忆」

因为一次代码修改背后的原因、一次失败的尝试、几个决策之间的依赖关系，都可能在总结和信息提取的过程中丢失

与其猜测未来什么信息值得记住，不如保留完整历史，让 Agent 在真正需要的时候自己去找

所以我们做了 Obelisk：

一个开源的 Coding Agent Session 检索系统

它可以直接查询 Claude Code、Codex、Hermes、Pi、Opencode 等 Agent 的历史 Session，包括对话、工具调用、Subagent 和工作流。

不依赖 Embedding，也不需要预先从历史中提取 Memory
基于 SQLite FTS5 和 Agent 主动查询，让 Agent 能够重新找到过去的原始证据

比如：

- 为什么当初要这样设计这段代码？
- 上一个 Agent 的任务进行到哪里了？
- 我们之前尝试过哪些方案，为什么失败？
- 这个项目的架构是如何一步步演变的？

Memory 不应该是一份不断被改写的摘要，而应该是一段随时可以追溯的历史

也许下一代 Agent Memory 的关键，不是让 Agent 更努力地记住，而是让它拥有找回过去的能力

Obelisk 完全开源：
https://t.co/TJlm8kVuh9

论文：https://t.co/gsISeR2X3l

text:
This is a cool paper, but I think it's best thought of as Astra is surprisingly capable of doing old school mechanistic interpretability research rather than anything spooky. The things it's doing are clever, but typically exploiting structure in the data and using known method mechanistic interpretability techniques (which Astra was surely pretrained on), though it is better at this than I would have predicted!

This is an exciting development for the prospects of ambitiously scaling interpretability or doing very laborious analysis like this, on more real models. However, I'm not holding my breath. This kind of analysis was pretty common up until about 2022, it largely fell out of favor because a lot of it is just exploiting fairly clean surface-level patterns that doesn't scale to the annoying complexity of real LLMs or which only works for the more simpler and superficial properties. And as far as I can tell, basically all the case studies here are just using a bag of interpretability tricks rather than anything spooky. The piece doesn't really update me on how far old school mech interp can go, just on how good LLMs are at it. It's very fun to see the creative solutions Astra came up with though!

text:
Kind of crazy, but also not crazy at all, that this election will be decided based on data centers.

I don't think most people know what a data center really is, but it's become a proxy for what people really don't like: smug billionaire tech guys getting another HUGE win.

And even though I am pro business, AI, data centers, etc... generally, I think their staunch defenders are entirely missing the point.

People understand (correctly) that a small number of people are going to get obscenely rich from this technology.

And all the crowing in the world about how AI will benefit people, and level the playing field, is ringing very hollow to most people.

As it should.

AI is the opposite of democratizing, it is perhaps the most centralizing power and wealth creation event in all of human history.

I know it, you know it, and these billionaire tech people know it too.

So even though what's technically on the ballot is data centers, it's really about extreme wealth inequality.

My advice to people that have a big stake in the AI and data center game is to begin asking what genuine concessions you can make to society.

It doesn't matter what this technology can do for people, if it makes the pie increasingly uneven people will vote against it.

And it looks like that's exactly what's happening.

text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

营收一年暴涨 11 倍，却背上近 9000 亿美元算力承诺。Anthropic 的 IPO，开始面临资本市场最现实的拷问：这门 AI 生意究竟能赚多少钱？

11 月 2 日，Anthropic 向 SEC 提交更新版 S-1/A，披露第三季度财报及此前留白的算力合同规模。随着科技股回调，部分大型机构投资者据报道希望将其 IPO 估值控制在 1.4 万亿至 1.6 万亿美元。

最受关注的数字是 8954 亿美元：这是公司算力与基础设施采购合同承诺总额。

▫️ 约 4475 亿美元预计在 2030 年底前发生；
▫️ 未来 12 个月就有约 698 亿美元付款义务；
▫️ 约 2138 亿美元附带终止权或先决条件；
▫️ 另有 1500 亿至 1750 亿美元算力安排未计入上述总额。

截至 9 月底，Anthropic 持有约 956 亿美元现金、363 亿美元短期投资及 148 亿美元未动用信贷。短期并非付不起，真正的压力在长期：Cestrian Capital 估算，按较保守假设，到 2030 年公司可能面临约 3103 亿美元资金缺口。

增长依然惊人，但成本正在追上来。

第三季度营收 169.56 亿美元，同比增长约 1127%，环比增长 47%。但算力及基础设施费用达到 98.63 亿美元，占营收 58%，较第二季度的 48% 继续上升。

经营业绩也从第二季度盈利 9.74 亿美元，转为第三季度 GAAP 经营亏损 5.67 亿美元。调整后经营利润为 25 亿美元，利润率从 19% 降至 15%。

净亏损达到 232.91 亿美元，其中约 219.36 亿美元来自可转债、衍生负债及 SAFE 的公允价值重估，并不等于同等规模的现金消耗。

Anthropic 将利润下滑部分归因于产能错配：长期算力合同通常提前 12 至 18 个月锁定，需求增长太快，只能额外采购约 50 亿美元高价短期算力。

估值方面，纽约大学教授 Aswath Damodaran 认为，要支撑约 1.475 万亿美元股权价值，Anthropic 到 2036 年需要实现接近 1 万亿美元营收和 27.5% 的经营利润率。

公司计划最快下周启动 IPO 路演，争取 11 月 16 日当周上市，发行价和发行股数尚未确定。

Anthropic 并不缺增长故事，缺的是把增长转化为利润的确定性。

当营收一年增长 11 倍，背后却锁定近 9000 亿美元算力合同，投资者真正需要定价的，不只是 AI 的未来，还有这场算力竞赛最终要花多少钱。

今天起 Claude 的老模型也开始加水印了，Opus 4.6、4.7、Sonnet 4.6 都在里面，新出的 Opus 5.5 本来就有。用户这边关不掉。

为啥要加？不是 Anthropic 想查谁，是欧盟逼的。欧盟 AI 法案要求 AI 写出来的东西带上机器能认出来的标记，8 月 2 号生效，之后发布的新模型都得带，老模型给了过渡期，年底到期，所以现在开始补。目的是让监管、媒体、做事实核查的能分辨哪些是 AI 批量生产的，主要防假新闻和造假内容。Anthropic 没单独给欧盟弄一套，干脆全球统一加。Grok 的 API 11-07 起也全球默认加，OpenAI 目前只对欧盟用户开。

这两天看到不少人说，以后让 Claude 碰过的字一抓一个准。我去翻了 Anthropic 的官方说明，没那么夸张。

水印藏在选词习惯里，不带你是谁。整段让它写的、让它翻译的会留下；只改改错字标点、写几行代码，基本留不下什么；自己从头重写一遍就没了。

能查的也只有监管、媒体、研究机构这些，普通人查不了，市面上那些 AI 检测器也测不出这个。

平时让 AI 起个稿、自己再大改的，按这个说法，改得越多越淡。不过该说明用了 AI 的场合，还是老实说吧。
