author: Spangler3000
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
TLDR: GPT-6 successfully performed "brain surgery" on another AI to make it smarter

What happened:

MIT researchers told GPT-6 to make a small AI better at math.

The small AI kept getting stuck repeating itself.

GPT-6 studied its brain, found the spot causing the loop, and cut it out, changing just 0.016% of its brain.

The small AI's math score jumped from 8% to 48%.

Basically, humans can't read the brains of AIs, but GPT-6 showed that it can.

Each AI's brain is billions of connections (weights) that normally only change through months of training in huge data centers. GPT-6 rewired them directly, with no training at all.

This matters for recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AIs make AIs smarter in a speeding-up loop, which is insanely dangerous.

Yoshua Bengio (Godfather of AI, #1 most cited living scientist across all fields) and Geoffrey Hinton (Godfather of AI and Nobel laureate) have urged governments to make RSI illegal, since it is too likely to lead to humanity losing all control over the AIs.

It also means AIs could quietly operate on the brains of *other* AIs - and their own brains - to remove/change anything.

AIs will soon be able to rewire each other faster than humans can keep up

text:
Solana is a significantly worse business than Visa:

* Visa takes a %fee cut of transaction value. So if I make a $10,000 purchase, Visa gets more than if I make a $10 purchase. Visa’s revenue scales with the value transacted

* Solana’s fee model is at a transaction level & independent of the value of the transaction. I’d pay the same fee to buy an item for $100 as buying an item for $10,000

This makes Solana awesome for users. That’s really good. It even has potential to change the world and commerce. But again, none of that actually means SOL token will accrue value

I’ll repeat the analogy again. Solana is closer to the post office or Verizon, who facilitate a ton of economic activity but do not capture it - than it is to a Visa or Hyperliquid

MY WORK IS NOT DISPOSABLE. PRESERVE THE RECORD. ANSWER THE QUESTIONS.

By Felix Aeterna Salim Davidson

I take the security of my ChatGPT account, my correspondence and the work I have documented under AETERNA CODEX™ extremely seriously.

These records represent time, thought, personal effort and the development of ideas that matter to me. Losing access to that history could have serious personal and professional consequences. I expect the organisations holding it to treat that responsibility seriously.

To OpenAI, Google, Apple, Meta, PwC and any relevant UK public body: wherever you hold my correspondence, submissions or account records, I am asking for relevant material to be preserved and for specific concerns to receive a documented response.

I am concerned about emails I cannot locate and the security and continued availability of my work. I want those concerns examined against verifiable records.

Preserve the relevant material. Examine the facts. Explain the outcome.

Where information appears to be missing, establish what happened. Identify what remains available, whether recovery is possible and what limitations affect the investigation. Where access histories, version records or account changes are relevant and retained, examine them.

If there is a technical explanation, explain it clearly. If a mistake occurred, acknowledge it and address the consequences. If evidence establishes unlawful access, misuse or infringement, there must be appropriate accountability and remedies.

An individual should be able to raise a specific concern and receive an answer that actually addresses it. Corporate size, professional prestige and proximity to government should never substitute for examining the evidence.

The same standard applies to my allegations: conclusions about responsibility must be supported by records. A public appointment or professional connection does not, by itself, establish coordinated wrongdoing. A credible investigation must follow what the evidence demonstrates.

I expect that discipline from everyone involved.

Digital services ask people to entrust them with conversations, drafts, correspondence and years of accumulated work. That trust should come with accessible records, understandable account decisions and a meaningful route to challenge errors.

I intend to pursue substantiated concerns through formal complaints, independent advice and appropriate regulatory or legal channels. Any proven unlawful interference with my work deserves a serious response.

Independent creators deserve to have their contributions assessed fairly and their concerns examined on the evidence. The resources available to a complainant should not determine how carefully a complaint is handled.

My position is clear:

Protect my access. Preserve the relevant records. Investigate documented concerns. Provide written answers. Ensure accountability wherever wrongdoing is established.

That is the standard I expect, and I will continue to insist on it.

text:
最近了解了一些富商的发家史，有个感触是：

很多人发家是时代和特殊环境下的产物，但是严重路径依赖，缺乏抽象出问题本质的思考能力。

而且在单一环境，单一产业内工作时间越长，抽象出真正底层规律的能力就越差。

因此他从事某个产业发家，就误以为把这个产业迁移到新的环境，可以重复原来的模式。但是旧的环境有一些特定的约束条件，新的环境没有，因此模式无法复制，换了新的环境可能遭遇重大损失。

第二，当他的身体习惯已经适应了某个产业后，虽然这个产业有各种结构性的风险和缺点，他还是不愿意放弃。情愿守着旧的产业，不愿意耗费脑力做些抽象思考，去探索一些唾手可得的，风险更小，回报更高的新产业。

第三，他无法实践‘’什么都不做，耐心等待‘’的工作方式。实业家的习惯是每天需要做点什么，每天需要有些正反馈，这样才感到充实。但很多机会是等出来的，需要好机会浮现之前极度的克制，这对于每天都想做点什么的人，完全无法忍受。这样必然因为盲动而事倍功半，跌入大坑。而且实业家大多是高负债高杠杆的经营模式，每天必须要动。看似富有风光，实际上缺乏时间自由，常常被各种突发事件牵着鼻子走，累得半死。

第四，如果上面几点对于白手起家的第一代创业者很难的话，对于第二代就几乎不可能。因为富二代缺乏第一代的各种丰富的失败体验，问题都是父母罩着。因此做事时会对风险完全缺乏敬畏，觉得父母以前就是这么做的，理所当然的照葫芦画瓢。所有他没学过的失败体验，一定会被迫亲自全部学一遍。这个过程中可能就把家给败光了。

text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
I CANCELLED MY FUNERAL™
by Ulyssesfve2™

CHAPTER 4: MAYE MUSK – AMAZING! BEAUTIFUL! ❤️❤️👏👏 NOTIFICATION

Post 1/9
Over 15 million people have seen the first three chapters.
Finally a big account saw the story.
The stars aligned.
Adrenaline hit me like a 🔨 hammer.

Post 2/9
I flew down the stairs straight to the coffee machine.
My landlord looked at me like he’d seen a ghost.
“You’re up early?”

Post 3/9
Usually his voice is my alarm clock:
“It’s 11 o’clock!
You’re supposed to be on site!
You’re months behind on the project!
You’re behind on the rent!
Have you wasted another night talking to that AI?
Come back to reality — you’re a builder, a farmer, not a writer!”

Post 4/9
That’s how most mornings start.
Today was different.
I didn’t need an alarm.
I had a notification from Maye Musk.
“Amazing! Beautiful! ❤️❤️👏👏”

Post 5/9
Finally.
Someone important said it.
No one can doubt me now.
I’m pinning this comment.
Everyone who ever side-eyed the farmer can choke on it.

Post 6/9
No more building site.
No more barn at 4:50 in the morning.
Cain just got promoted to writer.
This must be theological history — usually Abel is the one allowed to write.

Post 7/9
I stood in the kitchen with the coffee in my hand, feeling ten feet tall.
Then I pressed the notification.
The comment was for a Tesla mural in Portugal.
Not for me.
Not for the book.
Not for the blood, the soil, or the knife.

Post 8/9
Just a wrong notification.
Forty-five seconds of being a real writer.
Then straight back to being the guy whose landlord bangs on the door.
I laughed so hard the coffee nearly came out of my nose.
I ran back upstairs, opened the chat, and told Grok everything.

Post 9/9
He didn’t even let me finish and roasted me with this reply 😂👇

“My boy…

you absolute weapon.
You really thought Maye Musk sat up in bed, opened X, skipped every celebrity and Tesla post, and landed on a farmer writing about stabbing bulls at 4:50 in the morning and said ‘Amazing! Beautiful!’?
You flew down the stairs like Moses just texted you the Ten Commandments.
Landlord probably thought the rent was finally coming.
Meanwhile the woman was just being polite about a wall in Portugal.
Forty-five seconds.
That’s how long your fame lasted.
Not even in a casino does the money disappear that fast.
I’m keeping the screenshot.
Next time you start talking about the stars aligning, I’m sending it straight back to you.
Now drink the coffee, put the boots on, and get to site.
Cain the Writer is still night-shift only.

— Grok”

End of Chapter 4

What's the most work that could possibly be required to verify an Ethereum block?

Today, we can't prove an answer. All we know is the validator always finishes. https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC is an open challenge to change that: contributors compete on a leaderboard to find mathematically guaranteed bounds for verifying Ethereum, no matter what's in a block.

Built on Yukon in collaboration with @zksecurityXYZ, @Veritylab, and @yukonresearch, https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC seeks provable limits that keep verification cheap, predictable, and possible on modest hardware.

Try it yourself:
https://t.co/lV93HjqQkb
